1930.bodyHtml: A new year begins. The economic crisis is worsening throughout the world, with no end in sight. The **NSDAP** seems to be strengthening in local elections. All very worrisome trends.

1931.bodyHtml: A new year begins. [? if works_program = 0 : Unemployment continues to spiral upwards. The strength of the **NSDAP** continues to rise. ?][? if works_program > 0 : A works program has been enacted in order to reduce unemployment. ?] [? if works_program > 0 and unemployed > 15 : However, unemployment remains too high for comfort. ?]

1932.bodyHtml:
A new year begins. [? if works_program = 0 : There is little to no good news in Germany. The economic depression has still not bottomed out. ?][? if works_program >= 1 and unemployed >= 20 : We have begun to launch a public works program, but unemployment is still stubbornly high. The people are beginning to finally have optimism, however. ?][? if works_program >= 1 and unemployed < 20 : We have begun to launch a public works program, and unemployment is finally starting to fall. The people are beginning to finally have optimism. ?]
The presidential election is in April of this year.

1933.bodyHtml: A new year begins. [? if works_program = 0 : There is finally some good news in Germany. The economic depression has begun the early stages of global recovery. ?][? if works_program >= 1 and unemployed >= 20 : We have begun to launch a public works program, but unemployment is still stubbornly high. The people are beginning to finally have optimism, however, with the global recovery beginning. ?][? if works_program >= 1 and unemployed < 20 : We have begun to launch a public works program, and unemployment is finally starting to fall. The people are beginning to finally have optimism. The depression has begun the early stages of recovery across the world as well. ?]

1934.bodyHtml:
= 1934
A new year begins. [? if works_program = 0 : The economic depression seems to have bottomed out, but there is still much suffering. It is not too late to launch an economic rescue program. ?][? if works_program >= 1 and unemployed >= 15 : We have begun to launch a public works program, but the economy is still troubled. The recovery has begun, but more must be done. ?][? if works_program >= 1 and unemployed < 15 : Our public works program has successfully guided us through the worst of the crisis. The economy is improving, and finally people have optimism for the future. ?]
[? if return_to_normalcy: With the return to normalcy, the political landscape in Germany is shifting. Liberalism is making a return among the middle classes, and the radical parties of the right are declining. ?]
[? if president = "Hindenburg" : The president is in poor health; he is not expected to live out the year. ?]

1934_end.bodyHtml: = A New Day in Germany After the death of Hindenburg and the presidential election of 1934, it seems as if an era of history is closing. The worst years of political and economic crisis are over, and Nazism's days are numbered. Perhaps Germany will finally enter into a new era of genuine peace...

abstain.titleHtml: This is highly controversial within the party!
abstain.subtitleHtml: The future of the Republic is at stake, and we are urging our supporters not to vote.
abstain.bodyHtml: None of the candidates are worthy of our support, and we are either unable or unwilling to field a candidate of our own. This decision is widely seen as irresponsible, given our status as the nominally largest party. [? if hindenburg_run: Hindenburg is privately relieved by this, as receiving our endorsement would personally pain him. ?] The **Communists** will seize upon our lack of an endorsement, attempting to position [+ communist_candidate_1932_disp +] as the sole left-wing candidate in the race, likely drawing many of our voters as a protest vote.

accept.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, we must accept this ultimatum if we are to maintain this coalition. The Nazis and **Communists** are waiting in the wings for us to fail, ready to pounce upon the instability that would result from a breakup of the governing coalition. The workers are furious at our betrayal, as are a good portion of our membership throughout the factions. Our loss is the **KPD**'s gain, and even the **NSDAP**, those lapdogs of the bourgeoisie, have joined in criticizing us for our austerity.

accept_2.subtitleHtml: We will support the suspension of the Reichstag.
accept_2.bodyHtml:
# There isn't enough resolution in this game to create conditions for when the DNVP would support Schleicher. It's possible that SPD support for Schleicher would push Hugenberg to ally with Hitler.
With the exception of the trade unions, every faction of the SPD is horrified by this betrayal of democracy.
[? if kpd_relation <= 10 and left_strength + center_strength < labor_strength: Somehow, the DNVP has agreed to Schleicher's proposal, forming a temporary alliance with the general against Nazis and Communists. ?][? if z_relation >= 50 : The Center Party also supports Schleicher's plan. ?][? if dvp_relation >= 30 : In addition, the DVP and some other smaller parties support this proposal. ?][? if kpd_relation > 10 or left_strength + center_strength >= labor_strength: The DNVP, despite being courted by Schleicher, is not interested in joining this alliance. DNVP chairman Hugenberg seems to prefer working with Hitler to any alliance that includes the SPD. ?]

accept_compromise_good.bodyHtml: We have pushed for an increase in both employer and employee contributions rather than to cut benefits for the program itself. The **LVP** accepts with the influence of [? if not stresemann_dead: Stresemann?][? if stresemann_dead: the Stresemannites?] and pressures from members of the former **[+ ddp_name +]**.

accept_compromise_worse.bodyHtml: We have accepted the compromise offered by the bourgeoisie. Many of the workers and unemployed see this as a betrayal, as we cut welfare without increasing employer contributions. We present it as the successful aversion of a much worse alternative.

accept_election.bodyHtml: President [+ president +] has called for emergency elections, to be held next month, under a caretaker government. The **SA** is permitted to act with impunity, intimidating voters into supporting the fascists.

adenauer.titleHtml: Konrad Adenauer, Mayor of Cologne, and an advocate for the Center Party "leaving the tower".
adenauer.bodyHtml: Konrad Adenauer, a staunch advocate of the Center Party's strategy to "leave the tower" and open itself to Protestant support, has decided to run for the presidency after achieving that very aim. Still relatively inexperienced in national politics, the Mayor is known for his strong anti-Prussian stance—going so far as to reject a chancellorship offer in 1926 on the grounds that Stresemann was "too Prussian." Aligned with Stegerwald and situated on the party's right wing, Adenauer has expressed interest in the so-called "taming strategy" toward the Nazis. His candidacy is supported by the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].

agrarian_bolshevism.subtitleHtml: A controversial policy involving settling unemployed workers on bankrupt estates in the east.
agrarian_bolshevism.bodyHtml: = "Agrarian Bolshevism" One of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP":Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP":CVP?]'s Labor Minister Adam Stegerwald’s pet projects is the dismantling of hopelessly bankrupt eastern estates to carve them into peasant homesteads. The problem is that there haven’t been many young workers eager to turn themselves into peasants. Still, with [? if not kvp_formed and dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **CNBLP**?][? if kvp_formed: **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?] member Hans Schlange-Schöningen newly sworn in as Commissar for Eastern Aid—following Treviranus’s move to the Transport Ministry—he’s struck a deal with Stegerwald: estates deemed “hopelessly bankrupt” will be handed over to the Labor Ministry. Backed by his promise to the unions, Stegerwald has pushed a decree that allows the government to purchase select estates at prices set by the Eastern Aid office. Unfortunately for Brüning, a copy of the decree has been leaked to the National Rural League (RLB). Its lobbyists—deeply embedded in Hindenburg’s circle—have denounced it as "Agrarian Bolshevism" slamming the measure as a descent into state socialism. They’ve made sure the President, who along with many friends owns eastern estates, see it as a personal attack.

agrarian_bolshevism.joever.bodyHtml:
The Agriculture Ministry, led by the respected Martin Schiele, does its best to defend the decree before Hindenburg—but to no avail.
In truth, policy disputes isn’t what will seal Brüning’s fate. Hindenburg had merely planned to give him a few more months to try his luck at Lausanne. But the scheming—and the sense of urgency—pushed by Schleicher, Meissner, and Oskar is forcing his hand toward an early, rash decision.

agricultural_policy.land_reform.bodyHtml:
With our policy of land reform, we are acquiring farmland from large estates, and giving the land to farmworkers' associations and small peasants. all_quiet.titleHtml: All Quiet on the Western Front
all_quiet.subtitleHtml: Censorship and violence over a movie...
all_quiet.bodyHtml: = All Quiet on the Western Front The American film *All Quiet on the Western Front*, based on the German novel *Im Westen nichts Neues* by Erich Maria Remarque, is a film about the experiences of German soldiers in the Great War, and how they gradually became disillusioned with the ideas of patriotism and nationalism. As an anti-war film, it is the target of major protest by far-right actors, especially the Nazis and the **Stahlhelm**. They are calling for the government to ban the film. If we do not ban it, the **SA** threatens to violently stop the film from being shown or watched.

choices.labelHtml: Ban the film, to prevent Nazi violence.
Allow the film to be shown.
Allow the film to be shown, and use the Prussian police to prevent Nazi disruptions.
In fact, everyone needs to learn the lessons of this film. Give free tickets to students and government employees.

all_quiet_oppo.subtitleHtml: Censorship and violence over a movie...
all_quiet_oppo.bodyHtml: = All Quiet on the Western Front The American film *All Quiet on the Western Front*, based on the German novel *Im Westen nichts Neues* by Erich Maria Remarque, is a film about the experiences of German soldiers in the Great War, and how they gradually became disillusioned with the ideas of patriotism and nationalism. As an anti-war film, it is the target of major protest by far-right actors, especially the Nazis and the **Stahlhelm**. They are calling for the government to ban the film. If we do not ban it, the **SA** threatens to violently stop the film from being shown or watched. Since we lack control over the Prussian state government, the decision to allow or ban the film will ultimately rest with the bourgeois parties.

all_quiet_oppo.allow.bodyHtml: The bourgeois parties have permitted the film to be shown despite threats from the far right. However, screenings are marred by violence. Showings of the film are eventually halted, allowing the Nazis to declare the outcome a victory for their movement.

allow.bodyHtml: The demonstration proceeds peacefully, with a minimal police presence. Onlookers admire the strength of the Communist workers, and perhaps some of our members have been peeled off. The **KPD** will never admit it, but they are developing a less hostile view towards us (even if they do not *like* us yet). Our centrist allies denounce the demonstration, but their cries are ineffectual.

allow_no_police.bodyHtml: When the march arrives in Altona, they are immediately confronted by an angry crowd of communists and socialists, who throw objects at the Nazis. Gunshots are heard, reportedly from rooftop snipers. In response, the **SA** engage the surrounding crowd and fire at the surrounding buildings. Dozens are killed, mostly civilians. The Nazis recruit off their dead martyrs.

allow_police_no_violence.bodyHtml: When the march arrives in Altona, they are immediately confronted by an angry crowd of communists and socialists, who throw objects at the Nazis. The police attempt to separate the two groups, to no avail. Gunshots are heard, reportedly from rooftop snipers. The police manage to keep their cool, the shots stop, and the march disperses without further violence.

allow_police_violence.bodyHtml: When the march arrives in Altona, they are immediately confronted by an angry crowd of communists and socialists, who throw objects at the Nazis. The police attempt to separate the two groups, to no avail. Gunshots are heard, reportedly from rooftop snipers (whom the police believe are communists). In response, the police fire into the surrounding buildings. Dozens are killed. All turn out to be civilians, and the reported snipers are never found. This incident has been called "Altona Bloody Sunday" in the media. The **Communists** assail the incompetence of the police, who are supposedly under our command.

allow_protect.bodyHtml: The bourgeois coalition in Prussia, who we are in a toleration agreement with, have surprisingly sent the Prussian police to prevent Nazi violence. Under the protection of the police, the people are allowed to watch the film in relative peace.

altona_clashes.ban_march.bodyHtml: We have banned the planned protest. The Nazis appeal the ban in the courts in the name of freedom of speech. Thankfully, the judiciary agrees with us that the Nazis' argument is specious.

america.bodyHtml: The Socialist Party of America is tiny and has limited support. There is not much we can do for them, and conversely, not much they can do for us.

appeal.bodyHtml: We argue that we are working hard to achieve the coalition's goals, and in the name of proletarian solidarity, we must make this coalition function. Surprisingly, the **KPD** hears our pleas, and is willing to give us six more months before the coalition goals must be achieved.

applied.titleHtml: Fund applied research in economically useful technologies.
applied.bodyHtml: Our research program focuses on collaborating with industry to develop useful technologies, creating new research institutions for applied science. This collaboration is focused on economic growth and development.

austrian_civil_war.subtitleHtml: In response to police attacks, the Austrian socialists are rising up...
austrian_civil_war.bodyHtml: = Uprising in Austria # pre-emptive democratic victory if sdapo strength >= 6 # long civil war if sdapo_strength = 5 or 4 - opportunity for interference/forced peace # instant defeat if sdapo_strength < 4 The crisis in Austria is continuing. The "Austrofascist" government led by Engelbert Dollfuß continues to rule by emergency decree. It has been persecuting its political opposition, primarily the social democrats of the **SDAPÖ**. [? if sdapo_strength < 6: Now, Austria is entering a state of civil war. When the police attempted to seize weapons from the Republikanischer Schutzbund, the Schutzbund responded with force, shooting at the government troops. Fighting has sporadically broken out between Schutzbund and government forces all over Austria. ?] [? if sdapo_strength >= 6: The government's attempts to suppress the socialist party and the Schutzbund were met with mass protest, supported by the **SPD**[? if foreign_minister_party = "SPD": and the German government?]. [? if eu_austria: They are also supported by the recently formed European Union, with economic sanctions targeting the government. ?] ?] Eventually...

austrian_civil_war.crushed.titleHtml: The rebellious Schutzbund has been crushed.
austrian_civil_war.crushed.bodyHtml: The uprising lasted for no more than a few days before it was crushed. The Schutzbund and **SDAPÖ** were too weak and too divided to stand against the forces of the state.

austrian_civil_war.force_peace.titleHtml: Can we bring the sides together for a peace?
austrian_civil_war.force_peace.bodyHtml: The Austrian government obviously sees us as biased, so there is no way they will let us host peace negotiations. However, negotiations begin nonetheless. In Switzerland, with Fascist Italy as the Austrofascists' protector and Germany as the **SDAPÖ**'s, a peace deal is hammered out. The socialists are disarmed and give up all pretense of revolution, while the right-wing paramilitaries are also disarmed. Dictatorship ends, and normal government is restored, with free elections. Given the **SDAPÖ**'s starting position, this is treated as a victory. Now begins the long work of reconstruction...

austrian_civil_war.long_war.bodyHtml: Neither side is backing down, and the **SDAPÖ** have formed an alternative government after defeating the government troops in some cities. Austria is in a state of civil war.

params.code: state.flags['sdapo_strength'] == 5 || state.flags['sdapo_strength'] == 4

austrian_civil_war.long_war_2.titleHtml: There is nothing we can do.
austrian_civil_war.long_war_2.bodyHtml: No matter our efforts, the war continues. Too many lives are extinguished. Refugees begin to flow into Germany, and trade suffers. Many are calling our Austrian interference a mistake.

austrian_civil_war.sdapo_victory.bodyHtml: The result is that the Austrofascists have backed down! Caught in an untenable position domestically and abroad, they have agreed to restore the National Council and resign from government, holding new elections. Now begins the long work of reconstruction. Our countries are likely to be brought closer together as a result. [? if eu_austria: This is a great success of the new European Union, and its prestige is seen to rise internationally. ?]

austrian_civil_war.support_sdapo_govt.titleHtml: The Foreign Ministry will support the democratic Austrian forces.
austrian_civil_war.support_sdapo_govt.bodyHtml: We provide diplomatic and some financial and material support to the **SDAPÖ** forces.

austrian_civil_war.support_sdapo_party.titleHtml: As a party, the **SPD** will provide the **SDAPÖ** with support.
austrian_civil_war.support_sdapo_party.bodyHtml: The **SPD** raises its resources to provide arms and volunteers for the **SDAPÖ**.

austrian_customs_union.subtitleHtml: The Foreign Ministry seeks closer ties to Austria...
austrian_customs_union.bodyHtml: = Austrian Customs Union [? if spd_in_government: The [+ foreign_minister_party +] foreign minister has a proposal for a customs union with Austria. We can either accept or reject this agreement. ?] [? if not spd_in_government: The government of Chancellor [+ chancellor +] has a proposal for a customs union with Austria. Most likely, this will happen whatever we decide. ?] The nationalist right has long yearned for closer ties with Austria, with the eventual goal of the merger of the two German-speaking countries. A customs union with Austria is the first step towards this goal. Additionally, many believe that a union with Austria would improve our current economic circumstances. However, the Allies, especially France, are likely to object. This agreement would break the terms of the Versailles Treaty, and could lead to economic sanctions, further hurting our economy.

austrian_customs_union.center_right_coal.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has called a retaliatory no confidence vote in Prussia, replacing our government with a center-right coalition composed of all parties to our right, except for the **DNF** and **NSDAP**. While this is a setback, it is not the worst possible outcome, as new elections could have led to significant gains for extremist parties. [? if z_leader != "Stegerwald": Adam Stegerwald?][? if z_leader == "Stegerwald": Heinrich Brüning?] of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia.

austrian_customs_union.new_prussia_elect.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has called a retaliatory vote in Prussia, forcing the dissolution of the Landtag for new elections. New Prussian elections have been set for [+ next_election_month_prussia : month +] [+ next_election_year_prussia +]. A double dissolution has shaken the people's faith in democracy, with the Nazis exploiting the instability to claim that democracy is unworkable, and that Germany needs a strong leader.

austrian_parliament.subtitleHtml: Our southern neighbor is sliding into dictatorship.
austrian_parliament.bodyHtml: # Must control foreign ministry or have made contact with Austrian socialists. = Suspension of the Austrian Parliament Due to a controversial proposal regarding a railroad strike in the Austrian National Council, all three presidents of the National Council resigned, leaving it without any presiding officers. This is a constitutional crisis. Austrian chancellor Engelbert Dollfuß has taken advantage of this crisis by suspending the parliament and ruling by emergency decree, forming an "Austrofascist" government. Dollfuß consolidates his power by persecuting his political opponents, especially our fellow Social Democrats in the **SDAPÖ** (Social Democratic Worker's Party of Austria). Is there anything we could do? # - use EU to sanction Austria (will prevent civil war and restore democracy) # - apply diplomatic pressure to Austria (without EU) # - fund the Schutzbund # after this, supporting Austrians will raise sdapo_strength; if sdapo_strength >= 2, they'll enter a long civil war; if sdapo_strength >= 5, they'll win.

austrian_parliament.eu_sanctions.bodyHtml: The European Union is a largely untested body, and from the beginning contained members that are at best quasi-democratic. Most of its members are more concerned by power politics than democratic values. However, as its founder, Germany holds a special influence in the EU, and we manage to persuade the other members to join in the pressure against Austrofascism. The Dollfuß regime does not give in, but it is weakened and isolated.

Many of the workers and unemployed see this as a betrayal, although we present it as the successful aversion of a much worse alternative. [? if (in_grand_coalition or (in_weimar_coalition and lvp_formed)): Meanwhile, the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] is aghast at the prospect of raising any taxes on businesses at all. ?]

ban.bodyHtml: We issued the order to ban the demonstrations, and sent police to enforce the ban. There was a confrontation between the police and **Communists**, and violence erupted. Reports say that the Berlin police killed dozens of demonstrators and innocent bystanders. The **Communists** are already calling this incident *Blutmai*, "Bloody May". This may end any attempt at reconciliation with the **KPD**, but the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **Christian People's**?] and [? if not lvp_formed: **People's**?][? if lvp_formed: **Liberal People's**?] parties approve of our action.

choices.labelHtml: It is the fault of corrupt and reactionary elements within the police. Purge those responsible.
It is the fault of the **Communists** for refusing to follow the rule of law.
It is an unfortunate incident that should not have happened, but is no one's fault at all.

ban_march.bodyHtml: We have banned the planned protest. The Nazis appeal the ban in the courts in the name of freedom of speech. Thankfully, the judiciary agrees with us that the Nazis' argument is specious.

ban_rfb.bodyHtml: The ban is enthusiastically carried out by the police, perhaps too enthusiastically. The Communists take this as one more reason why the Socialists are traitors to the left. However, the moderate and center-right parties approve, as do the police.

ban_sa.bodyHtml: As it turns out, the Nazi **SA** has many allies in the police and bureaucracy. Our relationship with the police weakens, and the **SA** can still organize illegally, right under the police's noses. [? if sa_banned_pro : Nevertheless, the **SA** is substantially weakened by our ban. ?] [? if coup_progress >= 6: There are reports of an imminent coup by the far-right. banking_crisis.subtitleHtml: The collapse of the German banking system...
banking_crisis.bodyHtml:
= Banking Crisis
The Darmstädter und Nationalbank, or Danat Bank, has collapsed! Along with it goes much of the German banking system. The cause seemed to be due to the government's pursuit of a customs union with Austria, which led to de facto international sanctions. This has set off a global ripple effect, deepening the depression and driving foreign banks into bankruptcy.
This is a bourgeois dispute, but the costs will be borne by the proletariat. The people are facing ever-increasing hunger and poverty, and perhaps we are partly to blame.

baumer.subtitleHtml: Leader of the **LVP**'s women's wing, and a moderate feminist. Has questionable views on the "national questions".
baumer.bodyHtml: Somehow, Gertrud Bäumer, long-time deputy leader of the **[+ ddp_name +]** and now the leader of the **LVP**'s women's wing, has been elected to the leadership of the **LVP**. This is quite a bizarre development, but her victory can be attributed to her passionate nationalism and romanticism, as well as her questionable views on Jews and race, which have garnered the support of nationalists within the party. Additionally, some within the party cynically believe that by electing a woman, they can appeal to a broader female electorate. For us, Bäumer's background as a former **[+ ddp_name +]** member may work in our favor, improving our relationship with the **LVP**. However, it remains to be seen whether she will gain more votes than she loses due to her moderate feminist stance, as many refuse to support her purely out of misogyny.

black_thursday.bodyHtml:
= Black Thursday
The stock market in America has had its biggest crash in history. It is too early to tell what the international effects will be, but it cannot be good. Our economy is already feeling the effects - unemployment will rise even more, and wages will fall. As always, it is the capitalists' crisis, and the workers' burden.

blutmai.bodyHtml: = May Day, 1929 Tensions run high in Berlin. The **Communists** are planning a demonstration to commemorate the 10th anniversary of the Spartacist Uprising. No one has forgotten that it was our party members who ordered the uprising's suppression, and the **Communists** still blame us for the deaths of Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht. Many non-communists are afraid of the possibility of another violent uprising, and our allies in the Prussian coalition are asking the Prussian Interior Ministry to ban the demonstrations.

choices.labelHtml: Allow the demonstrations to proceed, but maintain a heavy police presence.

blutmai.allow.bodyHtml: The demonstration proceeds peacefully, with a minimal police presence. Onlookers admire the strength of the Communist workers, and perhaps some of our members have been peeled off. The **KPD** will never admit it, but they are developing a less hostile view towards us (even if they do not *like* us yet). Our centrist allies denounce the demonstration, but their cries are ineffectual.

blutmai.allow_police.bodyHtml: The demonstration proceeds peacefully under the watchful eyes of the police. Onlookers admire the strength of the Communist workers, and perhaps some of our supporters have been peeled off.

blutmai.ban.bodyHtml: We issued the order to ban the demonstrations, and sent police to enforce the ban. There was a confrontation between the police and **Communists**, and violence erupted. Reports say that the Berlin police killed dozens of demonstrators and innocent bystanders. The **Communists** are already calling this incident *Blutmai*, "Bloody May". This may end any attempt at reconciliation with the **KPD**, but the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **Christian People's**?] and [? if not lvp_formed: **People's**?][? if lvp_formed: **Liberal People's**?] parties approve of our action.

choices.labelHtml: It is the fault of corrupt and reactionary elements within the police. Purge those responsible.
It is the fault of the **Communists** for refusing to follow the rule of law.
It is an unfortunate incident that should not have happened, but is no one's fault at all.

blutmai.communist_fault.bodyHtml: If the **KPD** continues to act illegally, they must suffer the consequences. Thus, we have banned the **RFKB**, their paramilitary group. The bourgeois and right-leaning parties approve.

blutmai.corrupt_police.bodyHtml: We arrested the police responsible for the killings, and put them on trial. [? if judicial_reform = 0 : Unfortunately, the reactionary judiciary let them go free with barely any punishment at all. ?] This assuages some of the **Communists**' outrage, but certainly not all.

blutmai.join.bodyHtml: It is difficult to persuade the **Communists** to let us march with them, given the histories of their party and ours. However, they eventually relent. The display of proletarian unity inspires the workers and terrifies the bourgeoisie and middle class. [? if in_grand_coalition or in_weimar_coalition: Our coalition partners in the government are outraged at our display with the communists, and are threatening to break up the government. ?] The far-right paramilitaries increase their recruitment to counter us.

blutmai.no_fault.bodyHtml: This position gains us no allies, and does not alienate anyone any further.

bolz.titleHtml: Eugen Bolz, formerly of the Center, is elected as their new leader.
bolz.subtitleHtml: Bolz is the current Minister-President of Württemberg, having governed harmoniously with Bazille's state **DNVP** for the entire duration - Catholic Right Wing
bolz.bodyHtml: Minister-President of Württemberg Eugen Bolz has been promoted to the leadership of the national **[+ z_party_name +]**. Bolz has worked harmoniously with the respected Wilhelm Bazille, a conservative leader of the moderate Württemberg **DNVP** since 1924, making him a natural choice as a compromise candidate. This has earned him nearly universal support within the party. However, Bolz's role as a compromise candidate has hindered his ability to effect significant change, as he must tread carefully to avoid alienating the factions that helped bring him to power. Bolz will attempt to bridge the confessional divides between Catholic and Protestant conservatives, with the party still divided along the lines of their party of origin. Given Bolz's refusal to enter a Weimar Coalition in Württemberg back in 1928, viewing the **SPD** as 'incapable of governing,' we do not expect much improvement in our relationship moving forward.

bourgeois_coalition_saxony.subtitleHtml: The incumbent coalition, which will survive on toleration from the **NSDAP**.
bourgeois_coalition_saxony.bodyHtml: The incumbent coalition has failed to win a majority, and toleration from the **NSDAP** is required. They've demanded the exclusion of the **ASPD**[? if not lvp_formed: and **[+ ddp_name +]**?] from the cabinet, and the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]'s new Minister-President Wilhelm Bünger has no choice but to agree. However, this decision was soon reverted and the **ASPD** is granted the Ministry of Work and Welfare. Despite the exclusion of many supporting parties from the cabinet in favor of non-partisan figures, they choose to tolerate the coalition nonetheless.

bourgeois_coalition_thuringia.titleHtml: The incumbent center-right coalition continues governing.
bourgeois_coalition_thuringia.subtitleHtml: The incumbent coalition holds a majority, one without the **NSDAP**.
bourgeois_coalition_thuringia.bodyHtml: Unexpectedly, the parties involved in the incumbent government have gained votes, and now no longer require the votes of the **NSDAP**. The continuation of the stable leadership over Thuringia will weaken the Nazis.

bourgeois_coalition_wurttemberg.titleHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] coalitions with the **WBWB**, the liberals, and other minor bourgeois parties.
bourgeois_coalition_wurttemberg.bodyHtml: The incumbent coalition consisting of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?],[? if not cvp_formed: **DNVP**,?] liberals and toleration from the **WBWB** has won another majority. The continuation of the stable leadership over Württemberg will weaken the Nazis.

bourgeois_glaze_eckener.titleHtml: Persuade the bourgeois parties to let us into their campaign committees.
bourgeois_glaze_eckener.subtitleHtml: This will allow for a more coordinated effort.
bourgeois_glaze_eckener.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and the liberals have been excluding us from their local campaign committees. However, by leveraging our ties to their left wings and affiliated trade unions, we manage to pressure them into allowing some socialists to participate.

bourgeois_parliament.bodyHtml: Although these are the affairs of the bourgeois, it still impacts us. The parliamentary alliance has an underlying anti-socialist agenda, and we will need to invest considerable effort into breaking apart the group in order to negotiate with its members individually.

bourgeois_parliament_collapse.bodyHtml:
= Bourgeois Parliamentary Group Collapses!
The various disagreements that have arisen between the bourgeois parties themselves, as well as with Chancellor Brüning, have caused the parliamentary group to fracture, with each party now going its own separate way. This division significantly weakens their collective influence over Brüning and his policies, granting him greater autonomy as he now negotiates with each party individually.

boxheim.subtitleHtml: A set of documents detailing a violent seizure of power by the Nazis is discovered...
boxheim.bodyHtml: = The Boxheim Documents In the elections in the State of Hesse, which resulted in no clear majority, we have remained in a caretaker capacity. [? if z_ideology == "Right": while the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and **NSDAP** attempt to negotiate a coalition agreement.?] This has allowed us to retain control of the Interior Ministry and granted our Wilhelm Leuschner, the authority to order house searches of Nazis following a tip from a disgraced **NSDAP** Landtag member. During these searches, a copy of a letter sent by **NSDAP** member Werner Best to the party leadership in Munich is discovered. The letter reveals their plan to violently seize power and includes guidelines for emergency decrees. Among these plans is a provision making access to food contingent on compulsory labor service, from which Jews would be exempt, implying they would receive no food at all. In an attempt to protect themselves from the severe damage this revelation causes to [? if not hitler_deported: Hitler's?][? if hitler_deported: their?] oath of legality, the **NSDAP** has defended the letter, claiming it was intended solely for a potential communist seizure of power. It is now up to the judiciary to determine the consequences of this anti-constitutional plan.

choices.labelHtml: We await the decision of the courts.
We await the decision of the courts.

boxheim.nothing.bodyHtml: Expectedly, the Ministry of Justice believes that the documents did not constitute a crime of high treason, as they argue that the document was directed against communist putschists, rather than the government. [? if bruning_time: We are sure that Chancellor Brüning is behind this downplaying, to keep cooperation with the far-right open. ?] We have at least discredited the Nazis in the eyes of many, and have managed to keep our Hesse government functioning in a caretaker capacity due to the collapse of talks between the **NSDAP** and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].

boxheim.pressure_drop.bodyHtml: Due to our thorough reform of the judicial system, the Nazis behind these documents can now be publicly exposed and prosecuted by the state for high treason. This has dealt a severe blow to the constitutional appearance of the **NSDAP**, causing great distrust between them and the bourgeois establishment, including President Hindenburg himself. Our Hesse government is set to continue in a caretaker capacity for the foreseeable future, following the collapse of talks between the **NSDAP** and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].

boycott_elections.titleHtml: Boycott the elections. Schleicher will rig it anyway.
boycott_elections.subtitleHtml: Maybe the other parties will join us.
boycott_elections.bodyHtml: There’s little point in participating in an election that’s clearly rigged. The most we can do is boycott the vote—depress turnout and deny Schleicher the legitimacy he desperately needs. But if we aren’t strong enough, we’ll simply hand the **DNEF** a majority government on a silver platter. However, if we commit, we might bring the other anti-Schleicher parties into the boycott as well. Strength in numbers. Are we sure?

choices.labelHtml: No, let's participate in the elections.

boycott_elections_2.bodyHtml: Alright. We'll see whether the other parties share the same sentiment. We already know the **KPD**[? if sapd_formed: and **SAPD**?] are with us—who else?

bracht.titleHtml: Franz Bracht is installed as the Center Party's new chairman.
bracht.bodyHtml: Undoubtedly thanks to Schleicher's meddling, Franz Bracht has been elected chairman of the Center Party. With Kaas’s endorsement and Schleicher's ability to "persuade" key party members to switch their votes, Bracht narrowly defeats Stegerwald and his more republican support base. The internal reaction has been surprisingly muted. Perhaps the Center Party’s gradual shift to the right has made a reactionary like Bracht finally acceptable—or perhaps other forces are quietly at work.

bredow.subtitleHtml: Deputy Defense Minister. Ideology suspected to be similar to Schleicher's.
bredow.bodyHtml:
Presenting himself as a continuation of Schleicher and as another non-partisan military man, von Bredow has won his close friend Schleicher's favor. Although former chancellor Schleicher is officially retired, he still pulls many strings behind the scenes, unwilling to give up that scheming of his. 
However, von Bredow is certainly no Schleicher, he possesses no vast network of political connections throughout all walks of life, and Schleicher's personal popularity has largely failed to transfer over to his hand picked successor.
Perhaps the house of cards Schleicher has carefully built will come tumbling down?

bruning.bodyHtml: Heinrich Brüning, a politician we know all too well, is running for the most powerful position in the Reich. He has a long history, tracing back to the Christian Trade Unions and his mentorship under Stegerwald, eventually rising to become the leader of the party's parliamentary group and its candidate for Chancellor. Despite his record of favoring austerity and deflationary policies in response to the Great Depression, he is a flexible figure—intelligent enough to recognize the dangers of the "taming strategy," and not entirely opposed to governing alongside the **SPD**. His candidacy is supported by the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].

bruning_collapse.bodyHtml: The [? if not lvp_formed and dvp_exist:**DVP** and the?][? if lvp_formed: right **LVP** and the?] **DNVP** have broken with Brüning, voting against the act when it came to a vote in the Reichstag. However, this decision has ignited fierce internal divisions within both parties. A significant pro-Brüning faction—including figures like Westarp, [? if not lvp_formed: Curtius?][? if lvp_formed: Dietrich?], and several influential industrialists such as Hans Luther—pushed for continued support, convincing a sizable minority in both parties to back the act as the bitter medicine for Germany’s economic woes. Despite these divisions, when the [? if not lvp_formed and dvp_exist:**DVP**?][? if lvp_formed or not dvp_exist:**DNVP**?] introduced a vote of no confidence, defectors from both parties tipped the scales, narrowly bringing down Brüning’s government. New elections have been scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +]. [? if not hoover_moratorium_seen: The one silver lining in this crisis is that with [+ chancellor +] announcing Germany’s inability to continue paying reparations, United States President Herbert Hoover has begun to lobby France to agree to a one-year suspension of payments. ?]

bruning_deflation.subtitleHtml: A potential step away from deflationary policy?
bruning_deflation.bodyHtml: = The Lautenbach Plan Brüning's deflationary and austerity policy, aimed at boosting Germany's competitiveness on the global stage after the crisis[? if reparations > -2: through a pause in reparations, which is Brüning's main objective?], has shown to have disastrous consequences for nearly everyone, exacerbating the current situation. Brüning and his cabinet believe that resolving the economic crisis internally is impossible; instead, they hope to achieve 'ignition'—accelerating recovery once the crisis has passed[? if reparations > -2:, through deliberately allowing the economic suffering to worsen to convince foreign powers that Germany couldn't afford to pay reparations. ?]. This bitter medicine has guided all of Brüning's economic policies, with the expectation that after the crisis, Germany will emerge stronger with lower labor costs[? if reparations > -2: and a reduction in reparations?][? if reparations == -2: and the fiscal autonomy provided by the pause in reparations?]. Wilhelm Lautenbach, a German economist, has proposed a job creation program focused on expanding credit availability, improving liquidity, and investing in infrastructure. He presented this plan during in a secret meeting with economic ministers in Brüning’s cabinet, independent experts, Reichsbank President Hans Luther, and our economic expert, Rudolf Hilferding, who personally supports Brüning's deflationary approach. This is how we are able to listen on their secret discussions. However, the widespread fear of inflation in Germany has strongly influenced many participants against this policy, serving as the primary obstacle to the actual enactment of this plan. Those in opposition to the deflationary policy and are open to public works include the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]'s Vice Chancellor and Finance Minister Hermann Dietrich, and the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]'s Labor Minister Adam Stegerwald. > *"The central bank cannot create money."* - Rudolf Hilferding, **SPD**'s lead economist, defending the Reichsbank, 1931.

bruning_deflation.lautenbach_adopted.bodyHtml:
The pause in reparation payments, a budgetary surplus, and a struggling economy have created the conditions necessary to persuade both the Brüning cabinet and many economic experts that a stimulus plan is essential. The economy has hit rock bottom, deflation is in its damaging second phase, and the Lautenbach Plan is considered crucial for a rapid 'ignition' of the German economy, especially as reparations have already been paused. However, due to the German public's fear of inflation, announcing any dramatic expansion of the money supply has proven impossible. As a result, the Reichsbank is forced to scale back the plan to avoid any potential scandal that could threaten the Brüning government.
Labor Minister Adam Stegerwald and Finance Minister Hermann Dietrich have devised a plan to allocate a billion dollars for public works, along with efforts to reduce 'sticky' wages to restore investor confidence. The plan also includes the purchasing of foreign debts to increase liquidity, expanding credit, and reducing interest rates. The deficit generated by these measures is also somewhat offset by the need to pay less unemployment benefits. With these measures, money is beginning to flow once again into the German economy.
> Chancellor [+ chancellor +]'s response is, public works?

bruning_deflation.lautenbach_fail.bodyHtml: Expectedly, the Lautenbach Plan has failed due to strong opposition from those who adhere to fiscal orthodoxy, which holds that deflation, despite its pain, is healthy because it weeds out inefficient producers. This contrasts with the Keynesian belief that a destructive second phase occurs, where economic recovery becomes possible but fails because of a collapse in investor confidence. Reichsbank President Hans Luther, who personally sympathizes with increasing the money supply and expanding credit, has shelved the idea. The conference only reached two unanimous conclusions: the German people's fear of inflation made it impossible to announce any dramatic program to expand the money supply, meaning the government would have to act secretly if it ever decided to implement Lautenbach's plan, and the government must continue its campaign to lower wages bound by long-term collective labor contracts and prices set by cartel agreements. However, Luther has made concessions to the Keynesians, quietly expanding the money supply and increasing credit availability, even abandoning the rule that 40% of money in circulation must be covered by gold and foreign exchange. Furthermore, generous financing of exports to the Soviet Union has helped counteract the effects of the withdrawal of foreign credits on both the money supply and the job market. > *"Stimulation can only help if we are already at the bottom....I do not believe that we are that far yet."* - Ernst Trendelenburg, Reich Minister of Economics, 1931.

bruning_dies_no_wp.bodyHtml: We are once again compelled to vote in favor of the [+ chancellor +] government to prevent the extremist parties on the far-right and left from translating their growing popular support into parliamentary gains. Some members of the **DVP**'s left wing, such as Curtius and Otto Thiel, have also voted with the government or abstained, going against their wider party. Unfortunately, all efforts to save the government have been in vain. Only [+ bruning_coalition +]% of the Reichstag voted to support Brüning’s government. As a result, new elections have been scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

bruning_dies_wp.bodyHtml: The **WP** has unexpectedly reversed its opposition to Brüning's government following last-minute concessions from the Chancellor. In a crucial no-confidence vote, they sided with the government, counteracting the impact of the **DVP**'s withdrawal. Additionally, some members of the **DVP**'s left wing, including Curtius and Otto Thiel, either voted with the government or abstained. This sudden shift by the **WP** has all but sealed its political demise. Already struggling to maintain support among the middle class, the party now faces mass defections, with local chapters either dissolving or breaking away entirely. Unfortunately, all of this effort is for naught, with only [+ bruning_coalition +]% of the Reichstag voting against the Brüning government. New elections have been set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

bruning_emergency_chancellor.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is pleased, and somewhat surprised, that we have appointed [+ chancellor +] as chancellor.

bruning_explode.bodyHtml: Groener, one of Brüning’s longest-standing and most loyal allies, is now out of the equation. Brüning, deeply loyal to him, was fully prepared to resign the chancellorship if Groener was forced out of the cabinet. However, unwilling to let Brüning risk his own position on his behalf, Groener chose to step down. His resignation as Minister of Defense has dealt a severe blow to the Brüning cabinet, further diminishing its chances of surviving the deepening political crisis triggered by the fallout from the local elections. Among Hindenburg’s inner circle of advisors, no one had been more steadfast in supporting Brüning than Groener. His departure has severely weakened the chancellor’s standing with the Reich President, leaving him fully exposed to the machinations of Schleicher and his entourage. With Groener gone, Schleicher is now free from external restraints to pursue his strategy of taming the Nazis, answerable only to Hindenburg. Sensing that Brüning has been fatally weakened, the Nazis have intensified their attacks on his government, seeking to bring it down once and for all.

bruning_joever.subtitleHtml: Hindenburg's inner circle is conspiring against him...
bruning_joever.bodyHtml: = Brüning's Race against Time Brüning's days are numbered. The only reason President Hindenburg is keeping him around is solely by the fact of his foreign policy expertise, and his claim that he's only 'one hundred meters from the finish line' from achieving a huge breakthrough in terms of securing an abolishment of reparations at Lausanne and Germany's rearmament at Geneva, an issue close to Hindenburg's heart. The only hope for Brüning's political salvation rests in those conferences. [? if not hindenburg_sacked: There is also no precedent of the President sacking a government that still enjoys a parliamentary majority. ?] However, General Kurt von Schleicher sees Brüning as the biggest obstacle in his 'taming strategy', as Brüning has refused to take serious efforts toward bringing the national opposition into government. The sense of urgency Schleicher has invoked onto the issue, along with his convincing of Hindenburg's State Secretary Otto Meissner and his son Oskar, has brought Hindenburg to make an early and rash decision on the matter.

bruning_joever.goerdeler.subtitleHtml: The Reich Price Commissioner and the Mayor of Leipzig. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": Former?] **DNVP** member.
bruning_joever.goerdeler.bodyHtml: To most political observers, Carl Goerdeler, Mayor of Leipzig and the Reich Prize Commissioner, and being a fiscal conservative arguing for a wide reaching reforms of the German welfare state and finances, was the expected successor to Brüning, with his name even being floated around as the Minister-President of Prussia of a Center-**NSDAP** coalition. However, his demands for authorization of sweeping fiscal reforms is too similar to that of Brüning in Schleicher's eyes, who supports a public works solution to Germany's economic woes. Goerdeler will not be the new chancellor.

params.source: successor_menu

bruning_joever.papen.subtitleHtml: An relatively unknown Catholic Conservative from the Center Party. Schleicher's preferred candidate.
bruning_joever.papen.bodyHtml: With Goerdeler and Westarp out of the equation, Hindenburg has grasped the straw Schleicher offered and appointed a far-right Catholic Conservative, Franz von Papen, from the Center Party, as chancellor. Papen is relatively unknown, only whose political experience is limited to two terms in the Prussian Landtag. The two have been friends since their days in the Prussian military academy. Papen's decision to take the chancellorship, despite [+ z_leader +]'s urging and Papen's promise not to, Hindenburg has used the same tactic on him as he used on Brüning, convincing him to accept the position. Due to Papen breaking his promise to [+ z_leader +] just after he made it, expulsion proceedings and against him are interrupted by his resignation from the Center Party, forever ruining his relations with the party necessary for a parliamentary majority as they strongly denounce him as the "Ephialtes of the Center Party". It's unknown of the exact reasons why Schleicher would choose a man like Papen as Brüning's successor, but we can assume he was trying to secure the support of the Center Party and Nazis, as he's a far-right member of the former, and that Papen would be an easy person to control. Time will tell if the **NSDAP** will honor its promises to Schleicher, which they'd purposefully refused to write on paper.

bruning_joever.schleicher_time.bodyHtml: Former Chancellor Brüning has been dismissed—despite commanding a parliamentary majority. It appears Schleicher has struck an unwritten deal with the **NSDAP**, promising “fruitful cooperation” with a new right-wing cabinet that[? if sa_nationwide_ban: lifted the ban on the **SA** and?] called for new Reichstag elections. It’s a shame that Schleicher would fall for [+ nsdap_leader +]’s lies. But the real question now is: who will succeed Brüning?

bruning_joever.westarp.subtitleHtml: Hindenburg's preferred choice, and [? if dnvp_leader != "Westarp":former?] **DNVP** party leader.
bruning_joever.westarp.bodyHtml: Hindenburg's personal preference is the [? if dnvp_leader != "Westarp":former?] **DNVP** leader that played a critical role in securing Hindenburg's reelection. The two has maintained contact over the past years, and share a hatred of Hugenberg. Despite this, in a meeting with Hindenburg, Westarp has declined the chancellorship and argued against dismissing Brüning, and against new elections that would destroy the German middle parties. Even when Hindenburg was reduced to tears, a strategy that had worked on Brüning before, Westarp remains firm in his refusal. Westarp will not be the new chancellor.

Despite the new right-wing cabinet, the national opposition is still refusing to support Brüning, as they want all the power to themselves.

bruning_lives_wp.bodyHtml: The **WP** has unexpectedly reversed its opposition to Brüning's government following last-minute concessions from the Chancellor. In a crucial no-confidence vote, they sided with the government, effectively neutralizing the impact of the **DVP**'s withdrawal. Additionally, some members of the **DVP**'s left wing, including Curtius and Otto Thiel, either voted with the government or abstained. This sudden shift by the **WP** has all but sealed its political demise. Already struggling to maintain support among the middle class, the party now faces mass defections, with local chapters either dissolving or breaking away entirely. Despite the formation of a more right-leaning cabinet, the national opposition remains unwilling to support Brüning, as they seek to claim full control for themselves.

bruning_public_works_act.bodyHtml: = Public Works Mobilization Act With Brüning focused on securing a foreign policy victory, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP":Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP":**CVP**?]'s Labor Minister Adam Stegerwald and the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]'s Vice Chancellor and Finance Minister Hermann Dietrich have been developing a job creation program. The Christian Socials and several **DNVP** figures, such as Günther Gereke, have also backed this approach. However, given the state of the national budget, such a program was not feasible without either severe welfare cuts or a breakthrough on reparations—delaying action until now due to fears of public backlash. Dietrich has since secured Reichstag approval to raise 1.4 billion Reichsmarks through a bond issue to fund the initiative. [? if not reparations_resolved: Yet the Reichsbank remains reluctant to provide support, at least not until the reparations issue is resolved at Lausanne in the coming months. As a result, Dietrich’s proposal has been sharply scaled back, with only 160 million Reichsmarks allocated and further austerity measures introduced in the upcoming act. The act’s centerpiece is the establishment of a new "Voluntary Labor Service" brigade, tasked with draining swamps and digging artificial lakes—at subminimum wages. ?][? if reparations_resolved: With reparations now resolved at Lausanne, the Reichsbank feels more comfortable authorizing spending. The act's centerpiece is the creation of a new "Voluntary Labor Service" brigade, tasked with draining swamps and digging artificial lakes—at subminimum wages. ?] [? if not reparations_resolved: Should Lausanne bring success, full funding for Dietrich’s program may still follow. Brüning's coalition just has to survive until then. ?]

bruning_public_works_act_real.subtitleHtml: The Brüning cabinet announces a job creation program.
bruning_public_works_act_real.bodyHtml: = Expansion of Public Works With the abolishment of reparations at Lausanne, the Brüning cabinet finally feels comfortable to expand funding for its recently enacted public works program. A billion dollars in bonds released by the government is used to fund the program, and money begins to flow in the economy again. This marks a real turning point, and along with the abolishment of reparations, the radicalizing effects of sky-high unemployment and the Versailles Treaty are diminished. The set of conditions that have enabled the Nazis's meteoric rise begins to unravel, depriving them of the fuel that once drove their ascent.

Despite Brüning’s longstanding belief that public works should follow the bottoming out of the depression, it appears he now sees that moment as having arrived—with the global recovery and the abolition of German reparations. Still, inflationary fears among the public have constrained any major expansion of the money supply, and the industrialists within the coalition have fought tooth and nail to gut the bill’s more expensive provisions. Fortunately, their votes are not required to pass it.

bruning_second_cabinet.subtitleHtml: Chancellor [+ chancellor +] has reorganized his cabinet!
bruning_second_cabinet.bodyHtml: = The Second Brüning cabinet The **DVP**'s Julius Curtius has resigned from the Foreign Ministry following the disastrous failure of the Austro-German customs union, which he was the architect of. With no more **DVP** ministers in cabinet, the last obstacle preventing them from breaking with Brüning's government has been removed. In an attempt to maintain their support, Brüning has formed a more conservative second cabinet, but this effort has proven insufficient—the **DVP** has now joined the national opposition, which also remains opposed to cooperating with his government. With the **DVP** now likely to vote alongside the extremist parties, the government's majority is at risk. If the remaining bourgeois parties follow suit, Brüning’s cabinet may no longer hold control. We must now decide whether to continue tolerating this more right-leaning Brüning government—now absent of leftist figures such as the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]’s Joseph Wirth—in the hopes the bourgeois parties reconsidering their opposition, or to finally break away from it. Additionally, Brüning has introduced his third emergency decree, which further reduces salaries, and cuts pensions and welfare benefits to address the deficit caused by the banking crisis.

bruning_second_cabinet.bruning_dies_no_w.bodyHtml: We are once again compelled to vote in favor of the [+ chancellor +] government to prevent the extremist parties on the far-right and left from translating their growing popular support into parliamentary gains. Some members of the **DVP**'s left wing, such as Curtius and Otto Thiel, have also voted with the government or abstained, going against their wider party. Unfortunately, all efforts to save the government have been in vain. Only [+ bruning_coalition +]% of the Reichstag voted to support Brüning’s government. As a result, new elections have been scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

bruning_second_cabinet.bruning_dies_wp.bodyHtml: The **WP** has unexpectedly reversed its opposition to Brüning's government following last-minute concessions from the Chancellor. In a crucial no-confidence vote, they sided with the government, counteracting the impact of the **DVP**'s withdrawal. Additionally, some members of the **DVP**'s left wing, including Curtius and Otto Thiel, either voted with the government or abstained. This sudden shift by the **WP** has all but sealed its political demise. Already struggling to maintain support among the middle class, the party now faces mass defections, with local chapters either dissolving or breaking away entirely. Unfortunately, all of this effort is for naught, with only [+ bruning_coalition +]% of the Reichstag voting against the Brüning government. bruning_second_cabinet.bruning_lives_no_.bodyHtml: We are once again compelled to vote in favor of the [+ chancellor +] government to prevent the extremist parties on the far-right and left from translating their growing popular support into parliamentary gains. Some members of the **DVP**'s left wing, such as Curtius and Otto Thiel, have also voted with the government or abstained, going against their wider party. Despite the new right-wing cabinet, the national opposition is still refusing to support Brüning, as they want all the power to themselves.

bruning_second_cabinet.bruning_lives_wp.bodyHtml: The **WP** has unexpectedly reversed its opposition to Brüning's government following last-minute concessions from the Chancellor. In a crucial no-confidence vote, they sided with the government, effectively neutralizing the impact of the **DVP**'s withdrawal. Additionally, some members of the **DVP**'s left wing, including Curtius and Otto Thiel, either voted with the government or abstained. This sudden shift by the **WP** has all but sealed its political demise. Already struggling to maintain support among the middle class, the party now faces mass defections, with local chapters either dissolving or breaking away entirely. Despite the formation of a more right-leaning cabinet, the national opposition remains unwilling to support Brüning, as they seek to claim full control for themselves.

bruning_survive.bodyHtml: The more radical anti-Brüning factions within the [? if not lvp_formed and dvp_exist:**DVP** and the?][? if lvp_formed: right **LVP** and the?] **DNVP** initially pushed to break with Brüning, threatening to vote against the act. However, the strong pro-Brüning faction—including figures like Westarp, Curtius, and influential industrialists such as Hans Luther—managed to sway their colleagues, arguing the act is a necessary, albeit painful, step to stabilize Germany’s economy. Their confidence in Brüning was further restored by the fact that the measures were not as severe as initially feared. As a result, the planned vote of no confidence has been shelved, allowing the bourgeois-right government to survive—at least for now.

bruning_toleration_right_collapse.subtitleHtml: The rise of the national opposition has forced them to act.
bruning_toleration_right_collapse.bodyHtml: = The **DNVP** breaks with Brüning The sharp rise of the **DNF** and **NSDAP** in local elections has triggered mass panic within the **DNVP**, as pessimism and a noticeable shift away from democracy rapidly take hold within the once-constructive "democratic" party. They now believe that only closer cooperation with the national opposition and a rightward shift in alignment with the nation can salvage their declining poll numbers. Their first step toward this goal is an attempt to bring down the Brüning government with the assistance of the anti-democratic parties, hoping either to force Brüning into reorganizing his cabinet or to trigger elections that could deliver a right-wing majority. However, Hugenberg and Hitler remain committed to their all-or-nothing strategy, demanding the chancellorship outright from Brüning. This leaves only the prospect of fresh elections as a possibility, with Hitler being very vague about what his government would look like. Given that Hugenberg and Hitler are far from the most trustworthy figures, the party remains in limbo for now. Hopefully [+ dnvp_leader +] can restore order within his party, and prevent new elections from delivering catastrophic gains for the far-right.

bruning_toleration_right_collapse.vonc_h.bodyHtml: Oskar Hergt, who was once forced to resign nearly a decade ago over his decision to allow a free vote on the Dawes Plan—the very plan that rescued Germany from hyperinflation and ushered in the Golden Twenties—is now tendering his resignation once again after failing to impose party discipline. History seems to be repeating itself: the **DNVP** is once again deeply divided, with its pragmatic wing supporting Brüning while its emboldened right wing aligns with the national opposition. The party now faces a fateful decision—either accept the bitter pill of working within the system or risk catastrophic consequences, possibly even the destruction of the Weimar Republic itself.

bruning_toleration_right_collapse.vonc_l.bodyHtml: Walther Lambach, a strong supporter of Brüning and, to some extent, democracy, has enforced party discipline to ensure the Reichstag delegation votes in favor of Brüning. However, the anger many within his party has against him and his Christian Social ideals has split the party almost down the middle.

bruning_toleration_right_collapse.vonc_m.bodyHtml: [? if dnvp_leader == "Schiele": Martin Schiele, a strong supporter of Brüning—and his Minister of Agriculture—has successfully persuaded the agrarian wing of the **DNVP** to oppose the vote of confidence. He also enlists the support of Westarp and incumbent cabinet members to lobby the rest of the party. However, some radical members, who remained in the party solely due to their shared hatred of Hugenberg, are expected to defy party discipline. ?][? if dnvp_leader == "Westarp": Kuno von Westarp, a longtime leader of the **DNVP** and one of Brüning's strongest supporters, has rallied members from all wings of the party to oppose the proposed vote of no confidence, warning of the political and economic instability that would follow if it passed. However, some radical members, who remained in the party solely due to their shared hatred of Hugenberg, are expected to defy party discipline. ?]

bruning_win.bodyHtml: Heinrich Brüning may be an advocate of economic austerity, but as president, he’s a clear step up from Hindenburg in both his republican convictions and his stance toward the **SPD**. Let’s hope he stands firm and keeps the Nazis out of power.

brunswick.bodyHtml: In order for the **NSDAP** to quickly and discreetly grant Hitler citizenship, they had to collaborate with the [? if dvp_exist: **DVP**?][? if not dvp_exist: **DNVP**?], who, while supportive of these efforts, insisted on maintaining an appearance of legality. During a meeting between the two parties, they agreed to give Hitler a position in the Brunswick embassy to the Reichsrat. Following this agreement, a heated debate erupted about whether Hitler would actually fulfill his obligations once he became a civil servant. However, after further reassurances, Hitler was sworn in and officially granted citizenship.

brunswick_fail.bodyHtml: In order for the **NSDAP** to quickly and discreetly grant Hitler citizenship, they had to collaborate with the [? if not lvp_formed and dvp_exist:**DVP**?][? if not lvp_formed and not dvp_exist:[? if not cvp_formed:**DNVP**?][? if cvp_formed:**[+ z_party_name +]**?]?][? if lvp_formed:**LVP**?], whose radical right-wing elements are in support, but the party as a whole opposes this move. During a meeting between the two parties, no agreement is reached. As a result, Hitler will remain a stateless person, and this will damage his reputation as the Führer of the Germans.

bureaucracy.bodyHtml: The bureaucracy is deeply reactionary, and many abuse their power to favor the political right. By removing the pro-monarchy and pro-dictatorship elements, we can democratize it. Some of our opponents claim that we are infringing on individual freedoms, but perhaps the security of the republic requires it.

businesses_lose_confidence.subtitleHtml: Big businesses are losing confidence in our government's policies.
businesses_lose_confidence.bodyHtml:
= Businesses Lose Confidence
Because of our government's policies, which are perceived as anti-business, the capitalists are reducing their investment and laying off workers. This has the immediate effect of raising unemployment and dissent against our government, especially among the middle class.
The business community has a variety of suggestions as to how we might improve the business environment.

bvp_coalition.titleHtml: The **BVP** coalitions with the Bavarian Peasants’ League and various bourgeois parties.
bvp_coalition.subtitleHtml: The BVP will make amends with the farmers.
bvp_coalition.bodyHtml: The former incumbent coalition consisting of the **BVP**, Bavarian Peasants’ League, and the various smaller bourgeois parties has continued. This show of stability will weaken the Nazis. Heinrich Held, the incumbent Minister-President and a pro-democratic member of the **BVP** remains in power.

params.source: election_menu

bvp_majority.titleHtml: The **BVP** has captured another majority.
bvp_majority.bodyHtml: The **BVP** has surprisingly won an outright majority, and no longer needs the support of the bourgeois parties. This has cemented Bavaria as one of the most stable state governments, maybe not "democratic" though. Heinrich Held, the incumbent Minister-President and a pro-democratic member of the **BVP** remains in power.

params.source: election_menu

bvp_toleration.titleHtml: The **BVP** has fallen short of a majority, but continue to rule in caretaker capacity.
bvp_toleration.subtitleHtml: Electing a new Minister-President—or dissolving the Landtag—requires an absolute majority. Deep antagonism between the opposition parties has made clearing that hurdle all but impossible.
bvp_toleration.bodyHtml: Despite the **BVP** falling short of a majority, even with the inclusion of other bourgeois parties, they continue to rule in as a caretaker government. [? if nsdap_bavaria_elections_vote >= 15: Negotiations with the **NSDAP** has collapsed, due to their disdain for Catholics. ?] Heinrich Held, the incumbent Minister-President and a pro-democratic member of the **BVP** remains in power.

cabinet_reshuffle.titleHtml: Demand a reshuffle of the cabinet.
cabinet_reshuffle.subtitleHtml: Schleicher’s cabinet remains dominated by deeply reactionary holdovers from the Papen cabinet of barons.
cabinet_reshuffle.bodyHtml: Although many reactionary figures in the cabinet have already been replaced by Center Party appointees, further reform is needed to nudge Schleicher’s government toward a more democratic appearance. The Finance Ministry, previously held by Schwerin von Krosigk, is handed over to a more neutral, non-partisan banker. The Interior Ministry and the Minister without Portfolio post are assigned to the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?] moderate, Gottfried Treviranus. The Agricultural Ministry is granted to Hans Schlange-Schöningen, a [? if not kvp_formed and dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **CNBLP**?][? if kvp_formed: **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?] agrarian in support of peasant homesteads. Though these shifts may seem minor on the surface, the entry of more democratic-leaning ministers into the cabinet makes our continued support more palatable to both the party and our electorate—and subtly shifts the balance in key cabinet votes.

[? if spd_votes >= 31:The SPD remaining electorally resilient despite the radicalizing effects of the economic depression has thwarted Hindenburg’s plan to burden us with governance and erode our popularity. You still have a chance.) ?]

campaign_high.titleHtml: Launch an extensive ground and propaganda campaign, reaching all corners of the state.
campaign_high.bodyHtml: Despite Lippe's small size, our campaign needs to rival the Nazis. Speakers are brought in from all over the country to preach to the workers about the dangers of Nazism, and highlight the **SPD**'s accomplishments on behalf of the working class. We made efforts to campaign among the traditionally conservative rural areas of the state, [? if not peoples_party: however, we have not historically campaigned much among the farmers, and they do not trust us over the Nazis. ?][? if peoples_party: with varying degrees of success. ?][? if democracy_paramilitary: Despite the **SA**'s attempts at disruption, Reichsbanner units brought in from other parts of the country maintain order. ?][? if not democracy_paramilitary: However, the **SA** has repeatedly disrupted our gatherings, and attacked many of our officials. ?] Although our campaigning efforts may finally have caught up to the one of the Nazis, they've received a welcome surprise by Hugenberg announcing a political truce with the **NSDAP**, a step toward reconciliation. As a result, their campaign is free from bourgeois counter-campaigns in the rural 60% of the state.

campaign_low.titleHtml: Leave campaigning to the local **SPD**.
campaign_low.bodyHtml: We don't need to worry about Lippe. Local campaigning efforts are left to the historically popular local **SPD** and Minister-President, who seek to maintain the loyalty of the state's working-class. Our campaign pales in comparison to the Nazi one by miles, who have received a welcome surprise by Hugenberg announcing a political truce with the **NSDAP**, a step toward reconciliation. Therefore, their campaign has free rein over the rural 60% of the state.
