cancel_elections.subtitleHtml: This is an anti-democratic move that may backfire.
cancel_elections.bodyHtml: Since we are currently ruling as part of an emergency government, we may use quasi-constitutional trickery to significantly delay these elections, and continue governing via Article 48. This is likely to be extremely unpopular both with our base and with the other parties. However, this may be necessary to prevent the extremists from gaining power.

cancel_elections_2.bodyHtml:
Fine. President [+ president +] has taken the unprecedented step of canceling these elections. New elections are scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].
Let us hope this does not backfire.

choices.labelHtml: Support Hugo Eckener as a joint Weimar Coalition candidate.
Support Konrad Adenauer of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].
Support Otto Gessler of the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?].

candidates.bodyHtml: The nationalists and Chancellor [+ chancellor +] have chosen to nominate Hans von Seeckt—former Chief of the German Army from 1920 to 1926, and a staunch conservative monarchist, infamous for his refusal to suppress the Kapp Putsch with the remark: "Reichswehr do not fire on Reichswehr". In recent years, he was elected to parliament under the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?], gradually drifting further to the radical right. He even appeared as a featured speaker at the Harzburg Rally. Now returned from a military advisory mission in China, Seeckt enters the race for the presidency—backed by many of Hindenburg’s former allies and the disgraced Schleicher. The Nazis, recognizing the precariousness of their position, have swallowed their pride and endorsed Seeckt for the presidency. [? if not hindenburg_term_extended: They deem him sufficiently right-wing—after all, he once wrote to his sister urging her to vote for [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] in 1932. ?] The **Communists** are too disorganized following Schleicher's crackdown, and are unable to field a candidate for president. They will be backing whoever we choose to back, provided it's a socialist. Many republicans of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?], and **SPD** float the idea of running Hugo Eckener, a nationally renowed Zeppelin captain, as a unity candidate. While he has some nationalistic views, he is also ardently opposed to Nazism. Barring that, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] are planning to run separate candidates in the first round if the **SPD** runs its own candidate. The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is considering nominating Konrad Adenauer, mayor of Köln and member of the Prussian state legislature. He calls for an alliance of conservative Christian democrats that encompasses both Catholics and Protestants. The [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] might nominate Otto Gessler, former defense minister, who has crossover appeal to conservatives in the moderate right and other parties who dislike the renewed nationalist-Nazi alliance. As for the **SPD**, we could support a joint Weimar Coalition candidate or run our own. A leading candidate is Albert Grzesinski of our Reformist faction. Former Interior Minister of Prussia and currently Berlin’s Police Chief, he has played a central role in combating both far-right and left-wing extremism. Most notably, he helped organize the general strike that brought down Schleicher. However, his hardline stance against the **Communists**—including his suppression of their demonstrations—has made him unacceptable to them. Alternatively, we could nominate Otto Wels, our party chairman and leader of the Centrist faction. He is palatable to the bourgeois parties and the Communists, who may begrudgingly tolerate his candidacy.

params.source: candidate_menu

candidates_dems.titleHtml: The **Communists**? The Weimar Parties? Who will they support?
candidates_dems.bodyHtml: With the **Communists** having been heavily suppressed during Schleicher’s tenure, they are no longer a significant political force. [? if kpd_banned: They are even banned outright, preventing them from endorsing their own candidate. With boycotting rendered pointless, they have no choice but to support whoever we put forward. ?][? if not kpd_banned: Grateful for our role in sparing them from Schleicher’s crackdown months ago, they are fully backing whoever we choose to nominate. ?] [? if z_candidate == "Adenauer": The Center is not fully convinced to back [+ dnef_candidate +] and has chosen to run its own candidate: Konrad Adenauer. The Mayor of Cologne since the Republic's inception, and a member of the Prussian legislature, he's an advocate for the Center Party "leaving the tower" to broaden its appeal among Protestants, Adenauer was first proposed by Stegerwald himself. Though situated on the right wing of his party, he remains firmly committed to the Weimar Republic and opposes Schleicher’s threats against it. ?] [? if heuss_run: The liberals are running Theodor Heuss—a journalist and vocal supporter of the Weimar Republic, and a staunch anti-Schleicherist within his own party. This stance has put him at odds with more pro-Schleicher elements in the German middle class. While unlikely to secure significant support, Heuss has positioned himself as a "Weimar" unity candidate in opposition to [+ dnef_candidate +]. ?][? if not heuss_run and ddp_candidate == z_candidate and z_candidate != dnef_candidate: The liberals, mired in electoral ruin, lack the resources or energy to field a candidate of their own. Instead, they have thrown their support behind [+ z_candidate +] as the bourgeois alternative to Schleicher. However, their backing is far from solid—pro-Schleicher elements remain rogue, as his message of national solidarity continues to resonate with the historically nationalist German liberal movement. ?][? if not heuss_run and ddp_candidate == dnef_candidate: The liberals, mired in electoral ruin, lack the resources or energy to field a candidate of their own. They have thrown their support behind [+ dnef_candidate +], heavily influenced by pro-Schleicher elements and propaganda that has resonated especially strongly with their rank-and-file. Many within the party now see it as their national duty to support Schleicher and his successor, believing this to be the only path toward restoring Germany’s great power status abroad and securing concessions at home. ?]

candidates_nats.bodyHtml: The nationalists are unified in their support for [+ dnef_candidate +], joined by the various splinter factions and the minor bourgeois parties. Although Hugenberg is—somehow—still contemplating a presidential run, a strongly worded threat has convinced him to remain silent.

candidates_nazis.bodyHtml: With Hitler gone from the political scene, the Nazis will be fielding Hermann Göring as their candidate. The **DSU** will be running [? if dsu_candidate == "Strasser": their party leader, Otto Strasser, as a separate candidate. ?][? if dsu_candidate == "Frick": Wilhelm Frick as a separate candidate. ?] [? if nvf_candidate == dnef_candidate: The remnants of the **NVF** will be backing [+ dnef_candidate +], as they remain within the **DNEF** umbrella. ?][? if nvf_candidate != dnef_candidate: The remnants of the **NVF** will be boycotting the election entirely—continuing their deluded course of waiting for the "right moment" to spark an armed rebellion. ?] With the Nazis movement remaining divided, none of their candidates have any remote chance to winning.

candidates_spd.bodyHtml: As for the **SPD**, we could support a joint Weimar Coalition candidate or run our own. The viability of a united front, however, depends entirely on our relations with former coalition partners—and whether they’ve fallen under Schleicher’s influence. Otto Braun is tired. He ran and failed in the previous two presidential elections, and no longer wishes to run. His wife is ill enough that he wishes to stay by her side. More importantly, he is deeply pessimistic about the situation we now face. Kurt Schumacher is an ambitious rising star in the party, and would be all too willing to run. He was a hero in the Great War, but his relatively young age might be relevant.

center_party_conference_kaas.subtitleHtml: Ludwig Kaas has resigned as the Center Party's chairman...
center_party_conference_kaas.bodyHtml: = Center Party Conference Ludwig Kaas has never truly embraced his role as party chairman, viewing it as a burden. He was elected as a compromise candidate, without actively campaigning for the position. Privately, he has made no secret of his desire to be relieved of the party chairmanship. With the stabilization of the Weimar Republic, Kaas believes he can retire without facing any significant consequences. Despite pleads from his party members and colleagues, Kaas has officially resigned as head of the Center Party. This decision will have little impact, as he spent most of his time in Rome anyway, delegating the management of the party to his allies Joos and Brüning. No other Center member has missed as many Reichstag sessions as Kaas. Now, the party must find a successor, with potential candidates being his deputy leader Joos, Brüning, Stegerwald, or perhaps another compromise candidate.

center_party_conference_kaas.bruning.subtitleHtml: Brüning is the leader of the Center's parliamentary group, and the party's economic expert.
center_party_conference_kaas.bruning.bodyHtml:
Heinrich Brüning, the current chancellor, an ally of Kaas and protege of Stegerwald has got another job under his belt now. Although his responsibilities as chancellor will leave very little room for him to manage the internal affairs of his party, with it once again being left to his colleagues. 
Nothing ever happens.

center_party_conference_kaas.guerard.subtitleHtml: Guérard is part of the Center's civil servant wing, and is in the dead center of the party politically.
center_party_conference_kaas.guerard.bodyHtml: Von Guérard, a rather plain government bureaucrat in charge of the Transport Ministry and former parliamentary group leader for the Center, has shifted to the left over the years. He is elected as a compromise candidate due to his inoffensiveness to any wing of the party. His political position aligns with that of former chancellor and party leader Wilhelm Marx, and he has voiced support for the continuation of the Weimar Coalition.

center_party_conference_kaas.joos.subtitleHtml: Joos is part of the Catholic worker groups, and the current deputy leader of the party responsible for organizational work.
center_party_conference_kaas.joos.bodyHtml: With our friendly relations, we have been able to influence the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] delegates to promote Joseph Joos to become the new [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] chairman. He has long been a friend of the **SPD**, and will be more inclined to collaborate with us compared to Kaas. He also increases the appeal of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] to the working class, though it comes at the cost of deepening the social and economic divisions once held together by religion. Unfortunately, the hands-off approach to internal party affairs under Kaas is expected to be maintained under his successor, limiting Joos's influence over the parliamentary delegation.

center_party_conference_kaas.stegerwald.bodyHtml: Adam Stegerwald has been elected as the chairman of the Center Party. He seems to represent a rightward turn from Marx, despite his trade union background, and will preside over a Center Party less inclined to compromise with the left. He views the Center Party as a prototype for a Christian, democratic, German, and social party, and aims to transform it according to the principles laid out in his proposed "Essen program" eight years prior. The Center Party's middle class wing are in uproar over the vote, despite Stegerwald conceding his leadership of the Reichstag delegation and the Minister-Presidency to his protege Heinrich Brüning. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": His election also attracts some Protestant **DNVP** dissidents and industrialists, who may result in a shift of the party towards the right. ?]

The Centrists are slowly losing their grip on the party.

center_right_coalition.bodyHtml: A center-right coalition is formed featuring an broad array of parties to the right of us. They will begin undoing years of reform and democratization that we fought hard to achieve and will let right-wing paramilitaries like the Stahlhelm and the Nazi **SA** run free. It won't take long for the government to collapse and for us to take power through new elections. But when it eventually does, we won't have much allies as our former coalition partners are beginning to shift to the right. When the time comes, who will stand with us? While this is a setback, it is not the worst possible outcome, as new elections could have led to significant gains for extremist parties. [? if z_leader != "Stegerwald": Adam Stegerwald?][? if z_leader == "Stegerwald": Heinrich Brüning?] of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia.

center_right_coalition_reenter.bodyHtml: = The **DNVP** Rejoins Government The Young Plan has been ratified, and the controversy surrounding it has largely subsided, prompting the **DNVP** to rejoin the cabinet it had previously abandoned. Their primary motivation for reentering the government is their fear of socialist influence over Brüning's policies due to our toleration of Brüning’s administration. As a result, Brüning no longer depends on our votes.

christiansocial.bodyHtml: The exodus of workers from our support base has greatly strengthened the Christian Socials within the **DNVP**, who seek to take advantage of our alienation of the trade unions. Walther Lambach has been elected leader of the **DNVP**, a trade union leader and the center of discourse within their party in the last congress. The loyalties of the Reichswehr, with its [+ reichswehr_strength +] thousand regular soldiers, and Prussian police, with [+ prussian_police_strength +] thousand members, are unclear. civil_war_long.bodyHtml: As the frontlines settle, a republican state—committed to the continuation of Weimar Germany—takes root in the West, while a newly formed Ruhr Red Army establishes **Communist** control over the Rhineland. The fragile alliance of far-right forces soon fractures, with the **Stahlhelm** and the **SA** turning against one another in violent internal conflict. Ernst Röhm eventually reduces [+ nsdap_leader +] to a puppet, seizing full control and unleashing unspeakable atrocities against the local Jewish and Polish populations in the territories under their control. A renewed offensive by republican forces exploits the chaos on the Right, culminating in the defeat of the reactionary militias. However, a brutal campaign continues in the Ruhr, where every town exacts a death toll of thousands. By 1936, Germany remains fractured. Poland has seized the moment to occupy parts of East Prussia and Silesia, citing the protection of ethnic Poles. Meanwhile, the French dispatch a "peacekeeping" force into the Rhineland. In the end, it is not so much a victory for the Republic as it is a decisive collapse of the far-right. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, but the French reoccupation of the Rhineland has complicated efforts. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own.

civil_war_long_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - The Black Spot of Europe Despite the Republic’s paper victory, revanchist sentiment over the loss of Eastern and Western territories, coupled with mass radicalization from the staggering death toll, destruction, hyperinflation, widespread hunger, and the absence of meaningful foreign aid, has deeply discredited the political establishment. Under pressure from the Reichswehr, martial law remains in place for years, with the military increasingly intruding into civilian governance. By 1939, a global recession—triggered by escalating instability across Europe and threats from the Soviet Union—obliterates the reconstruction progress made by the ruling **SPD**, plunging the country into yet another crisis. Following a March on Berlin, a "Third Positionist" regime seizes power, led by a new political party composed of former Nazis and disillusioned socialists. Germany pivots toward autarky and radical self-reliance, sealing its borders to foreigners. The regime earns the moniker "Black Spot of Europe," ruling from 1940 to 1996. During this period, it successfully coerces the withdrawal of foreign troops from the Rhineland and reclaims its lost eastern territories—including the Polish Corridor—in 1946, capitalizing on Poland's distraction with the Soviet threat and the shifting priorities of the Western Allies as they fight war with Japan. Today, Germany remains largely isolated from the rest of the world, with the successor to the dictatorship of old being not much better, being ruled by oligarchs and the wealthy who are relicts of the past regime. Now, the task of Social Democracy is to prepare for the next election. The incumbent government of Wolfgang Schäuble is unpopular, and we stand to gain. Perhaps the next government will have a socialist plurality.

civil_war_long_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - A European Future In exchange for the return of the Rhineland and the lifting of its post-war reparations burden, Germany is compelled to enter a defensive pact with France and Britain. With assistance from the League of Nations and the United States, the so-called "Morgenthau Plan", funded by the Western Allies, successfully facilitates German reconstruction and ushers in a Wirtschaftswunder under the leadership of Chancellor Konrad Adenauer. By the end of the decade, the economies of the West become increasingly interconnected. Further integration into a nascent "European Union"—featuring free trade and the free movement of people—is negotiated by the internationalist **SPD** and the **LVP**. Renewed Soviet threats to Eastern European nations like Finland and Poland, alongside the democratization of Austria and Italy, have once again galvanized a united European response to Bolshevik aggression. Today, Germany remains a pillar of a federal European Union stretching from Lisbon to Athens. Now, the task of Social Democracy is to prepare for the next election. The incumbent government of Klaus Schwab is unpopular, and we stand to gain. Perhaps the next government will have a socialist plurality.

civil_war_lost.bodyHtml: We have lost the civil war. At least it was a quick coup, and ended before Germany could be plunged into total war.

civil_war_win.bodyHtml: Following a brief civil war between republican forces and the far-right, we’ve been given a blank slate to rebuild Germany on a truly democratic and social foundation—free, for now, from the fear of reactionary reprisals. A minor coup attempt by General Bredow is foiled, and with it, the Reichswehr is finally brought under the banner of the republic. But it is not all sunshine and rainbows. The civil war has devastated countless lives, and the costs of reconstruction and welfare have triggered the return of hyperinflationary nightmares. Hunger now exceeds levels seen during the Great Depression, and many are already growing disillusioned with their supposed saviors. Though the reactionary and far-right forces were defeated on the battlefield, it's only a matter of years before a new right-wing movement emerges and takes root among the weary and discontented populace. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, but the French reoccupation of the Rhineland has complicated efforts. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?].. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own.

civil_war_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - A False Victory The fracturing of the **SPD** into the **SVD** and the **SED** in the wake of post-war optimism deeply divided the German left. As in 1920, leftist disunity once again produced a scenario where a "New Weimar Coalition"—composed of the **SVD**, LVP, and **CSRP**—was unable to secure a majority. This led to repeated snap elections, ultimately fueling another resurgence of extremism. It was only through the formation of the German National Unity Front—a broad alliance of all bourgeois parties—and the election of Otto Gessler as president that Germany finally escaped its political deadlock. The resulting coalition of the **ZCA**, **LVP**, and **DBP** emerged as the new “natural governing bloc,” as persistent ideological rifts continued to paralyze the left. The **SVD**, increasingly marginalized, was at times compelled to tolerate these centrist cabinets in the name of stability—abandoning its Marxist roots in the process and ceding leadership of the left to the more radical **SED**. Only with the third wave of democratization in the 1990s did the long-divided German left begin to reunify. The gradual moderation and eventual merger of the **SED** and the **SVD** culminated in the formation of the **VSPD**, which at last returned to government after decades in opposition.

civil_war_win_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - The Socialist Dream Despite the blank slate granted to the **SPD** to reshape Germany in its image, the country has faced relentless challenges: the hyperinflationary crisis of the 1930s, the resurgence of the far-right in the 1940s, and a series of counterproductive bans that only emboldened reactionary forces. Yet, step by step, Germany rebuilds. Even following the **SPD**’s splintering into the **SED** and **SVD** due to foreign policy disputes in the 1940s, both parties cooperated to construct a comprehensive welfare state—one that could stand alongside the Nordic models in its scope and ambition. The bourgeois opposition—comprising the **ZCA**, **LVP**, and **DBP**—was relegated to a state of permanent irrelevance, unable to halt the wave of reforms: the rise of workplace councils, sweeping nationalizations, and the assertion of state control over the Reichsbank. However, the stagflation of the 1970s marked the beginning of the end for traditional leftist dominance. As the middle class expanded at the expense of the working class, the foundations of class politics began to erode—giving rise to a new multiparty system and ending the era of unchallenged socialist rule.

civil_war_won.titleHtml: We have won the civil war.
civil_war_won.bodyHtml: We have won the civil war against the reactionary forces. Germany will be changed forever, but it is too early to know how.

civil_war.defeat.bodyHtml: = Total Defeat Our forces are no match for those of the reactionaries. Reichsbanner fighters are quickly overpowered by the forces of the **Stahlhelm**, **SA**, and Reichswehr. Many are killed before the rest surrender. Our remaining leaders flee the country or face execution, as the reactionaries take absolute power over Germany. Our resistance will be recorded in the history books, and in the future, our names will be honored. But for now, all is lost.

civil_war.republic_victory.bodyHtml: = Victory for the Republic The battle lines hold, and the **SA**, **Stahlhelm**, and pro-coup Reichswehr forces are defeated. Today, the forces of the republic prevail over the fascists and the reactionaries. There is a new revolution in Germany. Let us hope it produces a longer-lasting peace than the previous one.

complacency.bodyHtml: Even in their weakened state, the Nazis are still a threat. We must not be too complacent.

completednvpsplit.bodyHtml: The moderates within the **DNVP** united under Westarp are unable to defeat Hugenberg in a vote. This is in part due to Hugenberg's efforts of consolidating power within the party organizations. The agrarian representatives in the party finally had enough with Hugenberg's "all or nothing" strategy, especially after he governed as de-facto party dictator, disregarding even those he has shared power with. The anti-Hugenberg forces within the party have all left to form a new Konservative Volkspartei (Conservative People's Party). It is a question of how long this party would last, with some members rather wanting to affiliate with the special interest parties. Hugenberg is left with a diminished **DNVP**, smaller than the faction that split from it.

params.source: kvp_formed_2

completednvpsplit_stegerwald.bodyHtml: The moderates within the **DNVP**, joined by the agrarian wing, are unable to defeat Hugenberg in a vote. This is in part due to Hugenberg's efforts of consolidating power within the party organizations. The agrarian representatives in the party finally had enough with Hugenberg's "all or nothing" strategy, especially [? if was_in_right_coalition: after he collapsed the right-wing coalition exactly a year ago[? if (tariffs < 0 or land_reform > 0): leaving them powerless to combat the land and tariff reforms we've enacted?]. ?][? if (tariffs < 0 or land_reform > 0) and not was_in_right_coalition and not dvp_reform: since they're left powerless to combat the land and tariff reforms enacted. ?][? if not (tariffs < 0 or land_reform > 0) and not was_in_right_coalition and dvp_reform: since the **DVP** has been eating into their voter base the past few months. ?][? if (tariffs < 0 or land_reform > 0) and not was_in_right_coalition and dvp_reform: since they're left powerless to combat the land and tariff reforms enacted. ?] The anti-Hugenberg forces within the party have all left in separate ways. Committed nationalists form a new Konservative Volkspartei (Conservative People's Party), while more pragmatic members and trade unionists choose to join the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]. It is a question of how long this party would last, since it finds itself in the small political base to the right of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], but to the left of the **DNVP**.

compromise.bodyHtml: The **LVP** ministers in the cabinet have offered a compromise that raises some taxes on the wealthy, along with lesser welfare cuts. Our members have mixed opinions on accepting this compromise. Reformists and Centrists support maintaining our government to keep the fascists and communists out, while Labor generally opposes any cuts, and the Left is opposed to compromises with the bourgeoisie. The **LVP** are themselves are split about this, the Reichstag delegation may go against the compromise fashioned by their own ministers. [? if lvp_ideology == "Left": However, the **LVP** has resisted the national shift towards the right for the most part. ?]If we do go ahead with this, the coalition hinges on the decision of the **LVP**.

choices.labelHtml: Reject the compromise and let this government fall.
Decide this at a later date.

compromise_success.bodyHtml: We have accepted the compromise offered by the bourgeoisie. Many of the workers and unemployed see this as a betrayal, although we present it as the successful aversion of a much worse alternative. Despite the intense lobbying by German industry, the **LVP** have voted for the compromise in the narrowest of votes.

constitutional_reform.bodyHtml: #subtitle: Major changes to government. # technically you could do some trickery to get a 2/3 quorum in the Reichstag by stopping some people from attending... if the **NSDAP** is boycotting the Reichstag, or if the **NSDAP** or **DNVP** are banned in the aftermath of a coup atempt... # alternatively, a constitutional referendum can be initiated, that requires a simple majority of voters to pass (as I understand article 76). This should depend on support for the republic and for democracy, and the relationships with the other parties (more similar to the presidential election). = Constitutional Reform # the ideas for constitutional reform here are based on the bundesrepublik basic law... I'm not sure if it's totally realistic to what someone like Mierendorff would've wanted. Many neorevisionists consider the Weimar Constitution to be inadequate. They believe that the clauses of the constitution are in part responsible for the instability of the country, and must change in order to build a more stable democratic republic. Ideas from both socialists and liberals. A constitutional reform requires either a two-thirds supermajority in the Reichstag, or a constitutional referendum with support from a majority of the electorate. If we do not have a supermajority in the Reichstag, we must be assured of strong support from the other parties for the constitutional referendum.

constitutional_reform.presidential_power.subtitleHtml: The president can no longer dissolve the Reichstag at will, or call a Reichsexekution on state governments.
constitutional_reform.presidential_power.bodyHtml: The wide-ranging presidential powers promised by the constitution are a potential gateway to authoritarianism. Thus, we can support reforms that limit the powers of the president, ending his power to unilaterally terminate an elected government and to remove state governments. The **KPD** is in favor of this reform, having been victims of the Reichsexekution in the past (when **KPD**-supported state governments in Thuringia and Saxony were removed). The democrats of the [? if not lvp_formed:**[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed:**LVP**?] also support this. constitutional_reform.vote_threshold.bodyHtml: # The left is opposed to this. Some political thinkers believe that the proliferation of minor parties is responsible for the instability of the republic. continue_left_saxony.titleHtml: We will continue our coalition with the **KPD**.
continue_left_saxony.bodyHtml: **Red** Saxony is maintained. The bourgeois parties hate us all the more, but their cries are ineffectual. We will continue transforming the state into a stronghold of socialism. [? if coup_progress >= 8: Amidst our electoral victory, a far-right coup attempt is rumored to be close at hand. Proceed with caution. ?]

continue_spd_majority.bodyHtml: We have maintained our solo majority in the Saxon Landtag.  This has all but cemented us as the natural governing party of Saxony.

continue_toleration_saxony.titleHtml: We will continue our toleration agreement with the incumbent government.
continue_toleration_saxony.bodyHtml: Our toleration agreement in Saxony continues. Our party's remaining leftist elements grow weary of this arrangement, and they are increasingly defecting to the **KPD** [? if sapd_formed: and **SAPD**?]. Nevertheless, we have at least avoided repeat elections.

convince_lvp_success.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, we have convinced the **LVP** to give Braun an official endorsement, to the shock of the party's industrial backers. In response, they begin to withdraw their support from the party en masse, and a significant portion of right-wing voters are refusing to support us.

convince_spd_schleicher.subtitleHtml: [? if chancellor == "Papen": It's almost impossible to argue to the party to pursue this line, at least with Papen as chancellor. ?][? if chancellor == "Schleicher": Cooperation with the General himself is not unthinkable, with his concessions made toward the unions. ?]
convince_spd_schleicher.bodyHtml: Slowly but surely, the ADGB leadership is beginning to warm to the idea of constructive cooperation with the so-called "Red General." However, much work remains to be done—many within the union, and the overwhelming majority of the **SPD**, remain firmly opposed to cooperating with the man [? if chancellor == "Papen": propping up the widely despised Papen cabinet?][? if chancellor == "Schleicher": who now heads a widely unpopular government?]. [? if wtb_adopted: Our adoption of the WTB Plan—and Schleicher’s public support for similar public works initiatives—has modestly increased the party’s willingness to consider cooperation. ?] [? if otl_prussian_coup_seen: Furthermore, his role in the coup against our Prussian government has only deepened the animosity toward both him and the **SPD**. ?] Rumors about our cooperation has damaged our standing among the working class.

convince_z.bodyHtml: We remind the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] leaders of [? if hindenburg_run: Hindenburg's anti-Catholicism, and try to convince them that Hindenburg's path will eventually lead to Hitler. ?][? if not hindenburg_run: our genuine republican and democratic credentials. ?] [? if in_weimar_coalition_prussia: We also remind them of the successes they've had as part of our Weimar coalition in Prussia with [+ spd_candidate_1932_disp +], and our support for the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] candidate Wilhelm Marx in the 1925 presidential election?][? if not in_weimar_coalition_prussia: We also remind them of our support for the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] candidate Wilhelm Marx in the 1925 presidential election?]. [? if bruning_time and hindenburg_run: Unfortunately, Hindenburg's support for Brüning's government has left them with little room to oppose the very president sustaining his cabinet. ?]

crisis.subtitleHtml: Sender can help support a left-wing economic program.

params.source: crisis_program.support_left

crisis_program.bodyHtml: = Addressing the Economic Crisis Our party is wracked as to how to deal with the economic crisis. From the centrist faction, Hilferding argues that the economic crisis must be allowed to play out, because it is simply a part of the cyclic nature of capitalism. [? if not wtb_concept: The Labor faction is arguing for increased welfare spending to alleviate the suffering of the workers. Their economist, Wladimir Woytinsky, has voiced support for a public works campaign involving deficit spending, but it will take time to iron out the details. Furthermore, he will need the united support of the ADGB; otherwise, he won't have the power to challenge Hilferding's stance. ?][? if wtb_concept: From labor, the economist Wladimir Woytinsky argues that we must pursue a massive public works program to reduce unemployment and stimulate demand, perhaps including deficit spending. His opponents, like Hilferding, argue that this plan will cause a return to hyper-inflation, and that it would not even help the economy. In addition, according to Hilferding, Woytinsky's strategy is opposed to Marxist principles. ?] [? if wtb_concept: The so-called WTB plan, after its chief supporters Woytinsky, Tarnow, and Baade, is receiving more attention within the party. ?] However, leftists in the party argue that the WTB plan is merely a bandage over the fundamental flaws of capitalism. They argue that the crisis is an opportunity to end capitalism through massive nationalizations of industry, and finally bring our country to socialism. Meanwhile, moderates and reformists draw up proposals for a limited plan of job creation through public works, funded through taxes, that does not involve deficit spending or large-scale restructuring of the economy. Labor argues that the plan is inadequate in its scale and ambition.

[? if spd_in_government == 1 : We can begin implementing the plan as soon as possible, as long as we have the Economic or Finance ministries. ?] Bourgeois opposition is likely to be fierce. [? if spd_in_government == 0 : It might be difficult to enact the plan, given present conditions. ?]

crisis_program.defer.bodyHtml: We hold off on making a decision on economic policy, awaiting more information. Woytinsky and his supporters argue that inaction is a form of action of its own.

crisis_program.support_centrist.subtitleHtml: Let the depression play itself out.
crisis_program.support_centrist.bodyHtml:
Woytinsky and the trade unions vehemently criticize the centrists for their policy. The workers are starving; are we going to callously abandon them and side with bourgeois austerity? On the other hand, the centrists criticize Woytinsky for promising the workers false hope; their position is that nothing can be done to alleviate the depression. They also speak of the fear of another round of hyperinflation that may result from deficit spending.
Our policy course is currently that nothing can be done to alleviate the depression.

crisis_program.support_labor.subtitleHtml: Call for increased public works and fiscal stimulus.
crisis_program.support_labor.bodyHtml:
Our support of the WTB plan alienates the orthodox Marxists of the Centrist faction, and faces both opposition and support from a variety of sources across the spectrum. Leftists argue that the plan is flawed because it leaves capitalism intact, while some reformists are cautiously optimistic.
We have not yet convinced the party to formally adopt the plan. More work needs to be done.

crisis_program.support_labor_pre.subtitleHtml: Call for welfare spending and emergency relief for the workers.
crisis_program.support_labor_pre.bodyHtml: The Labor faction hasn't come up with a concrete solution to our economic woes yet, but has called for increased welfare spending in light of the rise in unemployment. Perhaps supporting their efforts will encourage a real solution to the crisis to be introduced.

crisis_program.support_left.subtitleHtml: Call for mass nationalizations and the transformation of the economy.

params.source: support_left_progress if nationalization_support < 5; adopt_left if nationalization_support >= 5

crisis_program.support_left_progress.bodyHtml: We attempt to convince the party to support a program of mass nationalizations in response to the economic crisis. Leftists argue that this policy is in accordance with our long-standing socialist platform, while reformists and some trade unionists argue that the plan is unrealistic, and that we need to focus on more immediate improvements to workers' lives. We have not yet formally adopted the plan. More work needs to be done.

crisis_program.support_moderate.subtitleHtml: Call for a limited program of job creation without deficit spending.

params.source: adopt_moderate if moderate_plan_support >= 3; support_moderate_progress if moderate_plan_support < 3

crisis_program.support_moderate_progress.bodyHtml:
We attempt to convince the party to support a moderate program of job creation without deficit spending. Advocates of the moderate plan argue that this plan is most likely to receive support from the bourgeois parties, and most practical in the immediate term. Opponents in the left and labor factions criticize the plan for being inadequate in its ambition.
We have not yet adopted the plan. More work needs to be done.

crushed.titleHtml: The rebellious Schutzbund has been crushed.
crushed.bodyHtml: The uprising lasted for no more than a few days before it was crushed. The Schutzbund and **SDAPÖ** were too weak and too divided to stand against the forces of the state.

cultural_figure.subtitleHtml: The next president should be a symbol of the new Germany...
cultural_figure.bodyHtml: Since the presidency has been made a largely ceremonial figure by our reforms, we might set a precedent by nominating a nonpartisan pro-democracy figure from the cultural, scientific, or literary worlds. There are many potential candidates...

choices.labelHtml: Actually, we should nominate someone else.

params.source: nazis_lose

culture.bodyHtml: It is not enough for the **SPD** to solely be a political party. The Worker Singer's League, Worker's Sports, and our schools and libraries are crucial to our members' lives. Funding these organizations makes our members more committed to the party, even when our policies might not be to their liking. [? if sa_strength > 500 : However, it feels frivolous to spend on sports and choirs when the fascists are murdering us in the streets. ?]

curriculum.bodyHtml: Many socialists believe that education in Germany is not fit for the modern era. Much of the educational system still follows imperial-era traditions of militaristic discipline, and far-right professors and students rule the universities. Nevertheless, there have been strides in bringing working-class children into the schools. What should be the major focus of our new curriculum? # note: education_science is a variable that affects how much education affects economic growth.

curtius.subtitleHtml: Curtius was a member of the former **DVP**, and is a committed Stresemannite and member of their left wing. He has since succeeded Stresemann on foreign policy matters.
curtius.bodyHtml: Julius Curtius, Stresemann's successor in foreign affairs and a former member of the **DVP**, has won the vote to succeed Luther for the chairmanship. Curtius is supported by the 'Pragmatic Center', and was put forth as a compromise candidate. As a former member of the **DVP**'s left wing, he is in favor of closer cooperation with us. However, his leadership has been quite uninspiring, to say the least. [? if foreign_minister_party == "LVP": The responsibilities of the foreign ministry prevent him from being involved in the day-to-day running of his party, which is now delegated to a group of his associates in the 'Pragmatic Center'. ?]

customs_union.titleHtml: Form a customs union with Austria?
customs_union.subtitleHtml: This will likely incur the wrath of France.
customs_union.bodyHtml: The right has long desired closer ties with Austria, with the eventual goal of the merger of the two German-speaking countries. A customs union with Austria is the first step towards this goal. Additionally, many believe that a union with Austria would improve our current economic circumstances. However, the Allies, especially France, are likely to object. This agreement would break the terms of the Versailles Treaty, and could lead to economic sanctions, further hurting our economy.

choices.labelHtml: No, we should do something else.

customs_union_2.bodyHtml: We have formed a customs union with Austria! The right-wing parties are praising us for this unexpected turn of events. Immediately, France and other neighboring countries lodge their protests. The longer-term response is yet to be seen.

Our loss is the **KPD**'s gain, and even the **NSDAP**, those lapdogs of the bourgeoisie, have joined in criticizing us for our austerity.

cvp_merger.bodyHtml: = The Center merges with the **DNVP** The Center Party, having undergone a major transformation into a center-right Christian People's Party under [+ z_leader +], has been flirting with the idea of merging with [+ dnvp_leader +]'s **DNVP** for the past few months. Their mutual participation in the currently governing right-wing coalition, newfound ideological closeness, and shared fears of both the Nazis and socialists—coupled with their electoral decline at the hands of the former—have pushed them toward closer cooperation. Following our fallout with the Center Party over their new direction, our remaining allies within their ranks have been sidelined, leaving them powerless to oppose the proposed merger. This shift has enabled the party’s leadership, alongside newly integrated right-wing Protestant politicians, to open negotiations with the **DNVP** on a possible unification. However, resistance remains: the **DNVP**’s old guard, led by figures like Westarp and Schiele, remain deeply skeptical of the merger, citing fundamental disagreements over key "national questions," such as reparations.

cvp_merger_lambach.cvp_dnvp.bodyHtml: A great deal of concessions are required to bring both sides to a comprehensive agreement, as both parties go through their differences and attempt to design a uniform policy if they were to merge. However, it is likely one party will have the upper hand in negotiations, either due to their electoral advantage, or reluctance forcing more sweeping concessions to be granted. Pro-merger factions: Far-Right (**Z**) Labor Right (**Z**) Protestant Right (**Z**) Christian Socials (**DNVP**) People's Conservatives (**DNVP**) Skeptical factions: Catholic Center (**Z**) National Conservatives (**DNVP**) Opposed factions: Christian Left (**Z**) Agrarians (**DNVP**) Balance of Power: [+ cvp_dnvp_balance : cvp_dnvp_balance +]

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.cvp_dvp_merger.bodyHtml: Before the Christian People's Party was to be announced to the public, representatives from the beleaguered **DVP** have shown their interest in joining the arrangement as well. This leaves the **[+ ddp_name +]** as the only liberal party in the political landscape, now flourishing with defections from the **DVP**'s left wing.

cvp_merger_lambach.economy.subtitleHtml: The debate over agriculture, welfare, and the depression.
cvp_merger_lambach.economy.bodyHtml: A potential big-tent Christian People's Party faces the difficult task of addressing the diverse economic concerns of its broad electoral base. This base spans across farmers, aristocrats, landowners, large businesses, small businesses, civil servants, white-collar workers, blue-collar urban workers, and many others from all walks of life.

params.source: economy_right if cvp_dnvp_balance < 20; economy_moderate if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 20 and cvp_dnvp_balance < 30; economy_left if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 30

cvp_merger_lambach.economy_left.bodyHtml: The Christians and Christian Socials have used their influence to advocate for a pro-worker and more ambitious economic policy, as a middle ground between capitalism and socialism. Taxation - Implement more progressive taxes and regulations, to ensure a fair Germany Economic Policy - Implement a 'Social market economy', a middle way between capitalism and socialism Great Depression - A public works program is needed, the people must get back to work

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.economy_moderate.bodyHtml: The Christians and nationalists have begrudgingly come to an agreement, as pragmatism wins the day. The party must represent its diverse base, for the *Volksgemeinschaft*. Taxation - Avoid tax increases at all costs Welfare - Focus on funding the current system, as the poor are suffering Labor - Against any socialistic policies, but neutrality in labor affairs is a key component of the *Volksgemeinschaft*. Great Depression - Experiment with a public works plan, combined with an increase in the money supply

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.economy_right.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians have used their leverage to edit in their economic beliefs into the party program. Taxation - Avoid tax increases at all costs, especially on businesses Welfare - Germany cannot afford welfare and maintain a balanced budget at the same time, one has to go Labor - Strongly against any socialistic policies that benefit the unions Great Depression - Maintain fiscal orthodoxy, productive industries and agriculture must be kept afloat though

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.monarchy.subtitleHtml: The debate over whether the party should be a republican or a monarchist one.
cvp_merger_lambach.monarchy.bodyHtml: The issue of the German monarchy remains highly divisive, with both parties holding starkly different views. Despite the unfeasibility of a restoration in the current political climate, the **DNVP** has never ceased advocating for a return to the days of the Kaiserreich. The Center Party, on the other hand, has consistently been a staunch republican force since the birth of the Weimar Republic. Perhaps the influence of the People's Conservatives and Christian Socials will outweigh the strong objections from the **DNVP**'s old guard.

params.source: monarchy_right if cvp_dnvp_balance < 30; monarchy_moderate if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 30 and cvp_dnvp_balance < 50; monarchy_left if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 50

cvp_merger_lambach.monarchy_left.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians attempted to insert their long-standing support for monarchism into the party platform, but were decisively outvoted by the staunchly republican Center, along with support from Lambach himself, having been the writer of the Lambach article years prior. Monarchy – Official endorsement of the republican system Democracy – Favors a more parliamentary system, with presidential decrees as a last resort

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.monarchy_moderate.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians have leveraged their influence to block an outright endorsement of republicanism in the party platform, ensuring their views remain represented despite being a vocal minority. Monarchy - No official party position on monarchism. Democracy - Supports a presidential government, otherwise maintain the status quo

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.monarchy_right.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians have successfully pushed for the inclusion of support for a constitutional monarchy in the party platform. However, it is no longer a central pillar of the party's ideology. Monarchy - Support for a constitutional monarchy, similar to the stance of the[? if not dvp_exist or lvp_formed: former?] **DVP**. Democracy - Favoring a strengthened presidency, while maintaining a pro-democratic stance

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.reparations.subtitleHtml: The debate over Germany's lost lands, the fulfillment of reparations, rearmament, and more.
cvp_merger_lambach.reparations.bodyHtml: The reparations issue remains the most contentious point of contention between the two parties, with starkly opposing views on how to handle Germany’s financial obligations. The **DNVP**, including Treviranus himself, staunchly opposed the Young Plan and has previously clashed with the Center over foreign policy achievements such as the Locarno Treaties in the past.

params.source: reparations_right if cvp_dnvp_balance < 50; reparations_moderate if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 50 and cvp_dnvp_balance < 60; reparations_left if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 60

cvp_merger_lambach.reparations_left.bodyHtml: The Christians have used their influence to push for a more restrained and diplomatic foreign policy, aligning with the legacy of Stresemann. Reparations - Germany should be develop closer ties with the West, hoping for a revision of the Versailles treaty The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to peacefully settle disputes in the East The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament, but scale it down

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.reparations_moderate.bodyHtml: The Christians and nationalists have begrudgingly come to an agreement, as pragmatism wins the day; Germany can't simply refuse to pay. Reparations - Germany should seek a policy of fulfillment, hoping for a revision of the Versailles treaty The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to pressure Poland for the return of our former lands, peacefully later down the line The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich, referendum for Eupen-Malmedy The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament and refitting of the army

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_lambach.reparations_right.bodyHtml: The nationalists and Christian Socials have used their leverage to edit in their most important goals to the party program. Reparations - Germany must push for the complete abolition of reparations and the revocation of the "war guilt" clause, but will continue payments in the meantime The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to pressure Poland for the return of our former lands, force if necessary later down the line The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich, push for an *Anschluss*, referendum for Eupen-Malmedy The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament and refitting of the army

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

The Center Party, on the other hand, has consistently been a staunch republican force since the birth of the Weimar Republic. Perhaps the influence of the People's Conservatives and Christian Socials will outweigh the strong objections from the **DNVP**'s old guard.

params.source: monarchy_right if cvp_dnvp_balance < 30; monarchy_moderate if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 30 and cvp_dnvp_balance < 50; monarchy_left if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 50

cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.monarchy_left.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians attempted to insert their long-standing support for monarchism into the party platform, but were decisively outvoted by the staunchly republican Center, along with support from Lambach himself, having been the writer of the Lambach article years prior. Monarchy – Official endorsement of the republican system Democracy – Favors a more parliamentary system, with presidential decrees as a last resort

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.monarchy_moderat.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians have leveraged their influence to block an outright endorsement of republicanism in the party platform, ensuring their views remain represented despite being a vocal minority. Monarchy - No official party position on monarchism. Democracy - Supports a presidential government, otherwise maintain the status quo

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.monarchy_right.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians have successfully pushed for the inclusion of support for a constitutional monarchy in the party platform. However, it is no longer a central pillar of the party's ideology. Monarchy - Support for a constitutional monarchy, similar to the stance of the[? if not dvp_exist or lvp_formed: former?] **DVP**. Democracy - Favoring a strengthened presidency, while maintaining a pro-democratic stance

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.reparations.subtitleHtml: The debate over Germany's lost lands, the fulfillment of reparations, rearmament, and more.
cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.reparations.bodyHtml: The reparations issue remains the most contentious point of contention between the two parties, with starkly opposing views on how to handle Germany’s financial obligations. The **DNVP**, including Treviranus himself, staunchly opposed the Young Plan and has previously clashed with the Center over foreign policy achievements such as the Locarno Treaties in the past.

params.source: reparations_right if cvp_dnvp_balance < 50; reparations_moderate if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 50 and cvp_dnvp_balance < 60; reparations_left if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 60

cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.reparations_left.bodyHtml: The Christians have used their influence to push for a more restrained and diplomatic foreign policy, aligning with the legacy of Stresemann. Reparations - Germany should be develop closer ties with the West, hoping for a revision of the Versailles treaty The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to peacefully settle disputes in the East The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament, but scale it down

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.reparations_mode.bodyHtml: The Christians and nationalists have begrudgingly come to an agreement, as pragmatism wins the day; Germany can't simply refuse to pay. Reparations - Germany should seek a policy of fulfillment, hoping for a revision of the Versailles treaty The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to pressure Poland for the return of our former lands, peacefully later down the line The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich, referendum for Eupen-Malmedy The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament and refitting of the army

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo_lambach.reparations_righ.bodyHtml: The nationalists and Christian Socials have used their leverage to edit in their most important goals to the party program. Reparations - Germany must push for the complete abolition of reparations and the revocation of the "war guilt" clause, but will continue payments in the meantime The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to pressure Poland for the return of our former lands, force if necessary later down the line The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich, push for an *Anschluss*, referendum for Eupen-Malmedy The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament and refitting of the army

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo.coalition.subtitleHtml: The debate over whether we should be considered as a coalition partner.
cvp_merger_oppo.coalition.bodyHtml: The integration of the staunchly anti-Marxist **DNVP** into the Center Party will likely rule out any future cooperation with them. However, a vocal minority of progressives still exists within the Center, who may argue in our favor.

cvp_merger_oppo.congress.titleHtml: With all differences resolved, the **CVP** is formed!
cvp_merger_oppo.congress.bodyHtml: The agreement is finalized, and the Christliche Volkspartei (Christian People's Party) is born. The **CVP** aims to follow the Essen Program of 1920, transforming the German Right into a party that rallies around Christian, democratic, German, and social principles.

cvp_merger_oppo.cvp_dnvp.bodyHtml: A great deal of concessions are required to bring both sides to a comprehensive agreement, as both parties go through their differences and attempt to design a uniform policy if they were to merge. However, it is likely one party will have the upper hand in negotiations, either due to their electoral advantage, or reluctance forcing more sweeping concessions to be granted. Pro-merger factions: Far-Right (**Z**) Labor Right (**Z**) Protestant Right (**Z**) Christian Socials (**DNVP**) People's Conservatives (**DNVP**) Skeptical factions: Catholic Center (**Z**) National Conservatives (**DNVP**) Opposed factions: Christian Left (**Z**) Agrarians (**DNVP**) Balance of Power: [+ cvp_dnvp_balance : cvp_dnvp_balance +]

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo.cvp_dvp_merger.bodyHtml: Before the Christian People's Party was to be announced to the public, representatives from the beleaguered **DVP** have shown their interest in joining the arrangement as well. This leaves the **[+ ddp_name +]** as the only liberal party in the political landscape, now flourishing with defections from the **DVP**'s left wing.

cvp_merger_oppo.cvp_party_congress_go.subtitleHtml: The future of this new party will be decided here.

cvp_merger_oppo.economy.subtitleHtml: The debate over agriculture, welfare, and the depression.
cvp_merger_oppo.economy.bodyHtml: A potential big-tent Christian People's Party faces the difficult task of addressing the diverse economic concerns of its broad electoral base. This base spans across farmers, aristocrats, landowners, large businesses, small businesses, civil servants, white-collar workers, blue-collar urban workers, and many others from all walks of life.

params.source: economy_right if cvp_dnvp_balance < 30; economy_moderate if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 30 and cvp_dnvp_balance < 40; economy_left if cvp_dnvp_balance >= 40

cvp_merger_oppo.economy_left.bodyHtml: The Christians and Christian Socials have used their influence to advocate for a pro-worker and more ambitious economic policy, recognizing that workers are a key part of the *Volksgemeinschaft*. Taxation - Implement more progressive taxes and regulations, to ensure a fair Germany Economic Policy - Implement a 'Social market economy', a middle way between capitalism and socialism Great Depression - A public works program is needed, the people must get back to work

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo.economy_moderate.bodyHtml: The Christians and nationalists have begrudgingly come to an agreement, as pragmatism wins the day. The party must represent its diverse base, for the *Volksgemeinschaft*. Taxation - Avoid tax increases at all costs Welfare - Focus on funding the current system, as the poor are suffering Labor - Against any socialistic policies, but neutrality in labor affairs is a key component of the *Volksgemeinschaft*. Great Depression - Experiment with a public works plan, combined with an increase in the money supply

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

cvp_merger_oppo.economy_right.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians have used their leverage to edit in their economic beliefs into the party program. Taxation - Avoid tax increases at all costs, especially on businesses Welfare - Germany cannot afford welfare and maintain a balanced budget at the same time, one has to go Labor - Strongly against any socialistic policies that benefit the unions Great Depression - Maintain fiscal orthodoxy, productive industries and agriculture must be kept afloat though

cvp_party_congress.subtitleHtml: The future of this new party will be decided here.
cvp_party_congress.bodyHtml: = First **[+ z_party_name +]** Congress The Christian People's Party (**[+ z_party_name +]**) has officially been founded! Adam Stegerwald, orchestrator of this arrangement and leader of the former Center, has been chosen as the interim leader of the new party. The **[+ z_party_name +]**'s inaugural congress will play a major role in shaping the direction of the newly founded party, and to elect a new chairman. It finally looks like we might have some competition now.

cvp_party_congress_go.subtitleHtml: The future of this new party will be decided here.

params.source: cvp_party_congress

cvp_party_congress_president.subtitleHtml: [+ cvp_leader +] will be resigning his positions to accept the presidency.
cvp_party_congress_president.bodyHtml: = Second **[+ z_party_name +]** Congress With the election of [+ president +]—the party chairman—as president, he naturally cannot retain both roles. He has since resigned, prompting a new party congress to select his successor. The party’s various factions are eager to assert themselves and steer its future direction. The outgoing chairman, now president, continues to wield considerable influence and is expected to endorse a candidate from his own faction.

cvp_party_congress_president.adenauer.titleHtml: Konrad Adenauer, formerly of the Center, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.adenauer.subtitleHtml: Adenauer, a long-time advocate for 'leaving the tower' and Mayor of Cologne since the Republic's inception - Catholic Center Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.adenauer.bodyHtml: # support losses are because he is a c*tholic Konrad Adenauer, the long-time Mayor of Cologne, has been elevated to the leadership of one of Germany's largest parties, which he strongly supported the formation of. Adenauer is committed to democratic principles and sits on the right wing of the former Center, without being tied to Christian labor. This has granted him the ability to rally a broad coalition of party leaders around his calm and stabilizing leadership against the more fringe politicians of the party. With his slogan 'No Experiments!', we do not expect any major changes to the party program under his leadership, fostering a sense among the people that the **[+ z_party_name +]** is a pole of stability that the German people can rally behind. In terms of our relationship with the Christians, Adenauer, being a former Center member, is relatively more friendly toward us than many others to his right. We can also count on the pressure from the Christian Left, who, similar to the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s left wing historically, are powerless to enact changes to the left but are influential in preventing changes to the right.

cvp_party_congress_president.bolz.titleHtml: Eugen Bolz, formerly of the Center, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.bolz.subtitleHtml: Bolz is the current Minister-President of Württemberg, having governed harmoniously with Bazille's state **DNVP** for the entire duration - Catholic Right Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.bolz.bodyHtml: Minister-President of Württemberg Eugen Bolz has been promoted to the leadership of the national **[+ z_party_name +]**. Bolz has worked harmoniously with the respected Wilhelm Bazille, a conservative leader of the moderate Württemberg **DNVP** since 1924, making him a natural choice as a compromise candidate. This has earned him nearly universal support within the party. However, Bolz's role as a compromise candidate has hindered his ability to effect significant change, as he must tread carefully to avoid alienating the factions that helped bring him to power. Bolz will attempt to bridge the confessional divides between Catholic and Protestant conservatives, with the party still divided along the lines of their party of origin. Given Bolz's refusal to enter a Weimar Coalition in Württemberg back in 1928, viewing the **SPD** as 'incapable of governing,' we do not expect much improvement in our relationship moving forward.

cvp_party_congress_president.gereke.titleHtml: Günther Gereke, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.gereke.subtitleHtml: Gereke has significant influence over the agricultural and industrial establishment, being a key member of the RLB and a founder of another rural association. - National Conservative and Agrarian Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.gereke.bodyHtml: Günther Gereke, a lawyer and prominent politician from rural Germany, has been elected as the new leader of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. What makes him notable is that he is an agrarian politician from west of the Elbe River, a leading reformist economic theorist, and someone with close ties to General Kurt von Schleicher. He bears similarities to Treviranus, though he is far less dogmatic in his beliefs. Thanks to Gereke’s strong relationship with the **CNBLP**, a rural special-interest party, he has successfully negotiated a merger of the declining party into the **[+ z_party_name +]**, though only a few officials remain in the effectively dead party. His support for a public works program has stemmed criticism from the labor factions, and his ability to unite the key interest groups on which the German Right depends on will help secure strong nationalist backing for the party. Needless to say, this has not sat well with the **[+ z_party_name +]**’s Catholic wing, and has made cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

cvp_party_congress_president.goerdeler.subtitleHtml: Goerdeler is the Mayor of Leipzig, harbouring fiscally conservative views and a support of monarchism. - People's Conservatives
cvp_party_congress_president.goerdeler.bodyHtml: The Mayor of Leipzig Carl Goerdeler has been promoted to the leadership of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. Goerdeler is aligned more with Westarp than anything, but Treviranus is willing to give the mayor a go. Goerdeler is known for his strong support and position in Brüning's cabinet, and his fiscal conservatism has attracted support of key industrial backers. Goerdeler's role as a compromise candidate has hindered his ability to effect significant change, as he must tread carefully to avoid alienating the factions that helped bring him to power. I actually don't know what to write for this guy, his WW2 anti-Nazi plots aren't relevant at this time since he viewed Hitler as an enlightened dictator at this time. I guess he supports taming the Nazis I guess? It goes without saying, this will make cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

cvp_party_congress_president.lambach.titleHtml: Walther Lambach, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.lambach.subtitleHtml: Lambach was apart of the Christian Social wing in the former DNVP. - Christian Social Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.lambach.bodyHtml: Somehow, the Christian Social wing, now diluted within a much larger party, has managed to elect one of their own as the leader of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. Walther Lambach, the writer of the Lambach article years ago[? if dnvp_leader == "Lambach":, and the most recent leader of the **DNVP**?], has won the vote largely due to the unified support of the Christian labor unions, who strongly back his vision for a *Volksgemeinschaft*. More worker-friendly policies have been added to the platform, such as expanding social welfare, increasing pensions, and implementing more progressive income taxes. They've even rejected austerity as a solution to Germany's current economic crisis, instead voicing support for public works. However, this has significantly strained industrial enthusiasm for the formation of the new party, and they have begun redirecting funds toward the liberals. This, however, is not good news for us. Christian Social ideology is deeply rooted in antisemitism, racism, nationalism, and religiosity. If anything, we've noticed worsening relations with the **[+ z_party_name +]**, as they attempt to present a non-Marxist alternative to the workers.

cvp_party_congress_president.lejeune_jun.titleHtml: Paul Lejeune-Jung, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.lejeune_jun.subtitleHtml: Major member of the former DNVP's Catholic wing, and aligned with Westarp's group. - National Conservative Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.lejeune_jun.bodyHtml: Paul Lejeune-Jung, leader of the **DNVP**'s Catholic wing, and an advocate for closer ties to the Center has been elected as leader of a merger between the two. His Catholic faith has made him acceptable to former Center members, and his alignment with Westarp's faction has solidified nationalist support. However, Lejeune-Jung's role as a compromise candidate has hindered his ability to effect significant change, as he must tread carefully to avoid alienating the factions that helped bring him to power. Lejeune-Jung will attempt to bridge the confessional divides between Catholic and Protestant conservatives, with the party still divided along the lines of their party of origin. It goes without saying, this will make cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

cvp_party_congress_president.stegerwald.titleHtml: Adam Stegerwald, formerly of the Center, is elected, no longer an interim leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.stegerwald.subtitleHtml: Stegerwald is relatively moderate, and his trade union roots are good news for our cooperation. - Catholic Labor Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.stegerwald.bodyHtml: Somewhat surprisingly, Center leader Adam Stegerwald is elected as the chairman of its successor party. This is largely attributed to the unified support from the various Christian labor unions and backing from former Center and Catholic politicians. However, he remains largely opposed by former **DNVP** members due to his willingness to cooperate constructively with the **SPD**. It was widely expected that, with the merger of the two parties, politicians like Stegerwald would shift to the left wing of the newly created party—and this has indeed proven true. His strongest supporters, aside from the trade unions, include the now strengthened Christian Left faction, which will push for a paternalistic economic policy and greater cooperation with the socialists. Stegerwald is also a committed republican, a stance that has pushed some ardent monarchists over to the **DNF**.

cvp_party_congress_president.treviranus.titleHtml: Gottfried Treviranus, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.treviranus.subtitleHtml: The leader of the Volkskonservativ movement, and an advocate for democratic principles. - People's Conservatives and Catholic Right Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.treviranus.bodyHtml: Gottfried Treviranus[? if dnvp_leader == "Treviranus":, the most recent leader of the **DNVP**?], leader of the thriving People's Conservative movement, is seen as the ideal candidate for the first chairman of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. His nationalist origin, strong ties to key figures like Westarp on the right, and his careful cultivation of relations with the Catholics have earned him broad support for his leadership. With his control of the colossally sized **[+ z_party_name +]**, Treviranus has finally been able to mold it into the Tory Democratic party he has long envisioned. His extensive connections with Schleicher, German industry[? if president == "Hindenburg":, President Hindenburg?], and the bourgeois elite are expected to greatly aid his leadership ambitions. Despite his democratic leanings, the [+ z_party_name +] remains firmly opposed to Marxism, effectively ruling out any prospects of coalition with us.

cvp_party_congress_president.vorbeck.titleHtml: War Hero Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.vorbeck.subtitleHtml: Lettow-Vorbeck is reluctant to lead, but perhaps his war hero status can serve as a unifying force? - National Conservative Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.vorbeck.bodyHtml: Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck is a war hero renowned for his undefeated record and his successful guerrilla campaign in German East Africa, with victories that rival those of Hindenburg. Despite multiple attempts to involve him in German politics, he has remained largely inactive, serving as a member of the Reichstag elected under the **DNVP**. However, the [? if vorbeck_deadlock: unending deadlock at the congress?][? if not vorbeck_deadlock and vorbeck_decline: drastic decline in the moderate right's vote share?][? if not vorbeck_deadlock and not vorbeck_decline and vorbeck_presidential: desire to utilize his character for a potential future election run?] has led to a growing number of factions rallying around his candidacy. The widespread popular support for him draws strong parallels to Hindenburg's own presidential candidacy declaration in 1925. Reluctantly, Lettow-Vorbeck has accepted the **[+ z_party_name +]**'s nomination as their next leader. However, he has little interest in managing the party’s internal affairs and has quietly delegated this responsibility to fellow conservatives like Westarp. Nonetheless, he remains the public face of the **[+ z_party_name +]** as chairman. The most crucial aspect of his election is his ability to inspire the German people to rally behind a Great War war hero once again, someone who embodies the image of stability and unity. Time will tell how long this popularity will last. It goes without saying, his election will make cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

cvp_party_congress_president.westarp.titleHtml: Kuno von Westarp, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress_president.westarp.subtitleHtml: A long-time DNVP stalwart, having prevented Hugenberg's takeover of the party in the past. - National Conservative Wing
cvp_party_congress_president.westarp.bodyHtml: A key figure of the German Right since the Republic's inception, Kuno von Westarp has ascended to the leadership role of the colossal Christian People's Party—certainly a significant step up. His election was primarily driven by the unified support of the entire former nationalist faction within the party. Westarp is highly experienced in managing internal dissent and is careful not to lean too heavily into any one particular wing of the party, aiming to avoid fracturing the organization. While the party program remains largely unchanged, there has been a noticeable increase in antisemitic and pro-monarchist rhetoric, as Westarp seeks to preserve the character of the now-defunct **DNVP** within this new entity. It goes without saying, Westarp's leadership will make cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.
