cvp_party_congress.adenauer.titleHtml: Konrad Adenauer, formerly of the Center, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.adenauer.subtitleHtml: Adenauer, a long-time advocate for 'leaving the tower' and Mayor of Cologne since the Republic's inception - Catholic Center Wing
cvp_party_congress.adenauer.bodyHtml: # support losses are because he is a c*tholic Konrad Adenauer, the long-time Mayor of Cologne, has been elevated to the leadership of one of Germany's largest parties, which he strongly supported the formation of. Adenauer is committed to democratic principles and sits on the right wing of the former Center, without being tied to Christian labor. This has granted him the ability to rally a broad coalition of party leaders around his calm and stabilizing leadership against the more fringe politicians of the party. With his slogan 'No Experiments!', we do not expect any major changes to the party program under his leadership, fostering a sense among the people that the **[+ z_party_name +]** is a pole of stability that the German people can rally behind. In terms of our relationship with the Christians, Adenauer, being a former Center member, is relatively more friendly toward us than many others to his right. We can also count on the pressure from the Christian Left, who, similar to the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s left wing historically, are powerless to enact changes to the left but are influential in preventing changes to the right.

cvp_party_congress.bolz.titleHtml: Eugen Bolz, formerly of the Center, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.bolz.subtitleHtml: Bolz is the current Minister-President of Württemberg, having governed harmoniously with Bazille's state **DNVP** for the entire duration - Catholic Right Wing
cvp_party_congress.bolz.bodyHtml: Minister-President of Württemberg Eugen Bolz has been promoted to the leadership of the national **[+ z_party_name +]**. Bolz has worked harmoniously with the respected Wilhelm Bazille, a conservative leader of the moderate Württemberg **DNVP** since 1924, making him a natural choice as a compromise candidate. This has earned him nearly universal support within the party. However, Bolz's role as a compromise candidate has hindered his ability to effect significant change, as he must tread carefully to avoid alienating the factions that helped bring him to power. Bolz will attempt to bridge the confessional divides between Catholic and Protestant conservatives, with the party still divided along the lines of their party of origin. Given Bolz's refusal to enter a Weimar Coalition in Württemberg back in 1928, viewing the **SPD** as 'incapable of governing,' we do not expect much improvement in our relationship moving forward.

cvp_party_congress.gereke.titleHtml: Günther Gereke, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.gereke.subtitleHtml: Gereke has significant influence over the agricultural and industrial establishment, being a key member of the RLB and a founder of another rural association. - National Conservative and Agrarian Wing
cvp_party_congress.gereke.bodyHtml: Günther Gereke, a lawyer and prominent politician from rural Germany, has been elected as the new leader of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. What makes him notable is that he is an agrarian politician from west of the Elbe River, a leading reformist economic theorist, and someone with close ties to General Kurt von Schleicher. He bears similarities to Treviranus, though he is far less dogmatic in his beliefs. Thanks to Gereke’s strong relationship with the **CNBLP**, a rural special-interest party, he has successfully negotiated a merger of the declining party into the **[+ z_party_name +]**, though only a few officials remain in the effectively dead party. His support for a public works program has stemmed criticism from the labor factions, and his ability to unite the key interest groups on which the German Right depends on will help secure strong nationalist backing for the party. Needless to say, this has not sat well with the **[+ z_party_name +]**’s Catholic wing, and has made cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

cvp_party_congress.goerdeler.subtitleHtml: Goerdeler is the Mayor of Leipzig, harbouring fiscally conservative views and a support of monarchism. - People's Conservatives
cvp_party_congress.goerdeler.bodyHtml: The Mayor of Leipzig Carl Goerdeler has been promoted to the leadership of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. Goerdeler is aligned more with Westarp than anything, but Treviranus is willing to give the mayor a go. Goerdeler is known for his strong support and position in Brüning's cabinet, and his fiscal conservatism has attracted support of key industrial backers. Goerdeler's role as a compromise candidate has hindered his ability to effect significant change, as he must tread carefully to avoid alienating the factions that helped bring him to power. I actually don't know what to write for this guy, his WW2 anti-Nazi plots aren't relevant at this time since he viewed Hitler as an enlightened dictator at this time. cvp_party_congress.lambach.titleHtml: Walther Lambach, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.lambach.subtitleHtml: Lambach was apart of the Christian Social wing in the former DNVP. - Christian Social Wing
cvp_party_congress.lambach.bodyHtml: Somehow, the Christian Social wing, now diluted within a much larger party, has managed to elect one of their own as the leader of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. Walther Lambach, the writer of the Lambach article years ago[? if dnvp_leader == "Lambach":, and the most recent leader of the **DNVP**?], has won the vote largely due to the unified support of the Christian labor unions, who strongly back his vision for a *Volksgemeinschaft*. More worker-friendly policies have been added to the platform, such as expanding social welfare, increasing pensions, and implementing more progressive income taxes. They've even rejected austerity as a solution to Germany's current economic crisis, instead voicing support for public works. However, this has significantly strained industrial enthusiasm for the formation of the new party, and they have begun redirecting funds toward the liberals. This, however, is not good news for us. Christian Social ideology is deeply rooted in antisemitism, racism, nationalism, and religiosity. If anything, we've noticed worsening relations with the **[+ z_party_name +]**, as they attempt to present a non-Marxist alternative to the workers.

cvp_party_congress.lejeune_jung.titleHtml: Paul Lejeune-Jung, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.lejeune_jung.subtitleHtml: Major member of the former DNVP's Catholic wing, and aligned with Westarp's group. - National Conservative Wing
cvp_party_congress.lejeune_jung.bodyHtml: Paul Lejeune-Jung, leader of the **DNVP**'s Catholic wing, and an advocate for closer ties to the Center has been elected as leader of a merger between the two. His Catholic faith has made him acceptable to former Center members, and his alignment with Westarp's faction has solidified nationalist support. However, Lejeune-Jung's role as a compromise candidate has hindered his ability to effect significant change, as he must tread carefully to avoid alienating the factions that helped bring him to power. Lejeune-Jung will attempt to bridge the confessional divides between Catholic and Protestant conservatives, with the party still divided along the lines of their party of origin. It goes without saying, this will make cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

cvp_party_congress.stegerwald.titleHtml: Adam Stegerwald, formerly of the Center, is elected, no longer an interim leader.
cvp_party_congress.stegerwald.subtitleHtml: Stegerwald is relatively moderate, and his trade union roots are good news for our cooperation. - Catholic Labor Wing
cvp_party_congress.stegerwald.bodyHtml: Somewhat surprisingly, Center leader Adam Stegerwald is elected as the chairman of its successor party. This is largely attributed to the unified support from the various Christian labor unions and backing from former Center and Catholic politicians. However, he remains largely opposed by former **DNVP** members due to his willingness to cooperate constructively with the **SPD**. It was widely expected that, with the merger of the two parties, politicians like Stegerwald would shift to the left wing of the newly created party—and this has indeed proven true. His strongest supporters, aside from the trade unions, include the now strengthened Christian Left faction, which will push for a paternalistic economic policy and greater cooperation with the socialists. Stegerwald is also a committed republican, a stance that has pushed some ardent monarchists over to the **DNF**.

cvp_party_congress.treviranus.titleHtml: Gottfried Treviranus, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.treviranus.subtitleHtml: The leader of the Volkskonservativ movement, and an advocate for democratic principles. - People's Conservatives and Catholic Right Wing
cvp_party_congress.treviranus.bodyHtml: Gottfried Treviranus[? if dnvp_leader == "Treviranus":, the most recent leader of the **DNVP**?], leader of the thriving People's Conservative movement, is seen as the ideal candidate for the first chairman of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. His nationalist origin, strong ties to key figures like Westarp on the right, and his careful cultivation of relations with the Catholics have earned him broad support for his leadership. With his control of the colossally sized **[+ z_party_name +]**, Treviranus has finally been able to mold it into the Tory Democratic party he has long envisioned. His extensive connections with Schleicher, German industry[? if president == "Hindenburg":, President Hindenburg?], and the bourgeois elite are expected to greatly aid his leadership ambitions. Despite his democratic leanings, the [+ z_party_name +] remains firmly opposed to Marxism, effectively ruling out any prospects of coalition with us.

cvp_party_congress.vorbeck.titleHtml: War Hero Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.vorbeck.subtitleHtml: Lettow-Vorbeck is reluctant to lead, but perhaps his war hero status can serve as a unifying force? - National Conservative Wing
cvp_party_congress.vorbeck.bodyHtml: Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck is a war hero renowned for his undefeated record and his successful guerrilla campaign in German East Africa, with victories that rival those of Hindenburg. Despite multiple attempts to involve him in German politics, he has remained largely inactive, serving as a member of the Reichstag elected under the **DNVP**. However, the [? if vorbeck_deadlock: unending deadlock at the congress?][? if not vorbeck_deadlock and vorbeck_decline: drastic decline in the moderate right's vote share?][? if not vorbeck_deadlock and not vorbeck_decline and vorbeck_presidential: desire to utilize his character for a potential future election run?] has led to a growing number of factions rallying around his candidacy. The widespread popular support for him draws strong parallels to Hindenburg's own presidential candidacy declaration in 1925. Reluctantly, Lettow-Vorbeck has accepted the **[+ z_party_name +]**'s nomination as their next leader. However, he has little interest in managing the party’s internal affairs and has quietly delegated this responsibility to fellow conservatives like Westarp. Nonetheless, he remains the public face of the **[+ z_party_name +]** as chairman. The most crucial aspect of his election is his ability to inspire the German people to rally behind a Great War war hero once again, someone who embodies the image of stability and unity. Time will tell how long this popularity will last. It goes without saying, his election will make cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

cvp_party_congress.westarp.titleHtml: Kuno von Westarp, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
cvp_party_congress.westarp.subtitleHtml: A long-time DNVP stalwart, having prevented Hugenberg's takeover of the party in the past. - National Conservative Wing
cvp_party_congress.westarp.bodyHtml: A key figure of the German Right since the Republic's inception, Kuno von Westarp has ascended to the leadership role of the colossal Christian People's Party—certainly a significant step up. His election was primarily driven by the unified support of the entire former nationalist faction within the party. Westarp is highly experienced in managing internal dissent and is careful not to lean too heavily into any one particular wing of the party, aiming to avoid fracturing the organization. While the party program remains largely unchanged, there has been a noticeable increase in antisemitic and pro-monarchist rhetoric, as Westarp seeks to preserve the character of the now-defunct **DNVP** within this new entity. It goes without saying, Westarp's leadership will make cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

ddp_alliance.subtitleHtml: Should we offer to help them?
ddp_alliance.bodyHtml: = The **[+ ddp_name +]**'s Proposal Due to the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s declining electoral performance, threatening to wipe out their Reichstag delegation come next election, many within their party like the retired Koch-Weser have been lobbying for a technical list connection with the **SPD**. Despite their electoral standing, many within their business wing like Theodor Heuss argue that allying with the socialists would be detrimental to their stance of economic freedom, while many on their left wing such as Ernst Lemmer argue it's a necessity in order to save their party and democracy. We can either offer to help the dying party out, increasing their parliamentary presence, or leave them on their own.

ddp_dietrich_explode.bodyHtml: = Hermann Dietrich resigns! [? if ddp_ideology != "Left": Hermann Dietrich has failed to meet the expectations of many within the party, with only the local organizations in Hamburg, Baden, and Württemberg showing any real signs of activity. Theodor Heuss has been particularly eager to find a replacement for Dietrich, but so far, no one has been willing to take on the leadership of this struggling party. Both Hermann Höpker-Aschoff, the party’s former leader in Prussia, and his successor have declined the role. ?][? if ddp_ideology == "Left": Since Dietrich's election to the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s leadership, the party has shifted to the left, making him—the candidate of the business wing—increasingly unpopular within the party. As a result, a vote of no confidence has been put forth, aiming to replace him with a more left-wing and energetic leader. ?] [? if ddp_ideology != "Left": The only viable option left would be Heuss himself, but he remains reluctant, preferring to focus on his family. With no prominent politician willing to take leadership, Dietrich remains as acting chairman until they do. ?][? if ddp_ideology == "Left": If the vote succeeds, which seems likely, Lemmer has shown reluctance about running for leadership again and may choose to endorse someone else for the position. ?]

ddp_dietrich_explode.heuss.subtitleHtml: He finally has the motivation to step up, and be the change he wants to see in the world.
ddp_dietrich_explode.heuss.bodyHtml: Theodor Heuss a journalist turned politician and a rising star has been elected as the chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]**. Although affiliated with the business wing of the party, his determined and genuine support for liberal democracy has earned him support from the party's left wing. Heuss's victory strengthens the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s cooperation with us, as he has urged his party members that it is crucial to save German democracy. A visible revival in party activities has already been seen, but funding still remains a major obstacle. Perhaps the **[+ ddp_name +]** isn't moribund after all?

ddp_dietrich_explode.luders.subtitleHtml: The most active woman within the **[+ ddp_name +]**, and strongly internationalist. Associated with the party's left wing.
ddp_dietrich_explode.luders.bodyHtml: Marie-Elisabeth Lüders, the second most important woman in the **[+ ddp_name +]**, and easily the most active advocate for the rights and wellbeing of women, children, and the workers of Germany, is elected to the leadership of the **[+ ddp_name +]**. This victory comes with the backing of Ernst Lemmer and his liberal trade unions, who have gained significant influence in recent months. Our relationship with the **[+ ddp_name +]** has greatly improved compared to how it was under Dietrich. Lüders is a strong internationalist and has previously advocated for Pan-European cooperation, which will benefit us in future negotiations. She was also one of the strongest opponents of the merger with the Young German Order, arguing against their antisemitism. However, it remains to be seen whether she will gain more votes than she loses due to her feminism, as many refuse to support her purely out of misogyny.

ddp_dietrich_explode.maier.subtitleHtml: A youthful and energetic rising star, free from helplessness, defeatism, and rigid dogma.
ddp_dietrich_explode.maier.bodyHtml: Reinhold Maier, a major figure in Württemberg politics and a rising star in the dying party, has been elected chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]**. Youthful and energetic, he is not bound by traditional liberal principles like many veteran members of the **[+ ddp_name +]**, making him a strong choice for a party plagued by defeatism and internal strife. For us, however, his position within the business wing means we have yet to see significant improvements in cooperation compared to Dietrich’s tenure. Anyhow, a visible revival in party activities is already underway, though funding remains a persistent obstacle. Perhaps the **[+ ddp_name +]** isn't moribund after all?

ddp_dietrich_explode.stolper.subtitleHtml: Creator of the famed Stolper Program, and a Jew.
ddp_dietrich_explode.stolper.bodyHtml: Gustav Stolper, a German-Austrian economist and the son of Jewish immigrants from Poland, has been elected chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]**, reinforcing a stereotype the party has long struggled to dispel. Despite this, Stolper—renowned for the economic program bearing his name—could be exactly what the **[+ ddp_name +]** needs to revitalize its middle-class support. Relations have improved compared to Dietrich’s tenure, as Stolper's strained ties with parties to the right of the **[+ ddp_name +]**—due to anti-Semitism—have made cooperation with us easier. Meanwhile, a visible revival in party activities is already underway, though funding remains a persistent obstacle. Perhaps the **[+ ddp_name +]** isn’t moribund after all?

ddp_fail.bodyHtml: As always, the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s left wing have rejected the plans to create a united Liberal People's Party. It seems that the infighting that plagues the **[+ ddp_name +]** remains alive and well. This outcome has greatly demoralized the German middle and has forced the disbandment of the Liberal Association.

ddp_party_congress.subtitleHtml: The [+ ddp_name +] decides their fate...
ddp_party_congress.bodyHtml: = **[+ ddp_name +]** Party Congress Koch-Weser, the long-time leader of the **[+ ddp_name +]**, has finally resigned. The internal opposition, especially following the Young German Order debacle, has reached a level that forced his retirement, though the demoralizing impact of being chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]** out of all parties have also contributed significantly. This year’s **[+ ddp_name +]** party congress is officially convened to elect a new leader and to determine the party's policies amid the worsening economic depression that threatens the survival of the bourgeois middle. The candidates to succeed Koch-Weser so far include Hermann Dietrich, representing the business wing; Theodor Heuss, a committed supporter of liberal democracy; and Ernst Lemmer, the leader of the liberal trade unions and the party's left wing.

ddp_party_congress_0.subtitleHtml: The German Democratic Party is becoming the German State Party.
ddp_party_congress_0.bodyHtml: = **DDP** Reformation The **DDP** is a fascinating party, plagued by infighting since the republic's foundation and struggling to define its platform in a failed attempt to appeal to voters from all demographics.[? if stolper_program_adopted: Recently, however, the party seems to have turned a new page, rallying around a renewed focus on middle-class interests. ?][? if not stolper_program_adopted: A recent attempt to shift focus toward the middle class has been quietly buried due to internal dissent, perhaps factionalism and personal rivalries may be a permanent feature of this party. ?] Pessimism is a widespread feeling within the party, leading to mounting pressure on leader Koch-Weser to do "something". After weeks of secret negotiations, the **DDP** is announcing the result of a proposed merger of the **DDP** and **VNR**, a party admired by senior party officials for its "dynamism". [? if not vnr_cool: However, the **VNR**'s weak electoral performance has led many to question whether a merger is worthwhile. ?]

ddp_party_congress_0.dstp_formed.bodyHtml: This has come as a complete shock to those inside and outside the party, for the **DDP** to merge with the political wing of a mildly anti-Semitic paramilitary group "Young German Order". Ongoing negotiations to unite the liberal and bourgeois parties has been considerably damaged, due to the **DDP**'s attempts to promote a left-wing split from the **DVP**. In this agreement, the **DDP** has promised a "extension of the party to the right", which can only spell trouble for our closest bourgeois ally. Despite this, the formation of the **DStP** wasn't a simple left-right divide within the party, the Social Republican Circle and labor leader Ernst Lemmer helps prevent a major split among the left. However, cracks are already beginning to show within this arrangement, it is only a matter of time before this experiment falls apart.

ddp_party_congress_0.status_quo.bodyHtml: As expected, a merger between a moderately anti-Semitic organization and a party seen as the party for the Jews has failed, with the Young German Order leader Artur Mahraun leaving negotiations citing irreconcilable differences. [? if not vnr_cool and not saxony_election_1930_seen: However, the main factor contributing to this is that, the **VNR** has never been tested electorally. ?][? if not vnr_cool and saxony_election_1930_seen: However, the main concern is that the **VNR** failed to win any seats in the only election they participated in, the Saxon Landtag elections. ?] However, internal opposition to Koch-Weser has reached a boiling point. Forces within the party are now pushing for his retirement due to his failure to revive the party and for jeopardizing the negotiations for a united liberal party.

ddp_party_congress_dstp.subtitleHtml: The conflict between the Young Germans and **Democrats** has reached a climax...
ddp_party_congress_dstp.bodyHtml: = Discontent in the **DStP** Since the formation of the **DStP** over the last few months, tensions between the old-line democrats and those who joined from the **VNR** have escalated significantly. It seems the consequences of merging a mildly anti-Semitic paramilitary group with a left-liberal party traditionally associated with the Jews have finally caught up to them. [? if change_ddp_votes < 0 and dstp_election: The electoral defeat suffered by the **DStP** in the most recent elections has further fueled internal discontent, with both sides blaming each other for the loss.?][? if not dstp_election: Despite this glaring contradiction, the new party has yet to test its worth in a national election, and skeptics on both sides have kept their criticisms subdued for the time being. ?] [? if dstp_election or next_election_time - time < 6: Among embittered democrats, it appears that nearly half of the voters in the Order cast their ballots for the **NSDAP** instead of the party they helped establish, with electoral gains only being reported in districts where their own candidate is at the top of the ballot.?] According to the agreement on which the founding of the **DStP** was based, Koch-Weser was to serve as the new party’s parliamentary leader, and Mahraun as the head of its national organization. However, this arrangement is blocked by a group of old-line democrats who succeeded in preventing Koch-Weser’s election as the head of the Reichstag delegation. Relations between the two groups further soured when Mahraun, acting as the "Reichsführer" of the **DStP**, attempted to alter the previously agreed organizational structure. This dispute over the separation of powers has led to open attacks between the opposing sides, with the old-line democrats seeking to sideline Artur Mahraun's Young German Order, and Mahraun refusing to relinquish his position as "Reichsführer."

ddp_party_congress_dstp.dstp_collapse.bodyHtml: Negotiations between Mahraun and the democrats have finally collapsed; the experiment has finally fallen apart. The members from Mahraun's **VNR** have split[? if dstp_election:, taking their Reichstag seats with them?]. Responsibility for the break is argued on both sides, with the old-line democrats Mahraun's refusal to compromise and the Order blaming purposeful obstruction. [? if dstp_election: In terms of consequences, the defection of the **VNR**-affiliated Reichstag delegates has severely diminished their parliamentary influence. [? if ddp_r < 3.6: So much so that the **DStP** is now too small to form a parliamentary faction and must negotiate with another party, which is challenging given the debacle that occurred months ago.?]?] An air of pessimism and despair has settled over the **DStP**, especially impacting Koch-Weser, who, deeply demoralized by the collapse of the **State Party**, has ultimately decided to retire from politics altogether. Overall, this entire debacle has essentially resulted in the **DStP** becoming the **DDP** with a new name, albeit with a more nationalistic and statist platform.

ddp_party_congress_dstp.dstp_maintained.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the contradiction that is the **DStP** continues to live on. After intense negotiations between the democrats in favor of the merger, like Koch-Weser, and the dissenting old-line democrats, they agree to elevate Koch-Weser to the chairman of the Reichstag faction. However, Mahraun's control over the party's national organization proved to be a much trickier problem, as Mahraun’s Order remained inflexible when it came to compromise. The deadlock is finally resolved when Mahraun agrees to cede some of his Reichsführer powers to the executive committee in exchange for a larger share of **VNR**-affiliated delegates at next month's party congress. It seems this experiment will persist, with the **DStP** adopting a more nationalistic and statist identity compared to the old **DDP**. Only time will tell how the party will fare against the rise of the **NSDAP**.

ddp_party_congress.deadlock.bodyHtml: The vote has been deadlocked, with no candidate ahead by enough to constitute a majority. You, the player, now has free will to choose a compromise candidate. Spend it wisely. Actually, you don't. Choose Heuss right now.

ddp_party_congress.dietrich.bodyHtml: Hermann Dietrich has, as expected, won the election to become chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]**, receiving support from the newly dominant business wing of the party, as well as from the old-line democrats who joined him in opposing the merger with the **VNR**. [? if chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government: Dietrich is known for formulating Brüning's emergency decrees during his tenure as Finance Minister, justifying them as the bitter medicine the country must endure on its road to recovery. ?][? if not (chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government) and agriculture_minister_party != "SPD": Dietrich is known for his fiscal conservatism and advocacy for rural Germany during his tenure as Minister of Agriculture. ?] However, his leadership has been quite uninspiring, to say the least—a sentiment shared by many within the party, though no one seems willing to challenge him. [? if agriculture_minister_party == ddp_name or economic_minister_party == ddp_name: The responsibilities of his ministry prevent him from being involved in the day-to-day running of his party, which has now been delegated to a group of his associates in the business wing, but this is unlikely to change much in terms of policy. ?]

params.source: achievement_calculation

ddp_party_congress.heuss.bodyHtml: Theodor Heuss a journalist turned politician and a rising star has been elected as the chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]**. Although affiliated with the business wing of the party, his determined and genuine support for liberal democracy has earned him support from the party's left wing. Heuss's victory strengthens the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s cooperation with us, as he has urged his party members that it is crucial to save German democracy. Despite his leanings toward the right, he has refrained from ousting the far-left elements of the party or shifting its platform drastically.

ddp_party_congress.lemmer.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, Ernst Lemmer has managed to rally a majority of the party to elect him as the chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]**. He is primarily supported by the 'Social Republican Wing,' the Young Democrats, pacifists, radical democrats, and the labor wing of the party. However, his election would not have been possible without the backing of those who worked alongside him in the failed attempt to unite with the **VNR** months earlier. Now, a trade unionist leads a liberal middle-class party—what a time we live in. Lemmer's victory significantly empowers the Social Republicans and left-wing elements within the **[+ ddp_name +]**, even drawing his former colleague Anton Erkelenz back into politics. We can expect his **[+ ddp_name +]** to adopt a 'social capitalist' platform,[? if stolper_program_adopted: to replace the Stolper program,?] aiming to include workers in the *Volksgemeinschaft*.

ddp_success.bodyHtml: Perhaps surprisingly, the **[+ ddp_name +]** has followed the **DVP**'s decision and affirmed their support for a united Liberal People's Party. It seems that the leftists within the **[+ ddp_name +]** have finally lost their battle to maintain the position of a 'Social and Republican party in the Weimar party system. However, the leftists within the **[+ ddp_name +]** will wield little influence in the wider party, which will consist of twice as many **DVP** members as **[+ ddp_name +]** members.

dealing_with_toleration.bodyHtml:
#subtitle: Despite not being in government, we can still provide support.
= Dealing with Toleration
We are currently acting as external support to the government of Chancellor [+ chancellor +]. How should we use our position?

choices.labelHtml: Stay the course, for stability's sake.

dealing_with_toleration_cvp.bodyHtml: #subtitle: Despite not being in government, we can still provide support. = Dealing with Toleration We are currently providing external support to the government of Chancellor [+ chancellor +], but our influence has been severely weakened due to the formation of the **[+ z_party_name +]** by former **DNVP** members. Furthermore, the **[+ z_party_name +]** is actively trying to distance itself from our support. How should we use our position?

choices.labelHtml: Stay the course, for stability's sake.

dealing_with_toleration_cvp.break_tolera.titleHtml: End the toleration agreement with a vote of no confidence!
dealing_with_toleration_cvp.break_tolera.bodyHtml: Are we sure about this? A vote of no confidence would trigger new elections, and potentially an increased vote-share for the extremist parties. [? if in_weimar_coalition_prussia or in_grand_coalition_prussia or in_popular_front_prussia: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] also threatens a no-confidence vote against us in Prussia, pressuring us to stay the course.?]

choices.labelHtml: No, we should stay the course.

dealing_with_toleration_cvp.center_right.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has called a retaliatory no confidence vote in Prussia, replacing our government with a center-right coalition composed of all parties to our right, except for the **DNF** and **NSDAP**. While this is a setback, it is not the worst possible outcome, as new elections could have led to significant gains for extremist parties. [? if z_leader != "Stegerwald": Adam Stegerwald?][? if z_leader == "Stegerwald": Heinrich Brüning?] of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia.

dealing_with_toleration_cvp.new_prussia_.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has called a retaliatory vote in Prussia, forcing the dissolution of the Landtag for new elections. New Prussian elections have been set for [+ next_election_month_prussia : month +] [+ next_election_year_prussia +]. A double dissolution has shaken the people's faith in democracy, with the Nazis exploiting the instability to claim that democracy is unworkable, and that Germany needs a strong leader.

dealing_with_toleration_cvp.urge_failure.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, the historically strict party discipline of the Center Party has carried over to its successor, which has successfully rallied the party against the bill. However, this is sure to spark discontent within the party, as it struggles to maintain its diverse coalition while also attempting to implement its fiscal reform policy.

dealing_with_toleration_cvp.urge_success.bodyHtml: The motion passes! Despite the historically strict party discipline within the former Center, the diverse base of the party has weakened the leadership’s control over its parliamentary delegation. However, this has left the incumbent cabinet vulnerable to strong attacks from the far-right, as it further cements their association with the socialists in the eyes of their industrial backers. [? if bruning_austerity_limited == 1: We have successfully prevented Brüning from decreasing taxes on high earners, thus lessening the burden of compensatory tax increases on the lower strata. ?][? if bruning_austerity_limited == 2: We have successfully pressured Brüning into appeasing us by reinstating the 40-hour workweek, although wages remain suboptimal. ?][? if bruning_austerity_limited >= 3: We have successfully pressured Brüning into reversing some salary cuts for civil servants. ?]

death_of_hindenburg_normal.subtitleHtml: The Great War hero and one-time president has died...
death_of_hindenburg_normal.bodyHtml: = The Death of Hindenburg Paul von Hindenburg has passed away at age 86. The nation engages in an outpouring of grief for its war hero and former president. Even for committed socialists and republicans, this is a bittersweet moment. Even though he was a manifestation of Prussian militarism and monarchism, he still led the nation through difficult times, without destroying democracy. It could always have been worse. With the passing of Hindenburg, it seems as if an era of history is closing. The worst years of crisis are over, and Nazism's days are numbered. Perhaps Germany will finally enter into a new era of genuine peace...

death_of_hindenburg_president.bodyHtml: = The Death of Hindenburg President Paul von Hindenburg has passed away at age 86. An era of history is closing, and the future remains to be seen. The nation engages in an outpouring of grief for its war hero and president, with even some sympathy among committed republicans and socialists. After all, Hindenburg steered the republic through some of its most challenging times, without giving in to extremists on the far right. Perhaps he is one reason democracy remains alive. New presidential elections are to be held as soon as possible. The German political landscape is wide open, with contenders from all over the political space. In the meantime, Supreme Court chief justice [? if judicial_reform < 4 : Erwin Bumke ?][? if judicial_reform >= 4 : Hermann Großmann ?] serves as the acting president. # Hermann Großmann is the supreme court chief justice in judicial reform.

choices.labelHtml: Who are the candidates so far?

death_of_hindenburg_president_rubicon.bodyHtml: = The Death of Hindenburg President Paul von Hindenburg has passed away at age 86. An era of history is closing, and the future remains to be seen. The nation erupts in grief over the death of its war hero and president—though this mourning is confined largely to the political right. With Schleicher not expected to live much longer, the era of Germany's two strongmen nears its end. Now, the country must determine who will author the next chapter of the Weimar Republic—if it will still be called that. New presidential elections are to be held as soon as possible. The **DNEF** is expected to field a single candidate, and their victory would guarantee a total consolidation of power for the foreseeable future—an outcome that must be prevented at all costs. In the meantime, Supreme Court chief justice [? if judicial_reform < 4 : Erwin Bumke ?][? if judicial_reform >= 4 : Hermann Großmann ?] serves as the acting president.

death_of_hindenburg_president_rubicon.ad.bodyHtml: Konrad Adenauer has won the presidency! With a committed republican at the helm of Germany, the threat to the Republic has, for the most part, subsided.

choices.labelHtml: Support Konrad Adenauer of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].
Support Theodor Heuss of the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?].

death_of_hindenburg_president_rubicon.ca.bodyHtml: The **DNEF** has nominated Kurt von Hammerstein-Equord—a Reichswehr general, long-time friend of Schleicher, and the current Chief of the Army. He considers himself a servant of the state rather than of any political party, and served as Schleicher’s liaison to the trade unions in recent months. He has also been responsible for overseeing the expansion of the Reichswehr during this time. Little else is known about his ideological convictions; like Schleicher, he is flexible.

death_of_hindenburg_president_rubicon.ca.titleHtml: The **Communists**? The Weimar Parties? Who will they support?
death_of_hindenburg_president_rubicon.ca.bodyHtml: With the **Communists** having been heavily suppressed during Schleicher’s tenure, they are no longer a significant political force. [? if kpd_banned: They are even banned outright, preventing them from endorsing their own candidate. With boycotting rendered pointless, they have no choice but to support whoever we put forward. ?][? if not kpd_banned: Grateful for our role in sparing them from Schleicher’s crackdown months ago, they are fully backing whoever we choose to nominate. ?] [? if z_candidate == "Adenauer": The Center is not fully convinced to back [+ dnef_candidate +] and has chosen to run its own candidate: Konrad Adenauer. The Mayor of Cologne since the Republic's inception, and a member of the Prussian legislature, he's an advocate for the Center Party "leaving the tower" to broaden its appeal among Protestants, Adenauer was first proposed by Stegerwald himself. Though situated on the right wing of his party, he remains firmly committed to the Weimar Republic and opposes Schleicher’s threats against it. ?] [? if heuss_run: The liberals are running Theodor Heuss—a journalist and vocal supporter of the Weimar Republic, and a staunch anti-Schleicherist within his own party. This stance has put him at odds with more pro-Schleicher elements in the German middle class. While unlikely to secure significant support, Heuss has positioned himself as a "Weimar" unity candidate in opposition to [+ dnef_candidate +]. ?][? if not heuss_run and ddp_candidate == z_candidate and z_candidate != dnef_candidate: The liberals, mired in electoral ruin, lack the resources or energy to field a candidate of their own. Instead, they have thrown their support behind [+ z_candidate +] as the bourgeois alternative to Schleicher. However, their backing is far from solid—pro-Schleicher elements remain rogue, as his message of national solidarity continues to resonate with the historically nationalist German liberal movement. ?][? if not heuss_run and ddp_candidate == dnef_candidate: The liberals, mired in electoral ruin, lack the resources or energy to field a candidate of their own. They have thrown their support behind [+ dnef_candidate +], heavily influenced by pro-Schleicher elements and propaganda that has resonated especially strongly with their rank-and-file. Many within the party now see it as their national duty to support Schleicher and his successor, believing this to be the only path toward restoring Germany’s great power status abroad and securing concessions at home. ?]

The nationalists are unified in their support for [+ dnef_candidate +], joined by the various splinter factions and the minor bourgeois parties. Although Hugenberg is—somehow—still contemplating a presidential run, a strongly worded threat has convinced him to remain silent.

With Hitler gone from the political scene, the Nazis will be fielding Hermann Göring as their candidate. The **DSU** will be running [? if dsu_candidate == "Strasser": their party leader, Otto Strasser, as a separate candidate. ?][? if dsu_candidate == "Frick": Wilhelm Frick as a separate candidate. ?] [? if nvf_candidate == dnef_candidate: The remnants of the **NVF** will be backing [+ dnef_candidate +], as they remain within the **DNEF** umbrella. ?][? if nvf_candidate != dnef_candidate: The remnants of the **NVF** will be boycotting the election entirely—continuing their deluded course of waiting for the "right moment" to spark an armed rebellion. ?] With the Nazis movement remaining divided, none of their candidates have any remote chance to winning.

As for the **SPD**, we could support a joint Weimar Coalition candidate or run our own. The viability of a united front, however, depends entirely on our relations with former coalition partners—and whether they’ve fallen under Schleicher’s influence. Otto Braun is tired. He ran and failed in the previous two presidential elections, and no longer wishes to run. His wife is ill enough that he wishes to stay by her side. More importantly, he is deeply pessimistic about the situation we now face. Kurt Schumacher is an ambitious rising star in the party, and would be all too willing to run. He was a hero in the Great War, but his relatively young age might be relevant.

[? if seldte_run_1934: The **DNVP** will nominate Franz Seldte, leader of the **Stahlhelm** paramilitary group. He will be endorsed by many of Hindenburg's most right-wing supporters. He will be endorsed by many of Hindenburg's most right-wing supporters. They are working more closely with the Nazis than before, and in the second round, the far-right parties are expected to consolidate into a single anti-republican front. ?][? if cvp_formed: The **[+ z_party_name +]** has come together in full support of nominating General Lettow-Vorbeck, a war hero who was once a member of the **DNVP**. Despite his initial reluctance, the popular general has agreed to their nomination, signaling his intent to uphold the legacy of Hindenburg. ?] [? if not seldte_run_1934: Alfred Hugenberg is dissatisfied with endorsing [+ reactionary_candidate_1934 +] and prefers to run himself. However, his finances have been crippled by having solely financed the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?] throughout the economic depression, which has also eroded the income from his media empire. [? if hugenberg_run_1934: Despite this, he has scraped together what remains of his personal fortune to launch a presidential campaign, hoping to leverage a second-round endorsement for concessions from [+ reactionary_candidate_1934 +]. ?][? if not hugenberg_run_1934: In an effort to preserve both his party’s solvency and what remains of his wealth, he has refrained from running or endorsing anyone—much to the frustration of his colleagues. ?] ?] [? if kpd_leader = "Conciliators" : Given the failure of Thälmann's previous runs for president, and his declining stature in the party, the **KPD** will be running Willi Münzenberg, a controversial figure sometimes called the "Red millionaire". He is a media magnate who leads a number of **Communist** front organizations. ?] [? if kpd_leader != "Conciliators" : This will be Ernst Thälmann's third run for president as leader of the **KPD**. Despite his previous electoral defeats, he retains the loyalty of the party as well as Stalin's Soviet Union. ?] [? if not cvp_formed: Many republicans of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?], and **SPD** float the idea of running Hugo Eckener, a nationally renowed Zeppelin captain, as a unity candidate. While he has some nationalistic views, he is also ardently opposed to Nazism. ?] [? if not cvp_formed: Barring that, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] are planning to run separate candidates in the first round if the **SPD** runs its own candidate. [? if adenauer_run_1934: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is considering nominating Konrad Adenauer, mayor of Köln and member of the Prussian state legislature. He calls for an alliance of conservative Christian democrats that encompasses both Catholics and Protestants.?][? if bruning_run_1934: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is considering nominating Heinrich Brüning, their former Chancellor, known for his popular and successful public works program. Widely credited with reviving Germany’s economy, he is expected to receive broad support from the bourgeois parties that participated in his government should he choose to run. ?]?] [? if ddp_candidate == "Gessler": The [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] might nominate Otto Gessler, former defense minister, who has crossover appeal to conservatives[? if dvp_exist and not lvp_formed: in the **DVP**?] and other parties who dislike the **DNVP**-**NSDAP** front. ?][? if ddp_candidate == "Heuss": The [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] might nominate Theodor Heuss, a prominent left-liberal journalist, who presents a strong defense of the Weimar Republic and its democratic institutions. He aims to be the candidate for the young generation, and bourgeois republicans. ?] As for the **SPD**, we could support a joint [? if not cvp_formed: Weimar?][? if cvp_formed: Social-[? if not lvp_formed: Liberal?][? if lvp_formed: Liberal?] ?] Coalition candidate or run our own. [? if braun_campaign : Otto Braun is tired. He ran and failed in the previous two presidential elections, and no longer wishes to run. His wife is ill enough that he wishes to stay by her side. ?][? if braun_campaign = 0 and not spd_prussia: Otto Braun is tired. After being deposed in Prussia, he has largely retired from politics, and is devoting his time to caring for his dying wife. ?][? if braun_campaign = 0 and spd_prussia : Otto Braun is tired. He does not wish to run, but he is willing to be convinced that he is needed at this moment. His wife is terminally ill, and he does not want more responsibilities. ?] Kurt Schumacher is an ambitious rising star in the party, and would be all too willing to run. He was a hero in the Great War, but his relatively young age might be relevant. [? if womens_rights >= 6 and family_law >= 2 and womens_work >= 2 and welfare > 0: Or, perhaps it is time for a woman to become president. Germany and the **SPD** have been leading on women's rights for years, and it is only fitting that we should elect the world's first female president. Perhaps Marie Juchacz could be seen as the "mother of the nation" for her work in social welfare. However, her divorce 28 years ago might make it difficult for the Catholics to support her. ?] [? if presidential_powers >= 1 and pro_republic >= 60 and pacifism >= 3: Since Germany has been largely democratized and presidential powers reduced, we can also support another non-traditional political figure, someone from the cultural, scientific, or literary spheres. They will perhaps be the symbol of a new Germany that has moved beyond its past. ?]

death_of_hindenburg_president.hergt_vict.bodyHtml: With Hergt’s victory—and without having relied on Nazi support—he is under no obligation to appoint [+ nsdap_candidate +] as chancellor. A committed monarchist, Hergt is expected to pursue steps toward restoring the Hohenzollerns. Unlike Hindenburg, he is far more openly partisan and intends to exclude the **SPD** from government throughout his seven-year term.

With Hergt’s victory—secured with the support of the Nazis—the balance of power shifts to them under the terms of their deal. However, Hergt remains deeply reluctant to appoint Adolf Hitler as chancellor[? if not hitler_citizen or hitler_deported:—which would require granting him German citizenship?]. Instead, he names **Stahlhelm** leader Franz Seldte as a compromise candidate between the two parties. Seldte will govern through presidential decree, leading a far-right cabinet.

death_of_hindenburg_president.hitler_con.bodyHtml: We have passed a constitutional amendment preventing the president from having the power to arbitrarily dismiss a government. To undo this, the far right has called a plebiscite on a new constitutional amendment. Stormtroopers are in the streets, "convincing" voters to support their proposal. Germany is nearing civil war.

choices.labelHtml: We will fight the fascists in the streets!
We can only defeat the fascists through democratic means!

Mann is willing to accept the nomination for president.

death_of_hindenburg_president.ossietzky_.bodyHtml: Carl von Ossietzky is a left-wing journalist who is the publisher of the Weltbühne, a news magazine. He is most known for exposing the secret German rearmament program in 1929, which brought him international renown. In the 1932 presidential election, he endorsed the **Communist** Thälmann. Ossietzky is extremely reluctant to become a politician, and has been an iconoclastic figure his entire life, criticizing the **SPD** as being part of the establishment. It is with a sense of irony that he accepts our nomination.

death_of_stresemann.bodyHtml: = The Death of Gustav Stresemann Gustav Stresemann, leader of the **DVP** and longtime foreign minister, has died at the tragically young age of 51. He was the primary force driving his party to support democracy; without him, the democratic forces in the Republic will be so much weaker. A hole has been left within the liberal movement at the worse possible time, and it is likely that the industrial wing of the party will complete their takeover and subsequently end cooperation with us. [? if dvp_leader == "Scholz": Ernst Scholz, his arch enemy on the right wing has succeeded him as leader of the **DVP**, and leadership election will be conducted in two months.?][? if dvp_leader == "Curtius": Julius Curtius, his successor in foreign affairs, and ally in the left wing of the party, has succeeded him as leader of the **DVP**, and leadership election will be conducted in two months.?]

defeat.bodyHtml: = Total Defeat Our forces are no match for those of the reactionaries. Reichsbanner fighters are quickly overpowered by the forces of the Stahlhelm, **SA**, and Reichswehr. Many are killed before the rest surrender. Our remaining leaders either flee the country or face execution, as the reactionaries and Nazis soon turn on each other. [? if papen_win: Following our defeat, the better-equipped Reichswehr and **Stahlhelm** turn against the weakening **SA**, defeating them after a brutal struggle. [+ nsdap_leader +] commits suicide, and many high-ranking **NSDAP** leaders are imprisoned. Papen has won—though with 90% of the country against him. ?][? if nsdap_win: Following our defeat, the fanatical **SA** overwhelms the smaller but well equipped Reichswehr, and uses defections of pro-Nazi elements in the **Stahlhelm** to their advantage. Eventually, Papen, hated by 90% of the German people, is captured and executed along with President Hindenburg. Ernst Röhm and the **SA** now have significant influence in the new Germany, vowing to go on a campaign of **unspeakable** **horror** against Jews, and endless wars of violent expansion that will ruin all of Europe. ?] Our resistance will be recorded in the history books, and in the future, our names will be honored. But for now, all is lost.

demographics.bodyHtml: **Demographic Groups** **Working Class**: The urban working class - blue-collar workers in factories, workshops, mines, and the like. Most are socialists, supporting either the **SPD** or **KPD**. They make up 40-50% of the population. **Old Mittelstand**: The old middle class consists of independent artisans, shopkeepers, and small-time businesspeople. They tend to be conservative and are the strongest base for the far-right. 10-15% of the population. **New Mittelstand**: The new middle class consists of white-collar workers and government employees. This is the base of liberalism. 10-15% of the population. **Rural**: Small and large farmers and independent rural workers. Protestant farmers usually supports the [? if not cvp_formed: **DNVP**?][? if cvp_formed: **[+ z_party_name +]**?]. [? if rural_nsdap_normalized >= 25: However the Nazis have gained a strong appeal among them?]. 20-30% of the population. **Catholics** are the largest religious minority, at about 30% of the population. dieckmann.subtitleHtml: Dieckmann is a member of the Saxon Landtag and a former member of the **DVP**, being a committed follower of Stresemann.
dieckmann.bodyHtml: (If you can find an image of him taken around this period of time, please message the modman.) Johannes Dieckmann, a relatively minor figure who only recently became president of the **LVP**'s parliamentary group in the Saxon Landtag, has been elected party chairman. A longtime associate of Stresemann and a member of the **DVP**'s left wing, Dieckmann even chaired a revolutionary soldiers' council in 1918. His youth and low profile have left him with few enemies—unlike Curtius—making him a palatable compromise. While he represents an improvement over Luther’s policies, it is a slight one.

dingeldey.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey was a member of the former **DVP**, and commonly associated with the industrial-right of the party.
dingeldey.bodyHtml: Eduard Dingeldey, previously part of the movement for bourgeois unity, has now been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Dingeldey is backed by the industrial forces on the right of the party, alongside former **DVP** members. He appears to be focused on fostering closer cooperation with the array of parties between the **LVP** and the **DNVP**. However, Dingeldey has thus far proven to be an ineffectual leader, often capitulating to the right wing of the **LVP**. Recently, we’ve observed a deterioration in relations with his party, alongside a noticeable rightward shift in the **LVP**'s internal politics.

dingeldey_explode.titleHtml: Dingeldey loses the vote of no confidence!
dingeldey_explode.bodyHtml: At a divisive party congress, prominent figures from the party’s left wing—such as Thiel, Glatzel, and Curtius—force a vote on Dingeldey’s leadership of the **DVP**. Dingeldey is ousted, replaced by zu Dohna, prompting the industrialist faction to withdraw its support and shift its funds to the right. However, the **DVP**’s move to distance itself from its former industrial backers—and its renewed campaign to revive Stresemann’s legacy—has done much to restore some of its lost electoral strength. Our relationship with the **DVP** has improved. Still, Dingeldey’s tenure radicalized the party toward the right, and the damage cannot be undone overnight.

dnef_collapse_3.titleHtml: Kuno von Westarp -[? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": Former?] **DNVP**
dnef_collapse_3.subtitleHtml: Hindenburg's preferred choice once again, and [? if dnvp_leader != "Westarp":former?] **DNVP** party leader.
dnef_collapse_3.bodyHtml: Without a clear governing majority, [+ old_chancellor +] loses the little confidence that [+ president +] had given him, which was no longer much after the collapse of the **DNEF** a few weeks ago. Westarp, despite being once again begged by an older and increasingly sick Hindenburg, has declined the offer. Instead, he recommends the appointment of rising star and Volkskonservativ leader Gottfried Treviranus. With deep ties to German industry, the Right, and a pseudo-republican veneer, Treviranus is a candidate aimed at stabilizing Germany’s worsening crisis. Much like Papen’s dismissal in favor of Schleicher, the political class breathes yet another sigh of relief. Even within the **SPD**, many find it easier to confront the devil they know rather than face Schleicher’s dynamic and unpredictable rule. Treviranus will seek to construct a working majority via parliament. The Reichstag will convene on [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], Week [+ next_reichstag_week +].

dnef_discontent.bodyHtml: The two factions within the **DNEF** have effectively undergone a split, their differences proving too vast to reconcile. With no resolution in sight, the minority faction has broken away, taking a segment of the party with them. [? if right_dnef: This unlucky minority is the **DNEF**’s right wing, which sought to transform the party into a vehicle for the restoration of the German monarchy. The ideological gulf was too great for the ailing Schleicher to bridge, leading to the formation of the DNEF-Fatherland League (**DNEF-VLB**)—perhaps an echo of the German Fatherland Party of old. ?] [? if left_dnef: This unlucky minority is the **DNEF**’s left wing, which hoped to redirect the party toward addressing social inequality and defending the welfare of the German worker. Disputes over monarchism and the role of labor in the new corporatist order proved irreconcilable for Schleicher, resulting in their secession and the founding of the DNEF-Social Bloc (**DNEF-SB**). ?] However, what is fascinating is that both factions now claim to be the “true” **DNEF**. Chancellor [+ chancellor +] has so far avoided taking sides, hoping to prevent further splintering of an already fragile alliance. Perhaps this is Schleicher’s influence at work—a political truce between two perfectly normal, merely “disagreeing” factions.

params.source: reichstag_view

dnef_live.bodyHtml: The two factions within the **DNEF** have been reconciled—by none other than Schleicher himself. Despite being weakened by illness, he has managed to pull strings behind the scenes, halting the party’s internal confrontation. For now, the ideology of "Schleicherism" has re-united the movement, and it appears that [+ chancellor +] will inherit much of the authority Schleicher once wielded.

dnef_win.bodyHtml: [? if president != "Hindenburg": During [+ president +]’s term as President, the?][? if president == "Hindenburg": Following the death of Hindenburg from old age and Schleicher due to health complications, General Hammerstein is elected in a landslide in a heavily rigged election. The?] hated Weimar system is dismantled, and a new March Constitution is passed near-unanimously. The Reichstag is reduced to a rubber stamp for the regime. Germany formally adopts a presidential system, with both the Presidency and Chancellorship held by various **DNEF** members, who rise through bribes, patronage, and backroom deals. Corruption is endemic. Elections are stage-managed, dominated by fraud and manipulation. The **SPD** is never formally banned and endures as a powerless "loyal opposition," unable to influence national policy. Though tolerated, they face constant harassment and suppression by the ruling regime. Despite the regime’s authoritarianism, social discontent remains subdued. A Wirtschaftswunder—an economic miracle—emerges as the Great Depression fades. In 1935, Germany secures equality in armaments at Geneva and begins agitating for the return of the Polish Corridor separating East Prussia from the Reich. In 1942, a "special military operation" is launched to seize Danzig. Poland refuses to cede territory, and with backing from France and a hesitant Britain, enters a state of war. A puppet regime is installed in occupied territories. A limited French offensive into the Saar fails, and the Western Allies remain at war only on paper. Sensing German isolation, the Soviet Union invades eastern Poland, citing abuses against native Belarusians and Ukrainians under military occupation. A new German–Soviet war erupts. Defense Minister Hammerstein cultivates ties with the "Little Entente"—states facing their own Soviet-backed revolutionary threats. An unofficial Mitteleuropa bloc emerges, with Germany at its core, squeezed between a Western capitalist bloc and the Eastern state-socialist order. In 1946, the war ends in stalemate. Poland is partitioned at the Vistula River. Romania and Bulgaria fall under Communist control. Western Europe grows closer to the United States, and a tripolar global order takes shape. By the late 1960s, economic stagnation and renewed domestic unrest—driven by the Red Army Faction and neo-Nazi agitation—force Chancellor Kurt Georg Kiesinger to begin relaxing the dictatorship. The corporatist house of cards that had maintained the regime's stability for decades begins to crumble as independent unions discreetly form. However, Germany remains far from a free and democratic country, the Reichswehr maintains constant watch over politics, exercising real control behind the scenes. Today, the **DNEF** operates as a conventional big-tent political party. Though still marred by corruption, it remains the third major force in German politics, behind the **CVP** and **VSPD**. The Mitteleuropa bloc persists as a fragile intermediary between the West and the East—neither liberal nor socialist, but something in between.

dnf_collapse_center_right_coalition.subtitleHtml: The bourgeois-right coalition has collapsed...
dnf_collapse_center_right_coalition.bodyHtml: = Hugenberg's exit from the coalition When Hugenberg established his own party, he successfully attracted a significant number of former **DNVP** Reichstag members to join his party and to oppose the current center-right coalition. The current government lacks a majority within the Reichstag and may be taken down with a no-confidence vote. We can either vote to bring down the government and hold new elections, or "tolerate" a government led by the remaining bourgeois parties. It would be extremely unpopular within our party to support a government that has the participation of the **DNVP**—despite their removal of the most extreme factions—would be highly unpopular within our party. - @vonc_no

dnvp_dvp.bodyHtml: With the merger all but finalized, the new party has agreed to call itself the **FKP**, or the Free Conservative Party, styling itself as the spirital successor to the Empire-era party of the same name. Many on the **DVP**'s left have defected to the flourishing [+ ddp_name +], seeing it as the last bastion of liberalism. If Stresemann were alive, he would be quite disappointed in what has become of his liberal party.

choices.labelHtml: The party now needs to elect a leader.

dnvp_dvp_merger.titleHtml: The **DVP** merges with the **DNVP**!
dnvp_dvp_merger.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey and [+ dnvp_leader +] has reached an agreement.
dnvp_dvp_merger.bodyHtml: = **DVP** merges with the **DNVP** The electoral decline of the bourgeois right, the significant shift of the **DVP** toward the right, and their shared fear of the Nazis and socialists have compelled the two parties to unite. The **DNVP**, as the larger party, will absorb the **DVP**, making key concessions to facilitate the merger. Internal reactions within the **DVP** are mixed. The Stresemannites and left wing vehemently oppose the merger, while the right-industrial faction supports it as a necessary step. Within the **DNVP**, opposition comes from its agrarian and Christian Social factions, who resist unification with the industrial-capitalist **DVP**. Additionally, the party’s old guard, led by Westarp, remains skeptical due to major differences on the "national questions".

choices.labelHtml: Regardless, an agreement has been reached.

dnvp_dvp_merger_glatzel.titleHtml: The **DVP** merges with the **DNVP**!
dnvp_dvp_merger_glatzel.subtitleHtml: Glatzel and [+ dnvp_leader +] has reached an agreement.
dnvp_dvp_merger_glatzel.bodyHtml: = **DVP** merges with the **DNVP** Glatzel has long been a strong advocate for deepening ties between the two right-wing parties, ultimately aiming for a merger. Even before ascending to the leadership of the **DVP**, he had been cultivating relations with Treviranus’s Young Conservatives[? if dnvp_leader == "Lambach": and Lambach's Christian Socials?]. With a friendly leadership now in control of the **DNVP**, the path to unification appears clear. Most of the **DVP** backs Glatzel’s merger ambitions, opposed only by a small but vocal left wing around Curtius and Luther, who insist on preserving the **DVP** as a liberal force. Within the **DNVP**, resistance stems primarily from its agrarian wing, reluctant to unite with the capitalist, and middle-class oriented **DVP**. The party’s old guard, led by Westarp, also remains skeptical—citing differences over the national questions.

choices.labelHtml: Regardless, an agreement has been reached.

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.titleHtml: The **DVP** merges with the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?]!
dnvp_dvp_merger_new.subtitleHtml: [+ dvp_leader +] and [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":[+ dnvp_leader +] ?][? if kvp_formed:[+ kvp_leader +] ?] have reached an agreement.
dnvp_dvp_merger_new.bodyHtml: = The **DVP** merges with the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?] Glatzel has long been a strong advocate for deepening ties between the two right-wing parties, ultimately aiming for a merger. Even before ascending to the leadership of the **DVP**, he had been cultivating relations with Treviranus’s Young Conservatives[? if dnvp_leader == "Lambach": and Lambach's Christian Socials?]. With a friendly leadership now in control of the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?], the path to unification appears clear. Most of the **DVP** backs Glatzel’s merger ambitions, opposed only by a small but vocal left wing around Curtius and Luther, who insist on preserving the **DVP** as a liberal force. Within the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?], resistance stems primarily from its agrarian wing, reluctant to unite with the capitalist, and middle-class oriented **DVP**. The party’s old guard, led by Westarp, also remains skeptical—citing differences over the national questions.

choices.labelHtml: Regardless, an agreement has been reached.

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.calculations.bodyHtml:
= **FKP** Leadership Election Now that the **DVP** and [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?] have merged, the newly formed **FKP** must decide who will lead it into this next chapter. Several distinct factions, ranging from industrialists to nationalists to trade unionists, are already vying for influence within the fledgling party. The election of a chairman at the **FKP**’s inaugural congress will determine the internal balance of power and shape their future direction. With its future orientation still fluid, the outcome of the leadership vote may define whether the **FKP** leans toward tolerance of the republic or if it embraces a more nationalist course. Major Factions: National Conservatives ([? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?]) [+ natcons_fkp +] Agrarians ([? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?]) [+ agrarians_fkp +] Industrialists (**DVP**) [+ industrialists_fkp +]
Right-wing Unions (**DVP** and [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?]) [+ dhv_fkp +] Stresemannites (**DVP**) [+ stressmanites_fkp +] People's Conservatives ([? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?]) [+ ppconservatives_fkp +]

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.dnvp_dvp.bodyHtml: With the merger all but finalized, the new party has agreed to call itself the **FKP**, or the Free Conservative Party, styling itself as the spirital successor to the Empire-era party of the same name. Many on the **DVP**'s left have defected to the flourishing [+ ddp_name +], seeing it as the last bastion of liberalism. If Stresemann were alive, he would be quite disappointed in what has become of his liberal party.

choices.labelHtml: The party now needs to elect a leader.

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.glatzel.subtitleHtml: Hailing from the reformist elements of the **DVP**, he seeks to create a unitary force on the right.
dnvp_dvp_merger_new.glatzel.bodyHtml: Against expectations, Frank Glatzel prevailed in a drawn‑out, multi‑round ballot at the **FKP**’s inaugural congress. Centrists like Treviranus and von Raumer were the first to fall in the election, ultimately endorsing Glatzel over hard‑line monarchists such as Hergt and Westarp. By the final ballot, Glatzel had assembled a coalition of moderate [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?] holdouts, white-collar union delegates, and the remaining **DVP** moderates, clinching the chairmanship despite standing on the party’s left. This outcome represents the best potential scenario for us, as Glatzel remains open to some negotiation with the **SPD**. However, the new **FKP** will still be a far more obstinate partner than Stresemann’s **DVP**, given the enduring influence of agrarian and industrialist factions. Any cooperation will likely be more constrained than in the past. Still, compared to the uncompromising hardliners who nearly won the contest, Glatzel’s victory is a relief.

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.hergt.subtitleHtml: A member of the Old Guard of the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?], backed by rural and conservative elements.
dnvp_dvp_merger_new.hergt.bodyHtml: After several rounds of elimination voting at the **FKP**’s inaugural congress, Oskar Hergt secured the chairmanship by uniting the party’s monarchist‑conservative wing. The moderate Frank Glatzel was the first to go, followed by Hans von Raumer, whose industrialist backers then fragmented between Treviranus and Hergt. In the penultimate round, Kuno von Westarp withdrew and threw his delegates behind Hergt rather than the centrist faction led by Gottfried Treviranus. Agrarian conservatives, church‑aligned delegates, and a sizable bloc of **DNVP** conservatives gave him the edge over Treviranus in the final ballot. Hergt’s victory has seen our relations with the **FKP** sour. His entrenched monarchism and hostility toward democratic processes have already led him to explore increased cooperation with the far right, including informal contacts with the Stahlhelm. Genuine legislative collaboration now seems all but impossible, making building coalitions in the future increasingly difficult.

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.raumer.subtitleHtml: Backed by manu prominent industrialists from the **DVP**, von Raumer aims to strengthen the bourgiois.
dnvp_dvp_merger_new.raumer.bodyHtml: After several rounds of elimination voting at the **FKP**’s inaugural congress, Hans von Raumer secured the chairmanship by consolidating the party’s pro‑business wing. The moderate Frank Glatzel was the first to fall in the competition. In the penultimate round, Gottfried Treviranus withdrew and threw his support behind von Raumer, rather than the hard‑line monarchists. Industrialists and big‑business delegates, long allied with von Raumer, rallied en masse, joined by former **DVP** deputies and even some trade unionists, giving him a decisive edge over Kuno von Westarp in the final ballot. This represents an interesting development for us. While von Raumer is firmly linked to the industrialist wing of **FKP**, he has demonstrated firm support for Grand Coalitions in previous governments. He even has a good working relationship with Rudolf Hilferding. However, he would still be active in trying to limit our policies in any future government. Additionally, many of his own supporters in the industrialist wing would seek to prevent any coalition with us, so cooperation will still be more difficult than it was with Stresemann's **DVP**.

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.treviranus.subtitleHtml: Treviranus, ardent reformer, and member of the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate":**DNVP** ?][? if kvp_formed:**KVP**?], has put himself forwards.
dnvp_dvp_merger_new.treviranus.bodyHtml: After a protracted, multi‑round ballot at the **FKP**’s inaugural congress, Gottfried Treviranus secured the party chairmanship. Building a coalition of moderate **DNVP** dissidents, rural‑Chamber delegates, and a sprinkling of pragmatic ex‑**DVP** members allowed him to do well in the first round. Frank Glatzel, representing the party’s moderates, was the first to be eliminated. Then industrial conservatives around Hans von Raumer, unwilling to back the hard‑line monarchists, shifted en masse to Treviranus by the penultimate ballot, giving him a clear path to the chairmanship against Kuno von Westarp. Many in our party have signaled their resigned acceptance of Treviranus. While they remain deeply suspicious of his nationalist rhetoric and austere economic agenda, they acknowledge he is less hostile to the Weimar order than the outright monarchists within his party. Hopefully, he will act as a bulwark against the rising [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": far?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": far?]-right in the country.

dnvp_dvp_merger_new.westarp.subtitleHtml: A radical right-wing member of the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?], seeking to transform the party in a hardline direction.
dnvp_dvp_merger_new.westarp.bodyHtml: After several rounds of elimination voting at the **FKP**’s inaugural congress, Kuno von Westarp prevailed to win the chairmanship by rallying the party’s rural and ethno‑nationalist wings. The moderate Frank Glatzel was the first to be eliminated. In subsequent ballots, moderate conservatives around Hans von Raumer and ex‑**DVP** figures split their votes between Treviranus and Hergt, while Westarp consolidated support from his agrarian‐traditionalist bloc. In the penultimate round, Oskar Hergt withdrew and threw his delegates behind Westarp rather than the centerists led by Gottfried Treviranus. Westarp’s ascension means that the right is now effectively devoid of democratic parties. His explicit antisemitism and paramilitary sympathies signal a dangerous shift toward radical exclusion and street‑tier violence. This will make stabilizing the republic increasingly difficult, as the right increasingly rejects the republic.

dnvp_party_congress.subtitleHtml: The DNVP chooses their new leader...
dnvp_party_congress.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Congress A leadership vote is being held at the German National People's Party(**DNVP**) congress following the resignation of former leader Kuno von Westarp. The in-fighting resulting from their electoral defeat last election, coupled with the question of governmental participation in a system they're fundamentally opposed to has come to a head at this congress. On the right is Alfred Hugenberg, a prominent industrialist and head of a media empire. He is vehemently opposed by the left of the party for his "Katastrophenpolitik", as he prefers to see the republic fall than participate in parliamentary government. With Westarp's refusal to run for re-election, despite urgent pleas from the moderates within the party, they have convinced the reluctant Oskar Hergt, former leader of the **DNVP** from 1918—1924, himself ousted by the right. The results of this congress may very well be a turning point in the history of the entire German nation.

dnvp_party_congress_2.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Congress The **DNVP** has suffered severe internal conflicts the past year over Hugenberg's leadership, the Young Plan referendum with its controversial "imprisonment" paragraph[? if young_plan_signatures >= 10:, the impending vote on it within the Reichstag ?], and the expulsion of their Reichstag member Gottfried Treviranus over a private letter suggesting a split within the party if Hugenberg is unable to be removed. [? if stegerwald_path: Furthermore, the expansion of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] to Protestant voters has eroded its traditional voter base, raising serious doubts about the party's future. ?] The "unity of the no" against Marxism has been losing its force over the years, and the referendum against the Young Plan has only exacerbated internal party tensions. However, Hugenberg's efforts to increase control over the party will make it more difficult to force him out. [? if young_plan_signatures < 10: The failure of the initiative against the Young Plan has strengthened the dissidents position. ?] [? if tariffs < 0: The reduction in tariffs have emboldened the agrarian wing go against Hugenberg's Katastrophenpolitik. ?] [? if land_reform > 0: Our land reform initiatives have[? if tariffs < 0: also?] emboldened the agrarian wing go against Hugenberg[? if tariffs >= 0:?'s Katastrophenpolitik?]. ?]

dnvp_party_congress_2_hergt.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Congress The internal dissent within the **DNVP** has risen again with conflict over their participation in the referendum against the Young Plan[? if was_in_right_coalition == 1: and their withdrawal from the government[? if spd_in_government == 1: leaving us in power?]?]. The "unity of the no" against Marxism has been losing its force over the years, and now is the time for the **DNVP** to define itself through the next challenging years. [? if young_plan_signatures >= 10: The success of the Young Plan referendum to reach the adequate signatures has bolstered the current leadership.?][? if weimar_ref_signatures >= 30: The high support for the referendum for the revision of the constitution has bolstered the current leadership.?]

dnvp_party_congress_2_hergt.christiansoc.bodyHtml: The exodus of workers from our support base has greatly strengthened the Christian Socials within the **DNVP**, who seek to take advantage of our alienation of the trade unions. Walther Lambach has been elected leader of the **DNVP**, a trade union leader and the center of discourse within their party in the last congress. He claims a middle ground between socialism and capitalism, and to reconcile capital and labor, it remains to be seen how his leadership would impact the political landscape.
