Gottfried Treviranus has been elected as leader of the **DNVP**, a member of the "Young Conservative" faction and is supportive of transforming the party into a constructive conservative force, akin to the British Tories. The defeat of the radical right and national conservative forces within the **DNVP** helps pave the way for Treviranus' vision of a Christian Democratic, albeit nationalist party. dnvp_party_congress_2_triumvirate.comple.bodyHtml: The moderates within the **DNVP** united under Westarp are unable to defeat Hugenberg in a vote. This is in part due to Hugenberg's efforts of consolidating power within the party organizations. The agrarian representatives in the party finally had enough with Hugenberg's "all or nothing" strategy, especially after he governed as de-facto party dictator, disregarding even those he has shared power with. The anti-Hugenberg forces within the party have all left to form a new Konservative Volkspartei (Conservative People's Party). It is a question of how long this party would last, with some members rather wanting to affiliate with the special interest parties. Hugenberg is left with a diminished **DNVP**, smaller than the faction that split from it.

dnvp_party_congress_2.dnvpsplit.bodyHtml: The Christian Socials within the **DNVP** have been wanting to separate themselves for a while now, the Young Plan referendum debacle has given them the pretext. During the vote on the "Freedom Law" in the Reichstag, they went against Westarp's compromise solution and denounced Hugenberg, causing him to expel the renegade deputies. They were soon joined in leaving the party by many members of the "Young Conservative" faction. However, the failure of them to bring the party organizations or the agrarian wing with them has mitigated the impact. Westarp has stayed within the party, leading the remaining moderates. Despite their hopes of ousting Hugenberg in the future, his position within the party has been bolstered by the departure. [? if stegerwald_path: The Christian Socials have found refuge within the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], and will shift the party rightwards with their nationalistic views. ?]

However, the national conservatives retain heavy control over the party and the **DNVP** isn't exactly a democratic party yet. dnvp_party_congress_3_hergt.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Congress The victory of the moderates within the **DNVP** has not entirely halted the party’s rightward shift since its electoral defeat. Hergt’s triumph over the democratic Young Conservatives, led by Treviranus, has dashed our hopes for a more democratic and constructive **DNVP**. While the initial turmoil following Hugenberg’s split and the Young Plan has subsided, a rightward shift in the party’s policies remains possible, especially as the **NSDAP** threatens to eclipse them. The ongoing crisis in Germany continues to radicalize the electorate—and, by extension, the bourgeois parties that represent them.

dnvp_party_congress_3_hergt.schiele.bodyHtml: [? if land_reform >= 1 : Due to the land reform policies enacted by our[? if not spd_in_government: previous?] government, the agrarian conservative elites have made it their strongest effort to rally the German right against them. This involves orchestrating a leadership change within the **DNVP**, the primary political home of agrarian conservatism. Oskar Hergt has been persuaded to resign, in favor of the president of the National Rural League (RLB), Martin Schiele. They hope that by electing the most influential figure in the agricultural community, they can safeguard the relevance of organized agriculture within Germany. ?][? if rural_spd_normalized >= 30 and land_reform == 0 : With the **SPD** making significant inroads among rural voters, the **DNVP** and its agrarian elites have persuaded Oskar Hergt to resign, passing the party's leadership to Martin Schiele, the president of the National Rural League (RLB). They hope that the most influential figure in the agricultural community can stem the tide and maintain the historic bond between agriculture and German conservatism in the years ahead. ?][? if rural_nsdap_normalized >= rural_dnvp_normalized and rural_spd_normalized < 30 and land_reform == 0 : Due to the significant inroads made by the insurgent **NSDAP** among their primary rural voter base, the **DNVP** and its agrarian elites have persuaded Oskar Hergt to step down, passing the party’s leadership to Martin Schiele, president of the National Rural League (RLB). They hope that the most influential figure in the agricultural community can stem the tide and maintain the historic bond between organized agriculture and German conservatism in the years ahead. ?] Schiele’s election has led to the merger of the majority of the **CNBLP** into the **DNVP**, strengthening its hold on the countryside and uniting the RLB in lobbying for agrarian interests. This consolidation has given rise to the renewal of the Green Front, an umbrella group of the RLB, peasant unions, and some Catholic and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]-affiliated agricultural organizations.

dnvp_party_congress_3_hergt.statusquo.bodyHtml: Oskar Hergt has been re-elected once again. However, he and the national conservatives within the party are increasingly looking toward alliances with forces to their right, as their previous hostility toward the **DNF** continues to fade. Furthermore, the bourgeois elites influencing the party have pushed its leadership to reconsider some form of cooperation with the **NSDAP**, aiming to integrate them as a "constructive component of the state" through a so-called 'taming strategy'. Recently, discussions have emerged about a new referendum—one designed to unite the German right, much like the Young Plan referendum attempted, but this time focused on prematurely dissolving the Prussian Landtag. Given the radicalized political climate, such a move would allow the **NSDAP**, which currently holds a meager [+ nsdap_r_prussia +]% of seats, to make significant gains.

dnvp_party_congress_3_lambach.subtitleHtml: The economic depression has radicalized the party...
dnvp_party_congress_3_lambach.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Congress Walther Lambach has been a divisive figure, alienating nearly every faction within the party—a feat only Hugenberg had previously accomplished. Under normal circumstances, he would have been removed long ago, but his efforts to expand the influence of his Christian Social faction have made the wider party wary of another split, yet another parallel to Hugenberg. The turmoil within the **DNVP** appears to be endless. First came Hugenberg’s split, then the Young Plan debacle and the Christian Social takeover—now Lambach is pushing to open the party to republicans as he first outlined in his controversial article that started this whole mess years ago. Meanwhile, the economic crisis and the rising **NSDAP**, threatening to eclipse the party, have only added fuel to the fire.

choices.labelHtml: Lambach solidifies the party’s Christian Social direction.
Lambach is taken down in a simple vote of no confidence.

dnvp_party_congress_3_lambach.lambach.bodyHtml: Against all odds, Walther Lambach survives a vote of no confidence at the party congress by allying with Treviranus’s Young Conservatives, securing a mandate to advance his vision for the **DNVP** in line with the late Adolf Stoecker, founder of the pre-war Christian Social Party. The party’s program, once tailored to its broad coalition, now includes significantly more worker-friendly policies, such as expanding social welfare, increasing pensions, and implementing progressive income taxes. they have even rejected austerity as a solution to Germany's current economic crisis. However, this shift has severely strained Lambach’s relationship with much of the party, particularly its industrial backers, who have begun withholding funding and redirecting it—albeit reluctantly—to more right-wing parties like the **DNF** and **NSDAP**. At the same time, severe internal opposition has moved to obstruct him any way they can, prompting Westarp to intervene and suppress a revolt within the party. As a result, Lambach was forced to make concessions, ensuring that his leadership would not stray too far from the **DNVP**'s traditional anti-Marxist and monarchist stance.

dnvp_party_congress_3_lambach.lambach_ou.bodyHtml: Lambach has, perhaps predictably, lost a vote of no confidence, forcing him to relinquish his leadership to a candidate from the party’s traditionally conservative establishment. The agrarian wing, long opposed to both Lambach and the Christian Socials—united with them only by their shared hatred for Hugenberg—argues that only the appointment of the National Rural League (RLB) president can restore the party’s tarnished reputation in rural Germany. Meanwhile, the national conservatives favor re-electing Westarp, citing his unifying presence and experience in managing party dissent. They credit him with preventing many of the party’s more reactionary members from drifting toward the **DNF** during Lambach’s tenure.

choices.labelHtml: The party rallies around Westarp, restoring him to his former position.
The mantle is transferred to Martin Schiele and the agrarians.

dnvp_party_congress_3_lambach.schiele.bodyHtml: [? if land_reform >= 1 : Due to the land reform policies enacted by our[? if not spd_in_government: previous?] government, the agrarian conservative elites have made it their strongest effort to rally the German right against them. To this end, they have elected Martin Schiele, president of the National Rural League (RLB), as chairman of the **DNVP**. By electing the most influential figure in the agricultural community, the party aims to safeguard the role of organized agriculture in Germany, and to restore the tarnished reputation the party has incurred under Lambach. ?][? if rural_spd_normalized >= 30 and land_reform == 0 : With the **SPD** making significant inroads among rural voters, the **DNVP** and its agrarian elites have elected the president of the National Rural League (RLB), Martin Schiele, to the chairmanship of the **DNVP**. By electing the most influential figure in the agricultural community, they aim to safeguard the role of organized agriculture in Germany, and to restore the tarnished reputation the party has incurred under Lambach. ?][? if rural_nsdap_normalized >= (rural_dnvp_normalized + 10) and rural_spd_normalized < 30 and land_reform == 0 : The significant inroads made by the insurgent **NSDAP** among their primary rural voter base under Lambach's tenure has deeply unsettled the party's agrarian conservatives. In response, they have elected the president of the National Rural League (RLB), Martin Schiele, as the new party leader. They believe that appointing Schiele, the most influential figure in the agricultural community, will halt this trend and preserve the longstanding alliance between agriculture and German conservatism by restoring the party’s tarnished reputation among rural voters after Lambach’s tenure.?]The new agrarian focus of the **DNVP** has alienated the working-class voters initially drawn to Lambach. In response, the Christian Social wing attempts to counteract this by successfully pressuring Schiele and Westarp to retain some of its worker-friendly provisions in its program. Schiele’s election has also led to the merger of the **CNBLP** into the **DNVP**, strengthening its hold on the countryside and uniting the RLB in lobbying for agrarian interests. This consolidation has given rise to the renewal of the Green Front, an umbrella group of the RLB, peasant unions, and some Catholic and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]-affiliated agricultural organizations.

dnvp_party_congress_3_lambach.westarp.bodyHtml: The **DNVP**’s shift toward Christian Corporatism and republicanism has stalled with the re-election of Kuno von Westarp as party leader, promoted from his role as chairman of the Reichstag delegation. So far, Westarp has avoided drastic changes to prevent a party split, frustrating the party’s more conservative and industrial backers, who had hoped his leadership would restore the **DNVP** to its previous course. At the same time, Westarp is careful not to alienate the Christian Social wing through drastic changes to the party program, fearing a split or the defection of its working-class base back to the **SPD**. As a compromise, he preserves some worker-friendly provisions in the party program and messaging. While this is not enough to hold onto the working-class support Lambach had built, the party offsets these losses by winning back monarchist and conservative voters from the **DNF**, aided by a resurgence in industrial funding.

dnvp_party_congress_3_treviranus.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Congress The victory of moderates within the **DNVP** has not entirely stopped the party’s rightward shift since its electoral defeat years ago. The surprise election of Gottfried Treviranus briefly reversed this trend, but the worsening economic crisis has swung the pendulum in favor of the party’s conservatives once again. Additionally, Treviranus's ambivalence on monarchism has sparked controversy, deepening divisions within the party—this time creating a genuine split, unlike the debate over Lambach’s article years prior. While the turmoil from Hugenberg’s split and the Young Plan has subsided, a further rightward shift remains possible, especially as the **NSDAP** threatens to eclipse them. Treviranus now faces a battle against the party’s reactionary elements as he works to modernize the **DNVP** and secure its democratic future.

choices.labelHtml: Treviranus manages to secure his and his party's future.
Westarp is restored to his former position.
The mantle is transferred to Martin Schiele and the agrarians.

Treviranus has been ousted in a vote of no confidence, in favor of the president of the National Rural League (RLB), Martin Schiele. By electing the most influential figure in the agricultural community, they aim to safeguard the role of organized agriculture in Germany, viewing Treviranus as too aligned with middle class interests. ?][? if rural_spd_normalized >= 30 and land_reform == 0 : With the **SPD** making significant inroads among rural voters, the **DNVP** and its agrarian elites have ousted Treviranus in a vote of no confidence, to elect Martin Schiele, the president of the National Rural League (RLB). They believe Schiele, the most influential figure in the agricultural community, can halt this shift and preserve the longstanding alliance between agriculture and German conservatism, seeing Treviranus as too aligned with middle-class interests. ?][? if rural_nsdap_normalized >= rural_dnvp_normalized and rural_spd_normalized < 30 and land_reform == 0 : Due to the significant inroads made by the insurgent **NSDAP** among their primary rural voter base, the **DNVP** and its agrarian elites have ousted Treviranus in a vote of no confidence, to elect Martin Schiele, president of the National Rural League (RLB). They believe Schiele, the most influential figure in the agricultural community, can halt this shift and preserve the longstanding alliance between agriculture and German conservatism, seeing Treviranus as too aligned with middle-class interests. ?] Schiele’s election has led to the merger of the **CNBLP** into the **DNVP**, strengthening its hold on the countryside and uniting the RLB in lobbying for agrarian interests. This consolidation has given rise to the renewal of the Green Front, an umbrella group of the RLB, peasant unions, and some Catholic and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]-affiliated agricultural organizations.

dnvp_party_congress_3_treviranus.trevira.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, Treviranus has survived efforts to replace him with a more conservative figure, securing a mandate to further reform the party—despite opposition from bourgeois and reactionary elites. [? if hugenberg_removed: However, he remains a puppet of the **DNVP**'s old guard—figures like Westarp and Hergt—who block any drastic shift toward People's Conservatism. ?] While some conservative and reactionary supporters defect to the **DNF** and even the **NSDAP**, the party compensates for these losses by attracting republicans previously alienated by the **DNVP**’s monarchist stance. Although monarchism remains in the party’s platform, it has taken a backseat to more pressing issues.

dnvp_party_congress_3_treviranus.westarp.bodyHtml: The **DNVP**'s shift toward Tory Democracy and republicanism has stalled with the re-election of Kuno von Westarp as party leader, promoted from his role as chairman of the Reichstag delegation. Experienced with managing internal dissent, Westarp avoids drastic changes to prevent a party split, frustrating the party’s more reactionary backers, who had hoped his election would return the **DNVP** to its previous course. While some republican voters drawn to Treviranus shift back toward bourgeois parties, Westarp’s more conservative leadership helps reclaim voters from Hugenberg’s **DNF**. However, he opposes active reconciliation with Hugenberg and his party.

dnvp_party_congress_4_westarp.subtitleHtml: Westarp has resigned from his position to accept the presidency.
dnvp_party_congress_4_westarp.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Congress With Westarp elected president, he can no longer serve as party chairman. An emergency party congress is therefore convened to choose his successor. Optimism runs high within the party—one of their own now holds the presidency, and they possess the power to exclude the **SPD** from government positions entirely. Paul Lejeune-Jung, leader of the **DNVP**’s small Catholic wing, is Westarp’s chosen successor. His main rival is Walter von Keudell, with links to People's Conservative faction and a former Interior Minister under Marx. Both are widely regarded as unifying figures and share a similar ideological outlook; the outcome of the vote is unlikely to significantly alter the party’s overall direction.

dnvp_party_congress_4_westarp.keudell.bodyHtml: Von Keudell, long considered the underdog, has won the election for the **DNVP** chairmanship. Branding himself as the voice of the "young generation," he criticized the party's entrenched ties to Ruhr industrialists and elites as liabilities that alienate younger voters. While his ascent irritates some within the party establishment, he is nonetheless expected to continue Westarp’s general decision-making style—albeit with a stronger focus on broadening support among the emerging urban middle class.

dnvp_party_congress_4_westarp.lejeune_ju.bodyHtml: Lejeune-Jung has, as expected, won the election with Westarp’s blessing, securing a comfortable majority. He is anticipated to continue Westarp’s decision-making style while working to broaden the **DNVP**’s appeal among conservative Catholics of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": CVP?]. Their first high-profile defector is Franz von Papen, an agrarian noble from the far right of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": CVP?], who brings a cohort of allies with him.

dnvp_party_congress.hergt.bodyHtml: With opinions on the inflammatory Lambach article being surprisingly divided among party members, a general republican sentiment across Germany, Alfred Hugenberg and his staunch anti-democratic beliefs struggling to convince moderate party members. More and more party members are beginning to blame their decline on the thesis of the Lambach article rather than their participation in a republican government. [? if tariffs < 0: Furthermore, our decrease in tariffs have rallied the agrarian wing against Hugenberg and his all-or-nothing policy. ?] Oskar Hergt has been elected as the new leader of the **DNVP** following a divisive congress. Hugenberg and his supporters have hinted towards a secession from the party's right wing, and Hugenberg himself is withholding financial support to the party.

dnvp_party_congress.hugenberg.bodyHtml: Alfred Hugenberg, channelling the anger created by the inflammatory Lambach article, which criticized the party's monarchist direction, the electoral defeat, and their participation in a system they fundamentally oppose, has won over the moderates in a simple majority vote for his candidacy. Hugenberg is set to alienate the left of his party and cause a possible secession due to his uncompromising stances on just about everything. Hugenberg is expected to bring about an end to internal party democracy and instill a Führerprinzip within the party. The former conservative catch-all party will be transformed into a party for his own goals. Westarp remains as the chairman for the **DNVP**'s Reichstag delegation for now, and will try his best to prevent a secession from the party, even with Hugenberg leading.

dnvp_party_congress.triumvirate.bodyHtml:
Both Hugenberg and Hergt lack the majority of votes needed within the party, and now are seeking a compromise solution between the two factions. A group of party members on the fence between the two, have suggested a triumvirate between Westarp, Hugenberg, and a representative from Prussia as a compromise, a proposal Hugenberg himself is supportive of, where he can control the party from the sidelines.
Westarp is not enthusiastic of such a proposal but agreed to take part in it for the sake of party unity. However, this arrangement is unstable and will not last long.

dnvp_split.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, the party district organizations remain loyal to Hugenberg, who has worked to fill the party bureaucracy with his own supporters. As a result, the defection of the entire moderate wing of the **DNVP** is less impactful than it would have been. Furthermore, many on the right believe that an internal resolution is not a strong enough pretext to break with the party and may choose to remain with Hugenberg.

dnvp_split_2.subtitleHtml: Westarp had enough of Hugenberg's antics.
dnvp_split_2.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** Moderates split! The moderate anti-Hugenberg wing of the **DNVP** had already decided to break with the party, and it was only a matter of finding the right pretext. This opportunity came when Hugenberg passed a resolution to strengthen his Führerprinzip over the party, making the decisions of the party executive committee and leader binding on all members of the party’s delegations to the Reichstag and state parliaments. The moderates within the party were powerless to stop the adoption of the resolution, which led to Westarp and the remaining moderates [? if not kvp_formed: splitting off into various parties on the moderate German right?][? if kvp_formed: to join their friends in the newly founded **KVP**?].

dnvp_wholesome.bodyHtml: Due to our shared values of wholesomeness and love, we have agreed to run a joint list with the **DNVP** and welcome them into our parliamentary group. However, because of this deal, we had to expel all our Jewish members, who join the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]. {!!}

dnvpsplit.bodyHtml: The Christian Socials within the **DNVP** have been wanting to separate themselves for a while now, the Young Plan referendum debacle has given them the pretext. During the vote on the "Freedom Law" in the Reichstag, they went against Westarp's compromise solution and denounced Hugenberg, causing him to expel the renegade deputies. They were soon joined in leaving the party by many members of the "Young Conservative" faction. However, the failure of them to bring the party organizations or the agrarian wing with them has mitigated the impact. Westarp has stayed within the party, leading the remaining moderates. Despite their hopes of ousting Hugenberg in the future, his position within the party has been bolstered by the departure. [? if stegerwald_path: The Christian Socials have found refuge within the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], and will shift the party rightwards with their nationalistic views. ?]

dstp_collapse.bodyHtml: Negotiations between Mahraun and the democrats have finally collapsed; the experiment has finally fallen apart. The members from Mahraun's **VNR** have split[? if dstp_election:, taking their Reichstag seats with them?]. Responsibility for the break is argued on both sides, with the old-line democrats Mahraun's refusal to compromise and the Order blaming purposeful obstruction. [? if dstp_election: In terms of consequences, the defection of the **VNR**-affiliated Reichstag delegates has severely diminished their parliamentary influence. [? if ddp_r < 3.6: So much so that the **DStP** is now too small to form a parliamentary faction and must negotiate with another party, which is challenging given the debacle that occurred months ago.?]?] An air of pessimism and despair has settled over the **DStP**, especially impacting Koch-Weser, who, deeply demoralized by the collapse of the **State Party**, has ultimately decided to retire from politics altogether. Overall, this entire debacle has essentially resulted in the **DStP** becoming the **DDP** with a new name, albeit with a more nationalistic and statist platform.

dstp_formed.bodyHtml: This has come as a complete shock to those inside and outside the party, for the **DDP** to merge with the political wing of a mildly anti-Semitic paramilitary group "Young German Order". Ongoing negotiations to unite the liberal and bourgeois parties has been considerably damaged, due to the **DDP**'s attempts to promote a left-wing split from the **DVP**. In this agreement, the **DDP** has promised a "extension of the party to the right", which can only spell trouble for our closest bourgeois ally. Despite this, the formation of the **DStP** wasn't a simple left-right divide within the party, the Social Republican Circle and labor leader Ernst Lemmer helps prevent a major split among the left. However, cracks are already beginning to show within this arrangement, it is only a matter of time before this experiment falls apart.

dstp_maintained.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the contradiction that is the **DStP** continues to live on. After intense negotiations between the democrats in favor of the merger, like Koch-Weser, and the dissenting old-line democrats, they agree to elevate Koch-Weser to the chairman of the Reichstag faction. However, Mahraun's control over the party's national organization proved to be a much trickier problem, as Mahraun’s Order remained inflexible when it came to compromise. The deadlock is finally resolved when Mahraun agrees to cede some of his Reichsführer powers to the executive committee in exchange for a larger share of **VNR**-affiliated delegates at next month's party congress. It seems this experiment will persist, with the **DStP** adopting a more nationalistic and statist identity compared to the old **DDP**. Only time will tell how the party will fare against the rise of the **NSDAP**.

dsu_in_gov.bodyHtml: Wilhelm Frick is nominated to the Interior Ministry[? if old_prussia_leader == "Schleicher": —both in the Reich and in Prussia?]. Gregor Strasser takes the vice-chancellorship—a title in name only. [? if prussia_leader == "Goerdeler": Although the **DSU** would’ve preferred Strasser installed in Prussia, Goerdeler stays on—as Schleicher’s loyal puppet and as a concession to the Center Party. ?] At the Nazis’ insistence, Hjalmar Schacht is brought in as an independent to head the Economic Ministry. To compensate for the Center Party’s loss of influence, they're given an additional Ministry without Portfolio. Not that the Center can complain—not with Bracht in charge.

duesterberg.bodyHtml: The Harzburg Front has fractured, with the **DNVP** and **Stahlhelm** nominating a separate candidate than the **NSDAP**, who rather run their own candidate. In a deal between the leadership of the **Stahlhelm** and Hugenberg, the **DNVP** is to support and campaign for whoever the **Stahlhelm** nominates, in exchange for the **Stahlhelm**'s full support for the **DNVP** in the upcoming local elections. The **Stahlhelm** have decided to nominate its deputy leader, Theodor Duesterberg.

duesterburg_wins.bodyHtml: Duesterberg is too ashamed to accept the Presidency, and out of the kindness of his heart, has given it to Otto Braun.

dvp_dingeldey_dnvp.titleHtml: The **DVP** and **DNVP** Conclude an Alliance!
dvp_dingeldey_dnvp.subtitleHtml: Is there anything "liberal" left in the **DVP**?
dvp_dingeldey_dnvp.bodyHtml: = **DVP** and **DNVP** Alliance With new elections approaching, the **DVP** is likely to be pushed into irrelevance by the surging **NSDAP**. In an effort to ensure his party's survival, Dingeldey has concluded an alliance with Hugenberg and the **DNVP**. While Dingeldey insists that the pact is purely technical and does not compromise the party’s political integrity, it proves to be the final straw for the **DVP**'s left wing. An accommodation with the anti-democratic and "socially reactionary" Hugenberg is widely seen as a betrayal of the National Liberal legacy that Stresemann and the founders of the **DVP** once championed.

dvp_dingeldey_dnvp.dvp_left_split.bodyHtml: Those on the **DVP**'s left wing who had quietly opposed Dingeldey's turn to the right have now resigned en masse. Hans Bechly, Frank Glatzel, and Otto Thiel—prominent figures within the white-collar DHV union—have also stepped down, with Bechly being the longtime chairman of the association. With their exodus, the party’s last remaining link to the German white-collar movement has been severed, along with a significant portion of its electoral base. The only consolation Dingeldey can claim is that the party’s loss in seats will be somewhat mitigated by its electoral connection to the **DNVP**.

[? if in_grand_coalition_prussia: Their inclusion in the Prussian government has also fostered a more conciliatory attitude toward us. ?]

dvp_party_congress.subtitleHtml: The **DVP** chooses their new leader...
dvp_party_congress.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Congress The **DVP** are having an internal party vote to elect a successor to former party leader and statesman Gustav Stresemann. Both the party and its electorate have been shifted significantly to the right in recent years. [? if not in_grand_coalition: The left of the **DVP** has also been diminished by the current absence of a coalition including both parties. ?] The candidate on the right is current party leader Ernst Scholz. Scholz has heavy ties to industry and a record of opposing bourgeois unity. [? if foreign_minister_party = "DVP" and economic_minister_party != "DVP": On the left is Foreign Minister Julius Curtius, who succeeded Stresemann for the position. However, Curtius has taken himself out of the running by taking the position. A movement to draft former Chancellor Hans Luther is met with his own personal reluctance, effectively leaving Scholz as the only suitable choice.?][? if foreign_minister_party != "DVP" and economic_minister_party = "DVP": On the left is Economic Minster Julius Curtius, who has favor among the youth groups. However, Curtius has taken himself out of the running by retaining his position. A movement to draft former Chancellor Hans Luther is met with his own personal reluctance, effectively leaving Scholz as the only suitable choice.?][? if foreign_minister_party != "DVP" and economic_minister_party != "DVP": On the left is Julius Curtius, who has favor among the youth groups. A movement to draft former Chancellor Hans Luther has failed to gain momentum, and the factions of the party have rallied behind their own prospective candidate.?]

dvp_party_congress_1.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Party Vote Over the past few months, the dire state of the economy—and of Germany as a whole—has pushed the landscape of bourgeois parties toward radicalization and a rightward shift. While the **DVP** resisted this trend with the election of [+ dvp_leader +] last year, the party’s right-wing industrial forces have now united their resources for one final effort to oust [+ dvp_leader +]. [? if dvp_leader == "Curtius": Julius Curtius, the incumbent chairman of the party, has been pressured to delegate some of his responsibilities to the newly appointed deputy leader, Eduard Dingeldey[? if foreign_minister_party == "DVP":, due to his preoccupation with his duties as Foreign Minister?][? if foreign_minister_party != "DVP":, due to his preoccupation with governmental affairs?]. Dingeldey was among the first within the **DVP** to support the movement for bourgeois unity. He also holds sufficiently conservative views—particularly regarding cooperation with the **SPD**—to garner support from Scholz and the party's right wing. Given his broad support within the party, the right wing of the **DVP** has put him forward as a replacement for Curtius, citing [? if foreign_minister_party == "DVP": his lackluster performance as Foreign Minister following Stresemann's death?][? if foreign_minister_party != "DVP": his lackluster performance as the successor of Stresemann?]. ?][? if dvp_leader == "Luther": Hans Luther, despite being elected with strong backing from German businesses, has partially fallen out of favor with his former supporters, mainly due to his unpopular stance in favor of constructive cooperation with the **SPD**. As the German electorate has shifted significantly to the right, the party's right wing sees this as a weakness to exploit. They have put forth Eduard Dingeldey, who was among the first in the **DVP** to support the movement for bourgeois unity, granting his support over the **DVP** affiliated bourgeois unity groups. He is also sufficiently conservative—particularly regarding cooperation with the **SPD**—to gain unified support from Scholz and the party’s right wing. ?]

dvp_party_congress_1.curtius.bodyHtml: Julius Curtius has once again won the vote to retain his position against the right wing of the **DVP**. The industrialists have lost their final battle, paving the way for the **DVP** to become a party Stresemann would be proud of—a genuinely liberal German People's Party, free from the obstruction of reactionary forces. This is more than excellent news for us and our relationship with the **DVP**, sending notable ripple effects throughout the entire party system. In response to their loss, the industrialists have shifted their donations toward the **DNVP** and even the **NSDAP**, hoping to establish a new political home for their interests.

dvp_party_congress_1.dingeldey.bodyHtml: Eduard Dingeldey has unexpectedly won the vote to replace [+ old_dvp_leader +] as chairman of the **DVP**. Backed by broad and unified support from the party’s right wing, led by Ernst Scholz, along with some reform-minded elements and **DVP**-affiliated youth groups, he has narrowly clinched victory in a vote of no confidence against [+ old_dvp_leader +]. Dingeldey's election represents a significant and irreversible shift to the right,[? if dvp_reform: with him even repealing Stresemann's reform of the internal party structure,?] granting the industrialists back their lost influence on the **DVP**'s decision making. [? if chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government: Dingeldey doesn't even feel great loyalty toward the Brüning government and believes that the party could only fulfill its mission towards bourgeois concentration after it is freed from the burden of governmental responsibility.?] Furthermore, Dingeldey is not particularly interested in a closer relationship with the **[+ ddp_name +]** and definitely not with us, but rather with parties to the right, such as the **DNVP** and even the **NSDAP**, to transform them into a 'constructive component of the state.' This does not bode well for the future of Weimar democracy.

dvp_party_congress_1.luther.bodyHtml: Hans Luther has, as expected, won his re-election for the **DVP**'s chairmanship. Despite his tarnished reputation among the party’s right wing, his broad support was sufficient for a decisive victory in the vote of no confidence. His plans for a united liberal—and even bourgeois—party to presumably counter the influence of the socialists have reassured most industrial donors, though some have begun shifting their funding toward the **DNVP**. This is excellent news for democracy and for our constructive cooperation with the **DVP**. The right-wing forces have been defeated once again, ensuring that the party will likely remain on its democratic path for the foreseeable future.

dvp_party_congress_2.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Party Vote Following the disastrous Austrian customs union project, of which he was the architect, he has tendered his resignation from both the Foreign Ministry and the leadership of the **DVP**. This debacle has significantly discredited him and his allies on the party’s left wing, leading to a rightward shift within the **DVP**, particularly at the local level. An internal election must now be held to determine Curtius’s successor. With the industrial wing largely weakened, none of the leading candidates have particularly strong ties to big business. Otto Thiel and Frank Glatzel, both members of the DHV - a conservative white-collar union - and leaders of the **DVP**'s Young Liberal wing, [? if not dvp_reform: are the leading voices pushing for a genuine People's Party?][? if dvp_reform: were instrumental in pushing the **DVP** toward reform years ago?]. Meanwhile, Siegfried von Kardorff, a veteran parliamentarian despite his past affiliation with the **DNVP**, has significantly moderated over the years and was a close follower of Stresemann, advocating for a Grand Coalition with the **SPD**. And, of course, Dingeldey is running again, undeterred by his previous defeat.

dvp_party_congress_2.dingeldey.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey aims to revert all of Curtius's progress.
dvp_party_congress_2.dingeldey.bodyHtml: Eduard Dingeldey has unexpectedly won the vote to replace [+ old_dvp_leader +] as chairman of the **DVP**. Backed by broad and unified support from the party’s right wing, and endorsed by Ernst Scholz, he has narrowly clinched victory against Kardorff. Dingeldey's election represents a significant and irreversible shift to the right,[? if dvp_reform: with him even repealing Stresemann's reform of the internal party structure,?] granting the industrialists back their lost influence on the **DVP**'s decision making. [? if chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government: Dingeldey doesn't even feel great loyalty toward the Brüning government and believes that the party could only fulfill its mission towards bourgeois concentration after it is freed from the burden of governmental responsibility.?] Furthermore, Dingeldey is not particularly interested in a closer relationship with the **[+ ddp_name +]** and definitely not with us, but rather with parties to the right, such as the **DNVP** and even the **NSDAP**, to transform them into a 'constructive component of the state.' This does not bode well for the future of Weimar democracy.

dvp_party_congress_2.glatzel.subtitleHtml: Glatzel, being a former member of the **DNVP** as well, has shown nationalist sympathies.
dvp_party_congress_2.glatzel.bodyHtml: Frank Glatzel is elected to become the new leader of the **DVP**, being more nationalist and right-wing than his colleague Thiel. He stands for a "New Nationalism," a solidarity among all classes, to defend the country's "living space" and to create freedom for the people. In his push for *Volksgemeinschaft*, to reduce the conflict between the classes, he has begun including more nationalistic and corporatist elements into the party platform. As expected, the remaining industrialists within the **DVP** are worried, as the party begins to shift towards including the demands of the worker. This has led to a dramatic shift in the party’s financial backing, as funding from big business dwindles and is replaced by donations and dues from the DHV and its affiliated members. His dynamic leadership should be closely watched.

dvp_party_congress_2.thiel.subtitleHtml: Thiel is a controversial unionist within the party, being more left wing than Glatzel.
dvp_party_congress_2.thiel.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, Otto Thiel has been elected as the new leader of the **DVP**! Compared to his colleague Glatzel, Thiel leans further left within the party’s unionist faction. He has even voiced support for increased welfare spending, arguing that austerity measures would only deepen the hardships faced by the people. In his push for *Volksgemeinschaft*, he has begun introducing more labor-friendly policies into the party’s platform, backing collective bargaining rights and worker protections. As expected, the remaining industrialists within the **DVP** are outraged—even those with sympathies toward the late Stresemann. This has led to a dramatic shift in the party’s financial backing, as funding from big business dwindles and is replaced by donations and dues from the DHV and its affiliated members. [? if in_grand_coalition: We have noticed a significant decrease in coalition tensions. ?]

dvp_party_congress_3_dingeldey.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Party Vote The non-industrialist and Stresemannite elements of the **DVP** have revolted, angered by their marginalization at the hands of the industrialists, who have pushed to realign Stresemann’s former party with the national opposition. Led by Wilhelm Kunz, a Berlin lawyer, and Count Alexander zu Dohna, a legal expert and widely respected figure on the party’s left wing, they aim to publicly challenge Dingeldey and the industrialist faction that has effectively puppeteered him. They both advocate for cooperation with the minor bourgeois parties and the **[+ ddp_name +]**, and firmly reject what they call the “psychosis of National Socialism.”

dvp_party_congress_3_dingeldey.dingeldey.titleHtml: Dingeldey loses the vote of no confidence!
dvp_party_congress_3_dingeldey.dingeldey.bodyHtml: At a divisive party congress, prominent figures from the party’s left wing—such as Thiel, Glatzel, and Curtius—force a vote on Dingeldey’s leadership of the **DVP**. Dingeldey is ousted, replaced by zu Dohna, prompting the industrialist faction to withdraw its support and shift its funds to the right. However, the **DVP**’s move to distance itself from its former industrial backers—and its renewed campaign to revive Stresemann’s legacy—has done much to restore some of its lost electoral strength. Our relationship with the **DVP** has improved. Still, Dingeldey’s tenure radicalized the party toward the right, and the damage cannot be undone overnight.

dvp_party_congress_3_luther.subtitleHtml: Luther resigns from his party positions to accept the presidency.
dvp_party_congress_3_luther.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Party Congress With Luther elected president, he naturally cannot continue serving as the **DVP**'s chairman. A party congress is convened to select his successor. This marks the first time Germany has elected a president from the political middle, and optimism within the party is running high. In contention is **DVP** veteran and parliamentarian Siegfried von Kardorff—a conventional politician endorsed by Luther and expected to continue his moderate course of supporting Bürgerblocks while keeping the door open to cooperation with the **SPD**. Also in the running are Otto Thiel and Frank Glatzel, both prominent figures within the DHV, a white-collar union that has long played a role in shaping **DVP** policy—though they likely lack the influence to carry one of their own to the chairmanship. Meanwhile, the **DVP**'s right wing—despite previous setbacks—remains very much alive. Their candidate is Otto Hugo, a co-founder of the party and a lobbyist for Ruhr heavy industry. Ideologically, he closely aligns with Scholz, maintaining a staunch and irreconcilable opposition to any cooperation with the **SPD**.

dvp_party_congress_3_luther.hugo.bodyHtml: Otto Hugo has unexpectedly won the vote to replace [+ old_dvp_leader +] as chairman of the DVP. His election marks a decisive and likely irreversible shift to the right[? if dvp_reform:, even repealing Stresemann’s reforms to the party’s internal structure?], as Hugo moves to ensure industrialist dominance over the **DVP**’s decision-making apparatus. Unsurprisingly, Hugo’s industrial ties and lack of public appeal—especially in contrast to Luther—have caused the **DVP** to suffer in the polls. The primary beneficiary is the **[+ ddp_name +]**, which is shifting rightward to capture the disaffected middle-class vote.

dvp_party_congress_reform.subtitleHtml: The **DVP** chooses their new leader...
dvp_party_congress_reform.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Congress The **DVP** are having an internal party vote to elect a successor to former party leader and statesman Gustav Stresemann. Despite recent reforms, both the party and its electorate have been shifting to the right in recent years. [? if not in_grand_coalition: The left of the **DVP** has also been diminished by the current absence of a coalition including both parties. ?] The candidate on the right is current party leader Ernst Scholz. Scholz has heavy ties to industry and a record of opposing bourgeois unity. Although the right of the party was weakened, nationalist influences have rose since Stresemann's death. On the left is Julius Curtius, [? if in_grand_coalition or in_right_coalition or in_center_right_coalition: the **DVP**'s [? if (foreign_minister_party == "DVP" and economic_minister_party != "DVP") or (foreign_minister_party == "DVP" and economic_minister_party == "DVP"): Foreign Minister who succeeded Stresemann in the role.?][? if economic_minister_party == "DVP" and foreign_minister_party != "DVP": Economic Minister, and a close ally of Stresemann?]?][? if not in_grand_coalition: a close ally of Stresemann and seen by many as his natural successor?]. A movement to draft former Chancellor Hans Luther is met with his own personal reluctance, but he remains a possible compromise candidate.

dvp_party_congress_reform.curtius.bodyHtml: Julius Curtius has won the vote to succeed Stresemann for the chairmanship. It seems like the industrialists have finally lost their fight to control the **DVP**, which has now become a genuine People's Party that Stresemann envisioned. This is still excellent news for us and our relations with the **DVP**. [? if in_grand_coalition: We have noticed a decrease in coalition tensions. ?]

dvp_party_congress_reform.luther.bodyHtml: Hans Luther has surprisingly won the vote to succeed Stresemann for the chairmanship. Luther has support among both the industrialists and the left of the party, giving him the ability to command strong influence over the party unlike his predecessors. Perhaps he's what the **DVP** needs in order to survive this crisis of German democracy. [? if (dnvp_ideology == "Radical" and not kvp_formed): Luther also manages to attract dissidents from Hugenberg's **DNVP**. ?] Luther is particularly supportive of uniting the liberal parties and even for the creation of a broad bourgeois party. [? if in_grand_coalition: He has also voiced support for maintaining the Grand coalition and cooperation between the two parties. ?][? if not in_grand_coalition and dvp_relation >= 40: He has voiced support for a coalition government involving us and cooperation between the two parties. ?][? if not in_grand_coalition and dvp_relation < 40: He has voiced skepticism to any potential coalitions involving us, because of the current absence of a coalition including both parties. ?]

dvp_party_congress.curtius.bodyHtml: Julius Curtius has surprisingly won the vote to succeed Stresemann for the chairmanship. The right-wing of the party have created a special vice-chairmanship position to maintain their influence on the party however. The Reichstag delegation are also able to act independently with Scholz remaining as their leader. Nonetheless, this is still excellent news for us and our relations with the **DVP**. [? if in_grand_coalition: We have noticed a decrease in coalition tensions. ?]

dvp_party_congress.luther.bodyHtml: Hans Luther has surprisingly won the vote to succeed Stresemann for the chairmanship. Luther has support among the industrialists and the left of the party, and commands strong influence over the party. Perhaps he's what the **DVP** needs in order to survive this crisis of German democracy. Luther is particularly supportive of uniting the liberal parties and even for the creation of a broad bourgeois party. [? if in_grand_coalition: He has also voiced support for maintaining the Grand coalition and cooperation between the two parties. ?][? if not in_grand_coalition: He has voiced support for a coalition government involving us and cooperation between the two parties. ?]

dvp_scholz_resign.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Executive Committee Meeting Ernst Scholz, recovering from surgery the past few months due to a resurgence of his health problems, has ultimately resigned in favor of his deputy Eduard Dingeldey, who is now guaranteed to succeed him as chairman. Eduard Dingeldey is one of the first within the **DVP** to support the movement for bourgeois unity and is popular with the youth and bourgeois unity groups that have coalesced on the **DVP**'s left wing, having rallied around Schnell and his efforts last month. Dingeldey is also sufficiently conservative on most political issues—particularly on the question of cooperation with the **SPD**—to gain support from the party's right wing.

dvp_scholz_resign.dingeldey.bodyHtml: Dingeldey's election to the chairmanship represents a triumph for the reform-minded elements on the **DVP**'s left wing and met with strong approval from the movement towards bourgeois unity. However, despite the enthusiasm exhibited by those on the left wing, his election doesn't seem to represent a shift to the left at all and only confirms the party's shift to the right. [? if chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government: Dingeldey doesn't even feel great loyalty toward the Brüning government and believes that the party could only fulfill its mission towards bourgeois concentration after it is freed from the burden of governmental responsibility.?] So far, he has proven to be a weak and ineffectual leader, capitulating to the right wing at every possible opportunity. Furthermore, Dingeldey is not particularly interested in a closer relationship with the **[+ ddp_name +]** and definitely not with us, but rather with parties to the right, such as the **DNVP** and even the **NSDAP**, to transform them into a 'constructive component of the state.' This does not bode well for the future of Weimar democracy.

economic_democracy.bodyHtml: #subtitle: How can we give workers more control over the means of production? = Economic Democracy A key part of the social democratic platform is that workers should have more control over the economy. This can be done either directly at the enterprise level, by giving works councils greater influence over management, or indirectly via the democratic government, by acquiring key industries from the capitalist class and placing them under democratic control. As we control the Labor [? if economic_minister_party == "SPD" : and Economic ?][? if finance_minister_party == "SPD" : and Finance ?] ministries, we can finally begin to implement our long-standing goals. economic_expansion.bodyHtml:
= Economic Expansion
The German economy has been growing steadily for an extended period of time, and has low inflation and unemployment. The government is rewarded by additional tax revenue from the same tax rates. Even the capitalists find that they have little to complain about when it comes to government policies. One downside of this economic growth, however, is the rising risk of inflation.

economic_policy.cut_salaries.subtitleHtml: This will radicalize the middle class. +1 budget
economic_policy.cut_salaries.bodyHtml: We have slashed wages for government employees by about 15%, framing it as a painful, but necessary step towards Germany's economic recovery. However, this justification doesn't persuade many, with many switching their allegiance away from the democratic parties toward the radical **NSDAP**.

economic_policy.empower_workers.titleHtml: Empower workers to take over factories.
economic_policy.empower_workers.subtitleHtml: We can promise to legalize factory occupations, giving the factories over to worker unions. This is highly confrontational, and would likely provoke a reaction from right-wing militants as well as capitalists.
economic_policy.empower_workers.bodyHtml: The capitalists are, predictably, up in arms about our policy of legalizing factory occupations. They call it illegal expropriation, and it is. Nevertheless, it is clear that they have failed, and we must take radical action. Fascists have been taking increasingly violent actions around the occupied factories, calling us thieves and looters. However, the some of the working-class supporters of the fascists have been peeled off, or at least the ones with a sense of class solidarity.

economic_policy.lautenbach_continuation.bodyHtml: Our spending on public works has reduced the need for unemployment insurance and welfare, while also increasing tax receipts through the multiplier effect as the new money circulates in the economy, helping to recover some of our spending. We continue to reinvest most of this new revenue into the program. The economy is finally showing signs of improvement. The bourgeois parties are pleased to see that we’re following through with their economic recovery plan and are offering their full support. The investor confidence generated by our successes has led to a small-scale revival of the private sector, along with capital inflows from foreign investors. [? if not lautenbach_wtb: However, the workers are dissatisfied with our slow pace in raising their wages. ?] [? if in_popular_front or in_left_front: The **KPD** opposes the economic plan, seeing it as a rescue of capitalism rather than a step towards real socialism. ?]

economic_policy.lautenbach_wtb.bodyHtml: We have considerably expanded the public works program, and together with a campaign to raise wages, money is beginning to flow through the economy. economic_policy.nationalize_deficit.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, we do not have the budget to begin buying out industrial facilities. Some are urging for deficit spending in order to purchase factories, while others are encouraging (currently illegal) factory takeovers by workers, or nationalization without compensation. Taking any of these actions would require a vast departure from our previous party stances.

choices.labelHtml: No, we should not do this.

By keeping production going, we can stave off the rising unemployment. ?] [? if nationalization_progress == 1 : The Left argues that this should only be a first step in the socialist transformation of the economy. Eventually, much of the economy must be brought under popular control. ?] [? if nationalization_progress > 1 : We purchase additional underutilized enterprises and run them in a coordinated socialist fashion with the works councils, hiring formerly laid off workers. A significant portion of the economy is now under public control. ?]

economic_sanctions.subtitleHtml: Our military buildup has caused sanctions from France and other countries.
economic_sanctions.bodyHtml:
#tags: event
= Economic Sanctions
In response to our military rearmament in contravention of the Versailles Treaty, the Western Allies have imposed economic sanctions on Germany. The costs of the sanctions are largely borne by the proletariat; the people are facing increasing poverty.

economy_left.bodyHtml: The Christians and Christian Socials have used their influence to advocate for a pro-worker and more ambitious economic policy, as a middle ground between capitalism and socialism. Taxation - Implement more progressive taxes and regulations, to ensure a fair Germany Economic Policy - Implement a 'Social market economy', a middle way between capitalism and socialism Great Depression - A public works program is needed, the people must get back to work

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

economy_moderate.bodyHtml: The Christians and nationalists have begrudgingly come to an agreement, as pragmatism wins the day. The party must represent its diverse base, for the *Volksgemeinschaft*. Taxation - Avoid tax increases at all costs Welfare - Focus on funding the current system, as the poor are suffering Labor - Against any socialistic policies, but neutrality in labor affairs is a key component of the *Volksgemeinschaft*. Great Depression - Experiment with a public works plan, combined with an increase in the money supply

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

economy_oppose.bodyHtml: After opposing the nationalization policy, the **KPD** has commenced a propaganda campaign against us, accusing the **SPD** of yet another perfidy.

economy_right.bodyHtml: The nationalists and agrarians have used their leverage to edit in their economic beliefs into the party program. Taxation - Avoid tax increases at all costs, especially on businesses Welfare - Germany cannot afford welfare and maintain a balanced budget at the same time, one has to go Labor - Strongly against any socialistic policies that benefit the unions Great Depression - Maintain fiscal orthodoxy, productive industries and agriculture must be kept afloat though

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

economy_support.bodyHtml: The **KPD** has gained credit with the workers for enabling many to keep their jobs. Meanwhile, the bourgeois parties and middle-class voters blame the **SPD** for enabling the nationalizations.

education_science.curriculum.bodyHtml: Many socialists believe that education in Germany is not fit for the modern era. Much of the educational system still follows imperial-era traditions of militaristic discipline, and far-right professors and students rule the universities. Nevertheless, there have been strides in bringing working-class children into the schools. What should be the major focus of our new curriculum? # note: education_science is a variable that affects how much education affects economic growth.

Despite the setbacks of the Great War, hyperinflation, and the politicized and reactionary attitudes of many academics, science in the German Republic is still the envy of the world. With a great expansion of funding, we hope to keep it that way, and expand on our achievements.

education_science.structure.titleHtml: Change the structure and funding of education.
education_science.structure.bodyHtml: Education in Germany has traditionally been organized on religious and class lines. Schools are often either Protestant or Catholic (or rarely Jewish), and religious classes are required in most mixed-denomination schools. In addition, the working class has at most eight years of public education in primary and middle schools, while the middle and upper classes have access to private schools and Gymnasiums that prepare students for universities. Thus, the universities tend to be dominated by conservatives and reactionaries, which has negative consequences for bureaucratic recruitment.

choices.labelHtml: Do not change school funding or organization.

einstein_r1.bodyHtml: Albert Einstein is a Nobel Prize-winning scientist, director of the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics, and international advocate for peace. He was a founding member of the German Democratic Party ([? if dstp_formed: whose successor would support him in the election?][? if not dstp_formed: who will support him in the election?]), but has also expressed sympathy towards socialism. He did not wish to run for president, disliking the public nature of campaigning, but we have somehow convinced him that his candidacy will be crucial to the future of Germany and the world. As a Jewish German pacifist, his becoming president would be a repudiation of everything the Nazis stand for. The **[+ ddp_name +]** will endorse Einstein's candidacy.

election_1928.boycott_elections.subtitleHtml: Maybe the other parties will join us.
election_1928.boycott_elections.bodyHtml: There’s little point in participating in an election that’s clearly rigged. The most we can do is boycott the vote—depress turnout and deny Schleicher the legitimacy he desperately needs. But if we aren’t strong enough, we’ll simply hand the **DNEF** a majority government on a silver platter. However, if we commit, we might bring the other anti-Schleicher parties into the boycott as well. Strength in numbers. Are we sure?

election_1928.bruning_oppo.bodyHtml: By refusing to join the grand coalition or tolerating it, we essentially throw the balance of government to the right wing. [? if right_coalition >= 50 and dnvp_ideology == "Radical" : There are enough votes to form a right-wing coalition that includes the **DNVP**. And of course, the **NSDAP** is not interested in coalition government. [? if z_no_confidence: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is voting against us. ?] [? if lvp_no_confidence and lvp_formed: The **LVP** will vote against us. ?] [? if kpd_no_confidence: The **KPD** votes against us. ?] [? if other_no_confidence: The assortment of minor parties are voting against us. ?] In total, [+ no_confidence_votes +]% of the Reichstag is against us. [? if no_confidence_succeeds : We have lost the vote of no confidence. ?]

choices.labelHtml: There will be new elections, which we will try to delay.

election_1928.far_right_braun.bodyHtml: President [+ president +] faces a dilemma. Is it "democratic" to let democracy be destroyed, if the majority of voters have willed it so? Some, even on the left, suggest that the Nazis would not *truly* be as horrific as their platform suggests, and that giving them power would let them discredit themselves in the eyes of the public. Alternatively, [+ president +] could use the emergency powers of the presidency. Article 48 has been used by Hindenburg to promulgate anti-democratic and anti-worker policies; can Article 48 be used for good as well as evil?

choices.labelHtml: We will form an emergency government with [+ president +]'s support.
Let the Nazis form their government.

[+ nsdap_leader +] has made his participation in government contingent on being appointed chancellor. It is up to President [+ president +] to decide. As this is a parliamentary cabinet, [+ president +] is more likely to appoint [+ nsdap_chancellor +].

election_1928.far_right_coup.titleHtml: The far-right parties immediately launch a military coup against us...
election_1928.far_right_coup.bodyHtml: The far-right parties, seeing that we are willing to deny them government by questionably democratic means, have decided that they can only take power by undemocratic means, and have risen up in force against the sitting government. Their numbers are bolstered by the many government workers who are against the prospect of a unified Socialist government. Police and soldiers defect to the **SA** and **Stahlhelm**.

election_1928.far_right_fail.bodyHtml: The reactionary establishment is still very skeptical of the Nazis, so instead, [+ president +] appoints Carl Friedrich Goerdeler, the Mayor of Leipzig, as Chancellor, to try to "tame" the Nazis. With [+ nsdap_leader +] and Hugenberg refusing to join any reformed Brüning cabinet, Hindenburg has sidestepped the issue by turning to the staunchly conservative Goerdeler, who renounced his affiliation with the **DNVP** to accept the post. Upon taking office, however, Goerdeler has yet to secure formal support from the **NSDAP** or [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?]—support he needs, given that the **SPD**[? if not lvp_formed: and likely the **[+ ddp_name +]**?] will not back his government. The coming months will reveal whether Goerdeler can govern—and if the **NSDAP** is truly serious about entering government.

election_1928.far_right_win.bodyHtml: [? if president == "Hindenburg" : President Hindenburg's camarilla ?][? if president != "Hindenburg" and president != "Braun": President [+ president +] ?][? if president == "Braun" : President Braun somehow ?] has decided that [+ nsdap_leader +] must be chancellor [? if president == "Hindenburg": , and the aging president accepts their recommendations. ?][? if president != "Hindenburg" : because it is what the constitution would stipulate. ?]

We can either spend resources to convince the **[+ ddp_name +]** and **DVP** to break away from this arrangement, or to find another governing arrangement. The **DVP** is very reluctant to this step.

election_1928.hindenburg_appoints_papen.bodyHtml: There is no path to a majority government. President Hindenburg is tired of the chaos, and appoints Franz von Papen as chancellor instead of Brüning. Papen is a independent formerly from the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], and is significantly to the right of the majority of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]. Papen is immediately faced with a vote of no confidence, given his unpopularity. However the **SPD** votes, he is guaranteed to fall, due to the unanimous hatred against him from all other parties. New elections have been set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

election_1928.left_coalition_civil_war.bodyHtml: In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing immediately launches a coup attempt. Troops of the **Stahlhelm** and Nazi **SA** enter Berlin and begin clashing with our supporters. Reactionary officers within the Reichswehr have taken their troops out of the barracks and joined them with the **Stahlhelm** to stop us from taking power.

election_1928.left_coalition_impossible.bodyHtml: A far left coalition is impossible.

params.source: coalition_menu

election_1928.left_coalition_no_civil_wa.bodyHtml: In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, discrediting the left and eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. Our task is to prove them wrong. [? if in_left_front_prussia: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** in Prussia too. ?] The **KPD** has taken an abstentionist position with regards to ministries. They claim to be participating as the "loyal opposition" in the worker's government, supporting us from the outside while also running their own propaganda campaigns to turn workers to their side. They seem to expect that we would inevitably fail, and that our failure would benefit them. Whatever their reasoning is, the **SPD** has control over the ministries of government.

election_1928.left_front_prussia.bodyHtml: The coalition negotiations were going relatively smoothly until the **KPD** bought up the topic of a reorganization of the Prussian government to include themselves. Previous United Left governments at the state level have faced Reichsexekution before, [? if president_ideology == "Right" or president == "Hindenburg": and President [+ president +] will almost certainly do so again if we were to form one.?][? if president_ideology == "Moderate": but it's unlikely [+ president +] will do such an anti-democratic act.?][? if president_ideology == "Left": but it's unlikely [+ president +] will repeat Ebert's mistakes.?] Despite this, the **KPD** are firm about their demands to be included. *Something* must be done to restore balance, again.

choices.labelHtml: oh, so now the kpd wants to lecture the spd on ‘betrayal’? that’s hilarious. let’s not forget who really sold out the working class. while the spd was out here trying to protect the weimar republic from fascist takeovers, what was the kpd doing? attacking social democrats, calling them 'class traitors' because we didn’t want to throw democracy in the trash and start a pointless revolution. yeah, ebert made some bad calls with the freikorps, but at least we were trying to keep things from falling apart. what was the kpd doing? cozying up to stalin, pretending like the weimar republic was already dead and going nowhere. you really wanna talk about betrayal? the kpd was too busy playing the martyr, splitting the left vote and giving fascists a clear path to power. congratulations, geniuses. splitting the vote in 1933 while you chant about 'class purity'—real smart move. the spd might’ve had its flaws, but we actually tried to make things better, to hold off the fascists and give the workers a fighting chance. you? you just played into their hands. revolution doesn’t happen by sitting on your high horse, refusing to cooperate and throwing temper tantrums. if anything, the kpd handed us over to hitler on a silver platter. so keep whining about 'betrayal' while you do nothing but tear down the very thing that could’ve stopped the fascists. nice job.

election_1928.left_front_prussia_groko.bodyHtml: We have kicked out the **DVP** and the other bourgeois parties from the existing Grand Coalition to form a United Left Coalition with the **KPD**. The bourgeois parties are infuriated by our betrayal, and any future coalitions with them may be impossible. The Minister-President position is transferred from Braun to[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are going to rule with the **KPD** on both levels of government. The **KPD** has provided a list of objectives for us to complete in parallel to our federal policies.

choices.labelHtml: The **KPD** presents us with a list of demands.

election_1928.new_elections_2.bodyHtml: There is no path to a workable Reichstag majority or minority government. The next elections are set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +]. The people's faith in democracy is shaken by this ordeal. Of course, the Nazis are exploiting the instability to claim that democracy is unworkable, and that Germany needs a strong leader.

election_1928.new_elections_spd.bodyHtml: Since the remaining bourgeois and right-wing parties cannot form a tolerable governing agreement, new elections have been called for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +]. The previous chancellor has resigned, and has been replaced by Heinrich Brüning, also of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], ruling as part of a presidential cabinet. We are seen as responsible for the failure to form a government, and many of our middle-class and even some working-class supporters have deserted the party.

election_1928.no_majority_goerdeler.bodyHtml: The prospect of new elections has proved daunting for the bourgeois parties—and for President Hindenburg himself. Disillusioned with Brüning, Hindenburg and his Camarilla have cast him aside and appointed Carl Friedrich Goerdeler, the Mayor of Leipzig, as Chancellor. With [+ nsdap_leader +] and Hugenberg refusing to join any reformed Brüning cabinet, Hindenburg has sidestepped the issue by turning to the staunchly conservative Goerdeler, who renounced his affiliation with the **DNVP** to accept the post. Upon taking office, however, Goerdeler has yet to secure formal support from the **NSDAP** or [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?]—support he needs, given that the **SPD**[? if not lvp_formed: and likely the **[+ ddp_name +]**?] will not back his government. The coming months will reveal whether Goerdeler can govern—and if the **NSDAP** is truly serious about entering government.

election_1928.no_majority_goerdeler_3.bodyHtml: Despite the prevailing belief that the Nazis have peaked, they remain a dominant force in the Reichstag. Under Schleicher’s influence—having now betrayed Goerdeler—President Hindenburg has appointed [+ nsdap_chancellor +] as Chancellor. The cabinet remains mostly unchanged, save for Wilhelm Frick taking over the Interior Ministry. Schleicher sees this as the only viable path forward. [+ nsdap_leader +] continues to pursue an all-or-nothing strategy, even after the election setback. Schleicher also believes he can shape cabinet policy from within, having already "convinced" Groener to resign and cleared the way for his own appointment as Defense Minister.

election_1928.no_majority_papen_2.bodyHtml: There is, once again, no clear path to a majority government. Nevertheless, Hindenburg has reaffirmed his confidence in the chancellor and granted him permission to continue ruling by decree. With the **NSDAP**'s poor electoral performance, the Camarilla is now convinced the party will be more reasonable in its demands and potentially open to tolerating the Papen cabinet. Negotiations with [+ nsdap_chancellor +] will resume in the coming weeks. However, Schleicher has begun to lose faith in Papen’s ability to reach an understanding with the Nazis—and if these talks fail, it may be the final straw that turns the schemer against yet another of his old friends.

election_1928.no_majority_papen_plus.bodyHtml: However, it's likely that even a coalition of all parties to the right won't receive a majority, not without the support of the antagonistic Center Party. election_1928.no_majority_schleicher.bodyHtml: Predictably, there is no clear path to a majority government, even with the fracturing of the **NSDAP**. Hindenburg is tired of the constant elections and presidential governments, but there is simply no way out. The prospect of negotiations with the Nazi movement remains unobtainable, even with their electoral defeat causing even more defections and the shattering of their party morale.

election_1928.no_majority_schleicher_2.bodyHtml: Schleicher's supporting parties have failed to secure a majority coalition in the Reichstag—at least, not one the chancellor finds acceptable. election_1928.no_majority_spd_right.bodyHtml: There is no path to an obviously workable majority. Since President [+ president +] is unwilling to work with a minority or caretaker **SPD** government, his preferred chancellor is Heinrich Brüning of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], who could lead a [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": "presidential" government?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": [? if center_right_coalition >= 50 and right_coalition < 50: center-right ?][? if center_right_coalition >= 50 and right_coalition >= 50: right ?] coalition ?].

election_1928.no_majority_trev.bodyHtml: Predictably, Treviranus has failed to assemble a majority coalition in support of his bourgeois-right cabinet. Hindenburg, increasingly frustrated and in rapid physical decline, may act more rashly than he did when appointing Papen a year ago. With Papen back in his inner circle after Schleicher’s fall, and his disillusionment with his nationalist allies deepening, the future grows more uncertain. We don't know what Hindenburg is planning on as a last resort. Once again, the question stands before us: do we choose to tolerate this cabinet? That is for you to decide. The new Reichstag will convene on [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], Week [+ next_reichstag_week +].

election_1928.popular_front_civil_war.bodyHtml: In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing immediately launches a coup attempt. Troops of the **Stahlhelm** and Nazi **SA** enter Berlin and immediately begin clashing with our supporters! Reactionary officers within the Reichswehr have taken their troops out of the barracks and joined them with the **Stahlhelm** to stop us from taking power. The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] manages to diffuse some of the hostility from the Reichswehr and the **Stahlhelm**, but fail to prevent the outbreak of fighting. We are forced to fight on the same side as the **KPD**, whether we want to or not.

election_1928.popular_front_no_civil_war.bodyHtml: In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that the Popular Front government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, discrediting the left and center and eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. Our task is to prove them wrong. [? if in_popular_front_prussia: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** in Prussia too. ?] The **KPD** has taken an abstentionist position with regards to ministries. They claim to be participating as the "loyal opposition" within the Popular Front government, supporting us from the outside while also running their own propaganda campaigns to turn workers to their side. They seem to expect that the Popular Front would inevitably fail, and that our failure would benefit them.
