election_1928.popular_front_prussia.bodyHtml: The coalition negotiations were going relatively smoothly until the **KPD** bought up the topic of a reorganization of the Prussian government to include themselves. [? if in_grand_coalition_prussia: This means that we are forced to kick the **DVP** from the ruling coalition to accommodate. ?][? if in_weimar_coalition_prussia and not in_minority_weimar_coalition_prussia: This means that we are to add the **KPD** to the ruling Weimar coalition, to form an Übergroß coalition. ?][? if in_weimar_coalition_prussia and in_minority_weimar_coalition_prussia: This means that we are to add the **KPD** to the ruling Weimar coalition, to form a majority Popular Front coalition. ?] *Something* must be done to restore balance, again.

choices.labelHtml: Oh, you think the SPD betrayed the working class? That’s rich coming from the KPD, the self-proclaimed “vanguard of the proletariat” that spent more time attacking socialists than fighting fascists. Let’s talk about the real betrayal, comrade. While the SPD was trying to stabilize the republic and fend off fascist coups like the Kapp Putsch, where was the KPD? Oh, right—screaming about how social democrats were “social fascists” because they wouldn’t dismantle democracy overnight. You act like the SPD didn’t have its flaws. Sure, Ebert called in the Freikorps to crush the Spartacist uprising. Not a good look, but let’s not pretend the KPD’s adventurism and refusal to cooperate didn’t weaken the left. While the SPD was defending trade unions and passing labor reforms, the KPD was cozying up to Moscow and declaring the Weimar Republic dead on arrival. And don’t get me started on the KPD splitting the left vote in 1933. Was “class purity” worth letting Hitler come to power? But sure, keep calling the SPD sellouts while you play revolutionaries and fail to realize that burning the whole system down doesn’t magically lead to socialism. If anything, it just opens the door for reactionaries to walk right in. The SPD wasn’t perfect, but at least they tried to hold the line. The KPD? A textbook case of “owning the libs” gone horribly wrong. Congratulations, comrade, your ideological purity cost us the Republic. Hope you’re proud.

election_1928.popular_front_prussia_grok.bodyHtml: We have kicked out the **DVP** from the government, and formed a Popular Front. The **DVP** is infuriated by our betrayal and any future coalitions with them may be impossible. The Minister-President position is transferred from Braun to[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. He is accepted with great reluctance to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and welcomed by the **KPD**. The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are going to rule with the **KPD** on both levels of government. The **KPD** has provided a list of objectives for us to complete in parallel to our federal policies. [? if president_ideology == "Right" or president == "Hindenburg": [+ president +] might object to this coalition, and may perform a Reichsexekution on our Prussian government, if we were to become too radical in our actions.?]

election_1928.schleicher_dsu.titleHtml: Schleicher invites the **DSU** into cabinet?
election_1928.schleicher_dsu.bodyHtml: Despite their addition barely doing much to grant Schleicher a majority, it signals a major step toward Schleicher's goal of integrating "favorable" Nazis into the state—as he acknowledges that this is how much he's going to get. Their poor electoral performance will grant them few cabinet posts, but there remains substantial risks in letting the Nazis govern. We could attempt to use our relations with the chancellor to prevent this, but he'll demand much concessions in return.

election_1928.schleicher_dsu_nay.subtitleHtml: This is a point of no return.
election_1928.schleicher_dsu_nay.bodyHtml: Exploiting our unusually good relations with the chancellor, we have moved to strike a deal with him to block Nazi entry into the cabinet. We have threatened mass action by organized labor and the withdrawal of the Reichsbanner from his plans. Yet Schleicher sees greater advantage in aligning with the Nazis regardless, and we are negotiating from a position of weakness. What shall we give up?

election_1928.schleicher_dsu_nay_2.titleHtml: The **DSU** is kept away from government!
election_1928.schleicher_dsu_nay_2.subtitleHtml: The Center Party has been flirting with a return to governance.
election_1928.schleicher_dsu_nay_2.bodyHtml: Schleicher has suspended talks with the **DSU** by deliberately creating an impasse over control of the Interior Ministry. In the meantime, the absence of Nazis in the cabinet has made it tolerable for the Center Party to return to government, with Adam Stegerwald securing the Labor Ministry and the nominal Vice Chancellorship, alongside other members claiming the Transport and Justice portfolios. The **BVP** is also granted the Postal Ministry. [? if z_leader == "Kaas": Schleicher has also secured Ludwig Kaas's backing by promising the immediate negotiation of a Reichskonkordat with the Vatican. ?] [? if old_prussia_leader == "Schleicher": The Prussian Reichskommissar post is also handed from Schleicher to Goerdeler—a signal that Schleicher has genuinely abandoned Papen's scheme for state centralization, and gestures toward an eventual return to democratic governance once stability is restored. Braun is overjoyed at this, and argues that only a break with Schleicher would change his mind. ?] The liberals and minor bourgeois parties have also rallied behind Schleicher once again. As part of our arrangement, he acknowledges the **SPD**'s need to remain in opposition—a necessary measure, as a **Communist** surge is an outcome neither of us desires.

election_1928.schleicher_dsu_yay.subtitleHtml: Schleicher will moderate their excesses, it's still a presidential government after all.
election_1928.schleicher_dsu_yay.bodyHtml: Wilhelm Frick is nominated to the Interior Ministry[? if old_prussia_leader == "Schleicher": in both the Reich and Prussia, with the latter now under the control of [+ prussia_leader +], appointed as commissioner?]. Gregor Strasser takes the vice-chancellorship—a title without power. At the Nazis’ insistence, Hjalmar Schacht is named to the Economic Ministry as an independent. Hans Kerrl, a Nazi parliamentarian, receives the post of Minister without Portfolio. Schleicher blocks Nazi claims to the Labor Ministry, unwilling to provoke organized labor and still hoping to bring Adam Stegerwald—and the Center Party—into his coalition.

election_1928.schleicher_labor.titleHtml: The ADGB falls under state influence.
election_1928.schleicher_labor.subtitleHtml: Class collaborationism will undermine the workers' power.
election_1928.schleicher_labor.bodyHtml: We have convinced the ADGB to appoint some sketchy pro-Schleicher unionists to many top positions in the organization. Only time will tell what Schleicher will instruct his followers to do, but we can guess it has something to do with class solidarity for the goal of Germany's rearmament. The working class is not entirely won over to the chancellor yet, and we stand to lose significant numbers of them to the **KPD**.

election_1928.schleicher_majority_coalit.titleHtml: Schleicher forms a majority government with only the **DNEF**.
election_1928.schleicher_majority_coalit.bodyHtml: Immediately after the election, the chancellor abandoned both dialogue and the appearance of cordiality with the other political parties. Power is his, and he intends to keep it. Without the constraints of the parliamentary system, he can do whatever he pleases. Only the collapse of his delicately built house of cards could topple a **DNEF** majority government.

election_1928.schleicher_reichsbanner.titleHtml: The Reichsbanner is integrated into the state.
election_1928.schleicher_reichsbanner.bodyHtml: The Reichsbanner has been largely disarmed, with Schleicher promising increased funding for the police to maintain order in the streets. The **SPD** is demoralized, as many Reichsbanner members defect to the **KPD** and their **RFB**. We are now compelled to back the Reichswehr's auxiliaries in their campaigns against the **Communists**.

election_1928.social_catholic_coalition_.titleHtml: Can we form a Social-Christian Coalition?
election_1928.social_catholic_coalition_.bodyHtml: We have enough votes to form a "Social-Christian Coalition" government consisting of the **SPD** and the **CVP**. However, whether the **[+ z_party_name +]**—filled with nationalist and staunchly anti-Marxist elements—would ever truly accept such a coalition is another matter entirely. Still, the mere fact that they are even willing to engage in talks is an encouraging early sign.

election_1928.social_catholic_coalition_.bodyHtml: We have somehow convinced the **[+ z_party_name +]** to enter in a Social-Christian Coalition with us! The nationalist elements within the **[+ z_party_name +]** are disgusted by this, never actually expecting the negotiations to have a successful conclusion. election_1928.taming_abandoned.bodyHtml: i'm too lazy to implement this right now, anyway [+ chancellor +] is ousted and replaced by good ol bruning

election_1928.thalmann_chancellor.bodyHtml: With great reluctance, President [+ president +] appoints [+ chancellor +] as chancellor. Immediately, [+ chancellor +] goes to work building a "Soviet Germany": consolidating as much power as possible in the **KPD**, purging state institutions of anti-communists, and sending street fighters against the "enemies of the people". In response to [+ chancellor +] being appointed Chancellor, the right-wing forces launches almost immediately launch an attempted coup. Troops of the **Stahlhelm** and Nazi **SA** enter Berlin and immediately begin clashing with our supporters! Reactionary officers within the Reichswehr have taken their troops out of the barracks and joined them with the **Stahlhelm** to stop the **KPD** from taking power. We are forced to be on the same side as the **KPD**, whether we want to or not.

election_1928.toleration_bruning.bodyHtml: We have decided to tolerate Brüning's government. This means that we will vote against no-confidence votes to make sure they fail, but also that we will not be directly participating as ministers in the government. Thus, we can prevent a new election and stop the far right from entering government.

embezzle_2.titleHtml: Meet with the Brüning cabinet, and lobby for state financing toward the Prussian government, with the goal of securing Hindenburg's reelection.
embezzle_2.subtitleHtml: [? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?][? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?] member and Vice-Chancellor Hermann Dietrich has shown a friendliness toward us. +3 resources
embezzle_2.bodyHtml: In a meeting with Chancellor Brüning, Defense Minister Groener, General Schleicher, Finance Minister and Vice-Chancellor Hermann Dietrich, and our own Carl Severing, discussions focused on the upcoming presidential election and the organization of an effective propaganda campaign for Hindenburg. Severing outlined the threat that Nazism—particularly the **SA**—posed to state authority and emphasized the election's critical role in keeping the Nazis in check. All present agreed that a decisive victory for Hindenburg and a campaign free from violent disturbances would greatly accelerate Germany’s economic recovery and domestic political stabilization. Achieving this, however, would require the use of state funds. Dietrich himself passionately advocated for this, having secretly transferred 1.8 million marks to Severing and the Prussian government with the understanding that the funds would be distributed among various pro-Hindenburg organizations in the State of Prussia. This approach allowed Dietrich and the government to support pro-Hindenburg groups outside the right-wing United Hindenburg Committees.

embezzle_3.titleHtml: We will use the state to finance Hindenburg's reelection.
embezzle_3.bodyHtml: We have contacted Gunther Gereke, [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **CNBLP**?] member responsible for raising funds for the Hindenburg campaign, and provided him with a sizable donation to secure and disburse five million marks to the campaign—though some of these funds have been diverted to his own party. This development has pleased both Schleicher and Hindenburg himself, who never expected us to prioritize state funds for a political campaign over feeding children. Not that the public will ever find out.

emergency_act_bruning.titleHtml: Act for the Protection of the Economy and Finance
emergency_act_bruning.subtitleHtml: Chancellor [+ chancellor +] introduces his most controversial act yet.
emergency_act_bruning.bodyHtml: = Act for the Protection of the Economy and Finance To eliminate the growing deficit in the national budget, Brüning has introduced an act that enforces sweeping government spending cuts while implementing a special “crisis tax” and raising various other taxes. To justify the hardships imposed on German society, Brüning coupled its promulgation with a public appeal, urging Germany’s international creditors to acknowledge the sacrifices demanded of the German people by providing relief from the nation’s “intolerable” reparations burden. The act is deeply unpopular, provoking widespread outrage across German society and fueling the intense agitation from the Nazis against the bourgeois parties, pressuring them to break with Brüning over the matter. The [? if not lvp_formed: [? if dvp_exist: **DVP** and?] **[+ ddp_name +]** [? if dvp_exist: are?][? if not dvp_exist: is?]?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP** is?] particularly affected, as they're the [? if not lvp_formed and dvp_exist:parties?][? if lvp_formed or not dvp_exist:party?] representing the social groups most impacted by these changes. Brüning's failure to consult [? if not lvp_formed:either party?][? if lvp_formed:them?] before introducing the bill has left the [? if not lvp_formed:liberal parties?][? if lvp_formed: liberals?] powerless to amend some of the most severe provisions, such as cuts to civil servants' salaries and an increase in the national sales tax. With the bourgeois-right holding a majority coalition, it is now up to them to resolve their differences if they wish to prevent their government from collapsing.

emergency_decree_bruning.bodyHtml: = Second Emergency Decree for Economy and Finance Intended to eliminate the growing deficit in the national budget, the emergency decree enacts sweeping cuts to government spending while introducing a special “crisis tax” and raising various other taxes. To justify the hardships imposed on German society, Brüning coupled its promulgation with a public appeal, urging Germany’s international creditors to acknowledge the sacrifices demanded of the German people by providing relief from the nation’s “intolerable” reparations burden. The decree is deeply unpopular, provoking widespread outrage across German society and fueling the intense agitation from the far-right against the bourgeois parties that still haven't split from Brüning's government, particularly the [? if not lvp_formed: [? if dvp_exist: **DVP** and ?]**[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?], as they're the [? if not lvp_formed and dvp_exist:parties?][? if lvp_formed or not dvp_exist:party?] representing the social groups most impacted by these changes. Brüning's failure to consult [? if not lvp_formed:either party?][? if lvp_formed:them?] beforehand has left the [? if not lvp_formed:liberal parties?][? if lvp_formed: liberals?] powerless to amend some of the most severe provisions, such as cuts to civil servants' salaries and an increase in the national sales tax. [? if not lvp_formed and not bourgeois_parliament and not liberal_parliament and dvp_exist: The already fragile alliance between the **DVP** and Brüning appears to be on the verge of collapse—an outcome that could seal the fate of his government. ?]

choices.labelHtml: There will be new elections, which we will try to delay.

empower_workers.titleHtml: Empower workers to take over factories.
empower_workers.subtitleHtml: We can promise to legalize factory occupations, giving the factories over to worker unions. This is highly confrontational, and would likely provoke a reaction from right-wing militants as well as capitalists.
empower_workers.bodyHtml: The capitalists are, predictably, up in arms about our policy of legalizing factory occupations. They call it illegal expropriation, and it is. Nevertheless, it is clear that they have failed, and we must take radical action. Fascists have been taking increasingly violent actions around the occupied factories, calling us thieves and looters. However, the some of the working-class supporters of the fascists have been peeled off, or at least the ones with a sense of class solidarity.

enabling_act.titleHtml: [+ nsdap_chancellor +] attempts to pass an enabling act.
enabling_act.bodyHtml: = Enabling Act Together with the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnf_formed: **DNF**?], and the dictatorial powers offered by the Reichstag Fire Decree, the far-right have won more than an outright majority. The law is considered a constitutional amendment, requiring two-thirds of the Reichstag to approve the bill. The **Communists** are de-facto banned, and many **SPD** deputies are imprisoned under the powers of the Reichstag Fire Decree. The Center Party is the deciding factor, seeking to save the Catholic population from persecution and a second Kulturkampf. **SA** men are positioned inside and outside the chamber, an intense atmosphere of fear settling over the nominally constitutional Center Party. Wirth and Brüning argue against the bill, while the majority of the party is in favor of it. The Nazis have promised constitutional safeguards, but have refused to put it in writing as requested by Hugenberg and the Center Party.

choices.labelHtml: The Center Party votes for the enabling act!
The Center Party votes against the enabling act!

enabling_act_2.subtitleHtml: It doesn't matter in the end.
enabling_act_2.bodyHtml: A concordat with the Vatican is signed months later, protecting the millions of German Catholics from potential Nazi persecution. The **NSDAP** becomes the sole political party. Franz von Papen is ousted from Prussia, remaining in the powerless position of Vice Chancellor. Hugenberg is forced to resign. Efforts to tame the Nazis have failed; their relentless consolidation of power leaves only the aging Hindenburg to check their unlimited authority. Schleicher is murdered during the Night of Long Knives, Papen delivers his infamous 'Marburg Speech' before resigning, and after Hindenburg’s death at 86 years old, Germany is lost.

The proposal is dead, although the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**, **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] are not pleased.

ending_slides.civil_war_long.bodyHtml: As the frontlines settle, a republican state—committed to the continuation of Weimar Germany—takes root in the West, while a newly formed Ruhr Red Army establishes **Communist** control over the Rhineland. The fragile alliance of far-right forces soon fractures, with the **Stahlhelm** and the **SA** turning against one another in violent internal conflict. Ernst Röhm eventually reduces [+ nsdap_leader +] to a puppet, seizing full control and unleashing unspeakable atrocities against the local Jewish and Polish populations in the territories under their control. A renewed offensive by republican forces exploits the chaos on the Right, culminating in the defeat of the reactionary militias. However, a brutal campaign continues in the Ruhr, where every town exacts a death toll of thousands. By 1936, Germany remains fractured. Poland has seized the moment to occupy parts of East Prussia and Silesia, citing the protection of ethnic Poles. Meanwhile, the French dispatch a "peacekeeping" force into the Rhineland. In the end, it is not so much a victory for the Republic as it is a decisive collapse of the far-right. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, but the French reoccupation of the Rhineland has complicated efforts. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own.

params.code: state.flags['civil_war_seen'] && state.flags['long_war'] && ! (state.flags['president'] == "Hergt" && state.flags['chancellor'] == "Seldte")

ending_slides.civil_war_long_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - The Black Spot of Europe Despite the Republic’s paper victory, revanchist sentiment over the loss of Eastern and Western territories, coupled with mass radicalization from the staggering death toll, destruction, hyperinflation, widespread hunger, and the absence of meaningful foreign aid, has deeply discredited the political establishment. Under pressure from the Reichswehr, martial law remains in place for years, with the military increasingly intruding into civilian governance. By 1939, a global recession—triggered by escalating instability across Europe and threats from the Soviet Union—obliterates the reconstruction progress made by the ruling **SPD**, plunging the country into yet another crisis. Following a March on Berlin, a "Third Positionist" regime seizes power, led by a new political party composed of former Nazis and disillusioned socialists. Germany pivots toward autarky and radical self-reliance, sealing its borders to foreigners. The regime earns the moniker "Black Spot of Europe," ruling from 1940 to 1996. During this period, it successfully coerces the withdrawal of foreign troops from the Rhineland and reclaims its lost eastern territories—including the Polish Corridor—in 1946, capitalizing on Poland's distraction with the Soviet threat and the shifting priorities of the Western Allies as they fight war with Japan. Today, Germany remains largely isolated from the rest of the world, with the successor to the dictatorship of old being not much better, being ruled by oligarchs and the wealthy who are relicts of the past regime. Now, the task of Social Democracy is to prepare for the next election. The incumbent government of Wolfgang Schäuble is unpopular, and we stand to gain. Perhaps the next government will have a socialist plurality.

ending_slides.civil_war_long_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - A European Future In exchange for the return of the Rhineland and the lifting of its post-war reparations burden, Germany is compelled to enter a defensive pact with France and Britain. With assistance from the League of Nations and the United States, the so-called "Morgenthau Plan", funded by the Western Allies, successfully facilitates German reconstruction and ushers in a Wirtschaftswunder under the leadership of Chancellor Konrad Adenauer. By the end of the decade, the economies of the West become increasingly interconnected. Further integration into a nascent "European Union"—featuring free trade and the free movement of people—is negotiated by the internationalist **SPD** and the **LVP**. Renewed Soviet threats to Eastern European nations like Finland and Poland, alongside the democratization of Austria and Italy, have once again galvanized a united European response to Bolshevik aggression. Today, Germany remains a pillar of a federal European Union stretching from Lisbon to Athens. Now, the task of Social Democracy is to prepare for the next election. The incumbent government of Klaus Schwab is unpopular, and we stand to gain. Perhaps the next government will have a socialist plurality.

ending_slides.civil_war_win.bodyHtml: Following a brief civil war between republican forces and the far-right, we’ve been given a blank slate to rebuild Germany on a truly democratic and social foundation—free, for now, from the fear of reactionary reprisals. A minor coup attempt by General Bredow is foiled, and with it, the Reichswehr is finally brought under the banner of the republic. But it is not all sunshine and rainbows. The civil war has devastated countless lives, and the costs of reconstruction and welfare have triggered the return of hyperinflationary nightmares. Hunger now exceeds levels seen during the Great Depression, and many are already growing disillusioned with their supposed saviors. Though the reactionary and far-right forces were defeated on the battlefield, it's only a matter of years before a new right-wing movement emerges and takes root among the weary and discontented populace. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, but the French reoccupation of the Rhineland has complicated efforts. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?].. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own.

ending_slides.civil_war_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - A False Victory The fracturing of the **SPD** into the **SVD** and the **SED** in the wake of post-war optimism deeply divided the German left. As in 1920, leftist disunity once again produced a scenario where a "New Weimar Coalition"—composed of the **SVD**, LVP, and **CSRP**—was unable to secure a majority. This led to repeated snap elections, ultimately fueling another resurgence of extremism. It was only through the formation of the German National Unity Front—a broad alliance of all bourgeois parties—and the election of Otto Gessler as president that Germany finally escaped its political deadlock. The resulting coalition of the **ZCA**, **LVP**, and **DBP** emerged as the new “natural governing bloc,” as persistent ideological rifts continued to paralyze the left. The **SVD**, increasingly marginalized, was at times compelled to tolerate these centrist cabinets in the name of stability—abandoning its Marxist roots in the process and ceding leadership of the left to the more radical **SED**. Only with the third wave of democratization in the 1990s did the long-divided German left begin to reunify. The gradual moderation and eventual merger of the **SED** and the **SVD** culminated in the formation of the **VSPD**, which at last returned to government after decades in opposition.

ending_slides.civil_war_win_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - The Socialist Dream Despite the blank slate granted to the **SPD** to reshape Germany in its image, the country has faced relentless challenges: the hyperinflationary crisis of the 1930s, the resurgence of the far-right in the 1940s, and a series of counterproductive bans that only emboldened reactionary forces. Yet, step by step, Germany rebuilds. Even following the **SPD**’s splintering into the **SED** and **SVD** due to foreign policy disputes in the 1940s, both parties cooperated to construct a comprehensive welfare state—one that could stand alongside the Nordic models in its scope and ambition. The bourgeois opposition—comprising the **ZCA**, **LVP**, and **DBP**—was relegated to a state of permanent irrelevance, unable to halt the wave of reforms: the rise of workplace councils, sweeping nationalizations, and the assertion of state control over the Reichsbank. However, the stagflation of the 1970s marked the beginning of the end for traditional leftist dominance. As the middle class expanded at the expense of the working class, the foundations of class politics began to erode—giving rise to a new multiparty system and ending the era of unchallenged socialist rule.

ending_slides.dnef_win.bodyHtml: [? if president != "Hindenburg": During [+ president +]’s term as President, the?][? if president == "Hindenburg": Following the death of Hindenburg from old age and Schleicher due to health complications, General Hammerstein is elected in a landslide in a heavily rigged election. The?] hated Weimar system is dismantled, and a new March Constitution is passed near-unanimously. The Reichstag is reduced to a rubber stamp for the regime. Germany formally adopts a presidential system, with both the Presidency and Chancellorship held by various **DNEF** members, who rise through bribes, patronage, and backroom deals. Corruption is endemic. Elections are stage-managed, dominated by fraud and manipulation. The **SPD** is never formally banned and endures as a powerless "loyal opposition," unable to influence national policy. Though tolerated, they face constant harassment and suppression by the ruling regime. Despite the regime’s authoritarianism, social discontent remains subdued. A Wirtschaftswunder—an economic miracle—emerges as the Great Depression fades. In 1935, Germany secures equality in armaments at Geneva and begins agitating for the return of the Polish Corridor separating East Prussia from the Reich. In 1942, a "special military operation" is launched to seize Danzig. Poland refuses to cede territory, and with backing from France and a hesitant Britain, enters a state of war. A puppet regime is installed in occupied territories. A limited French offensive into the Saar fails, and the Western Allies remain at war only on paper. Sensing German isolation, the Soviet Union invades eastern Poland, citing abuses against native Belarusians and Ukrainians under military occupation. A new German–Soviet war erupts. Defense Minister Hammerstein cultivates ties with the "Little Entente"—states facing their own Soviet-backed revolutionary threats. An unofficial Mitteleuropa bloc emerges, with Germany at its core, squeezed between a Western capitalist bloc and the Eastern state-socialist order. In 1946, the war ends in stalemate. Poland is partitioned at the Vistula River. Romania and Bulgaria fall under Communist control. Western Europe grows closer to the United States, and a tripolar global order takes shape. By the late 1960s, economic stagnation and renewed domestic unrest—driven by the Red Army Faction and neo-Nazi agitation—force Chancellor Kurt Georg Kiesinger to begin relaxing the dictatorship. The corporatist house of cards that had maintained the regime's stability for decades begins to crumble as independent unions discreetly form. However, Germany remains far from a free and democratic country, the Reichswehr maintains constant watch over politics, exercising real control behind the scenes. Today, the **DNEF** operates as a conventional big-tent political party. Though still marred by corruption, it remains the third major force in German politics, behind the **CVP** and **VSPD**. The Mitteleuropa bloc persists as a fragile intermediary between the West and the East—neither liberal nor socialist, but something in between.

ending_slides.left_win.bodyHtml: The United Front Government, under President [? if president == "Rosenfeld": Kurt Rosenfeld?][? if president == "Thälmann": Ernst Thälmann?][? if president == "Münzenberg": Willi Münzenberg?][? if president == "Ossietzky": Carl von Ossietzky?][? if president == "Mann": Heinrich Mann?], withstood everything thrown its way—capitalist treachery, institutional sabotage, and constant subversion by reactionaries. In 1937, after winning a second election and slightly increasing its majority, the government faced a coup attempt led by the reactionary elements of the Reichswehr and increasingly radicalized nationalists and far-right forces. The coup failed. The abortive putsch was crushed by the proletarian masses and shattered the political landscape of Weimar. The far left of the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]—splinters from their parties who maintained ambiguity towards the coup—split off to form the **RDP** and **CSRP**, both of which soon joined the United Front. With the bourgeois center increasingly marginalized, the botched coup gave the United Front the momentum needed to finally purge the Republic of reactionary forces and initiate a socialist economy. Eventually a constitutional convention was called to begin a Socialist Republic.

ending_slides.left_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - Spartakus Rises Again The convention is called, and with overwhelming support, it dismantles the old bourgeois institutions. At last, after all these years, the German Soviet Republic is formed—and this time, "All Power to the Soviets" is more than just a slogan. The **SPD** takes the lead in constructing the Soviet Republic. Though the process is complex and at times byzantine, born of compromise among many factions, it is unmistakably revolutionary. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. In a world largely hostile to socialism, we stand as a shining example: the economy is socialized, and economic control is placed directly in the hands of the proletariat. The Soviet Union remains distant, as does the West. We emerge as a beacon of socialism amid the growing tensions of a Cold War—between the **Soviets**, an authoritarian Kuomintang-led China, and an independent India on one side, and the capitalist West on the other. We maintain a strictly neutral stance, offering principled opposition to both blocs. In doing so, we inspire many nations to follow our political and geopolitical path. Our shining socialist republic manages to survive, until the end of an inconclusive Cold War in détente. As a key neutral player throughout the Cold War, we reap the benefits—becoming a center for dialogue and commerce. With the arrival of détente, more and more nations join us in non-alignment. All is not golden though. Our republic is prone to infighting, as the various proletarian groups represented in the economy often clash over resource allocation. Additionally, our council-centered system faces criticism for its inability to adapt to modern conditions, with growing signs of bureaucratic inefficiency. Nevertheless, as we enter the 2000s, the Deutsche Räterepublik remains a bastion of socialism and orthodoxy. Our politics, culture, and economy are still deeply proletarian. Albeit third way and even capitalist parties remain on our right—and hardline vanguardists on our left—the **SPD** and its successor parties maintain a firm hold on the Republic.

ending_slides.left_win_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - The Vanguard Takes the Helm As the Constitutional Assembly convenes, it is gradually decided that the new socialist state will take inspiration from the Russian Revolution and the Soviet Union’s vanguardist model. The **SPD**—whether convinced, divided, or simply powerless to stop the shift—accepts it. The two **socialist** parties rapidly merge into a single party that monopolizes power in the new state, while allowing some minor parties to remain as bloc parties. The **Socialist Unity Party** (**SED**) takes the helm. The regime immediately begins aligning with the Soviet Union and puts forth its first *Gosplans*. Soon, the State becomes a member of the Eastern Bloc. World War II breaks out as a massive conflict between the capitalist and communist worlds. It ends with a vast Eastern Bloc stretching from Lisbon to Arkhangelsk. A Cold War begins against the United States, Britain, Kuomintang-led China, and the French government in exile. The **SED** assumes an important role in the Soviet Bloc as the leader of the second most industrialized country. Germany experiences decades of growth under the economic plans, calming most dissent within the country. To combat the remaining opposition, the Party establishes the Stasi, inspired by the Soviet Union’s NKVD. Alongside the Soviet Bloc, the Soviet Republic of Germany largely wins the Cold War. Key factors include the collapse of European Africa, the Chinese Civil War ending with an unaligned socialist China, and the United States and Britain shifting towards isolationism. However, by the 1990s, economic problems worsen: inflation rises, corruption grows, and the People’s Democracies begin to decay. Dissent grows to levels even the harshest Stasi measures fail to contain. Amid these conditions, General Secretary Gorbachev of the Soviet Union initiates a controlled transition toward genuine democratic socialism inspired by the Chinese model. Today, Germany holds its first elections under this new system. The political spectrum is dazzling and complex, though heavily weakened and under state supervision. The quasi-capitalist **CNVP** and **LSV** form a coalition against the socialists and are gaining momentum. New socialist parties emerge as the **SED** fractures between hardliners and reformers. Perhaps the next government will have a **SEPD** majority.

ending_slides.monarchy_win.bodyHtml: With the Nazi movement in decline following the end of the economic depression and an internal leadership struggle, and with the election of the nationalist Hergt alongside the appointment of the **Stahlhelm**'s Seldte, it appears that reaction has triumphed over revolution. Although various neo-Nazi splinters emerged after [+ nsdap_leader +]’s final descent into delusion, the ideology itself remains irrevocably discredited. Following the peaceful return of the Saarland via referendum in 1935, the Reichswehr suppressed an attempted uprising by the **SA** and purged the remaining Nazi elements from government. In the heavily managed 1936 elections, under the watch of "electoral monitors", the monarchist parties secured a manufactured mandate. Soon after, a secret rearmament program was launched, and shortly after, the crowning of Wilhelm III—blessed by his father—restores Germany's constitutional monarchy. With ambitions focused on reclaiming lost territories in the East and Alsace-Lorraine in the West, Germany began courting allies for its revisionist aims. The restoration of Habsburg rule in Austria and the toppling of Mussolini in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III drastically altered the balance of power in Europe. When Poland refused to return former imperial lands, the British, and more reluctantly the French, turned a blind eye to escalating German border skirmishes. The Communist victory in Spain, and the wave of revolutions it triggered across the continent, forced the imperial powers to prioritize containment of the Soviet threat above all else. Africa remains colonized until the 1980s and 90s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance evolved into a global axis of its own, encompassing numerous Communist regimes worldwide. Today, Germany is a dominant party state, ruled by the elites of the **DNVP**, who have maintained control for nearly a century. Although dissatisfaction with the monarchy and the growing strength of the opposition have forced some minor reforms, each new election consistently delivers a majority for the incumbent coalition. However, cracks are beginning to show in the system. New, young, and popular **SPD** leaders are making inroads despite state repression, with Sahra Wagenknecht being the first to achieve a significant victory, having been elected Minister-President of Thuringia. Perhaps the next government will have a mere nationalist plurality.

ending_slides.papen_win.bodyHtml: Despite being hated by nearly 90% of the population, Franz von Papen's surprising victory—secured through the backing of the elites and the Reichswehr—brought him to power in a deeply fractured Germany. However, consolidating that power proved difficult. Despite the eradication of organized communist and social democratic resistance, the Ruhr remains ablaze with unrest. Meanwhile, ongoing conflict between Papen and Kurt von Schleicher, who still maintains significant influence within the military, further destabilizes his regime. Papen's nationalist foreign policy has won him few friends abroad, and his goal of unshackling Germany from the chains of Versailles remains distant. In an effort to restore order, Papen forms a "National Regeneration Government", rooted in conservative Christian values, militarism, and monarchism. Following the death of President Paul von Hindenburg, Wilhelm III is crowned as a figurehead monarch, while real power remains concentrated in the hands of the political elite and industrial magnates. Germany is transformed into a dictatorship, with the "New State" envisioned by Papen centralizing authority in the executive. After a period of economic recovery in the late 1930s, Papen turns his attention toward foreign policy, seeking to broker an entente with the French to combat Bolshevism in the East. When these efforts failed, he turned to cooperate with Austrofascist Austria and Mussolini’s Italy, who remained among Germany’s few continental allies. However by the 1950s, however, the regime begins to decay. Corruption, unrest, and economic stagnation—coupled with Papen’s death—trigger a political thaw. The "Prussian Spring" ushers in a wave of democratic reforms, but the entrenched elites of the old system work to protect their interests. The military retains an active and unofficial role in politics, making it impossible for the reconstituted **SPD** to assume power without risking a coup. Africa remains colonized until the 1980s and 90s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a Soviet Union surviving intact but slightly liberalized, serving as the key pillar in a global alliance encompassing the Communist regimes worldwide. Today, Germany is a multiparty democracy, following the ousting of the successor conservative party founded by figures of the former regime. Yet all is not well in the republic. Friedrich Merz, now President, has drawn criticism for invoking nostalgia for the old system, sparking fears of democratic backsliding and concentration of power in favor of the oligarchs. Now, the task of Social Democracy is to prepare for the next presidential election. Our Sahra Wagenknecht is considering running for another non-consecutive term; perhaps she is our only hope to topple Merz.

ending_slides.taming_lose.bodyHtml: With the appointment of [+ chancellor +] and the passage of the Enabling Act, Germany is lost. Schleicher, increasingly sidelined by health issues, fades into irrelevance. Following[? if president == "Hindenburg": President Hindenburg's and?] his[? if president == "Hindenburg": own?] death, General Werner von Blomberg assumes the presidency, marking the end of the failed taming experiment. The bourgeois establishment that once collaborated with the Nazis is purged en masse during the Night of the Long Knives and offer no serious resistance thereafter, aside from the failed Oster conspiracy in 1938 by former Schleicher loyalists.

ending_slides.weimar_mega_win.titleHtml: The Weimar Republic Marches On
ending_slides.weimar_mega_win.bodyHtml: At the turn of the decade, the Great Depression and widespread disillusionment with the Weimar system left few optimists in Germany. Yet, the Republic—forged by the will of the people all those years ago—has weathered a crisis of unprecedented proportions. Social Democracy endures, as do its detractors. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, choosing to forget and forgive. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own.

ending_slides.weimar_mega_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - One and a Half Party system The **SPD**'s rule over Germany has endured for decades, following its sublime management of the Great Depression and successful expansion of support beyond the urban working class. To this day, the **SPD** retains its status as the "natural governing party," having only been out of office during brief stints in times of crisis. Only a united coalition of all parties from the **SRPD** to the **DNVP** has ever managed to take power—only to quickly collapse, paving the way for yet more years of **SPD** rule.

ending_slides.weimar_mega_win_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - Bloc Politics The Weimar Coalition has begun to fracture, as the Center Party exits the alliance and repositions itself as a center-right force. However, lingering animosity toward the parties further to the right prevents any formal unification. Instead, the newly formed Christian People's Party has opted to form a new electoral alliance—the "People's Bloc"—alongside the **DNVP** and the newly established **NLP**—which is essentially a renamed continuation of its predecessor. We are only able to enter government as part of a "left bloc" with the **RDP**, **CSRP**, and **LSPD**. This has continued to this day, but the inclusion of the purportedly neo-Nazi **NDPD** into the People's Bloc—capitalizing on public discontent over a refugee crisis sparked by wars in an impoverished and unstable Africa—is deeply concerning.

ending_slides.weimar_win.titleHtml: The Weimar Republic Limps Forward
ending_slides.weimar_win.bodyHtml: Following the scarring experience of the Nazi movement’s rapid rise and implosion, the flaws of the Weimar system became impossible to ignore. But in the end, the fascists and communists who once battled in the streets now stand together in soup lines. Though a number of neo-Nazi movements would emerge after [+ nsdap_leader +]’s mask of sanity slipped, the ideology itself remains irrevocably discredited. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, choosing to forget and forgive. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own. ending_slides.weimar_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - The World's Most Unstable Republic The political deadlock that defined the gravest crisis of the Weimar Republic has persisted over the years. The **DNVP** has never been fully reconciled with a system it was fundamentally opposed to from the start. Meanwhile, the estrangement of the Center Party from the Weimar Coalition has only deepened right-wing hostility toward the **SPD**. The presidency has remained out of reach for the **SPD**, with successors to Hindenburg's worldview continuing to preside over Germany and obstruct our return to executive power. In 1939, a recession—sparked by European instability and rising tensions with the Soviet Union—triggered another wave of extremism. The Reichswehr was forced to step in to prevent a "March on Berlin" by both communists and fascism. Though real democracy was formally restored in the 1960s following massive public discontent, the **DSU** has remained a persistent force on the far-right. Recently rebranding itself as the **NDPD**, it has capitalized on growing public anger over a refugee crisis driven by continued war and instability across Africa.

eu_sanctions.bodyHtml: The European Union is a largely untested body, and from the beginning contained members that are at best quasi-democratic. Most of its members are more concerned by power politics than democratic values. However, as its founder, Germany holds a special influence in the EU, and we manage to persuade the other members to join in the pressure against Austrofascism. The Dollfuß regime does not give in, but it is weakened and isolated.

european_union.titleHtml: Take steps to form a "European Union".
european_union.subtitleHtml: Is a "United States of Europe" possible?
european_union.bodyHtml: Forming a "United States of Europe" has long been part of the **Social Democratic** foreign program. Finally, we are taking steps towards it. Given our positive relations with the other countries of Europe, we can begin to hold multilateral negotiations for more European federalism. It will take time to hammer out the exact shape of this future "European Union", however.

european_union_2.titleHtml: We can sign a treaty to form a European Union!
european_union_2.bodyHtml: Along with France, Great Britain, and many other states of Western and Eastern Europe, we have signed a treaty to form a European Union! It is hoped that Europe has learned the lessons of the Great War; never again will there be another war that tears the continent apart. A major component of the union is the free movement of people and goods across the countries of Europe, as well as the stabilization of currency exchange rates. This provides new markets for German products and new sources of investment. Fascist Italy remains a problem, and the Soviet Union also lies outside the system. But for now, there is new hope for peace and prosperity throughout the continent.

expose.titleHtml: Expose the secret rearmament plans of the previous foreign ministry!
expose.bodyHtml:
The previous foreign ministry, despite its benevolent and peaceful face, was secretly helping the Reichswehr to build up its forces, in contravention of the Treaty of Versailles.

expose_him.bodyHtml: We expose to the public Schacht's dealings with the Nazis. For better or worse, he is cowed, and refrains from taking further actions against us.

expose_rohm.bodyHtml: We have published the Röhm letters under the title *Der Fall Röhm* (The Röhm Affair), distributing the pamphlet across all corners of Germany. This has damaged the Nazi Party’s appeal among its more socially reactionary supporters and has even sparked a plot among some Nazi members to murder Röhm. The pamphlet argues that a party tolerating homosexuality at its highest levels must seek to "poison the people and destroy its moral strength." It warns that this would lead to Germany’s decline, akin to the fall of ancient Rome, and claims that by keeping Röhm in power, the Nazis are complicit in "knowingly and intentionally furthering the seduction of German youths into becoming homosexual minions." Despite this, Hitler has swiftly come to Röhm’s defense, publicly reaffirming his position as leader of the **SA**. The electoral performance of the Nazis remains largely unaffected, but the impression this controversy leaves on President Hindenburg may yet prove significant. Meanwhile, the pamphlet’s publisher, Helmuth Klotz, has been brutally beaten by Nazi deputies inside the Reichstag building as an act of revenge—an event that has overshadowed the scandal itself.

choices.labelHtml: Attempt to persecute Röhm! homosexual acts are prohibited by Paragraph 175, allowing us to open up legal action against him.

faq.bodyHtml: = FAQ **Hindenburg keeps sacking me! How do I prevent it?** It's hard to prevent him from sacking you if you plan to stay in office for the full four years, but pausing reparations (by not exposing rearmament), keeping the Reichswehr loyal, maintaining a budget surplus, keeping a high pro republic support, a low coalition dissent, avoiding land reform, and keeping unemployment and NSDAP poll numbers low, all help. Remember, him sacking you is not the end of the world, and being free from the burden of government could be a blessing in disguise. Sometimes you have to accept it. **How impactful is government burden?** A main problem with newer players is that, they overestimate the negative effects of not completing government burden. It is not the end of the world if you miss a goal or two or three, some sacrifices are needed if you need to garner the budget for an economic plan. That said, you also can't afford to completely ignore the Labor Ministry; repeated failures there will significantly increase internal dissent. **How do I impact a party's ideologies and get certain paths? Is it RNG?** Nothing in Dynamic relies on RNG, aside from card draws. The Support for the Republic value plays a crucial role in determining party congress outcomes, particularly within the **DNVP**. The liberal parties, on the other hand, are primarily influenced by governmental actions—moving toward economic democracy and left-wing policies will push them rightward, while maintaining good relations and avoiding major socialist policies will bring them closer. Relations also matter significantly, making the negotiation skills of Müller and Braun highly valuable. **What happened to the WTB Plan?** Woytinsky only came up with the plan in late 1931 after the Banking Crisis, so to represent this, you need to get the event where Woytinsky proposes the concept in order to support it. The event is dynamic, and can trigger depending on factors such as: the state of the economy, deflation, labor faction strength, and most importantly internal party dissent. Appointing Woytinsky as an advisor aids significantly, as his presence passively increases the rate. **What is Dynamic Mode?** Dynamic mode is the intended way to play the mod, combining elements of both easy and historical modes. It reduces RNG with the shuffle leadership and card dismissal features of easy mode while retaining the starting variables of historical mode, such as relations and Reichsbanner strength. **How do I elect Stegerwald?** You will have to get Stegerwald as the leader of Prussia, either through Braun resigning, or having a right-wing coalition form. **How do I cross the rubicon?** Hindenburg needs to dismiss Chancellor Brüning following the 1932 Presidential elections. This unlocks Rubicon Mode, which remains active for the rest of the game. Since this is the historical sequence of events, you'll need to follow a similar political path, such as securing a Hugenberg-led **DNVP**, to have a better chance of unlocking it. **Why is the left path so hard?** Unlike Redux, this mod does not include any post–civil war content or additional **KPD** or revolutionary paths. This is primarily due to time constraints—by the time of release, the mod had already been in development for over 9 months. As a result, the only truly "viable" path is the Reformist one, given the immense difficulty of building socialism within a bourgeois democracy—especially with figures like Hindenburg as president and the hostility of the bourgeois parties. # for the angry redditors.... **Why can't I form a coalition with a moderate Christian-Socialist DNVP or KVP?** The Christian Socials of the DNVP, and the party as a whole, remain a racist and antisemitic party, though they are more willing to operate within a democratic framework. The "Christian Socialism" of Weimar Germany is not the Christian Socialism of today; a better comparison would be Austria’s Christian Social Party. It is a nationalist, corporatist, and deeply religious right-wing ideology. The KVP is still a strongly anti-Marxist and nationalistic party at heart, and it would be against everything they stand for to coalition with the socialists.

Some, even on the left, suggest that the Nazis would not *truly* be as horrific as their platform suggests, and that giving them power would let them discredit themselves in the eyes of the public. Alternatively, [+ president +] could use the emergency powers of the presidency. Article 48 has been used by Hindenburg to promulgate anti-democratic and anti-worker policies; can Article 48 be used for good as well as evil?

choices.labelHtml: We will form an emergency government with [+ president +]'s support.
Let the Nazis form their government.

far_right_coalition_prussia.bodyHtml: There are enough votes for the Nazis and the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP** ?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF** ?] to form a coalition. Hermann Göring is elevated to the position of Minister-President and immediately starts dismantling its democratic institutions. A wave of terror and repression unfolds, targeting the socialists and communists. Violence erupts in the streets, with bullets flying and leftists being killed or imprisoned.

far_right_coalition_saxony.titleHtml: The NSDAP enters the governing coalition.
far_right_coalition_saxony.subtitleHtml: Unfortunately, there is no other viable option.
far_right_coalition_saxony.bodyHtml: After a failed negotiation previously, the bourgeois parties are now willing to offer a ministerial position to the **NSDAP** in exchange for their support. Gregor Strasser, leader of the **NSDAP**'s left wing, has been appointed as the new Interior Minister, a role he had been denied in the past due to his more radical anti-capitalist views. Saxony, once a stronghold of socialism and democracy, is now being dismantled by the Nazis. The "democratic" aspect more so, as Strasser has pushed for the cabinet to adopt pro-worker and anti-capitalist policies in an attempt to win their votes. The state police, now largely comprised of Nazis, are actively suppressing socialist and communist organizations and meetings. Socialist newspapers critical of the government have been banned, and civil servants with suspected socialist or democratic leanings are being purged in large numbers. However, there is a real possibility that Strasser could be removed from his position by his coalition partners, as they were never a huge fan of him.

far_right_coalition_thuringia.titleHtml: The incumbent coalition is expanded to include the **NSDAP**.
far_right_coalition_thuringia.subtitleHtml: A testament to how biased the "democratic" parties are when it comes to working with us.
far_right_coalition_thuringia.bodyHtml: Wilhelm Frick, a convicted Beer Hall Putsch participant, becomes the first Nazi to hold a ministerial-level post in Germany. He is given control of the Interior and Education Ministries, and by passing an "Enabling Act" through a simple majority as an emergency decree, granting him the power to radically transform Thuringia. Gone are the days of Red Thuringia. Suspected socialists and democrats are purged en masse from the civil service. A state police force is established, with Frick preferentially employing Nazi officials. All communist teachers and mayors are dismissed, and newspapers critical of government policy are banned. [? if prussia_leader == "Braun" and interior_minister_party == "SPD": Fortunately, Carl Severing is able to halt the recruitment of Nazis into the police force by suspending state subsidies, effectively ending the practice. ?] With control of the Education Ministry, Frick appoints racial researchers and known Nazis to top positions at many universities and bans the anti-war book *All Quiet on the Western Front* from being read or played. His attempts to grant Hitler German citizenship have so far failed, forcing Hitler to look elsewhere.

far_right_coup.titleHtml: The far-right parties immediately launch a military coup against us...
far_right_coup.bodyHtml: The far-right parties, seeing that we are willing to deny them government by questionably democratic means, have decided that they can only take power by undemocratic means, and have risen up in force against the sitting government. Their numbers are bolstered by the many government workers who are against the prospect of a unified Socialist government. Police and soldiers defect to the **SA** and **Stahlhelm**.

far_right_fail.bodyHtml: The reactionary establishment is still very skeptical of the Nazis, so instead, [+ president +] appoints Carl Friedrich Goerdeler, the Mayor of Leipzig, as Chancellor, to try to "tame" the Nazis. With [+ nsdap_leader +] and Hugenberg refusing to join any reformed Brüning cabinet, Hindenburg has sidestepped the issue by turning to the staunchly conservative Goerdeler, who renounced his affiliation with the **DNVP** to accept the post. Upon taking office, however, Goerdeler has yet to secure formal support from the **NSDAP** or [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?]—support he needs, given that the **SPD**[? if not lvp_formed: and likely the **[+ ddp_name +]**?] will not back his government. The coming months will reveal whether Goerdeler can govern—and if the **NSDAP** is truly serious about entering government.

far_right_win.bodyHtml: [? if president == "Hindenburg" : President Hindenburg's camarilla ?][? if president != "Hindenburg" and president != "Braun": President [+ president +] ?][? if president == "Braun" : President Braun somehow ?] has decided that [+ nsdap_leader +] must be chancellor [? if president == "Hindenburg": , and the aging president accepts their recommendations. ?][? if president != "Hindenburg" : because it is what the constitution would stipulate. ?]

fight.bodyHtml: Do we realize that this means civil war, against the full force of the state?

choices.labelHtml: We are not ready for war. Instead, we will vote against the government in the Reichstag.

fight_2_pre_civil_war.bodyHtml: Our forces confront the fascists on the streets of Berlin, and armed fighting erupts. Neither side is dislodged from their positions.

fight_2_win.bodyHtml: Our forces confront the fascists, and somehow, the fascists retreat! They were overwhelmed by our display of strength, and have chosen to slink away. The attempted coup is over, at least for now. The show of force has reinvigorated support for the republic and for the **SPD**, and has weakened the fascists.

fight_constitution.titleHtml: This is unconstitutional! We will keep our positions in government, and ask the courts to keep us in power.
fight_constitution.bodyHtml: The courts agree that President [+ president +] is wrong to dismiss us, and that we should remain in the government. The President might respect the court's decision for now, but the fascists in the streets do not. They are still demanding snap elections or the resignation of the government, and will remain in the streets until we either meet their demands, or they are forced out.

fight_mild.titleHtml: We'll launch peaceful protests and a general strike. Schleicher can't rule without the people's support.
fight_mild.subtitleHtml: But he may seize on this as a pretext to escalate the crackdown.
fight_mild.bodyHtml: We are in no position to fight a civil war against the full force of the state, but we cannot let Schleicher live without consequences. We have an array of options at our disposal, the [? if not unions_independent: ADGB?][? if unions_independent: workers?] can launch a general strike, and use the Reichsbanner as leverage, if we had maintained its strength. Cracking down on the universally hated **RFB** is one thing, but a mass republican movement? We don't know if Schleicher will budge. Our former coalition partners and members are skeptical to potentially risk the survival of the **SPD** to protest in solidarity with the **Communists**. Do we continue to bide our time?

fight_mild_2.titleHtml: The workers stopped the Kapp Putsch in 1920.
fight_mild_2.subtitleHtml: And we can do it again.
fight_mild_2.bodyHtml: We are not alone. [? if spd_alone: Well, we actually are, never mind. ?] [? if not stegerwald_path: Catholics?][? if stegerwald_path: Christians?] - [? if z_against_schleicher: In Favor?][? if not z_against_schleicher: Political Neutrality?] Left Liberals - [? if libs_against_schleicher: In Favor?][? if not libs_against_schleicher: Political Neutrality?] [? if not spd_alone: The Weimar Coalition parties are nominally against such unconstitutional acts as well. While they may not have an armed self-defense militia, they have several hundred thousand employees in blue-collar and white-collar jobs, and could completely cripple the economy if they act alongside the socialist Free Unions. ?]

fightback_other.bodyHtml: If the bourgeois wants to appeal to the workers, then we will simply find support elsewhere. The **KPD** makes inroads on our inaction. The left of the **SPD** is opposed to this path, seeing it as diluting the class character of the party. On the other hand, reformists support branching out to different classes.

fightback_working.bodyHtml: We increase our messaging among the workers, fighting back against the shift to the right. It isn't enough, but it is something.

fiscal_policy.raise_tariffs.subtitleHtml: +2 budget. Other countries will retaliate by increasing tariffs of their own. [? if tariffs > 5 : Further increases in tariffs will not raise revenue, as we have already nearly reached economic autarky. ?]
fiscal_policy.raise_tariffs.bodyHtml:
Increasing tariffs leads to higher prices for basic goods, increasing inflation and hurting consumption among the working class. Retaliatory tariffs reduce the competitiveness of German exports, raising unemployment among workers. They also lead to an atmosphere of international suspicion, reducing our ability to negotiate with other countries.
On the other hand, agricultural producers and some small businesses benefit from higher tariffs, as farmers can now command higher prices for grain, and formerly uncompetitive businesses are now able to function.

force_fail.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, our forces fail to dislodge the **SA** from their positions surrounding Hitler. He is seen as both a strong and powerful leader and a victim, further reinforcing his image. The Nazis are left stronger than ever.

force_peace.titleHtml: Can we bring the sides together for a peace?
force_peace.bodyHtml: The Austrian government obviously sees us as biased, so there is no way they will let us host peace negotiations. However, negotiations begin nonetheless. In Switzerland, with Fascist Italy as the Austrofascists' protector and Germany as the **SDAPÖ**'s, a peace deal is hammered out. The socialists are disarmed and give up all pretense of revolution, while the right-wing paramilitaries are also disarmed. Dictatorship ends, and normal government is restored, with free elections. Given the **SDAPÖ**'s starting position, this is treated as a victory. Now begins the long work of reconstruction...

force_success.bodyHtml: The confrontation ends with the police and Reichsbanner prevailing, capturing Hitler so he can be deported! This is a sign of weakness, and his physical distance makes organizing difficult, impeding the Nazi effort to win more votes. In Hitler's absence, Joseph Goebbels has become the temporary leader of the Nazi party, with substantial influence from Hermann Göring.

foreign_policy.customs_union.titleHtml: Form a customs union with Austria?
foreign_policy.customs_union.subtitleHtml: This will likely incur the wrath of France.
foreign_policy.customs_union.bodyHtml: The right has long desired closer ties with Austria, with the eventual goal of the merger of the two German-speaking countries. A customs union with Austria is the first step towards this goal. Additionally, many believe that a union with Austria would improve our current economic circumstances. However, the Allies, especially France, are likely to object. This agreement would break the terms of the Versailles Treaty, and could lead to economic sanctions, further hurting our economy.

choices.labelHtml: No, we should do something else.

foreign_policy.customs_union_2.bodyHtml: We have formed a customs union with Austria! The right-wing parties are praising us for this unexpected turn of events. Immediately, France and other neighboring countries lodge their protests. The longer-term response is yet to be seen.

foreign_policy.european_union.titleHtml: Take steps to form a "European Union".
foreign_policy.european_union.subtitleHtml: Is a "United States of Europe" possible?
foreign_policy.european_union.bodyHtml: Forming a "United States of Europe" has long been part of the **Social Democratic** foreign program. Finally, we are taking steps towards it. Given our positive relations with the other countries of Europe, we can begin to hold multilateral negotiations for more European federalism. It will take time to hammer out the exact shape of this future "European Union", however.

foreign_policy.european_union_2.titleHtml: We can sign a treaty to form a European Union!
foreign_policy.european_union_2.bodyHtml: Along with France, Great Britain, and many other states of Western and Eastern Europe, we have signed a treaty to form a European Union! It is hoped that Europe has learned the lessons of the Great War; never again will there be another war that tears the continent apart. A major component of the union is the free movement of people and goods across the countries of Europe, as well as the stabilization of currency exchange rates. This provides new markets for German products and new sources of investment. Fascist Italy remains a problem, and the Soviet Union also lies outside the system. But for now, there is new hope for peace and prosperity throughout the continent.

foreign_policy.improve_east.titleHtml: Improve our relations with our eastern neighbors.
foreign_policy.improve_east.bodyHtml: We also aim to improve relations with our eastern neighbors, Poland and Czechoslovakia, who are rightfully terrified of German aggression. Hopefully we can convince them of our peaceful intentions.

foreign_policy.improve_soviet.titleHtml: Improve our relations with the **Soviet Union**.
foreign_policy.improve_soviet.subtitleHtml: We could also broach the question of the **KPD**...
foreign_policy.improve_soviet.bodyHtml: The Soviet Union also suffered from the international order created by the Treaty of Versailles; they have been participating in our secret rearmament program. The Treaty of Rapallo in 1922 affirmed our friendly relations. The Soviets are asking for economic and developmental assistance. They are still a poor country on the whole, and are desperately trying to catch up to the western powers. There is a chance that our anti-communist coalition partners would be upset, but we could assuage them by asking the Soviets for secret assistance in training and equipping the Reichswehr.

choices.labelHtml: Provide aid, in exchange for Reichswehr assistance.
Provide aid, in exchange for only good relations.

foreign_policy.improve_soviet_eco.titleHtml: Expand our exports to the **Soviet Union**.
foreign_policy.improve_soviet_eco.subtitleHtml: A win for our economy and for our relationship with the **KPD**.
foreign_policy.improve_soviet_eco.bodyHtml: The Soviet Union, with its centrally planned economy and isolation from global markets, has insulated itself from the effects of the Great Depression. They have since been rapidly industrializing in accordance with their Five-Year Plan, making them a prime partner for exports, especially as tariffs from our nominal trading partners in the West have increased, along with their general isolation from international markets. The Soviets are pleased by this, and we stand to reap the economic benefits. The only downside is that the right-wing propaganda machine has decried this action, pressuring [? if president == "Hindenburg": President Hindenburg and?] the bourgeois parties to break with us.

foreign_policy.improve_west.titleHtml: Improve our relations with the Western Allies.
foreign_policy.improve_west.bodyHtml: The key to peace in Europe is a rapprochement between France and Germany. We are taking steps towards that rapprochement. [? if young_plan_seen == 0 : This is difficult to do when France is occupying a major portion of Germany's territory, but we are working on that part. ?]

foreign_policy.kpd.bodyHtml: We also mention the **KPD** in our conversations with the Soviet ambassador. They claim that the **KPD** is entirely independent of the Soviet government, and that the conflict is Thälmann's doing. But, soon after our conversation we notice a slight improvement in attitudes from the **KPD**.

foreign_policy.reduce_reparations.titleHtml: The Western Allies are finally willing to pause our reparations payments!
foreign_policy.reduce_reparations.bodyHtml: Finally, given both the economic circumstances and our continued negotiations, the Western Allies are willing to pause our reparations payments! Much of the credit must go to Western president Hoover, who has been friendlier towards us than the Europeans. This has reduced tensions within our government, and our party has gotten credit for the achievement.

foreign_policy.schleicher_spd.subtitleHtml: This will be a severe betrayal of our values!
foreign_policy.schleicher_spd.bodyHtml: General Schleicher has demanded that we raise the issue of rearmament, which remains restricted under the Treaty of Versailles. However, French Premier Édouard Herriot seized on this as an admission that Germany is, in fact, capable of paying its reparations and would simply redirect freed-up funds toward rearmament. [? if military_parity:[? if eu: However, with the formation of the European Union and its defense agreements, preventing Germany’s rearmament has become increasingly irrelevant. As a result, military restrictions are lifted!?][? if not eu: However, our exceptionally friendly relations with the Western Allies have led them to begrudgingly grant us flexibility in rearmament, believing that we could serve as a bulwark against the Bolsheviks.?] As a result, the **NSDAP** has lost yet another propaganda tool. However, we continue to suffer heavy losses to the **Communists**[? if not lvp_formed: and **[+ ddp_name +]**, who we have suffered serious defections to?]. ?] [? if not military_parity: This has caused great embarrassment to our pacifist and democratic image, both at home and abroad. Damn you, Schleicher! ?]
