foreign_policy.settle_reparations.titleHtml: We will finally settle the reparations issues with the Western Allies!
foreign_policy.settle_reparations.subtitleHtml: The issue of reparations and future payments will finally be resolved.
foreign_policy.settle_reparations.bodyHtml: With our success in negotiating a pause in reparation payments, the Western Allies have been convinced of our sincere commitment to pacifism and distancing from militarism. Additionally, France's new left-wing Prime Minister has been considerably more amicable than their predecessor. As a result, we have secured their agreement to a conference aimed at finally settling the reparations issue. In the end, Germany is required to make only a final payment of three billion marks, effectively ending future reparation obligations. This has greatly boosted investor confidence and sparked a new wave of capital inflows to Germany. This has greatly eased tensions within our government, with our party receiving credit for the achievement—much to the detriment of the **NSDAP**, which had built much of its appeal on the narrative of Germany’s "national slavery."

foreign_policy.soviet_economic_aid_no.bodyHtml: The Soviets are slightly upset, but they seemed to expect this answer.

foreign_policy.soviet_economic_aid_yes.bodyHtml: The Soviets are pleased that we have sent them aid, and have not asked for anything specific in exchange. Our coalition partners are less pleased.

choices.labelHtml: Ask if Moscow could help repair our relations with the **KPD**.
Do the Soviets know about the Wittorf Affair? Do they know that we know?

foreign_policy.soviet_economic_aid_yes_m.bodyHtml: The Soviets are pleased that we have sent them aid, and have agreed to help train our military. The Reichswehr appreciates our support.

foreign_policy.support_austria.titleHtml: Diplomatically support Austrian democracy against the Dollfuß dictatorship.
foreign_policy.support_austria.bodyHtml: We provide verbal backing to Austrian democracy, wage a war of words against Austrofascism, and promulgate additional trade sanctions. Time will tell if it will be enough.

foreign_policy.support_austria_2.titleHtml: Provide material support to Austrian democracy against the Dollfuß dictatorship.
foreign_policy.support_austria_2.bodyHtml: In public, we provide verbal backing to Austrian democracy, wage a war of words against Austrofascism, and promulgate additional trade sanctions. Privately, we provide financial and various forms of "support" to our comrades in Austria in their struggle against dictatorship.

foreign_policy.wittorf.bodyHtml: Of course Stalin and the various leaders of the Comintern know about the Wittorf Affair, but they do not seem to know that we know as well. The Comintern was planning to build a narrative around the affair that absolves Thälmann, but perhaps now they will be less inclined to defend him.

choices.labelHtml: Do not enact any policies for now.

fr_uk.bodyHtml: The socialists of France and Britain can influence their governments to be friendlier towards Germany. Hopefully they will reduce our reparations burden.

params.source: france_coalition_menu

france_coalition_menu.bodyHtml: France is known for its historically unstable governments, with most cabinets lasting a few months at best. The last four years have been governed by various groupings of parties to the right of the **SFIO**, our socialist comrades. Perhaps it's their turn to rule now, with the return of the Left-Cartel alliance. However, concerns over their radical economic policies may push the **PRS** and **PRRRS** to form a coalition with the **AD** instead.

free_kpd.bodyHtml: Restrictions are lifted and police are deployed to protect Communist demonstrations and organizations from the far-right.

frick.bodyHtml: The **NSDAP** has nominated Wilhelm Frick, who is expected to receive backing only from his own party. [? if hindenburg_run: The decision to run Frick instead of the more charismatic and popular Hitler stems from Hitler’s deep reluctance to challenge the universally respected and personally popular President Hindenburg—believing such a move would tarnish his image. Gregor Strasser’s argument ultimately prevailed over Goebbels’, and Hitler has chosen to sit this one out. ?][? if not hindenburg_run: The decision to run Frick instead of the more charismatic and popular Hitler stems from Hitler’s reluctance to enter an unwinnable race, fearing it would damage his image. By putting forward the more pragmatic Frick, he hopes to attract some conservative support ahead of the local elections.?] Should Frick win, he would serve as little more than a proxy for the Nazi leader.

fundraising.bodyHtml:
= Fundraising
For better or for worse, the party cannot exist without money. Without the support of wealthy industrialists, we depend on membership dues to sustain our efforts.
We receive dues at the end of each year, but can adjust them throughout. Low party dissent can secure more funds, and vice versa.

fundraising.increase.subtitleHtml: We will gain [+ dues + 1 +] resources per year. +1 resource [? if unemployed >= 15 : Given the present economic situation, this may be painful. ?][? if dues >= 4 : Dues are already rather high; increasing them might reduce our membership. ?]
fundraising.increase.bodyHtml: Our members grumble at this, and some of the less committed members leave. But now, we have access to additional resources. [? if unemployed >= 15 : Because of the presently high unemployment, our members are feeling the extra burden hard. ?] The higher dues will make it more difficult for the **SPD** to expand electorally.

game_over.braun_victorious.bodyHtml: Otto Braun has been elected as President of Germany. He had never desired to be the most powerful man in Germany, but now he is.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.civil_war_lost.bodyHtml: We have lost the civil war. At least it was a quick coup, and ended before Germany could be plunged into total war.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.civil_war_won.titleHtml: We have won the civil war.
game_over.civil_war_won.bodyHtml: We have won the civil war against the reactionary forces. Germany will be changed forever, but it is too early to know how.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.communist_victory.bodyHtml: The **KPD** has won power in Germany, with our assistance. They will try to remake Germany in the Soviet image. How much they succeed is yet to be determined.

params.code: state.flags['chancellor_party'] == "KPD" || state.flags['president'] == "Thälmann" && state.flags['total_defeat'] == 0 && state.flags['long_war'] == 0

eg_menu

game_over.emergency_government.titleHtml: **SPD** ruling in an emergency government.
game_over.emergency_government.bodyHtml: The **SPD** is ruling as part of an emergency minority government, led by President [+ president +] and Chancellor [+ chancellor +]. This is a temporary and unstable arrangement, leaving the door open to further authoritarianism.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.european_union.titleHtml: There is now a European Union!
game_over.european_union.bodyHtml: We have helped to form a European Union to bring peace and prosperity to the continent. Time will tell how effective it will be.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.fun_zone.bodyHtml: At the checkpoints of 33%, 66% and 100%, you will receive special rewards for your progress in the game.

params.source: eg_menu if started == 1; root.start_menu_2 if started == 0

game_over.hitler_wins.titleHtml: Adolf Hitler is in undisputed control over Germany.
game_over.hitler_wins.bodyHtml: Adolf Hitler is in undisputed control over Germany. The **SPD**, along with all of the democratic forces, have failed. [? if civil_war_seen == 1 : At the very least, we fought back. Perhaps our resistance will be celebrated in an impossible-to-forsee future. ?]

game_over.long_war.titleHtml: Germany is gripped by civil war.
game_over.long_war.bodyHtml: Germany is currently in the grip of a civil war, a brutal affair that has no obvious end. Thousands of lives have already been extinguished, and it is likely that the war will not stop until Germany's cities are reduced to ruins. [? if is_favorable == 0 : The current conditions are not favorable for us. ?][? if west_relation >= 2: Our cause is popular in the West, but their sclerotic governments are reluctant to send us aid. ?][? if soviet_aid >= 1 : The Soviet Union has aided the Communists, but not the socialists and democrats, in an attempt to shape Germany's future government. ?][? if east_aid >= 1 : Poland and Czechoslovakia have sent some assistance against the fascists. ?]

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.nationalization_achieved.titleHtml: Socialization of the economy has commenced.
game_over.nationalization_achieved.bodyHtml: As part of our socialist economic plan, we have nationalized a substantial portion of the economy, beginning the transition to actual socialism.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.no_hitler.titleHtml: Hitler does not yet control Germany...
game_over.no_hitler.bodyHtml: Hitler does not yet control Germany. [? if chancellor == "Papen" : However, Chancellor Papen's authoritarianism and far-right politics are paving the way for Hitler, or someone like him, to take power. ?] [? if chancellor == "Schleicher" : However, Chancellor Schleicher's authoritarianism and scheming is paving the way for Hitler, or someone like him, to take power. ?][? if resist_coup == 1 and republic_victory == 0 and long_war == 0 and coup_victory == 0 : Given our defeat in the Prussian coup, the far-right appears to be ascendant. ?][? if chancellor == "Brüning" : However, Chancellor Brüning's austerity policies and the continuation of the depression are paving the way for Hitler, or someone like him, to take power. ?] [? if hitler_deported == 1 : We have deported Hitler back to Austria. Hopefully he will never return. ?]

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.nsdap_win.titleHtml: Despite the deportation of Hitler, the Nazis have still taken power...
game_over.nsdap_win.bodyHtml:
Despite the deportation of Hitler, the **NSDAP** has somehow still wormed its way into power.

[? if long_war == 1 : We are fighting them for control of Germany. ?]

game_over.peoples_party_achieved.bodyHtml: The **SPD** has been declared a "People's Party", representing all of the people, not just the working class. This policy has many supporters and detractors, and what will become of the party is still unclear.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.president_einstein.bodyHtml: Albert Einstein, possibly the most famous scientist in the world, has been elected as President of Germany. As a German Jew and a pacifist, he is the repudiation of everything the Nazis stood for, and a symbol of a new German Republic that has moved beyond its checkered past.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.president_grzesinski.bodyHtml: Albert Grzesinski has been elected President of Germany. As a young and ambitious **SPD** member, he will be shaping Germany for years to come.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.president_juchacz.bodyHtml: Marie Juchacz has been elected as President of Germany. She is the first woman to be elected as the head of state of any republic, and will contribute to shaping Germany for years to come.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.president_schumacher.bodyHtml: Kurt Schumacher has been elected as President of Germany. As a young and ambitious **SPD** member, he will be shaping Germany for years to come.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.president_wels.bodyHtml: Otto Wels has been elected President of Germany. What a long journey it has been for the **SPD**'s chairman through the Republic. He will be shaping Germany for years to come.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.rosenfeld_victorious.bodyHtml: Kurt Rosenfeld has been elected as President of Germany. He had never desired to be the most powerful man in Germany, but together with the **KPD**, we are in for a socialist future.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.spd_victorious.bodyHtml: The **SPD** is still in government, under Chancellor [+ chancellor +]. Given the circumstances, this is a substantial accomplishment.

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.spd_victorious_2.bodyHtml:
We were forced to strike a deal with Kurt von Schleicher, abandoning our pacifist and anti-militarist roots. With his reputation as a schemer, he could betray us at any moment.
Was it really worth it?

params.source: eg_menu

game_over.unemployment_high.bodyHtml: Unemployment is still at dangerously high levels. Even though Hitler is not in power, the situation is ripe for instability and extremism.

game_over.war_against_hitler.bodyHtml: Adolf Hitler has taken power in Germany. However, we have rallied the democratic forces of the country against him, and are fighting back. The outcome of this war is uncertain.

gereke.titleHtml: Günther Gereke, formerly of the DNVP, is elected as their new leader.
gereke.subtitleHtml: Gereke has significant influence over the agricultural and industrial establishment, being a key member of the RLB and a founder of another rural association. - National Conservative and Agrarian Wing
gereke.bodyHtml: Günther Gereke, a lawyer and prominent politician from rural Germany, has been elected as the new leader of the **[+ z_party_name +]**. What makes him notable is that he is an agrarian politician from west of the Elbe River, a leading reformist economic theorist, and someone with close ties to General Kurt von Schleicher. He bears similarities to Treviranus, though he is far less dogmatic in his beliefs. Thanks to Gereke’s strong relationship with the **CNBLP**, a rural special-interest party, he has successfully negotiated a merger of the declining party into the **[+ z_party_name +]**, though only a few officials remain in the effectively dead party. His support for a public works program has stemmed criticism from the labor factions, and his ability to unite the key interest groups on which the German Right depends on will help secure strong nationalist backing for the party. Needless to say, this has not sat well with the **[+ z_party_name +]**’s Catholic wing, and has made cooperation within the party impossible for the foreseeable future.

gessler.titleHtml: Otto Gessler, controversial former Defense Minister and former **DDP** member.
gessler.bodyHtml: Otto Gessler, who served as Defense Minister for eight years following Noske’s departure and preceding Groener, is a conservative and a republican by reason rather than conviction—often at odds with his colleagues in the **DDP** throughout his tenure. He made little effort to reform the Reichswehr and played an active role in the Reichsexekution against our United Left governments in Saxony and Thuringia during the German October. Now, after stepping away from politics in early 1928, he seeks a return to the national stage. His candidacy is supported by the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]. [? if not lvp_formed: He is also nominally supported by the **[+ ddp_name +]**, which has grown more right-wing and more accepting over the years. ?]

gessler_win.bodyHtml: Otto Gessler has made a comeback and won the presidency. Despite his[? if lvp_formed:  former?] affiliation with the **DDP**, he isn’t as friendly as his colleagues. However, he is a significant step up from Hindenburg. Let’s hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

gestapo.bodyHtml:
For now, the organization remains confined to Prussia, but its presence is felt everywhere. Local party members whisper that their phones are tapped, and troublesome politicians vanish—never to be seen again. With the police now firmly under government control, they decide which crimes to overlook and coordinate raids hand-in-hand with the Reichswehr.
Yet, their reach still depends on the willingness of people to betray their comrades by reporting them to the police.

gift.bodyHtml: This is a gift to the Communists, a boost to their theory that parliamentary democracy will never benefit the working class.

params.source: what_do

give_up.bodyHtml: Speeches are made. Votes are held. Bullets fly in the streets. Some socialists are killed or jailed. Others flee the country. What can votes even do at this juncture? The Reichstag is burned, ostensibly by a foreign communist. In the wake, the Nazis pass decrees giving them unlimited power. They, combined with the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnf_formed: **DNF**?], will win a majority at the next elections. Germany is lost.

His removal, along with the replacement of many Nazi cabinet ministers, has stopped Germany's slippery slope into dictatorship. [? if chancellor == "Brüning": Heinrich Brüning of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is appointed as interim chancellor. ?][? if chancellor == "Wels": Otto Wels of the **SPD** is selected as appointed chancellor. ?] The next elections are set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

give_up_2.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, the President’s left-wing leanings make him an unacceptable figure to the reactionary strongholds of the state. The Reichswehr refuses to take his side over that of [+ chancellor +]. Despite holding the highest office in the land, the President finds himself powerless, outmaneuvered by [+ chancellor +]. Eventually, he is ousted through legally questionable means, and new elections are held under the watchful eye of **SA** troopers—securing Hitler’s rise to absolute power. Germany is lost.

give_up_3.bodyHtml: The Reichswehr has placed more trust in [+ president +] than in Chancellor [+ old_chancellor +], and under this influence, [+ old_chancellor +] was forced to accept his defeat. His removal, along with the replacement of many Nazi cabinet ministers, has stopped Germany's slippery slope into dictatorship. Heinrich Brüning of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is selected as interim chancellor. The next elections are set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

give_up_4.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, President Hindenburg is forced to concede defeat after a war game orchestrated by Schleicher reveals that the Reichswehr and Police cannot prevail in a civil war against the **SA** and other paramilitary forces. Reduced to little more than a figurehead, Hindenburg remains in office—signing off on every decree, fully aware that any resistance would plunge his beloved nation into civil war. Germany is lost.

give_up_prussia.bodyHtml: Fine. We no longer control the government of Prussia. The vote has been called off. The Minister-President position is transferred to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].

glatzel.subtitleHtml: Glatzel, a former member of the **DNVP** and **DVP**, advocates the idea of broadening the party's appeal to workers.
glatzel.bodyHtml: Frank Glatzel, a trade unionist affiliated with the conservative white-collar union, the DHV, has been elected the new leader of the **LVP**. He advocates for a "New Nationalism," emphasizing solidarity among all classes to defend the country's "living space" and to foster freedom for the people. In his push for *Volksgemeinschaft*, aimed at reducing class conflict, he has incorporated more nationalistic and corporatist elements into the party platform. This vision gained him the support of nationalists and Stresemannites within the **LVP**, with the paramilitary group "Young German Order" even backing his leadership bid. As expected, this shift has caused concern among the remaining industrialists in the **LVP**, as the party moves away from its traditional sole focus on middle-class interests. This has resulted in a significant change in the party’s financial backing, with funding from big business dwindling and being replaced by donations and newly established dues. His dynamic leadership should be closely watched.

goerdeler.subtitleHtml: Former nationalist mayor of Leipzig. Strong conservative.
goerdeler.bodyHtml: Goerdeler, an outspoken conservative on the German Right, with personal authoritarian and monarchist leanings, represents Schleicher’s signal of a return to partisan rule in essence. Despite breaking with his former party to join the **DNEF**, his appointment is seen by workers and republicans as little different from naming a **DNVP** man. Yet, the fact that he is not a military figure like Schleicher or his circle has brought some measure of relief. Though a long-time opponent of Alfred Hugenberg and his faction, Goerdeler remains a conservative at heart and is expected to continue the dismantling of the despised Weimar order. But Goerdeler is no Schleicher. He lacks the vast network of political ties that his patron carefully cultivated across German society, and Schleicher’s personal popularity has failed to pass to his chosen successor. Moreover, Goerdeler is known for his hardline fiscal conservatism and anti-social stance, having once called for the abolition of unemployment insurance during the Papen era. Perhaps the house of cards Schleicher so carefully built is already beginning to wobble.

goerdeler_2.bodyHtml: Before the Reichstag was to convene, Goerdeler presents a decree to dissolve it. He expects that, with the exodus of voters from the **NSDAP** and the certainty of their collapse next election, they will be forced to become more sensible. New elections have been set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

goerdeler_3.subtitleHtml: No agreement is able to be reached.
goerdeler_3.bodyHtml: Brüning's point is proven: the national opposition is not sincere in their intentions of entering government and governing responsibly. Perhaps an agreement can still be reached, but time is running out before the Reichstag reconvenes. The immediate fallout from the collapse in negotiations has led many Nazi protest voters and disillusioned conservatives to abandon ship, convinced that the **NSDAP** is incapable of actually governing.

goerdeler_cabinet_1.subtitleHtml: A purely "temporary arrangement" until the national opposition can be brought into government.
goerdeler_cabinet_1.bodyHtml: = Goerdeler I The country still needs to be governed, and Goerdeler is forced to announce new cabinet picks, who he stresses as purely caretaker until an agreement can be struck with the national opposition. This has resulted in a cabinet dominated by independents, who sit in the seats of posts that Goerdeler intends to give up in a potential future government. The left-liberal ministers are sacked, signalling a break by Goerdeler. The **DNVP** is given a sizable role in the government, with Wilhelm von Gayl holding the Interior Ministry, and Treviranus taking the Transport Ministry. Martin Schiele, who served under Marx, will serve as Agricultural minister once more. The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has grown increasingly apprehensive about its role in the Goerdeler cabinet, refusing to commit ministers like Adam Stegerwald and Brüning to the Labor and Foreign Ministries, respectively. Their refusal to serve alongside the anti-social Hugenberg has thrown a wrench into ongoing negotiations.

goerdeler_cabinet_1.goerdeler.bodyHtml: General Kurt von Schleicher, now the most influential member of the Camarilla and increasingly entangled in political scheming, begins courting the intractable Hugenberg. With the national opposition divided, Schleicher concludes that the **NSDAP** would have no choice but to fall in line. Hugenberg makes his demands clear: he wants the Vice-Chancellorship, control of the Economic Ministry, and sole authority over economic policy. This suits Goerdeler, a fellow fiscal conservative—but Hugenberg, emboldened by his leverage, overreaches. He adds that his former party rival, Martin Schiele, should resign in favor of Count Eberhard von Kalckreuth, a Hugenberg supporter within the National Rural League (RLB). An impasse forms, prompting Schleicher to turn to [+ nsdap_leader +], whose party is—surprisingly—now seen as more reasonable than Hugenberg’s. > *"I do not understand, Herr Geheimrat, how you cannot be satisfied with Schleicher’s concessions. You simply cannot demand a hundred percent change in the political system. A complete change in the political system cannot occur all at once but only gradually."* - Theodor Duesterberg, to Hugenberg

goerdeler_cabinet_1.goerdeler_2.bodyHtml: With Brüning out of the way, Schleicher has vastly overestimated his ability to "tame" the Nazis. [+ nsdap_leader +] has flatly rejected any government that includes Groener or Brüning, and has demanded that his party receive either the Chancellorship or the Defense Ministry—along with several other cabinet posts—arguing that only such control can guarantee the mass support the new government requires to function. This is, however, entirely unacceptable to Goerdeler—and even more so to President Hindenburg, who categorically refuses to grant either the Chancellorship or the Defense Ministry to a member of [+ nsdap_leader +]’s party. Moreover, Hindenburg insists that Brüning and Groener remain in the cabinet, as Foreign and Defense Minister respectively, still valuing Brüning’s diplomatic expertise.

Perhaps an agreement can still be reached, but time is running out before the Reichstag reconvenes. The immediate fallout from the collapse in negotiations has led many Nazi protest voters and disillusioned conservatives to abandon ship, convinced that the **NSDAP** is incapable of actually governing.

goerdeler_cabinet_2.bodyHtml: = Goerdeler I Collapses With Hugenberg and [+ nsdap_leader +]'s intransigence—and their irreconcilable differences with the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and President Hindenburg—Goerdeler’s position is untenable. In a vote of no confidence, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has abandoned him, leaving only the minor parties between the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?] backing his government.

goerdeler_cabinet_2_alt.bodyHtml: = Goerdeler I Survives A parliamentary coalition composed of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and all parties to its right—excluding the **NSDAP**—somehow holds a majority. Hugenberg, emboldened by an electoral boost from an influx of more "reactionary" Nazi voters, has once again grown overconfident, now believing he no longer needs the **NSDAP** to enter government. He assumes that [+ nsdap_leader +], increasingly pressured by senior figures like Strasser and Frick, will eventually cave to preserve party unity and join the government on his terms. In the meantime, Hugenberg has taken the first step—accepting appointments as Vice-Chancellor and Finance Minister. Martin Schiele has been removed, replaced by the more conservative Kalckreuth.

goerdeler_cabinet_2_alt.goerdeler.titleHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] refuses to work with Hugenberg!
goerdeler_cabinet_2_alt.goerdeler.bodyHtml: As expected, the majority of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] refuses to entertain the idea of governing alongside a figure like Hugenberg—especially after his remarks on the campaign trail calling for the outright abolition of welfare. Furthermore, it is unlikely that Goerdeler would stop this, as he himself has proposed gutting unemployment insurance to cut costs. Even Brüning, the de-facto leader of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]'s parliamentary delegation believes that their planned austerity has gone too far. Yet Hugenberg and Goerdeler refuse to accept the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]'s demands for economic policy guarantees. Once again, a deadlock has taken hold.

goring.bodyHtml: The **NSDAP** has nominated Hermann Göring, who is expected to receive support solely from his own party. Normally, Hitler would have been their candidate, but for one reason or another, he is disqualified from the race. With his reputation as a decorated fighter ace from the Great War and his strong ties to the conservative establishment and industrial elites, Göring will win over some nationalists who might have otherwise been wary of Hitler. Still, Göring is widely expected to act as little more than a proxy, taking direction from the Nazi leader operating behind the scenes.

government.bodyHtml: The German Republic, called by some of our detractors as the "Weimar Republic", is a parliamentary republic with a somewhat weak president and a strong parliament, called the Reichstag. The Reichstag is responsible for governing, while the President has a largely ceremonial role but also has some important governing responsibilities. The Reichstag is elected based on a proportional representation system, giving parties seats roughly proportional to their vote share in each electoral district. The Reichstag then elects the Chancellor and the cabinet by a majority vote, who are responsible for government. A majority vote-of-no-confidence can remove the current government. The President is elected by a national direct vote, in two rounds. The second round is used if the first round does not result in a majority for one candidate; the candidate who receives a plurality in the second round becomes president (there is no obligation for weaker candidates to drop out). The role of the president is mostly to represent Germany, but he also has some crucial governing powers. The president and chancellor can together use emergency decrees to govern, bypassing the Reichstag. The president can also appoint or remove a chancellor when a parliamentary majority is unable to be established, and can thus influence the formation of a government. Germany is divided into a number of states, each of which have their own governments with some responsibilities. By far the largest and most important state is Prussia.

grand_coalition_spd_lead.bodyHtml: As expected, the **SPD** is the largest party, and this time, we are expected to take the lead role in the formation of the next government, including selecting the chancellor. hergt.bodyHtml: With opinions on the inflammatory Lambach article being surprisingly divided among party members, a general republican sentiment across Germany, Alfred Hugenberg and his staunch anti-democratic beliefs struggling to convince moderate party members. More and more party members are beginning to blame their decline on the thesis of the Lambach article rather than their participation in a republican government. [? if tariffs < 0: Furthermore, our decrease in tariffs have rallied the agrarian wing against Hugenberg and his all-or-nothing policy. ?] Oskar Hergt has been elected as the new leader of the **DNVP** following a divisive congress. Hugenberg and his supporters have hinted towards a secession from the party's right wing, and Hugenberg himself is withholding financial support to the party.

hergt_victory_lite.bodyHtml: With Hergt’s victory—and without having relied on Nazi support—he is under no obligation to appoint [+ nsdap_candidate +] as chancellor. A committed monarchist, Hergt is expected to pursue steps toward restoring the Hohenzollerns. Unlike Hindenburg, he is far more openly partisan and intends to exclude the **SPD** from government throughout his seven-year term.

hergt_victory_nazi.bodyHtml: With Hergt’s victory—secured with the support of the Nazis—the balance of power shifts to them under the terms of their deal. However, Hergt remains deeply reluctant to appoint Adolf Hitler as chancellor[? if not hitler_citizen or hitler_deported:—which would require granting him German citizenship?]. Instead, he names **Stahlhelm** leader Franz Seldte as a compromise candidate between the two parties. Seldte will govern through presidential decree, leading a far-right cabinet.

heuss.subtitleHtml: Despite the party's decline, Heuss's liberal democratic ideals continue to enjoy strong support.
heuss.bodyHtml: Fortunately, Heuss has survived the vote of no confidence and will remain the leader of the **LVP**, securing support from Curtius and many Stresemannites. This victory will temporarily silence dissent from the right-industrial faction and strengthen our ties with the party.

With strong backing from the industrial-right faction of the **LVP**, Dingeldey is now the frontrunner in the upcoming leadership election. [? if not curtius_resign_lvp and not (curtius_banking_crisis and banking_crisis_seen): The Pragmatic Center has put forward Curtius as their candidate, leading Dietrich to withdraw and endorse him. ?][? if curtius_resign_lvp or (curtius_banking_crisis and banking_crisis_seen): The Pragmatic Center has nominated Dietrich as their candidate, though there is hesitation about electing yet another former **[+ ddp_name +]** member. ?]

high_inflation.subtitleHtml: Workers are seeing their purchasing power decline.
high_inflation.bodyHtml: = High Inflation Inflation has risen. People of all social classes are seeing their purchasing power fall. Memories of the hyperinflation period of 1923 echo through the public conscious, even though the present inflation is not nearly as severe. The bourgeois parties and their laissez-faire platforms stand to gain from this, to a lesser degree the Nazis. The people and the press are clamoring for action to reduce inflation.

hindenburg.bodyHtml: President Hindenburg is, of course, running for re-election, and many in our party are prepared to support him as the last bastion of democracy against Hitler and the Nazis. The Hindenburg Mythos serves as a powerful rallying point for all parties, as he maintains high personal popularity despite everything Germany has endured. However, the more support he receives from the German left and center, the more Hindenburg views it as a stain on his personal honor. The refusal of August von Mackensen and other high-ranking officers with whom he served during the war to embrace his candidacy proved particularly painful to the Reich president. In response, he may shift further to the right after the election in an effort to restore his sense of honor and to appease his former comrades and friends on the German Right. This urge has only been reinforced by the Harzburg Front’s refusal to support him without concessions, as they see Hindenburg as the greatest obstacle to their rise to power.

choices.labelHtml: We await the decision of the Harzburg Front.

hindenburg_appoints_papen.bodyHtml: There is no path to a majority government. President Hindenburg is tired of the chaos, and appoints Franz von Papen as chancellor instead of Brüning. Papen is a independent formerly from the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], and is significantly to the right of the majority of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]. Papen is immediately faced with a vote of no confidence, given his unpopularity. However the **SPD** votes, he is guaranteed to fall, due to the unanimous hatred against him from all other parties. New elections have been set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

hindenburg_drop_out.bodyHtml: President Hindenburg has decided not to run for re-election, citing his health problems and old age as the primary reasons. He feels that the current national situation doesn't warrant a reelection campaign. This development could be either beneficial or detrimental to us. If we wanted to rally behind Hindenburg to oppose Hitler and the Nazis, the absence of a unifying, widely supported national figure—one capable of garnering support from both the moderate left and right—leaves us at a disadvantage. On the other hand, if we decide to run a candidate of our own, the lack of someone with Hindenburg's charisma could make it easier for us to secure a victory. The absence of a candidate for the German middle and moderate right to rally behind creates a vacuum, which will likely be filled as other parties announce their candidates in the near future.

Support Konrad Adenauer of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?].

hindenburg_explode_president.candidates.bodyHtml: The nationalists and Chancellor [+ chancellor +] have chosen to nominate Hans von Seeckt—former Chief of the German Army from 1920 to 1926, and a staunch conservative monarchist, infamous for his refusal to suppress the Kapp Putsch with the remark: "Reichswehr do not fire on Reichswehr". In recent years, he was elected to parliament under the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?], gradually drifting further to the radical right. He even appeared as a featured speaker at the Harzburg Rally. Now returned from a military advisory mission in China, Seeckt enters the race for the presidency—backed by many of Hindenburg’s former allies and the disgraced Schleicher. The Nazis, recognizing the precariousness of their position, have swallowed their pride and endorsed Seeckt for the presidency. [? if not hindenburg_term_extended: They deem him sufficiently right-wing—after all, he once wrote to his sister urging her to vote for [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] in 1932. ?] The **Communists** are too disorganized following Schleicher's crackdown, and are unable to field a candidate for president. They will be backing whoever we choose to back, provided it's a socialist. Many republicans of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?], and **SPD** float the idea of running Hugo Eckener, a nationally renowed Zeppelin captain, as a unity candidate. While he has some nationalistic views, he is also ardently opposed to Nazism. Barring that, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] are planning to run separate candidates in the first round if the **SPD** runs its own candidate. The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is considering nominating Konrad Adenauer, mayor of Köln and member of the Prussian state legislature. He calls for an alliance of conservative Christian democrats that encompasses both Catholics and Protestants. The [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] might nominate Otto Gessler, former defense minister, who has crossover appeal to conservatives in the moderate right and other parties who dislike the renewed nationalist-Nazi alliance. As for the **SPD**, we could support a joint Weimar Coalition candidate or run our own. A leading candidate is Albert Grzesinski of our Reformist faction. Former Interior Minister of Prussia and currently Berlin’s Police Chief, he has played a central role in combating both far-right and left-wing extremism. Most notably, he helped organize the general strike that brought down Schleicher. However, his hardline stance against the **Communists**—including his suppression of their demonstrations—has made him unacceptable to them. Alternatively, we could nominate Otto Wels, our party chairman and leader of the Centrist faction. He is palatable to the bourgeois parties and the Communists, who may begrudgingly tolerate his candidacy.

hindenburg_explode_referendum.bodyHtml:
= Referendum to Recall President Hindenburg
After a month of intense, violence-filled campaigning and relentless propaganda from both sides, the German people now vote on Hindenburg’s fate—a decision that may determine the future of the Republic itself.
Unlike previous referendums, this one requires only a majority of those voting—not of all eligible voters—to succeed.

hindenburg_explode_referendum_campaign.subtitleHtml: How should we campaign for the referendum?
hindenburg_explode_referendum_campaign.bodyHtml: = Hindenburg Referendum campaign With the referendum fast approaching, we have a chance to intensify our campaign and tip the scales in our favor. President Hindenburg’s health has deteriorated significantly since the last election, leaving him unable to participate—delegating the campaign effort to Treviranus and the nationalists. The **ASPD** have declared their full support for Hindenburg, while the **DSU** backs him more quietly. This fragmented and feeble campaign on the Right may offer us a chance to win through sheer voter turnout. That said, we must not grow complacent.

hindenburg_explode_referendum_campaign.b.bodyHtml: The Weimar Coalition has reunited to defend the very constitution we forged together—holding joint rallies and coordinating their messaging in a show of unity. This helps dismantle the Right’s narrative that the referendum is a socialist power grab.

hindenburg_explode_referendum.hindenburg.bodyHtml:
Unfortunately, the referendum has failed with [+ hindenburg_ref_votes +]% of the vote. So much for nothing.
Hindenburg has been agitated by the weakness of the incumbent government and, under the influence of his Camarilla, will decide on Treviranus's successor himself, as he considers another set of Reichstag elections unacceptable.

The referendum succeeds with [+ hindenburg_ref_votes +]% of the vote—Germany is saved! If the current coalition holds, we may finally elect a democratic president capable of guiding the nation out of the chaos left by Hindenburg and Schleicher.
Disgraced and isolated, Hindenburg is forced to resign from the presidency. In his place, [? if president == "Bumke (acting)": Erwin Bumke?][? if president == "Großmann (acting)": Hermann Großmann?], President of the Reich Court, has been elevated to acting president until new elections are held.
Presidential elections are scheduled for Week [+ rubicon_president_week +] of [+ rubicon_president_month : month +], [+ rubicon_president_year +].

params.source: hindenburg_ref_win if hindenburg_ref_votes >= 50; hindenburg_ref_lose if hindenburg_ref_votes < 50

hindenburg_explode_referendum.schizo.bodyHtml:
Under the influence of Franz von Papen—and apparently Schleicher as well—Hindenburg has appointed Wilhelm III, eldest son of the last German Emperor, as Chancellor, reportedly with his father’s blessing.
It is clear the chaos of the past year has taken its toll. In the end, Hindenburg now trusts no one but his dearest friend, Papen. It's unknown of the former chancellor's reasoning behind such a pick, but perhaps he would've hoped that reinstating a monarchy, the people can rally around him as they once rallied around Hindenburg. 
A bloody three-way civil war is inevitable.

hindenburg_extended.bodyHtml: Despite opposition from the left-wing parties, the resolution passes with the support of all parties to our right[? if not lvp_formed:, except for the **[+ ddp_name +]**[? if not z_in_gov_mini: and Center Party?]?][? if lvp_formed and not z_in_gov_mini: except for the Center Party?].

hindenburg_extention.subtitleHtml: An amendment to the constitution can be made...
hindenburg_extention.bodyHtml: = Resolution to Extend Hindenburg's Term A resolution has been introduced by the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical" and bruning_time: [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical" and not bruning_time: [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]?] to amend the constitution and extend Hindenburg's term by two years. If all parties apart from those in the national [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": opposition?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": opposition?] and the **Communists** were to vote in favor, it would surpass the required two-thirds majority. Despite Hindenburg being the candidate of the right and strenuously opposed by the Weimar Coalition parties in 1925, he has, contrary to our fears, not used his office to subvert the constitution and the republic as a whole. This has put him at odds with his more conservative supporters who backed him in 1925. We can either support this resolution, postponing elections in what many in the party believe to be an anti-democratic act, or vote with the extremists against it.

hitler_bad.titleHtml: How will this affect [+ nsdap_leader +] and his party?
hitler_bad.bodyHtml: In a meeting between [+ nsdap_leader +] and the Nazi gauleiters immediately after the Lippe results became known, it was clear—they were not pleased. The consensus among the leadership was that [+ nsdap_leader +]’s all-or-nothing strategy is failing. They cannot simply wait for Hindenburg to have a sudden change of heart, nor can they rely on a victory at the ballot box. In an attempt to crush dissent, [+ nsdap_leader +] unleashed the full force of his anger on Strasser—denouncing the man who once helped elevate him as a traitor and accusing him of long-standing subversion. He warned that anyone questioning his strategy was aligning themselves with the disgraced Strasser. But many in the room still sympathized with Strasser’s arguments, and the tirade only deepened their disillusionment with the man they had once seen as a prophet. The denunciation—and the evident unrest among the Nazi leadership—quickly leaked to the press. Word soon reached Chancellor von Schleicher, who was elated at their collapse and hopeful that it might finally compel [+ nsdap_leader +] to act more rationally.

hitler_cabinet_1.bodyHtml: = The Enabling Act As the Reichstag gets back to business once again, the bill on debate is not one of no-confidence, but rather an "Enabling Act" proposed by [+ nsdap_chancellor +] and the **NSDAP**. With Schleicher's blessing, the cabinet believes that certain elements of the constitution will have to suspended in order to crush the **Communists** and Reichsbanner. However, this is not something the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] can easily swallow...

hitler_eh.bodyHtml: In a meeting between [+ nsdap_leader +] and the Nazi gauleiters, immediately after the Lippe results were known, things could have turned disastrous if the results had been worse, with unrest already rising among the grassroots. While the Nazi gains somewhat mitigated the unrest, the gauleiters still voiced concerns about [+ nsdap_leader +]'s strategy. Leaks of discontent continue to reach the press. In an attempt to suppress dissent, he unleashed the full force of his anger against Strasser, condemning the person responsible for his rise to power as a traitor and accusing him of numerous offenses stretching back many years. [+ nsdap_leader +] implied that anyone expressing doubts about his all-or-nothing strategy was an accomplice of the disgraced Strasser. This appears to have silenced dissent among the gauleiters. His denunciation of his former ally has been kept out of the press, deliberately by [+ nsdap_leader +] to shield the party from political fallout due to rumors of a split within its ranks. However, the bad news eventually reaches Chancellor von Schleicher, as the only person willing to cooperate with him in the party is, in fact, 'finished.'

hitler_explode.titleHtml: How will this affect [+ nsdap_leader +] and his party?
hitler_explode.bodyHtml: In a meeting between [+ nsdap_leader +] and the Nazi gauleiters immediately after the Lippe results became known, it was clear—they were outraged. The consensus among the leadership was that [+ nsdap_leader +]’s all-or-nothing strategy was failing, and the party was collapsing fast. They could no longer wait for Hindenburg to have a sudden change of heart, nor could they rely on a victory at the ballot box. In a fit of rage, [+ nsdap_leader +] launched into a long and incoherent tirade against Strasser—denouncing the man who once helped elevate him as a traitor and accusing him of long-standing subversion. Many in the room still sympathized with Strasser’s arguments, and the outburst only deepened their disillusionment with the man they had once regarded as a prophet. After [+ nsdap_leader +] seemingly lost control, a growing minority within the party now openly call for a reconciliation with Strasser and the **NSDAP** entering the Schleicher cabinet. The unrest within the party has quickly leaked to the press, with numerous local **NSDAP** and **SA** leaders now at each other’s throats, accelerating the party's collapse.

hitler_naturalization.subtitleHtml: Hitler still hadn't achieved German citizenship yet...
hitler_naturalization.bodyHtml: = Naturalization of Adolf Hitler The leader of the Nazis, Adolf Hitler, remains a stateless person after renouncing his Austrian citizenship in 1925. Numerous attempts have been made by him and his supporters to secure a civil service appointment, as this would automatically grant him German citizenship under existing law—making it the easiest path to naturalization. Citizenship is a prerequisite for Hitler to become President or Chancellor and would bolster his image as the "Führer of the Germans." [? if thuringia_nsdap: Wilhelm Frick, former **NSDAP** minister in Thuringia, has managed to appoint Hitler as Gendarmerie Commissioner in a small Thuringian town. However, for reasons unknown, Hitler tore up his own certificate of appointment. ?][? if brunswick_hitler: In the small Free State of Brunswick, a **NSDAP**-**DNVP** coalition has been governing with the support of the bourgeois parties. In an attempt to secure Hitler's citizenship, they sought to appoint him as a professor in secret. However, the scheme was exposed and halted due to his lack of academic qualifications. A parliamentary inquiry is now in progress, but further legal prosecution is blocked by the bourgeois parties. This revelation has tarnished his reputation across Germany. ?] With the presidential elections approaching, it is likely that Hitler will make one final attempt to obtain citizenship.

hugenberg_dnf.bodyHtml: Hugenberg and the **DNF**, once buoyed by their early popularity as one of the few parties to unconditionally back Papen, have since soured their relations with the chancellery. Hugenberg's demand for full control over the agricultural and economic ministries has strained ties, and his uncompromising opposition to Schleicher has sparked discontent within the **DNF**—a party once built entirely from his loyalists. Many of his former allies are now bewildered that Hugenberg would turn against a fellow reactionary, especially one who ostensibly shares his vision of steering Germany toward authoritarian rule. With Hugenberg’s personal fortune—once sustained by his media empire—running dry, and industrial backers remaining firmly opposed to his leadership, frustrated members and former confidants are abandoning ship. They now flock to the German National Unity Front, preferring to back Schleicher directly without Hugenberg standing in their way.

choices.labelHtml: The German National Unity Front welcomes its new members.

hugenberg_dnvp.bodyHtml: Initially, Hugenberg and his **DNVP** initially stood to gain the most by backing the reactionary Papen cabinet. However, relations soured with the chancellery after Schleicher refused to grant him full control over the agricultural and economic ministries. His uncompromising opposition to Schleicher has sparked widespread discontent within the **DNVP**, eroding Hugenberg’s once unchallenged authority among both party leaders and the rank-and-file. Many find it bewildering that Hugenberg would oppose a fellow reactionary, especially one presumably sharing his goal of steering Germany toward authoritarian rule. With internal party democracy long dead—party congresses stacked with loyalists serving as mere rubber stamps—dissenters have little choice. Now, the majority within the party are seizing Schleicher’s lifeline: the absorption of friendly nationalists into the German National Unity Front, where they hope to finally gain a hand in shaping the chancellor's future policies.

choices.labelHtml: The German National Unity Front welcomes its new members.

hugenbergremoval.bodyHtml: [? if young_plan_signatures < 10: The failure of the Young Plan referendum to reach the 10% threshold?][? if young_plan_signatures < 10 and was_in_right_coalition: and?] [? if was_in_right_coalition: Hugenberg's unpopular decision to exit the right-wing coalition exactly a year from now?] and the declining popularity of the **DNVP** has convinced the majority of the party to vote out Hugenberg, replacing him with Treviranus, a member of the "Young Conservative" wing of the party. The Young Conservatives are in favor of governmental participation, advancing their goals in the framework of the system. However, the national conservatives retain heavy control over the party and the **DNVP** isn't exactly a democratic party yet. [? if stegerwald_path: This leaves the **DNVP** as a more nationalistic, conservative alternative to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]. ?] In response, Hugenberg threatens to take himself and his supporters into a new splinter party, which is unlikely to gain much support, considering he remains deeply unpopular beyond his loyal following.

hugo.subtitleHtml: Otto Hugo aims to consolidate party control in the hands of the industrialists.
hugo.bodyHtml: Otto Hugo has unexpectedly won the vote to replace [+ old_dvp_leader +] as chairman of the DVP. Backed by unified support from the party’s right wing and endorsed by Ernst Scholz, he narrowly defeated Kardorff. His election marks a decisive and likely irreversible shift to the right[? if dvp_reform:, even repealing Stresemann’s reforms to the party’s internal structure?], as Hugo moves to ensure industrialist dominance over the **DVP**’s decision-making apparatus. He holds openly hostile views toward parties to the left of the **DVP**, and prefers alignment with the **DNVP** and even the **NSDAP** over cooperation with us. Unsurprisingly, Hugo’s industrial ties and lack of public appeal—especially in contrast to Luther—have caused the **DVP** to suffer in the polls. The primary beneficiary is the **[+ ddp_name +]**, which is shifting rightward to capture the disaffected middle-class vote.

ideology.bodyHtml: #subtitle: Setting the party's ideological direction. = Questions of Ideology The **SPD** is torn between many different ideological currents. The Center Marxism of Karl Kautsky remains the best way to resolve our internal contradictions.

Pursue the fusion of socialism and patriotism.

ideology.reform.bodyHtml: The reformist wing of the party seeks to preserve the Republic and the democratic system of government, and is most supportive of coalitions with the other pro-democracy parties.

params.source: changed if changed = 1

ideology.socpat.bodyHtml: The social patriot wing of the party, widely regarded as Schleicher's puppets, is the most supportive of the **SPD** and ADGB adopting a more nationalist stance.

params.source: changed if changed = 1

if.bodyHtml: We develop an entire campaign against antisemitism under the auspices of the **Iron** **Front**. Hopefully our campaign can sway the workers away from Nazism.

params.code: state.flags['confronting_antisemitism'] += 2; state.flags['sa_strength'] -= 20; state.flags['democratization'] += 1; state.flags['pacifism'] += 1; state.flags['nationalism'] -= 5*(1-state.flags['dissent']); state.flags['workers_nsdap'] -= 6*(1-state.flags['dissent']);
params.source: confronting_antisemitism += 2; sa_strength -= 20; democratization += 1; pacifism += 1; nationalism -= 5*(1-dissent); workers_nsdap -= 6*(1-dissent);

if_end.bodyHtml: The **Iron** **Front** has given a new energy to our party.

if_training.bodyHtml: As part of the **Iron** **Front**, we are increasing coordination between the Reichsbanner and the unions, and many union members want to become more involved.

implement_wtb_deficit.bodyHtml: We have entered the realm of deficit spending. Our coalition partners are disgusted, but the works plan is enacted anyway. Money is beginning to flow through the economy via investments in large-scale public works. [? if in_popular_front or in_left_front: The **KPD** opposes the WTB plan, seeing it as a rescue of capitalism rather than a step towards real socialism. ?] ####################### left economic policies (socializations)

implement_wtb_no_deficit.bodyHtml: We have started to enact the WTB plan. Money is beginning to flow through the economy via investments in large-scale public works. The bourgeois parties express concerns about inflation and spending, preferring tax cuts to address the economic crisis. improve_east.titleHtml: Improve our relations with our eastern neighbors.
improve_east.bodyHtml: We also aim to improve relations with our eastern neighbors, Poland and Czechoslovakia, who are rightfully terrified of German aggression. Hopefully we can convince them of our peaceful intentions.

improve_relations.titleHtml: Improve relations with the parties of the coalition.
improve_relations.bodyHtml: We have increased our level of contact and discussions with the parties of the coalition, primarily the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] [? if not lvp_formed and dvp_exist:and **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed:and **LVP**?]. The **DNVP** does its best to obstruct our efforts at constructive cooperation with Brüning. Our attempts to reach out to the center-right are met with disdain by leftists within our party.

improve_soviet.titleHtml: Improve our relations with the **Soviet Union**.
improve_soviet.subtitleHtml: We could also broach the question of the **KPD**...
improve_soviet.bodyHtml: The Soviet Union also suffered from the international order created by the Treaty of Versailles; they have been participating in our secret rearmament program. The Treaty of Rapallo in 1922 affirmed our friendly relations. The Soviets are asking for economic and developmental assistance. They are still a poor country on the whole, and are desperately trying to catch up to the western powers. There is a chance that our anti-communist coalition partners would be upset, but we could assuage them by asking the Soviets for secret assistance in training and equipping the Reichswehr.

choices.labelHtml: Provide aid, in exchange for Reichswehr assistance.
Provide aid, in exchange for only good relations.

improve_soviet_eco.titleHtml: Expand our exports to the **Soviet Union**.
improve_soviet_eco.subtitleHtml: A win for our economy and for our relationship with the **KPD**.
improve_soviet_eco.bodyHtml: The Soviet Union, with its centrally planned economy and isolation from global markets, has insulated itself from the effects of the Great Depression. They have since been rapidly industrializing in accordance with their Five-Year Plan, making them a prime partner for exports, especially as tariffs from our nominal trading partners in the West have increased, along with their general isolation from international markets. The Soviets are pleased by this, and we stand to reap the economic benefits. The only downside is that the right-wing propaganda machine has decried this action, pressuring [? if president == "Hindenburg": President Hindenburg and?] the bourgeois parties to break with us.

improve_west.titleHtml: Improve our relations with the Western Allies.
improve_west.bodyHtml: The key to peace in Europe is a rapprochement between France and Germany. We are taking steps towards that rapprochement. [? if young_plan_seen == 0 : This is difficult to do when France is occupying a major portion of Germany's territory, but we are working on that part. ?]

increase.subtitleHtml: We will gain [+ dues + 1 +] resources per year. +1 resource [? if unemployed >= 15 : Given the present economic situation, this may be painful. ?][? if dues >= 4 : Dues are already rather high; increasing them might reduce our membership. ?]
increase.bodyHtml: Our members grumble at this, and some of the less committed members leave. But now, we have access to additional resources. [? if unemployed >= 15 : Because of the presently high unemployment, our members are feeling the extra burden hard. ?] The higher dues will make it more difficult for the **SPD** to expand electorally.

increase_employers.subtitleHtml: Employers are strongly against this. [? if in_grand_coalition: The [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] will likely break the coalition. ?][? if in_weimar_coalition and lvp_formed: The **LVP** will likely break the coalition. ?]
increase_employers.bodyHtml: We have increased employer contributions to the unemployment insurance fund, allowing the program to continue without hurting workers and the unemployed. infotext.bodyHtml: Dynamic Social Democracy is an ambitious overhaul mod aimed to bring historical realism and a dynamic party system to the late Weimar Republic. This mod heavily focuses on the Nazi Party's rise to power, and puts emphasis on the disastrous mistakes made by the parties surrounding the **SPD**, which effectively enabled Adolf Hitler's eventual appointment by Hindenburg. This aspect is not represented in the base game, which instead focuses on the player's direct impact. The Weimar party system in this mod reacts to your every move, adjusting ideologies and strategies accordingly. Hindenburg and the bourgeois parties now serve as more realistic and impactful obstacles, as they did in real life. A real life example is the situation following the 1928 federal election, despite the **SPD**'s clear electoral mandate in 1928, the Center, **DVP**, and Hindenburg himself initially opposed the formation of the Grand Coalition. However, Stresemann's intervention, Hindenburg's desire to use the **SPD**'s anti-militarist stance to renegotiate German reparations, and his strategy to burden the **SPD** with governance to decrease their popularity, is what made this unlikely arrangement possible. What was initially seen with positivity by the **SPD** at the time; their entrance into government may be one of the biggest reasons for the demise of German democracy. By March 1930, all of the factors above were no longer in play, the line between the **DVP** and the parties on the far-right were blurred, the Young Plan was ratified, and the **SPD** was suffering as a result of the economic depression. The appointment of Bruning under an emergency government wasn't improvised when the **DVP** took down the Grand Coalition, it has been an idea longed by Schleicher, Hindenburg, and many reactionary elites. "On 6 January 1930, Hugenberg was summoned to meet President Paul von Hindenburg, who told him that now the Young Plan had been passed, he had no more need for Müller, and he was planning to bring in a new presidential government very soon that would be "anti-parliamentary and anti-Marxist"." Your primary goal is to save German democracy, saving Social Democracy is secondary.

inter_party_relationships.bodyHtml: #subtitle: Building relations with the other political parties of Germany. = Inter-Party Relationships The **SPD** cannot govern by itself yet. Because we do not have an electoral majority, we need the support of other parties. Recently, our governments have consisted of the Weimar Coalition of the **SPD**, Center, and [? if ddp_name == "DDP" and not lvp_formed: **Democratic**?][? if ddp_name == "DStP" and not lvp_formed: **State**?][? if lvp_formed: **Liberal People's**?] parties. [? if cvp_formed: However the formation of the **[+ z_party_name +]** has only really made cooperation with the liberals possible. ?] We can reach out and build additional connections with these parties, or perhaps we can stand alone.

inter_party_relationships.kpd_rectificat.bodyHtml: One stumbling block for our relations with the **KPD** is our history of conflict, dating back to 1918 and 1919. The **KPD** is especially contemptuous of Gustav Noske, the **SPD** "bloodhound" who reportedly ordered the violent suppression of the Spartacist uprising and other **KPD** revolts. They also blame us for the deaths of Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht, two **SPD**-turned-**KPD** leaders who were killed during the suppression of the uprising. For further improvements in **KPD** relations, it might be necessary to expel Noske, and hold some sort of commemoration for Luxemburg and Liebknecht.

inter_party_relationships.nsdap.bodyHtml: We have began our work in wholesomeifying Gregor Strasser, who is beginning to form a moderate pro-democratic National Social Democratic faction within the **NSDAP** under Hitler's nose. Our Left and Center factions voice their disapproval.

This leads to tensions with the moderates and reformists within our party, and criticism from the conservative and liberal parties.

interior.titleHtml: The Nazis crack down on the Reichsbanner and **RFB**!
interior.subtitleHtml: Ordered by Wilhelm Frick of the Interior Ministry.

params.source: interior_1 if not dsu_policy; interior_2 if dsu_policy

interior_1.bodyHtml: With the Nazis now controlling the Interior Ministry, they hold jurisdiction over the federal police. [? if prussia_leader != "Strasser": Without control of the Prussian Interior Ministry, their reach is limited—though they have already begun turning the federal police into a force loyal to the Nazis. ?][? if prussia_leader == "Strasser": The Prussian Interior Ministry, however, is the real prize—its police force now answers entirely to them, with widespread purges of republican officials taking place. ?]Fortunately, Schleicher has barred Nazi Party members from joining the police, maintaining the same restriction already enforced in the Reichswehr. Lately, we have observed the police exclusively targeting Reichsbanner and **RFB** fighters, while openly shielding far-right demonstrations from our protests. They have even persuaded Schleicher to transfer command of the Reichswehr's militia to the Interior Ministry, citing the need for centralized control.

interior_2.bodyHtml: The Nazis have continued cracking down on even lawful leftist activity, on bogus claims of "inciting violence." It seems Frick is doing Schleicher's dirty work for him—cracking down on democrats and all, while Schleicher is still viewed highly in the eyes of many workers.

international_relations.bodyHtml: #subtitle: Building ties with our fraternal socialist parties. At the Labor and Socialist International, we can forge contacts with our fraternal socialist parties in Europe and across the world.

choices.labelHtml: Build relationships with the French SFIO and British Labour Party to move their governments in Germany's favor.
Learn organization and street fighting from the Austrian SDAPÖ.
Learn the path of economics and reform from the Scandinavian social democrats.
Forget the second international - embed a spy in the Comintern's conference.
Contact the Socialist Party of America.
We do not need international contacts at the moment.

international_relations.america.bodyHtml: The Socialist Party of America is tiny and has limited support. There is not much we can do for them, and conversely, not much they can do for us.

[? if austrian_parliament_seen and not austrian_civil_war_seen: We are also helping the Austrian Social Democratic Worker's Party build up their resources in preparation for a future struggle, legally and illegally. ?]

Needless to say, this is not good for our relationship with the communists. By observing the Comintern, we can better understand the **KPD**, enabling us to potentially improve relations, or counter the **KPD** if it may come to that.

international_relations.scandi.bodyHtml: The programs of the Nordic socialists involve active government intervention in the economy. We can learn from their economic strategies, and how they moved beyond their working-class base to attract a broader set of constituents.

jarres.titleHtml: Karl Jarres, mayor of Duisburg, former Vice-Chancellor, and the **DVP**'s candidate in 1925.
jarres.bodyHtml: Karl Jarres, having been compelled to withdraw his candidacy in 1925 in favor of Hindenburg, has once again entered the race. While not an overtly partisan figure—having remained relatively quiet in national politics in recent years—Jarres is expected to share many of the same anti-**SPD** biases that Hindenburg currently harbors. Moreover, he subscribes to the "taming strategy" concerning the Nazis. It is imperative that we field a candidate of our own to prevent such an outcome. His candidacy is supported by the **DVP**.

jarres_win.bodyHtml: Perhaps surprisingly, Karl Jarres has made an unforeseen comeback and won the presidency. We hope that his governance will be an improvement over that of Hindenburg, and that he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

join.bodyHtml: It is difficult to persuade the **Communists** to let us march with them, given the histories of their party and ours. However, they eventually relent. The display of proletarian unity inspires the workers and terrifies the bourgeoisie and middle class. judiciary.bodyHtml: = Judiciary Reform The Judiciary is one of the most reactionary components of the government, along with the military. Many jurists have held office since the days of the Emperor. They give violent fascists like Adolf Hitler laughably light sentences, while ruthlessly persecuting leftists and pacifists for lesser crimes. [? if judicial_reform <= 0 : There is great demand in our membership for reforming the judiciary, although this may bring us into a collision course with our coalition allies. ?] [? if judicial_reform == 1 : We have started on the path to judicial reform. While some of the most antediluvian and biased justices have been replaced, many still remain. More should be done. ?] [? if judicial_reform >= 2 : We have successfully reformed the judiciary, to some extent. At the very least, the courts will not actively obstruct our attempts to prosecute crimes committed by the far-right. ?]

kaiser_party_congress.bodyHtml: = 1930 [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] Conference The election of Jakob Kaiser to the leadership of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has stalled any progress toward transforming the party into a true Christian People's Party. His left-leaning stances have alienated potential voters on the Protestant Right, leaving the party adrift—uncertain of its identity. Is it to remain a predominantly Catholic, left-leaning party of labor and social reform, or evolve into a broader, right-of-center *Volkspartei*? Despite Kaiser himself supporting Stegerwald’s original vision of Christian unity, he has paradoxically become the chief obstacle in the eyes of the party’s right wing—figures like Stegerwald and Adenauer now seek to remove him, hoping to steer the party back toward its previous course. However, we retain significant influence within the party’s Christian Left faction and its affiliated trade unions—leverage that could tip the scales back in Kaiser’s favor, should we choose to intervene.

kaiser_party_congress.adenauer.subtitleHtml: The Mayor of Cologne, and a strong supporter of 'leaving the tower'. Situated on the right-wing of the party.
kaiser_party_congress.adenauer.bodyHtml: The influx of Protestant conservatives into the Center Party has rendered Jakob Kaiser’s leadership untenable. In a decisive internal vote of no confidence, Kaiser has been ousted—replaced by Stegerwald ally and long-serving Mayor of Cologne, Konrad Adenauer. Adenauer seeks to carry forward Stegerwald’s vision: transforming the party into the dominant force of the German Right. Unsurprisingly, this development has sparked outrage among the Christian Left and Kaiser’s supporters, many of whom have resigned their posts in protest. The party’s close ties to left-leaning unions have been severely strained, plunging the organization into temporary disarray as labor-aligned factions voice their anger. Yet despite this internal upheaval, the party remains poised to continue its cannibalization of the fragmented right—especially the beleaguered **DNVP**. This shift is symbolized by the party's rebranding as the Christliche Volkspartei (Christian People's Party). [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": Talks of a merger with the **DNVP** are becoming increasingly common—though support is limited to their People's Conservatives and Christian Socials. A merger remains impossible without one of those factions having strong, centralized leadership within their party. At the same time, we must prevent any government cooperation between them and the Center—lest we allow conditions for such a union to emerge. ?]

kaiser_party_congress.kaiser.bodyHtml: Through our grassroots connections and sheer determination, we have somehow managed to secure the reelection of Jakob Kaiser as chairman of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]. His removal had once seemed all but inevitable—yet, by some miracle, the present conditions have convinced a majority of the party to rally behind him once more. As a gesture of compromise, however, Kaiser has agreed to officially rename the party to the Christliche Volkspartei (Christian People's Party). Beyond this cosmetic change—given the historic Catholic association with the 'Center' label—the party's platform remains largely unchanged. Even so, this outcome has enraged the party’s right wing. Many of its Protestant conservatives have resigned in protest, retreating to their party of origin.

kellogg_briand.bodyHtml: #face-image: img/portraits/StresemannGustav.jpg = Kellogg-Briand Pact An international treaty has been negotiated which promises an end to war. The treaty, negotiated by American Secretary of State Frank Kellogg and French foreign minister Aristide Briand, promises that its signatories will renounce the use of war, and will promise to settle their disputes peacefully. Countries throughout the world are lining up to sign this idealistic agreement. Its detractors argue that it has no enforcement mechanism, and thus is merely a worthless piece of paper. [? if foreign_minister_party = "DVP": Our foreign Minister Gustav Stresemann has signed the treaty. The reaction is generally muted; both pacifists and militarists are skeptical about the efficacy of the treaty. Additionally, during [+ foreign_minister +]'s trip to Paris, there has been success in bringing the French to consider withdrawing from the Rhineland early and to agree to another review of our reparations by foreign experts. ?][? if foreign_minister_party = "Z": Our foreign Minister Joseph Wirth has signed the treaty. The reaction is generally muted; both pacifists and militarists are skeptical about the efficacy of the treaty. Additionally, during [+ foreign_minister +]'s trip to Paris, there has been success in bringing the French to consider withdrawing from the Rhineland early and to agree to another review of our reparations by foreign experts. ?]

kellogg_briand.not_enough.bodyHtml: Despite the idealism behind the treaty, it is inadequate for its goal of preventing wars. There must be some enforcement mechanism, perhaps automatic trade sanctions, or an intervention force controlled by the League of Nations. As it stands, the League of Nations and this treaty is toothless.

Additionally, during [+ foreign_minister +]'s trip to Paris, there has been success in bringing the French to consider withdrawing from the Rhineland early and to agree to another review of our reparations by foreign experts.

kellogg_briand.step_forward.titleHtml: The treaty is a step forward for peace.
kellogg_briand.step_forward.bodyHtml: Despite our misgivings about the treaty, it still represents a step forward for the cause of international peace.

keudell.bodyHtml: Von Keudell, long considered the underdog, has won the election for the **DNVP** chairmanship. Branding himself as the voice of the "young generation," he criticized the party's entrenched ties to Ruhr industrialists and elites as liabilities that alienate younger voters. While his ascent irritates some within the party establishment, he is nonetheless expected to continue Westarp’s general decision-making style—albeit with a stronger focus on broadening support among the emerging urban middle class.

kpd_ban.titleHtml: The "Reichstag Fire Decree" is signed by Hindenburg.
kpd_ban.bodyHtml: Contained within the Reichstag Fire Decree are measures that nullify key civil liberties and rights guaranteed by the Weimar constitution. This grants Schleicher the full power of the state to prosecute **Communists**, radical socialists, and anyone the government deems a threat. Ernst Thälmann is arrested the following day, along with the **KPD**'s Reichstag deputies. Many others flee to Moscow; those less fortunate are thrown into forced labor camps, sentenced to grueling hours on public works. **RFB** fighters are summarily executed by special local courts. The Reichswehr and far-right militias eagerly suppress protests and replace local **Communist** mayors with [? if dnef_formed: **DNEF**?][? if not dnef_formed: Schleicher?] loyalists. [? if prussia_leader == "Goerdeler": Goerdeler, despite hopes that he would shift toward democratic rule, ignores the Center Party's objections and rules with Schleicher's full confidence. ?][? if prussia_leader == "Braun" or prussia_leader == "Stegerwald" or prussia_leader == "Luther" or prussia_leader == "Brüning": The Prussian government refuses to side with Schleicher here, and does not enforce his orders. ?] [? if sapd_formed: Alongside the **KPD**, the **SAPD** is declared complicit and its members are hunted down just the same. Are we really going to let the government throw our former comrades into prisons? ?][? if not sapd_formed: Are we really going to let the government throw our comrades into prisons? ?]

kpd_blutmai.bodyHtml: After the events of Blütmai, reconciling with the Communists is difficult, if not impossible. Nevertheless, we must try.
