kpd_conference.subtitleHtml: The **KPD** chooses their new central committee - will the Wittorf Affair have an influence on their choice?
kpd_conference.bodyHtml: = **KPD** Party Conference Now is the **KPD**'s national party conference, where they will choose their new leadership. The shadow of the Wittorf Affair hangs over it. On one hand are the hardline supporters of Thälmann, who support a "social fascists" policy that places the **SPD** as equivalent to the Nazis. On the other hand is the "Conciliator" faction, who support a more cooperative policy towards the **SPD**. After our discussion with the Soviets, we are inclined to believe that Stalin is at least open to the Conciliators. In order to affect the **KPD**'s leadership elections, we have to influence both the Comintern leaders as as well as the **KPD** membership.

kpd_conference.conciliator_fail.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, we could not influence the **KPD** leadership election against the hardliners. Thälmann quickly moves to consolidate absolute leadership, expelling or exiling his opponents.

kpd_conference.conciliator_success.titleHtml: The Conciliators are the new leadership of the **KPD**.
kpd_conference.conciliator_success.bodyHtml: With our support, the Conciliators have won the leadership contest! The new leadership is a group of Conciliators, including Arthur Ewert, Hugo Eberlein, and Ernst Meyer. Thälmann remains, but largely as a figurehead only, it seems. We hope that the new leadership will be more inclined towards cooperation.

kpd_policy.subtitleHtml: The **KPD** ministers are carrying out their policy portfolios.
kpd_policy.bodyHtml: #tags: event #max-choices: 1 # disable this event for now - the **KPD** is abstentionist in government. This position is loosely based on Paul Levi's ideas during the Kapp Putsch. A **KPD** that is willing to support an SPD government would necessarily have some different policy ideas from the Thälmann Stalinist line, so I looked to the earlier Paul Levi **KPD** as well as the French popular front for ideas. # ironically the hypothetical **KPD** position towards the Popular Front is basically analogous to the SPD position towards the Brüning government (i.e. toleration). # Sources: Gaido, Daniel. “Paul Levi and the Origins of the United-Front Policy in the Communist International.” Historical Materialism 25, no. 1 (2017): 131–74. https://doi.org/10.1163/1569206x-12341515. # LaPorte, Norman H. “The German Communist Party in Saxony, 1924-1933 : Factionalism, Fratricide and Political Failure,” 1998. http://dspace.stir.ac.uk/handle/1893/3259. = **KPD** Policy # The Communist-run ministries are pursuing their own policy course. It is up to us whether to support or oppose these policies. # different policies for every minister choice

kpd_policy.economy.subtitleHtml: The Economy Ministry is pursuing a policy of nationalizations.
kpd_policy.economy.bodyHtml: The **KPD**-controlled Economy Ministry is planning a policy of mass nationalizations. [? if budget < 3 : They plan to use deficit spending to finance state takeovers of underutilized industrial enterprises, and run them for the benefit of the workers. ?] [? if budget >= 3 : They plan to buy out closed and underutilized industrial enterprises, and run them at full capacity for the benefit of the workers. ?] Do we support this policy?

kpd_policy.economy_oppose.bodyHtml: After opposing the nationalization policy, the **KPD** has commenced a propaganda campaign against us, accusing the **SPD** of yet another perfidy.

kpd_policy.economy_support.bodyHtml: The **KPD** has gained credit with the workers for enabling many to keep their jobs. Meanwhile, the bourgeois parties and middle-class voters blame the **SPD** for enabling the nationalizations.

kpd_rectification_of_history.bodyHtml: One stumbling block for our relations with the **KPD** is our history of conflict, dating back to 1918 and 1919. The **KPD** is especially contemptuous of Gustav Noske, the **SPD** "bloodhound" who reportedly ordered the violent suppression of the Spartacist uprising and other **KPD** revolts. They also blame us for the deaths of Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht, two **SPD**-turned-**KPD** leaders who were killed during the suppression of the uprising. For further improvements in **KPD** relations, it might be necessary to expel Noske, and hold some sort of commemoration for Luxemburg and Liebknecht.

choices.labelHtml: Yes, we must apologize for our past actions.
No, we have no need to apologize.

kpd_vote_of_no_confidence.thalmann.bodyHtml: With great reluctance, President [+ president +] appoints [+ chancellor +] as chancellor. Immediately, [+ chancellor +] goes to work building a "Soviet Germany": consolidating as much power as possible in the **KPD**, purging state institutions of anti-communists, and sending street fighters against the "enemies of the people". In response to [+ chancellor +] being appointed Chancellor, the right-wing forces launches almost immediately launch an attempted coup. Troops of the **Stahlhelm** and Nazi **SA** enter Berlin and immediately begin clashing with our supporters! Reactionary officers within the Reichswehr have taken their troops out of the barracks and joined them with the **Stahlhelm** to stop the **KPD** from taking power. We are forced to be on the same side as the **KPD**, whether we want to or not.

kpd_vote_of_no_confidence.try_assuage.bodyHtml: How do we assuage the **KPD**?

Never mind. Let the vote happen.

labor_affairs.bodyHtml:
= Labor Affairs
The industrial Ruhr region is aflame with labor unrest. The employers have started a major lockout to force the workers to take more cuts to wages and benefits. There is a need for the Labor Ministry to arbitrate in conflicts between employers and workers.
#- @cancel_advisor_action

choices.labelHtml: Support the employers in their demands.
Try to strike a compromise between the sides.

labor_affairs.balance.subtitleHtml: Both sides need to share the pain in the current crisis.
labor_affairs.balance.bodyHtml:
Many workers are unhappy at our compromises, but they will learn to accept that we are all in a shared struggle against economic forces.
# options: support the workers in their demands, pushing back against the employers.
# this is the approach favored by the unions. While they do not get everything they desire, an agreement favorable to the workers is reached. The employer associations and their bourgeois allies accuse us of overstepping our bounds.
# try to make some compromise between the sides. Both sides need to share the pain in the current crisis.
# whatever it takes, end the strikes and unrest as soon as possible.
# this is not our business to intervene.
# We are the party of labor, and it is not our business to intervene? There is incredulity in the ranks. The workers are less likely to trust us in the future.

labor_affairs.support_employers.subtitleHtml: Popular among the bourgeoisie, much less so among the workers.
labor_affairs.support_employers.bodyHtml: The more radical workers despise our suppression of their strikes, recalling the days of Friedrich Ebert.

labor_influence.bodyHtml: An internal vote within the **SPD**'s leadership is called to finally settle the matter. With our hard work, we have finally convinced the majority of the party to adopt the WTB plan! [? if spd_in_government == 1 : We can begin implementing the plan as soon as possible, as long as we have the Economic and Finance ministries. ?][? if spd_in_government = 0 : We should emphasize the plan in our electoral propaganda. ?]

labor_oppose.bodyHtml: We oppose the **KPD**'s policy, and prevent it from being enacted. The **KPD** is displeased, as are the workers who would have stood to benefit.

labor_rights.bodyHtml:
#subtitle: Working hours, safety regulations, and unemployment insurance.
= Labor Rights
With control of the Labor Ministry, we can set national standards for labor. Our supporters expect us to enforce a 40-hour work week and enforce safety regulations, as well as fully fund the unemployment insurance program.
# enforce a 40-hour work week
# develop and enforce safety regulations in mines and industries
# works councils are part of another card...

Employers, however, resist this policy, arguing for more flexibility in hiring and firing.

labor_rights.working_hours.bodyHtml:
While a 40-hour work week was declared during the German Revolution in 1918, enforcement has become increasingly porous over the years. The capitalists have successfully added numerous exceptions and loopholes, returning to the old regime of forced overtime for workers.
Now, with the force of the Labor Ministry, we are finally enforcing the rights of workers to their own time. The bourgeoisie and their political representatives are displeased.

labor_unrest.subtitleHtml: Clashes between workers and employers in the Ruhr...
labor_unrest.bodyHtml: = Labor Unrest The mining and metals industry of the Ruhr region is beset by a wave of strikes against cuts to wages and benefits. Meanwhile, employers have started a retaliatory lockout to force their workers to accept these cuts. Both the strikers and the employers look to the **SPD** in the government to resolve this crisis.

choices.labelHtml: Support the employers in their demands.
Try to strike a compromise between the sides.

labor_unrest.balance.subtitleHtml: Both sides need to share the pain in the current crisis.
labor_unrest.balance.bodyHtml: We manage to convince Labor Minister [+ labor_minister +] (****[+ z_party_name +]****) to strike a compromise between both sides. Many workers are unhappy at our compromises, but they will learn to accept that we are all in a shared struggle against economic forces. This is perhaps the best we could do given the present circumstances.

lambach.bodyHtml: Against all odds, Walther Lambach survives a vote of no confidence at the party congress by allying with Treviranus’s Young Conservatives, securing a mandate to advance his vision for the **DNVP** in line with the late Adolf Stoecker, founder of the pre-war Christian Social Party. The party’s program, once tailored to its broad coalition, now includes significantly more worker-friendly policies, such as expanding social welfare, increasing pensions, and implementing progressive income taxes. they have even rejected austerity as a solution to Germany's current economic crisis. However, this shift has severely strained Lambach’s relationship with much of the party, particularly its industrial backers, who have begun withholding funding and redirecting it—albeit reluctantly—to more right-wing parties like the **DNF** and **NSDAP**. At the same time, severe internal opposition has moved to obstruct him any way they can, prompting Westarp to intervene and suppress a revolt within the party. As a result, Lambach was forced to make concessions, ensuring that his leadership would not stray too far from the **DNVP**'s traditional anti-Marxist and monarchist stance.

lambach_ousted.bodyHtml: Lambach has, perhaps predictably, lost a vote of no confidence, forcing him to relinquish his leadership to a candidate from the party’s traditionally conservative establishment. The agrarian wing, long opposed to both Lambach and the Christian Socials—united with them only by their shared hatred for Hugenberg—argues that only the appointment of the National Rural League (RLB) president can restore the party’s tarnished reputation in rural Germany. Meanwhile, the national conservatives favor re-electing Westarp, citing his unifying presence and experience in managing party dissent. They credit him with preventing many of the party’s more reactionary members from drifting toward the **DNF** during Lambach’s tenure.

choices.labelHtml: The party rallies around Westarp, restoring him to his former position.
The mantle is transferred to Martin Schiele and the agrarians.

land_reform.subtitleHtml: -1 budget - Break up the large aristocratic estates and give land to landless workers.
land_reform.bodyHtml:
With our policy of land reform, we are acquiring farmland from large estates, and giving the land to farmworkers' associations and small peasants. In essence, this brings class struggle to the countryside, breaking the semi-feudal property relations present in East Prussia and other areas with large estates. The bourgeois parties and large farmers despise our intrusion into the sacredness of private property, while leftists are cautiously optimistic.
[? if president == "Hindenburg": This policy has especially earned us the ire of President Hindenburg and his inner circle. ?]

lausanne.titleHtml: At least we walked away with something.
lausanne.bodyHtml: Germany’s reparations burden has been slashed by 90%, with no payments due for another three years. This eases the strain on the national budget and gives the government new room to maneuver on monetary and fiscal policy. Unfortunately for Papen, this does little to ease the near-universal hatred of his government. The far-right has denounced the treaty as a failure, outraged by his inability to secure any political or military concessions. Meanwhile, the republican parties and press have handed the credit to Brüning, who laid the groundwork for the conference in the first place. This development would've certainly been more impactful if Brüning had remained in office. Papen’s tarnished reputation among the Western Allies has severely undermined Germany’s standing at the Geneva Disarmament Conference. With many now convinced that militarism has triumphed in Berlin, Schleicher’s efforts to negotiate military parity are likely to face steep resistance.

lausanne_conference.bodyHtml: = Lausanne Conference At the Lausanne Conference, the Allies met with German representatives to resolve the issue of war reparations once and for all. Given the ongoing economic crisis, they concluded that Germany would be unable to resume payments after the moratorium ends. Therefore, our reparations have been reduced by 90%! In the end, Germany is required to make only a final payment of three billion marks, effectively ending future reparation obligations. This has greatly boosted investor confidence and sparked a new wave of capital inflows to Germany. This should reduce the strain on our budget. [? if spd_in_government and foreign_minister_party == "SPD": Even though this is not our accomplishment, our foreign ministry is eager to take credit for this accomplishment. ?][? if not spd_in_government and foreign_minister_party != "SPD": Even though this is not the work of the foreign ministry, it is eager to take credit for this accomplishment. ?] [? if bruning_time: Brüning, having skillfully leveraged the issues of foreign policy and reparations, stands to gain significantly. He has long argued that his austerity and deflationary measures were justified if they led to the abolition of reparations—and now, that vision has been realized. President Hindenburg is ecstatic at this outcome, lauding Brüning’s diplomatic prowess alongside his inner circle. Meanwhile, the urgency to bring the national opposition into government has waned, with many believing their support has reached their peak. ?]

lausanne_conference.military_parity.titleHtml: But of course, Schleicher stipulates that we demand military parity.
lausanne_conference.military_parity.subtitleHtml: This will be a severe betrayal of our values!
lausanne_conference.military_parity.bodyHtml: General Schleicher has demanded that we raise the issue of rearmament, which remains restricted under the Treaty of Versailles. However, French Premier Édouard Herriot seized on this as an admission that Germany is, in fact, capable of paying its reparations and would simply redirect freed-up funds toward rearmament. lausanne_pre.bodyHtml: = Brüning's Dilemma [? if hoover_memorandum_seen: Following the disastrous fallout from the Banking Crisis, Brüning has successfully managed to secure key concessions from the Western Allies regarding debts and Germany's economic maneuverability. However, Germany's economic crisis continues to worsen, and the Beneduce Report has stated that Germany cannot afford reparations payments in the foreseeable future. The British government has invited the Western Allies to participate in an international reparations congress in Lausanne, as per the recommendations of the bankers. ?][? if reparations == -2 and not hoover_memorandum_seen: With the moratorium on reparations in place, there is considerable uncertainty regarding what will happen to Germany's reparations burden once it expires. Brüning argues that this uncertainty has stifled investor confidence and hindered Germany's recovery from the economic crisis. The dire state of German finances has also contributed to this, with the Beneduce Report painting a bleak picture of Germany's ability to repay reparations in the foreseeable future. The British government has invited the Western Allies to participate in an international reparations congress in Lausanne, as per the recommendations of the bankers. ?] This is where the dilemma arises: France's government cannot discuss any permanent revision of the Young Plan until after their elections in May. Brüning faces a choice: he can either push for a prolongation of the moratorium on reparations for another three years, or he can wait until June for a potential complete abolition of reparations.

lausanne_pre.lausanne.subtitleHtml: A lot can happen between now and then.
lausanne_pre.lausanne.bodyHtml: Brüning’s decision to postpone the Lausanne conference until June faces sharp criticism from top economic advisors, who argue that the outright abolition of reparations would remain impossible even then. Instead, they urge him to pursue détente and secure access to new French loans—an idea Hindenburg has adamantly opposed, vowing to resign rather than sign such an agreement. Brüning, however, has reason to believe waiting is the right move. France is facing a severe fiscal shortfall and remains reluctant to cut off a crucial revenue stream. That is, if Brüning can hold on until June.

lautenbach_adopted.bodyHtml:
The pause in reparation payments, a budgetary surplus, and a struggling economy have created the conditions necessary to persuade both the Brüning cabinet and many economic experts that a stimulus plan is essential. The economy has hit rock bottom, deflation is in its damaging second phase, and the Lautenbach Plan is considered crucial for a rapid 'ignition' of the German economy, especially as reparations have already been paused. However, due to the German public's fear of inflation, announcing any dramatic expansion of the money supply has proven impossible. As a result, the Reichsbank is forced to scale back the plan to avoid any potential scandal that could threaten the Brüning government.
Labor Minister Adam Stegerwald and Finance Minister Hermann Dietrich have devised a plan to allocate a billion dollars for public works, along with efforts to reduce 'sticky' wages to restore investor confidence. The plan also includes the purchasing of foreign debts to increase liquidity, expanding credit, and reducing interest rates. The deficit generated by these measures is also somewhat offset by the need to pay less unemployment benefits. With these measures, money is beginning to flow once again into the German economy.
> Chancellor [+ chancellor +]'s response is, public works?

lautenbach_fail.bodyHtml: Expectedly, the Lautenbach Plan has failed due to strong opposition from those who adhere to fiscal orthodoxy, which holds that deflation, despite its pain, is healthy because it weeds out inefficient producers. This contrasts with the Keynesian belief that a destructive second phase occurs, where economic recovery becomes possible but fails because of a collapse in investor confidence. Reichsbank President Hans Luther, who personally sympathizes with increasing the money supply and expanding credit, has shelved the idea. The conference only reached two unanimous conclusions: the German people's fear of inflation made it impossible to announce any dramatic program to expand the money supply, meaning the government would have to act secretly if it ever decided to implement Lautenbach's plan, and the government must continue its campaign to lower wages bound by long-term collective labor contracts and prices set by cartel agreements. However, Luther has made concessions to the Keynesians, quietly expanding the money supply and increasing credit availability, even abandoning the rule that 40% of money in circulation must be covered by gold and foreign exchange. Furthermore, generous financing of exports to the Soviet Union has helped counteract the effects of the withdrawal of foreign credits on both the money supply and the job market. > *"Stimulation can only help if we are already at the bottom....I do not believe that we are that far yet."* - Ernst Trendelenburg, Reich Minister of Economics, 1931.

The bourgeois parties express concerns about inflation and spending, preferring a more cautious approach. However, they accept our plan, reassured by the surplus we’ve built up. Our spending on public works has reduced the need for unemployment insurance and welfare, while also increasing tax receipts through the multiplier effect as the new money circulates in the economy, helping to recover some of our spending. We continue to reinvest most of this new revenue into the program. [? if in_popular_front or in_left_front: The **KPD** opposes the economic plan, seeing it as a rescue of capitalism rather than a step towards real socialism. ?]

left_cartel_france.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the **PRRRS** have decided to enter government with the **SFIO**, despite their concerns over economic matters. Radical Édouard Herriot has been appointed as the new Prime Minister. This is excellent news for our relations with France, as he and our socialist comrades are much more open to renegotiating Germany's reparation payments compared to the previous government. There are even talks of a United States of Europe within their new left-wing cabinet.

left_coalition.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the left coalition is successfully formed, without appointing a communist as Minister-President. The consensus choice for Minister-President, accepted by the **SPD**, **KPD**, is[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work.. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, discrediting the left and eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. Our task is to prove them wrong. [? if in_left_front_prussia: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** in Prussia too. ?] The **KPD** has taken an abstentionist position with regards to ministries. They claim to be participating as the "loyal opposition" in the worker's government, supporting us from the outside while also running their own propaganda campaigns to turn workers to their side. They seem to expect that we would inevitably fail, and that our failure would benefit them. Whatever their reasoning is, the **SPD** has control over the ministries of government.

left_conflict.bodyHtml: Stresemann and the left-wing of the **DVP** pushed through the reform by an extremely narrow margin, only achieved by Stresemann's threats to resign if it were not to pass. Half of the party's Reichstag delegation is tied to industry, which are now without much influence within the **DVP**, and even the **DNVP** with Hugenberg's leadership. They are now in open conflict with the left-wing of the **DVP** and are withholding their financial contributions. We have noticed a small improvement in relations with the **DVP**, and them moving away from the radical right. The **[+ ddp_name +]** has also voiced approval to the actions of the congress and have opened up talks for further cooperation. This also has a ripple effect within the **[+ ddp_name +]**, shifting them leftwards.

left_front_prussia.bodyHtml: The coalition negotiations were going relatively smoothly until the **KPD** bought up the topic of a reorganization of the Prussian government to include themselves. Previous United Left governments at the state level have faced Reichsexekution before, [? if president_ideology == "Right" or president == "Hindenburg": and President [+ president +] will almost certainly do so again if we were to form one.?][? if president_ideology == "Moderate": but it's unlikely [+ president +] will do such an anti-democratic act.?][? if president_ideology == "Left": but it's unlikely [+ president +] will repeat Ebert's mistakes.?] Despite this, the **KPD** are firm about their demands to be included. *Something* must be done to restore balance, again.

choices.labelHtml: oh, so now the kpd wants to lecture the spd on ‘betrayal’? that’s hilarious. let’s not forget who really sold out the working class. while the spd was out here trying to protect the weimar republic from fascist takeovers, what was the kpd doing? attacking social democrats, calling them 'class traitors' because we didn’t want to throw democracy in the trash and start a pointless revolution. yeah, ebert made some bad calls with the freikorps, but at least we were trying to keep things from falling apart. what was the kpd doing? cozying up to stalin, pretending like the weimar republic was already dead and going nowhere. you really wanna talk about betrayal? the kpd was too busy playing the martyr, splitting the left vote and giving fascists a clear path to power. congratulations, geniuses. splitting the vote in 1933 while you chant about 'class purity'—real smart move. the spd might’ve had its flaws, but we actually tried to make things better, to hold off the fascists and give the workers a fighting chance. you? you just played into their hands. revolution doesn’t happen by sitting on your high horse, refusing to cooperate and throwing temper tantrums. if anything, the kpd handed us over to hitler on a silver platter. so keep whining about 'betrayal' while you do nothing but tear down the very thing that could’ve stopped the fascists. nice job.

The bourgeois parties are infuriated by our betrayal, and any future coalitions with them may be impossible. The Minister-President position is transferred from Braun to[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are going to rule with the **KPD** on both levels of government. The **KPD** has provided a list of objectives for us to complete in parallel to our federal policies.

left_win.bodyHtml: The United Front Government, under President [? if president == "Rosenfeld": Kurt Rosenfeld?][? if president == "Thälmann": Ernst Thälmann?][? if president == "Münzenberg": Willi Münzenberg?][? if president == "Ossietzky": Carl von Ossietzky?][? if president == "Mann": Heinrich Mann?], withstood everything thrown its way—capitalist treachery, institutional sabotage, and constant subversion by reactionaries. In 1937, after winning a second election and slightly increasing its majority, the government faced a coup attempt led by the reactionary elements of the Reichswehr and increasingly radicalized nationalists and far-right forces. The coup failed. The abortive putsch was crushed by the proletarian masses and shattered the political landscape of Weimar. The far left of the [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]—splinters from their parties who maintained ambiguity towards the coup—split off to form the **RDP** and **CSRP**, both of which soon joined the United Front. With the bourgeois center increasingly marginalized, the botched coup gave the United Front the momentum needed to finally purge the Republic of reactionary forces and initiate a socialist economy. Eventually a constitutional convention was called to begin a Socialist Republic.

left_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - Spartakus Rises Again The convention is called, and with overwhelming support, it dismantles the old bourgeois institutions. At last, after all these years, the German Soviet Republic is formed—and this time, "All Power to the Soviets" is more than just a slogan. The **SPD** takes the lead in constructing the Soviet Republic. Though the process is complex and at times byzantine, born of compromise among many factions, it is unmistakably revolutionary. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. In a world largely hostile to socialism, we stand as a shining example: the economy is socialized, and economic control is placed directly in the hands of the proletariat. The Soviet Union remains distant, as does the West. We emerge as a beacon of socialism amid the growing tensions of a Cold War—between the **Soviets**, an authoritarian Kuomintang-led China, and an independent India on one side, and the capitalist West on the other. We maintain a strictly neutral stance, offering principled opposition to both blocs. In doing so, we inspire many nations to follow our political and geopolitical path. Our shining socialist republic manages to survive, until the end of an inconclusive Cold War in détente. As a key neutral player throughout the Cold War, we reap the benefits—becoming a center for dialogue and commerce. With the arrival of détente, more and more nations join us in non-alignment. All is not golden though. Our republic is prone to infighting, as the various proletarian groups represented in the economy often clash over resource allocation. Additionally, our council-centered system faces criticism for its inability to adapt to modern conditions, with growing signs of bureaucratic inefficiency. Nevertheless, as we enter the 2000s, the Deutsche Räterepublik remains a bastion of socialism and orthodoxy. Our politics, culture, and economy are still deeply proletarian. Albeit third way and even capitalist parties remain on our right—and hardline vanguardists on our left—the **SPD** and its successor parties maintain a firm hold on the Republic.

left_win_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - The Vanguard Takes the Helm As the Constitutional Assembly convenes, it is gradually decided that the new socialist state will take inspiration from the Russian Revolution and the Soviet Union’s vanguardist model. The **SPD**—whether convinced, divided, or simply powerless to stop the shift—accepts it. The two **socialist** parties rapidly merge into a single party that monopolizes power in the new state, while allowing some minor parties to remain as bloc parties. The **Socialist Unity Party** (**SED**) takes the helm. The regime immediately begins aligning with the Soviet Union and puts forth its first *Gosplans*. Soon, the State becomes a member of the Eastern Bloc. World War II breaks out as a massive conflict between the capitalist and communist worlds. It ends with a vast Eastern Bloc stretching from Lisbon to Arkhangelsk. A Cold War begins against the United States, Britain, Kuomintang-led China, and the French government in exile. The **SED** assumes an important role in the Soviet Bloc as the leader of the second most industrialized country. Germany experiences decades of growth under the economic plans, calming most dissent within the country. To combat the remaining opposition, the Party establishes the Stasi, inspired by the Soviet Union’s NKVD. Alongside the Soviet Bloc, the Soviet Republic of Germany largely wins the Cold War. Key factors include the collapse of European Africa, the Chinese Civil War ending with an unaligned socialist China, and the United States and Britain shifting towards isolationism. However, by the 1990s, economic problems worsen: inflation rises, corruption grows, and the People’s Democracies begin to decay. Dissent grows to levels even the harshest Stasi measures fail to contain. Amid these conditions, General Secretary Gorbachev of the Soviet Union initiates a controlled transition toward genuine democratic socialism inspired by the Chinese model. Today, Germany holds its first elections under this new system. The political spectrum is dazzling and complex, though heavily weakened and under state supervision. The quasi-capitalist **CNVP** and **LSV** form a coalition against the socialists and are gaining momentum. New socialist parties emerge as the **SED** fractures between hardliners and reformers. Perhaps the next government will have a **SEPD** majority.

leipart.union_unity.bodyHtml: We have reduced tensions with the Labor faction, and increased its strength in the party.

lejeune_jung.bodyHtml: Lejeune-Jung has, as expected, won the election with Westarp’s blessing, securing a comfortable majority. He is anticipated to continue Westarp’s decision-making style while working to broaden the **DNVP**’s appeal among conservative Catholics of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": CVP?]. Their first high-profile defector is Franz von Papen, an agrarian noble from the far right of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": CVP?], who brings a cohort of allies with him.

lemmer.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, Ernst Lemmer has managed to rally a majority of the party to elect him as the chairman of the **[+ ddp_name +]**. He is primarily supported by the 'Social Republican Wing,' the Young Democrats, pacifists, radical democrats, and the labor wing of the party. However, his election would not have been possible without the backing of those who worked alongside him in the failed attempt to unite with the **VNR** months earlier. Now, a trade unionist leads a liberal middle-class party—what a time we live in. Lemmer's victory significantly empowers the Social Republicans and left-wing elements within the **[+ ddp_name +]**, even drawing his former colleague Anton Erkelenz back into politics. We can expect his **[+ ddp_name +]** to adopt a 'social capitalist' platform,[? if stolper_program_adopted: to replace the Stolper program,?] aiming to include workers in the *Volksgemeinschaft*.

The vote succeeds, and our government has resigned. Chancellor [+ chancellor +] remains as the head of a caretaker government, but no longer has the power to enact new policies.

The vote succeeds, and our government has resigned. Chancellor Brüning has been appointed as the head of a new cabinet, consisting solely of the bourgeois parties. He immediately proceeds to cut welfare spending substantially.
[? if not bruning_event_seen and year >= 1930: New elections haven't been called yet but it's likely that they will be soon, considering Brüning most likely doesn't have the majority of the Reichstag behind him. ?]

let_persecute.bodyHtml: The case progresses slowly, given the military secrets involved, and there will be no determination made for a while. The Reichswehr is pleased of our loyalty. However, the affair has made the Western powers suspicious of our resurgent militarism, as well as displeasing the left wing of the party.

lettow_vorbeck_victory.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, a nationalist not far different from Hindenburg, has been elected president. A return to government under his leadership—his Camarilla certainly won’t allow it. Let’s hope his personal disdain for the Nazis keeps them from ever entering government.

levi.bodyHtml: = Paul Levi Levi is a former leader of the **KPD** who left over their devotion to violence and revolutionary adventurism.

levi.building_the_left.subtitleHtml: Push the **SPD** to the left.
levi.building_the_left.bodyHtml: We have increased the strength of the left faction with the **SPD**. This raised concern among the moderate reformists in the party.

levi.kpd_cooperation.subtitleHtml: Any cooperation between the parties requires compromise from the **KPD** as well as the **SPD**.
levi.kpd_cooperation.bodyHtml: Levi attempts to reach out to his former colleagues to dissuade the **KPD** from their current extreme Stalinist path. Some concessions are extracted.

liberalize_fail.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, our proposal is voted down in the Reichstag, with the Catholic [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] party (our long-time partners) speaking in particularly vehement opposition, and some of our own members breaking party discipline. The activists, feeling demoralized from this attempt, have decided to bide their time.

liberalize_success.bodyHtml: With the support of a "progressive coalition" including the **KPD** and [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: leftist **LVP** members?], we have successfully passed a bill to legalize abortion in Germany! This has heartened our more progressive supporters, while hurting our relations with the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]. With the increasing political discourse around abortion, the religiously-oriented [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and **DNVP** have gained conservative votes at the expense of the **NSDAP**.

library.demographics.bodyHtml: **Demographic Groups** **Working Class**: The urban working class - blue-collar workers in factories, workshops, mines, and the like. Most are socialists, supporting either the **SPD** or **KPD**. They make up 40-50% of the population. **Old Mittelstand**: The old middle class consists of independent artisans, shopkeepers, and small-time businesspeople. They tend to be conservative and are the strongest base for the far-right. 10-15% of the population. **New Mittelstand**: The new middle class consists of white-collar workers and government employees. This is the base of liberalism. 10-15% of the population. **Rural**: Small and large farmers and independent rural workers. Protestant farmers usually supports the [? if not cvp_formed: **DNVP**?][? if cvp_formed: **[+ z_party_name +]**?]. [? if rural_nsdap_normalized >= 25: However the Nazis have gained a strong appeal among them?]. 20-30% of the population. **Catholics** are the largest religious minority, at about 30% of the population. [? if not cvp_formed: They disproportionately support the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]?][? if cvp_formed: They find themselves split between supporting the **CVP** and the **SPD**. ?] (or the **Bavarian People's Party** in Bavaria). **Jews** account for between 0.5% to 1% of the population, and tend to support liberal parties, [? if ddp_name == "DDP" or not ddp_name: mostly the DDP?][? if ddp_name == "DStP": although the mild antisemitism of the Young German Order and it's association with the **[+ ddp_name +]** has driven them away?], although substantial numbers support the **SPD** or **KPD**.

library.factions.bodyHtml: **Internal factions of the** **SPD** Overall dissent: [+ dissent_percent : dissent +] **Left** Many leftists are former members of the **USPD** (the left-wing, anti-war Independent Social Democratic Party), or are young radicals. Many are interested in closer cooperation with the **KPD**, and some support extra-parliamentary action. Strength: [+ left_strength : strength +] Dissent: [+ left_dissent : dissent +] **Centrists** Centrists in the **SPD** are followers of the doctrine of orthodox Marxism as expounded by Karl Kautsky and later Rudolf Hilferding. They seek a middle course between reform and revolution, while defending the democratic state. Strength: [+ center_strength : strength +] Dissent: [+ center_dissent : dissent +] **Labor** Many **SPD** members are also part of the ADGB, the federation of free trade unions. Their goal is economic reform and benefits for organized workers. Strength: [+ labor_strength : strength +] Dissent: [+ labor_dissent : dissent +] **Reformists** Reformists are pragmatic participants in government, and seek to expand the welfare state and defend democracy against the far-right and left. [? if spd_prussia : They are dominant in the state government of Prussia. ?] Strength: [+ reformist_strength : strength +] Dissent: [+ reformist_dissent : dissent +] [? if neorevisionism: **Neorevisionists** ?] [? if neorevisionism: Neorevisionists focus on defending the republic and expanding democracy, while also expanding the party's base beyond the working class to create a people's party. They support new propaganda methods and extra-parliamentary action in defense of the republic. ?] [? if neorevisionism: Strength: [+ neorevisionist_strength : strength +] ?] [? if neorevisionism: Dissent: [+ neorevisionist_dissent : dissent +] ?] [? if social_patriot: **Social Patriots** ?] [? if social_patriot: Social Patriots combine support for pro-worker social programs with fervent German nationalism and anti-communism. Many of those who identify with this tendency seem to be little more than lapdogs of Schleicher[? if dnef_formed : and his **DNEF**?]. library.government.bodyHtml: The German Republic, called by some of our detractors as the "Weimar Republic", is a parliamentary republic with a somewhat weak president and a strong parliament, called the Reichstag. The Reichstag is responsible for governing, while the President has a largely ceremonial role but also has some important governing responsibilities. The Reichstag is elected based on a proportional representation system, giving parties seats roughly proportional to their vote share in each electoral district. The Reichstag then elects the Chancellor and the cabinet by a majority vote, who are responsible for government. A majority vote-of-no-confidence can remove the current government. The President is elected by a national direct vote, in two rounds. The second round is used if the first round does not result in a majority for one candidate; the candidate who receives a plurality in the second round becomes president (there is no obligation for weaker candidates to drop out). The role of the president is mostly to represent Germany, but he also has some crucial governing powers. The president and chancellor can together use emergency decrees to govern, bypassing the Reichstag. The president can also appoint or remove a chancellor when a parliamentary majority is unable to be established, and can thus influence the formation of a government. Germany is divided into a number of states, each of which have their own governments with some responsibilities. By far the largest and most important state is Prussia.

library.weimar_timeline.bodyHtml: = Timeline of the SPD and the Republic (until 1928) **1875**: The SPD is formed as a merger of the General German Workers' Association, founded by Ferdinand Lassalle, and the Social Democratic Workers' Party of Germany, led by Wilhelm Liebknecht and August Bebel. Eventually, the SPD grows to become the largest party in the German Empire. **1914**: The Great War begins. The SPD votes in favor of war credits, with substantial internal dissent. This begins a policy of *Burgfriedenspolitik*, a general peace between all political parties and trade unions. **1917**: The USPD, a left-wing anti-war split from the SPD, is formed. **1918**: Following defeats in the war and uprisings by soldiers, sailors, and workers, SPD leader Philip Scheidemann proclaims the German Republic, and Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicates from his throne. An armistice is declared, ending the Great War. Conflict between center-left social democrats and far-left radicals erupts in the streets of Berlin and elsewhere. **1919**: The Spartacist Uprising, in which communist workers attempt to seize control of government, is launched. The uprising is defeated by the Social Democratic government, now led by President Friedrich Ebert and Chancellor Philipp Scheidemann, with the support of the far-right Freikorps militas. The two key leaders of the uprising, Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht, are murdered by the Freikorps. The Treaty of Versailles is signed under great protest from all political factions in Germany, officially ending the Great War. The Weimar Constitution is signed. The first "Weimar Coalition" government is formed, led by the SPD, DDP, and Center (Z) parties. **1920**: The Kapp Putsch, an attempt by reactionary actors within the military to take power, is launched, and is defeated by the workers with a general strike. This is followed by left-wing uprisings in the Ruhr, which are defeated by the Reichswehr and Freikorps. The Weimar Coalition is defeated in the elections, with the right and far left increasing in vote share. Elected governments in this period are very unstable, often only lasting a matter of months. There is a split in the USPD, with the majority faction joining with the KPD and the Soviet Union's Communist International (Comintern) alliance. **1921**: Communist uprisings in Saxony and Hamburg are defeated. Matthias Erzberger, the Center Party leader who signed the Versailles Treaty, is assassinated. **1922**: The Treaty of Rapallo is signed, which normalized relations with the Soviet Union. Walther Rathenau, the DDP Foreign Minister, is assassinated. The SPD reunites with most of the remaining USPD. **1923**: Hyperinflation begins, largely due to the economic policy of "passive resistance" against the French occupation of the Ruhr and the Versailles reparations. The currency is rapidly devalued as prices for necessities rise to billions of Reichsmarks. The government launches a Reichsexekution against Saxony, which was led by a joint SPD-KPD government. The Nazi "Beer Hall Putsch" is launched in Munich, and fails, with the arrest of Hitler. Eventually, new policies manage to stabilize the currency, and the French occupation ends. **1924**: Parliamentary elections are held in May and December, the latter leading to the bourgeois-right governments that last until 1928. Hitler is released from prison. The Dawes Plan for the repayment of the Versailles reparations is negotiated, which reduces payments and increases economic growth. Germany begins to enter a period of relative stability, with the end of the hyperinflation crisis. **1925**: President Friedrich Ebert dies, and new presidential elections are held, leading to the narrow election of Paul von Hindenburg in the second round. Hindenburg is a war hero and a right-wing reactionary. The SPD adopts the Heidelberg Program as its party platform. The Locarno Treaties are signed, which confirmed Germany's post-war western borders. **1926**: A referendum on the expropriation of the princes, supported by the SPD and KPD, fails.

local_election_1932.spd_majority.titleHtml: The **SPD** forms a majority government.
local_election_1932.spd_majority.bodyHtml: We have somehow managed to capture a majority in the Landtag, and have put our Minister-President as the head of the most conservative state in the country. Hopefully this doesn't end badly like last time. Bavaria has been governed by the political right ever since 1921, and the **BVP** has often covered for reactionary political activity. Now, we are able to change that and aggressively counter the **SA** thugs roaming the streets [? if sa_nationwide_ban: and more aggressively enforce the national ban of the organization that the conservative Held government had mostly ignored ?].

local_election_1932.spd_majority_wurttem.titleHtml: The **SPD** forms a majority government.
local_election_1932.spd_majority_wurttem.bodyHtml: Somehow, we have captured the majority of seats, bypassing the coalition negotiation process and appointing an **SPD** Minister-President for the first time in a decade. Kurt Schumacher is elected as Minister-President.

params.source: election_menu

local_election_1932.united_left.titleHtml: The **SPD** will form a coalition government with the **KPD**?
local_election_1932.united_left.bodyHtml: The conservative stronghold of the republic, home to the largest concentration of Catholics and general forces of reaction has finally fallen to the forces of the Left. Few could have expected the seeds of socialism, much less communism to once again take root in Bavaria, but the election results showed have made this impossibility into a living nightmare for the right. **Stahlhelm** brigands, along with the Nazi **SA** are already rushing to prepare a coup against what they see as a communist takeover in progress, and we may soon have a civil war on our hands. The legacy of the Bavarian Worker’s Republic has been avenged, but at what cost?

local_election_1932.united_left_wurttemb.titleHtml: The **SPD** will form a coalition government with the **KPD**?
local_election_1932.united_left_wurttemb.bodyHtml: Even as the forces of the bourgeoisie have remained numerous in the Landtag, the newly unified Left has triumphed over the reigning coalition and inserted ourselves into a new Red Württemburg. Of course, the rabidly anti-socialist nature of the previous government does not make this transition easy, with mass purges of the police force to ensure that we can retain our influence with communist assistance. We can expect that **Stahlhelm** units, met with such a loss in the elections, will soon bring their fury to the stairs of the Reichstag.

local_election_1932.weimar_coalition_wur.titleHtml: A Weimar Coalition is formed!
local_election_1932.weimar_coalition_wur.subtitleHtml: We have somehow convinced the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] to let us into government.
local_election_1932.weimar_coalition_wur.bodyHtml: Despite the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] in Württemberg being historically hostile, we've managed to convince them to form a majority Weimar Coalition. We will now focus on eliminating the nationalist and anti-democratic biases in the police force. Eugen Bolz retains the Minister-President position, as part of our agreement.

params.source: election_menu
wurttemberg_coalition_menu

local_election_1932.wurttemberg_coalitio.bodyHtml: The Center Party in Württemberg has historically been unfriendly toward us, opting to continue governing in a minority coalition with the **DNVP** as they view us as incapable of governing, even when a Weimar Coalition was possible in 1928. Under the stable leadership of Eugen Bolz and Wilhelm Bazille, Württemberg has surprisingly managed to mitigate the worst effects of the economic depression. However, its police force is notorious for its anti-socialist bias, targeting us more aggressively than the more violent Nazis.

local_election_1932.z_toleration_wurttem.titleHtml: The incumbent [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] government has fallen short of a majority, but continue to rule in caretaker capacity.
local_election_1932.z_toleration_wurttem.subtitleHtml: Electing a new Minister-President—or dissolving the Landtag—requires an absolute majority. Deep antagonism between the opposition parties has made clearing that hurdle all but impossible.
local_election_1932.z_toleration_wurttem.bodyHtml: Despite the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and its Protestant conservative partners falling short of a majority, they continue to rule as a caretaker government. This outcome mirrors the one of the 1928 elections, so perhaps this outcome is to be expected.

params.source: election_menu

local_election_france.bodyHtml:
= Elections, [+ month : month +] [+ year +]
The French Third Republic are to hold their legislative elections now.

choices.labelHtml: May our socialist comrades do their best...

local_election_france.center_right_franc.titleHtml: The **PRS** and **PRRRS** enter government with the right-liberal **AD**.
local_election_france.center_right_franc.subtitleHtml: The economically right-wing **PRRRS** and **RI** are opposed to the **SFIO**'s socialistic policies.
local_election_france.center_right_franc.bodyHtml: While not the best outcome, the return of the Radical Édouard Herriot to the Prime Minister position is excellent news for our relations with France, as he is much more open to renegotiating Germany's reparation payments compared to the previous government.

params.source: france_coalition_menu

local_election_france.france_coalition_m.bodyHtml: France is known for its historically unstable governments, with most cabinets lasting a few months at best. The last four years have been governed by various groupings of parties to the right of the **SFIO**, our socialist comrades. Perhaps it's their turn to rule now, with the return of the Left-Cartel alliance. However, concerns over their radical economic policies may push the **PRS** and **PRRRS** to form a coalition with the **AD** instead.

local_election_france.left_cartel_france.subtitleHtml: The strong electoral results of the **SFIO** and **PRS** have pressured the **PRRRS** to enter government with their electoral allies.
local_election_france.left_cartel_france.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the **PRRRS** have decided to enter government with the **SFIO**, despite their concerns over economic matters. Radical Édouard Herriot has been appointed as the new Prime Minister. This is excellent news for our relations with France, as he and our socialist comrades are much more open to renegotiating Germany's reparation payments compared to the previous government. There are even talks of a United States of Europe within their new left-wing cabinet.

local_election_france.pop_front_france.titleHtml: The **SFIO** abandons the **PRRRS** and forms a government with the **PCF**!

local_election_france.right_wing_france.titleHtml: A Right-wing Coalition is somehow formed, without needing the **PRRRS**.

local_election_lippe.bodyHtml:
= Elections, [+ month : month +] [+ year +]
The state elections for the Free State of Lippe are to take place.

local_election_lippe_campaign.subtitleHtml: A minuscule Free State prepares for its election next week.
local_election_lippe_campaign.bodyHtml: = Lippe Landtag Campaigning Being the only state election between Schleicher's appointment and Strasser’s resignation, which, alongside several local elections, has painted a picture of the Nazi Party's rapid decline, the Nazis are eager to pour all their resources into a victory in this microstate. The intensity of their campaign is unprecedented, with [+ nsdap_chancellor +] and dozens of nationally prominent Nazi leaders holding rallies as many as a dozen times per day. A defeat here would cement the growing belief that the party is collapsing—and deny them a much-needed propaganda victory to revitalize their flagging morale. The local **SPD** remains strong, having secured 39% of the vote in the last election and winning a majority of the urban vote. Meanwhile, the various bourgeois parties that once dominated the rural areas have become irrelevant and are likely to crumble under the weight of the **NSDAP** campaign. The odds favor the Nazis: the near-total absence of Catholics, a 60% rural population, and the fact that this state constitutes just a quarter of a percent of Germany’s population—all make it possible for them to blanket the area with propaganda and demonstrations at minimal cost. This is a high-stakes campaign: if the Nazis fail to make a strong showing despite their all-out effort, the consequences will be enormously magnified. Given the state’s tiny size, the real question isn’t whether we can afford to campaign—but how much we’re willing to invest in it.

params.source: campaign_menu

local_election_lippe_campaign.campaign_h.titleHtml: Launch an extensive ground and propaganda campaign, reaching all corners of the state.
local_election_lippe_campaign.campaign_h.bodyHtml: Despite Lippe's small size, our campaign needs to rival the Nazis. Speakers are brought in from all over the country to preach to the workers about the dangers of Nazism, and highlight the **SPD**'s accomplishments on behalf of the working class. We made efforts to campaign among the traditionally conservative rural areas of the state, [? if not peoples_party: however, we have not historically campaigned much among the farmers, and they do not trust us over the Nazis. ?][? if peoples_party: with varying degrees of success. ?][? if democracy_paramilitary: Despite the **SA**'s attempts at disruption, Reichsbanner units brought in from other parts of the country maintain order. ?][? if not democracy_paramilitary: However, the **SA** has repeatedly disrupted our gatherings, and attacked many of our officials. ?] Although our campaigning efforts may finally have caught up to the one of the Nazis, they've received a welcome surprise by Hugenberg announcing a political truce with the **NSDAP**, a step toward reconciliation. As a result, their campaign is free from bourgeois counter-campaigns in the rural 60% of the state.

local_election_lippe_campaign.campaign_l.titleHtml: Leave campaigning to the local **SPD**.
local_election_lippe_campaign.campaign_l.bodyHtml: We don't need to worry about Lippe. Local campaigning efforts are left to the historically popular local **SPD** and Minister-President, who seek to maintain the loyalty of the state's working-class. Our campaign pales in comparison to the Nazi one by miles, who have received a welcome surprise by Hugenberg announcing a political truce with the **NSDAP**, a step toward reconciliation. Therefore, their campaign has free rein over the rural 60% of the state.

local_election_lippe_campaign.campaign_m.titleHtml: Launch a campaign among the urban sections of Lippe, focusing on the working-class.
local_election_lippe_campaign.campaign_m.bodyHtml: Despite Lippe's small size, we must step up our ground game. Speakers are brought in from all over the country to preach to the workers about the dangers of Nazism, and highlight the **SPD**'s accomplishments on behalf of the working class. [? if democracy_paramilitary: Despite the **SA**'s attempts at disruption, Reichsbanner units brought in from other parts of the country maintain order. ?][? if not democracy_paramilitary: However, the **SA** has repeatedly disrupted our gatherings, and attacked many of our officials. ?] Our campaign still pales in comparison to the Nazis, who were given a significant boost when Hugenberg announced a political truce with the **NSDAP**, marking a step toward reconciliation. As a result, their campaign now has free rein over the rural 60% of the state.

local_election_lippe_campaign.schleicher.titleHtml: Chancellor Schleicher offers to lend supporting parties state funding.
local_election_lippe_campaign.schleicher.bodyHtml: Schleicher, in recognition of the **SPD**'s relative support for his cabinet, has granted us access to secret state funding for the campaign. This move is also likely to improve the party's perception of the chancellor.

params.source: campaign_menu

local_election_lippe.hitler_bad.titleHtml: How will this affect [+ nsdap_leader +] and his party?
local_election_lippe.hitler_bad.bodyHtml: In a meeting between [+ nsdap_leader +] and the Nazi gauleiters immediately after the Lippe results became known, it was clear—they were not pleased. The consensus among the leadership was that [+ nsdap_leader +]’s all-or-nothing strategy is failing. They cannot simply wait for Hindenburg to have a sudden change of heart, nor can they rely on a victory at the ballot box. In an attempt to crush dissent, [+ nsdap_leader +] unleashed the full force of his anger on Strasser—denouncing the man who once helped elevate him as a traitor and accusing him of long-standing subversion. He warned that anyone questioning his strategy was aligning themselves with the disgraced Strasser. But many in the room still sympathized with Strasser’s arguments, and the tirade only deepened their disillusionment with the man they had once seen as a prophet. The denunciation—and the evident unrest among the Nazi leadership—quickly leaked to the press. Word soon reached Chancellor von Schleicher, who was elated at their collapse and hopeful that it might finally compel [+ nsdap_leader +] to act more rationally.

local_election_lippe.hitler_eh.titleHtml: How will this affect [+ nsdap_leader +] and his party?
local_election_lippe.hitler_eh.bodyHtml: In a meeting between [+ nsdap_leader +] and the Nazi gauleiters, immediately after the Lippe results were known, things could have turned disastrous if the results had been worse, with unrest already rising among the grassroots. While the Nazi gains somewhat mitigated the unrest, the gauleiters still voiced concerns about [+ nsdap_leader +]'s strategy. Leaks of discontent continue to reach the press. In an attempt to suppress dissent, he unleashed the full force of his anger against Strasser, condemning the person responsible for his rise to power as a traitor and accusing him of numerous offenses stretching back many years. [+ nsdap_leader +] implied that anyone expressing doubts about his all-or-nothing strategy was an accomplice of the disgraced Strasser. This appears to have silenced dissent among the gauleiters. His denunciation of his former ally has been kept out of the press, deliberately by [+ nsdap_leader +] to shield the party from political fallout due to rumors of a split within its ranks. However, the bad news eventually reaches Chancellor von Schleicher, as the only person willing to cooperate with him in the party is, in fact, 'finished.'

local_election_lippe.hitler_explode.titleHtml: How will this affect [+ nsdap_leader +] and his party?
local_election_lippe.hitler_explode.bodyHtml: In a meeting between [+ nsdap_leader +] and the Nazi gauleiters immediately after the Lippe results became known, it was clear—they were outraged. The consensus among the leadership was that [+ nsdap_leader +]’s all-or-nothing strategy was failing, and the party was collapsing fast. They could no longer wait for Hindenburg to have a sudden change of heart, nor could they rely on a victory at the ballot box. In a fit of rage, [+ nsdap_leader +] launched into a long and incoherent tirade against Strasser—denouncing the man who once helped elevate him as a traitor and accusing him of long-standing subversion. Many in the room still sympathized with Strasser’s arguments, and the outburst only deepened their disillusionment with the man they had once regarded as a prophet. After [+ nsdap_leader +] seemingly lost control, a growing minority within the party now openly call for a reconciliation with Strasser and the **NSDAP** entering the Schleicher cabinet. The unrest within the party has quickly leaked to the press, with numerous local **NSDAP** and **SA** leaders now at each other’s throats, accelerating the party's collapse.

local_election_lippe.hitler_good.titleHtml: How will this affect [+ nsdap_leader +] and his party?
local_election_lippe.hitler_good.bodyHtml: In a meeting between [+ nsdap_leader +] and the Nazi gauleiters, immediately after the Lippe results were known, things could have turned disastrous if the results had been worse, with unrest already rising among the grassroots. However, the Nazi gains have alleviated their concerns about his all-or-nothing strategy, and [+ nsdap_leader +] used the opportunity to finally address the Strasser issue. He unleashed the full force of his anger against Strasser, condemning the person responsible for his rise to power as a traitor and accusing him of numerous offenses stretching back many years. [+ nsdap_leader +] implied that anyone expressing doubts about his all-or-nothing strategy was an accomplice of the disgraced Strasser. This appears to have silenced dissent among the gauleiters. His denunciation of his former ally has been kept out of the press, deliberately by [+ nsdap_leader +] to shield the party from political fallout due to rumors of a split within its ranks. However, the bad news eventually reaches Chancellor von Schleicher, as the only person willing to cooperate with him in the party is, in fact, 'finished.'

params.source: lippe_coalition_menu

local_election_lippe.nothing_ever_happen.titleHtml: The **NSDAP** fails to make a breakthrough.
local_election_lippe.nothing_ever_happen.bodyHtml: The **NSDAP**, despite going all-out on this campaign, only managed to achieve gains of [+ change_nsdap_votes_lippe +]%. This serves as evidence that the movement is in decline, though slowly. Nevertheless, the **NSDAP** continues to use their modest gains as cheap propaganda, though few are swayed. Replicating the success of their Lippe campaign—conducted in a state that comprises barely a quarter of a percent of Germany’s population—across the entire country is not feasible, particularly given their financial troubles. The victory feels artificial.

local_election_lippe.nsdap_big_win.titleHtml: The **NSDAP** score a crushing victory.
local_election_lippe.nsdap_big_win.bodyHtml: Unexpectedly, the **NSDAP** matched their peak electoral performance—proof that the movement isn’t dying, but growing. This is a major propaganda win for the **NSDAP**, sure to energize the party and reinforce the belief that [+ nsdap_leader +]’s all-or-nothing strategy is paying off. It’s only a matter of time before Hindenburg acknowledges the Nazi surge.

local_election_lippe.nsdap_explode.bodyHtml: The **NSDAP** is in free fall! Despite throwing everything they had into this campaign, their vote share has actually declined—a humiliating blow that confirms the movement’s rapid implosion. Donors are abandoning them, defections are accelerating, and local organizations are collapsing. Even fanatics at the highest levels of the party are starting to lose faith. The threat they once posed is rapidly fading, and with the pressure on Schleicher easing, the worst may finally be over.

local_election_lippe.nsdap_joever.titleHtml: The **NSDAP**'s suffers a crushing defeat!
local_election_lippe.nsdap_joever.bodyHtml: The **NSDAP** has suffered a crushing defeat! Despite throwing everything into this campaign, their vote share has actually declined. This is clear evidence that the movement is collapsing rapidly—and that new elections would be disastrous for the Nazi cause. Donations are drying up, party membership is plummeting, defections are soaring, and the political pressure on Schleicher has eased. Land is in sight.

local_election_lippe.nsdap_moderate_win.titleHtml: The **NSDAP** score a dubious triumph.
local_election_lippe.nsdap_moderate_win.bodyHtml: The Nazis fell short of their peak results—but still gained votes compared to the last election. To the casual observer, the **NSDAP** looks like it’s back on the rise, and they’ve seized on the outcome as a cheap propaganda boost to reenergize their disillusioned base. But if we were to look closer. The **NSDAP** cannot replicate the scale of its Lippe campaign—conducted in a state with barely a quarter of a percent of Germany’s population—across the country, especially given its financial troubles. The victory feels artificial. Still, pressure to bring [+ nsdap_chancellor +] into government is once again rising.

local_election_saxony_1930.far_right_coa.titleHtml: We will enter a toleration agreement with the incumbent government.
local_election_saxony_1930.far_right_coa.bodyHtml: After a failed negotiation previously, the bourgeois parties are now willing to offer a ministerial position to the **NSDAP** in exchange for their support. Gregor Strasser, leader of the **NSDAP**'s left wing, has been appointed as the new Interior Minister, a role he had been denied in the past due to his more radical anti-capitalist views. Saxony, once a stronghold of socialism and democracy, is now being dismantled by the Nazis. The "democratic" aspect more so, as Strasser has pushed for the cabinet to adopt pro-worker and anti-capitalist policies in an attempt to win their votes. The state police, now largely comprised of Nazis, are actively suppressing socialist and communist organizations and meetings. Socialist newspapers critical of the government have been banned, and civil servants with suspected socialist or democratic leanings are being purged in large numbers. However, there is a real possibility that Strasser could be removed from his position by his coalition partners, as they were never a huge fan of him.

local_election_saxony_1930.grand_coaliti.titleHtml: A [? if lvp_formed and stegerwald_path: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed or not stegerwald_path: Grand?] Coalition is formed!
local_election_saxony_1930.grand_coaliti.subtitleHtml: We have somehow reconciled with the bourgeois parties, that they're willing to govern with us again.
local_election_saxony_1930.grand_coaliti.bodyHtml: Somehow, the bourgeois parties are willing to form a [? if lvp_formed and stegerwald_path: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed or not stegerwald_path: Grand?] Coalition with us, rather than continuing their current government with Max Heldt and the right-wing parties. With the **ASPD** (whose Saxon chapter is notably more sane) now convinced of our reformist path, they have rejoined the Saxon **SPD**! This development has weakened the **NSDAP**, who are now relegated to the powerless opposition.

local_election_saxony_1930.no_majority.subtitleHtml: [? if true_bourgeois_coalition_saxony < 50 and spd_coalition_saxony < 50: All possible coalitions lack a majority. ?][? if spd_coalition_saxony >= 50 and not spd_coalition_possible_saxony: The bourgeois parties are antagonistic to our Saxon organization. ?][? if spd_coalition_saxony >= 50 and left_strength >= 20: Our party itself rejects the possibility of a majority coalition with the liberals. ?]
local_election_saxony_1930.no_majority.bodyHtml: With the bourgeois parties unable to secure a majority, and the **NSDAP** refusing to enter government, the Landtag is in a deadlock. The Schieck Cabinet remains in power as a caretaker government, but a simple majority vote can still dissolve the Landtag, making toleration a necessity. [? if mega_bourgeois_coalition_saxony >= 50: The coalition of parties in between the **KPD** and the anti-democratic Right constitute a majority, but it is our decision whether or not to tolerate the incumbent government, to prevent new elections from being called. ?][? if mega_bourgeois_coalition_saxony < 50: The coalition of parties in between the **KPD** and the anti-democratic Right don't even constitute a majority, making any majority government impossible. ?]

local_election_saxony_1930.saxony_coalit.bodyHtml: The rapid rise of the **NSDAP** is alarming, as the economic depression continues to radicalize voters toward the right. Their support largely comes from the bourgeois right, whose vote is splintered across various bourgeois and special interest parties. Lacking a strong, unified right-of-center alternative, many have turned to the **NSDAP** as a protest vote. Meanwhile, the **ASPD** is essentially dead, having secured a negligible [+ aspd_saxony_elections_vote +]% of the vote. While discussions of a merger with the Saxon **SPD** have emerged, but our party's leftist tilt has so far stalled any meaningful progress. With Schieck elected as Minister-President, he remains in power as a caretaker government, staying in office unless an alternative majority emerges. However, a majority vote can still dissolve the Landtag, making toleration a crucial factor in maintaining stability.

local_election_saxony_1930.spd_majority.bodyHtml: Unexpectedly, we've found ourselves controlling a majority of the Saxony landtag and being able to form a goverment of just the **SPD**! It is unclear how the bourgeois and reactionaries will react to a Red Saxony but without the communists... [? if aspd_share > 0: The ASPD seeing as we no longer require on coalition negoations to form goverment has decided to join us. ?]

local_election_saxony_1930.toleration_sa.titleHtml: We will enter a toleration agreement with the incumbent government.
local_election_saxony_1930.toleration_sa.bodyHtml: Together with the bourgeois parties, we've successfully blocked the **NSDAP**'s vote for new elections. This marks one of the first uses of toleration to prevent the Nazis from gaining more influence. The Schieck Cabinet will remain unchanged, composed only of the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP** and **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?].

local_election_saxony_1930.true_bourgeoi.titleHtml: The Schieck government has garnered a majority to rule via parliament.
local_election_saxony_1930.true_bourgeoi.subtitleHtml: The bourgeois parties have survived the onslaught from the Nazis, at least for now.
local_election_saxony_1930.true_bourgeoi.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the bourgeois parties have held their ground, The **NSDAP** is heavily demoralized by this defeat, as they are relegated to the powerless opposition role. They had expected the national political climate to benefit them, and to allow them to influence government.

local_election_saxony_1930.united_left_s.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, despite reluctance on both sides due to fears that the reactionary Hindenburg will order a Reichsexekution if a coalition were to form, Red Saxony is restored! As one of the most left-wing and industrial states in Germany, we will use our leverage to implement comprehensive reforms and transform Saxony into a stronghold of socialism. Hindenburg’s patience is especially thin. Tread carefully.

local_election_saxony_1933.far_right_coa.titleHtml: The NSDAP enters the governing coalition.
local_election_saxony_1933.far_right_coa.subtitleHtml: Unfortunately, there is no other viable option.
local_election_saxony_1933.far_right_coa.bodyHtml: After a failed negotiation previously, the bourgeois parties are now willing to offer a ministerial position to the **NSDAP** in exchange for their support. Gregor Strasser, leader of the **NSDAP**'s left wing, has been appointed as the new Interior Minister, a role he had been denied in the past due to his more radical anti-capitalist views. Saxony, once a stronghold of socialism and democracy, is now being dismantled by the Nazis. The "democratic" aspect more so, as Strasser has pushed for the cabinet to adopt pro-worker and anti-capitalist policies in an attempt to win their votes. The state police, now largely comprised of Nazis, are actively suppressing socialist and communist organizations and meetings. Socialist newspapers critical of the government have been banned, and civil servants with suspected socialist or democratic leanings are being purged in large numbers. However, there is a real possibility that Strasser could be removed from his position by his coalition partners, as they were never a huge fan of him.

local_election_saxony_1933.no.subtitleHtml: We are not willing to risk a civil war at this time.

local_election_saxony_1933.no_majority.bodyHtml: With the bourgeois parties unable to secure a majority, and the **NSDAP** refusing to enter government, the Landtag is in a deadlock. The Schieck Cabinet remains in power as a caretaker government, but a simple majority vote can still dissolve the Landtag, making toleration a necessity. [? if mega_bourgeois_coalition_saxony >= 50: The coalition of parties in between the **KPD** and the anti-democratic Right constitute a majority, but it is our decision whether or not to tolerate the incumbent government, to prevent new elections from being called. ?][? if mega_bourgeois_coalition_saxony < 50: The coalition of parties in between the **KPD** and the anti-democratic Right don't even constitute a majority, making any majority government impossible. ?]

local_election_saxony_1933.pres_kpd.bodyHtml: There is absolutely no way that President [+ president +] is going to let this stand, and he has ordered a Reichsexekution against the Saxon government. Expectedly, the Nazis refuse to stand down.

local_election_saxony_1933.pres_spd.bodyHtml: President [+ president +] now faces a dilemma. As terrible as they are, the Nazis did win a majority, so do they not have a mandate to govern? Moreover, they will almost certainly resist any attempted Reichsexekution, triggering a civil war.

local_election_saxony_1933.pres_victory.bodyHtml: Strasser has backed down!  Unfortunately, as there was no other viable path to a coalition in the Landtag, it will need to be dissolved for new elections once more.

local_election_saxony_1933.president_oop.bodyHtml: Thanks to our own constitutional amendment, the president no longer has the power to call Reichsexekutions, and we are thus powerless to prevent this development.

local_election_saxony_1933.reichsex_dile.bodyHtml: President [+ president +] is considering the use of a Reichsexekution to stop the Nazi terror in Saxony. This might risk a civil war, however. Even if it succeeds, we'll likely just end up in an election loop again.

local_election_saxony_1933.sapd_aspd_ddp.titleHtml: Perhaps our splinter parties and the **[+ ddp_name +]** could be persuaded, in the name of stability?
local_election_saxony_1933.sapd_aspd_ddp.bodyHtml: We have cobbled together a majority coalition with other constitutional left-of-center parties.  Hopefully it lasts.

local_election_saxony_1933.saxony_coalit.bodyHtml:
# Reminder of possible coalition outcomes from 1929/1930 Saxon elections:
# Heldt toleration, Schieck toleration, Heldt groko, 1930 Groko, Successful United Left, United Left Reichsexekution, SPD majority, Schieck majority, Nazis enter
# Relevant variables: saxony_toleration, saxony_groko, red_saxony, saxony_joever, saxony_spd, saxony_right_2, saxony_nsdap
# Coalitions are still a work in progress for sure.  Initial ones down here are just the 1930 text repeated, plus a little more.

local_election_saxony_1933.soclib_saxony.titleHtml: We will form a coalition with only the liberals[? if reformists_resign or not aspd_dead: and the **ASPD**?].
local_election_saxony_1933.soclib_saxony.subtitleHtml: With the **CVP** having lurched to the right, this may be a viable option.
local_election_saxony_1933.soclib_saxony.bodyHtml: Somehow, the liberals are willing to form a coalition with us, without the increasingly reactionary **CVP** on board.
