local_election_saxony_1933.spd_majority.bodyHtml: Unexpectedly, we've found ourselves controlling a majority of the Saxony landtag and being able to form a goverment of just the **SPD**! It is unclear how the bourgeois and reactionaries will react to a Red Saxony but without the communists... [? if aspd_share > 0: The ASPD seeing as we no longer require on coalition negoations to form goverment has decided to join us. ?]

local_election_saxony_1933.toleration_sa.titleHtml: We will enter a toleration agreement with the bourgeois parties.
local_election_saxony_1933.toleration_sa.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, we have been relegated to toleration of the bourgeois parties. The Schieck Cabinet is re-established, composed only of the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP** and **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?][? if stegerwald_path: and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]?].

local_election_saxony_1933.true_bourgeoi.titleHtml: The bourgeois parties have garnered a majority to rule via parliament.
local_election_saxony_1933.true_bourgeoi.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the bourgeois parties have secured a majority all on their own. The **NSDAP** is heavily demoralized by this defeat, as they are relegated to the powerless opposition role. They had expected the national political climate to benefit them, and to allow them to influence government.

local_election_saxony.bourgeois_coalitio.subtitleHtml: The incumbent coalition, which will survive on toleration from the **NSDAP**.
local_election_saxony.bourgeois_coalitio.bodyHtml: The incumbent coalition has failed to win a majority, and toleration from the **NSDAP** is required. They've demanded the exclusion of the **ASPD**[? if not lvp_formed: and **[+ ddp_name +]**?] from the cabinet, and the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]'s new Minister-President Wilhelm Bünger has no choice but to agree. However, this decision was soon reverted and the **ASPD** is granted the Ministry of Work and Welfare. Despite the exclusion of many supporting parties from the cabinet in favor of non-partisan figures, they choose to tolerate the coalition nonetheless.

local_election_saxony.grand_coalition_sa.titleHtml: A [? if lvp_formed and stegerwald_path: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed or not stegerwald_path: Grand?] Coalition is formed!
local_election_saxony.grand_coalition_sa.subtitleHtml: We have somehow reconciled with the bourgeois parties, that they're willing to govern with us again.
local_election_saxony.grand_coalition_sa.bodyHtml: Somehow, the bourgeois parties are willing to form a [? if lvp_formed and stegerwald_path: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed or not stegerwald_path: Grand?] Coalition with us, rather than continuing their current government with Max Heldt and the right-wing parties. With the **ASPD** (whose Saxon chapter is notably more sane) now convinced of our reformist path, they have rejoined the Saxon **SPD**!

local_election_saxony.no_majority.subtitleHtml: [? if bourgeois_coalition_saxony < 50 and spd_coalition_saxony < 50: All possible coalitions lack a majority. ?][? if spd_coalition_saxony >= 50 and not spd_coalition_possible_saxony: The bourgeois parties are antagonistic to our Saxon organization. ?][? if spd_coalition_saxony >= 50 and left_strength >= 15: Our party itself rejects the possibility of a majority coalition with the liberals. ?]
local_election_saxony.no_majority.bodyHtml: With the bourgeois parties unable to secure a majority even with the toleration of the **NSDAP**, and their refusal to form a coalition with us, no viable majority can be established. The ruling coalition fears that calling new elections will only accelerate their decline and further erode their support. In an effort to avoid this, they are more open to negotiating a toleration agreement.

local_election_saxony.saxony_coalition_m.bodyHtml: The bourgeois parties have historically been hostile to us in state politics, particularly after the notorious **SPD**-**KPD** United Left government faced a Reichsexekution six years ago. The split of our reformist wing into the **ASPD** further pushed our state organization toward the left. [? if aspd_saxony_elections_vote <= 3: With the **ASPD**'s disastrous result of [+ aspd_saxony_elections_vote +]%, their viability as a political force in the state is coming to an end, with bourgeois parties are seeking a replacement for Max Heldt. ?][? if aspd_saxony_elections_vote > 3: The **ASPD** has not suffered the decline we thought it would, winning [+ aspd_saxony_elections_vote +]% of the vote. Whether Max Heldt remains is up to the bourgeois parties. ?] Despite our cooperation on the local level, the national **KPD** is unlikely to ever accept a coalition.

local_election_saxony.spd_majority.bodyHtml: Unexpectedly, we've found ourselves controlling a majority of the Saxony landtag and being able to form a government of just the **SPD**! It is unclear how the bourgeois and reactionaries will react to a Red Saxony but without the **Communists**... [? if aspd_share > 0: The **ASPD** seeing as we no longer require on coalition negotiations to form government has decided to join us. ?]

local_election_saxony.toleration_saxony.titleHtml: We will enter a toleration agreement with the incumbent government.
local_election_saxony.toleration_saxony.bodyHtml: We have entered a toleration agreement with the bourgeois cabinet, and have made it unnecessary for them to cooperate with the **NSDAP**. As part of our agreement, the bourgeois parties have allowed Max Heldt to retain his Minister-President position, and for the **ASPD** to occupy the Work and Welfare ministry. Despite the unsavory qualities of the **ASPD**, they're still Marxist at the end of the day. The leftist Saxon organization has protested at our intervention, and many have jumped ship to the **KPD**.

local_election_saxony.true_bourgeois_coa.titleHtml: The incumbent Heldt III cabinet will continue.
local_election_saxony.true_bourgeois_coa.subtitleHtml: They are able to retain their majority. Surprising.
local_election_saxony.true_bourgeois_coa.bodyHtml: The surprisingly good results for the incumbent coalition[? if aspd_saxony_elections_vote >= 4: and **ASPD**?] have allowed them and Heldt to continue governing. The **NSDAP** is discouraged by this defeat, as they had hoped to use their gains to influence the government.

As one of the most left-wing and industrial states in Germany, we will use our leverage to implement comprehensive reforms and transform Saxony into a stronghold of socialism. Hindenburg’s patience is especially thin. Tread carefully.

local_election_thuringia.bourgeois_coali.titleHtml: The incumbent center-right coalition continues governing.
local_election_thuringia.bourgeois_coali.subtitleHtml: The incumbent coalition holds a majority, one without the **NSDAP**.
local_election_thuringia.bourgeois_coali.bodyHtml: Unexpectedly, the parties involved in the incumbent government have gained votes, and now no longer require the votes of the **NSDAP**. The continuation of the stable leadership over Thuringia will weaken the Nazis.

local_election_thuringia.far_right_coali.titleHtml: The incumbent coalition is expanded to include the **NSDAP**.
local_election_thuringia.far_right_coali.subtitleHtml: A testament to how biased the "democratic" parties are when it comes to working with us.
local_election_thuringia.far_right_coali.bodyHtml: Wilhelm Frick, a convicted Beer Hall Putsch participant, becomes the first Nazi to hold a ministerial-level post in Germany. He is given control of the Interior and Education Ministries, and by passing an "Enabling Act" through a simple majority as an emergency decree, granting him the power to radically transform Thuringia. Gone are the days of Red Thuringia. Suspected socialists and democrats are purged en masse from the civil service. A state police force is established, with Frick preferentially employing Nazi officials. All communist teachers and mayors are dismissed, and newspapers critical of government policy are banned. [? if prussia_leader == "Braun" and interior_minister_party == "SPD": Fortunately, Carl Severing is able to halt the recruitment of Nazis into the police force by suspending state subsidies, effectively ending the practice. ?] With control of the Education Ministry, Frick appoints racial researchers and known Nazis to top positions at many universities and bans the anti-war book *All Quiet on the Western Front* from being read or played. His attempts to grant Hitler German citizenship have so far failed, forcing Hitler to look elsewhere.

local_election_thuringia.grand_coalition.titleHtml: A [? if lvp_formed: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed: Grand?] Coalition is formed!
local_election_thuringia.grand_coalition.subtitleHtml: We have somehow reconciled with the bourgeois parties, that they're willing to govern with us again.
local_election_thuringia.grand_coalition.bodyHtml: Somehow, the bourgeois parties are willing to form a [? if lvp_formed: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed: Grand?] Coalition with us, rather than continuing their current government. We will use our positions in government to root out right-wing and nationalist sympathies within the civil service and to strengthen republican sentiment.

local_election_thuringia.no_majority.subtitleHtml: [? if bourgeois_coalition_thuringia < 50 and far_right_coalition_thuringia < 50 and spd_coalition_thuringia < 50: All possible coalitions lack a majority. ?][? if (bourgeois_coalition_thuringia < 50 and not toleration_possible) or (spd_coalition_thuringia >= 50 and not spd_coalition_possible): The bourgeois parties still haven't forgiven us. ?]
local_election_thuringia.no_majority.bodyHtml: With the bourgeois parties unable to secure a majority even with the inclusion of the **NSDAP**, and their refusal to form a coalition with us, no viable majority can be established. The ruling coalition fears that calling new elections will only accelerate their decline and further erode their support. In an effort to avoid this, they are more open to negotiating a toleration agreement.

local_election_thuringia.no_majority_2.titleHtml: A majority still can't be found!
local_election_thuringia.no_majority_2.subtitleHtml: [? if not toleration_possible: This is getting ridiculous. ?][? if toleration_possible: We will refuse to tolerate the bourgeois government, forcing new elections. ?]
local_election_thuringia.no_majority_2.bodyHtml: [? if not toleration_possible: The bourgeois parties remain unwilling to accept our offer of toleration. [? if far_right_coalition_thuringia + ddp_r_thuringia >= 50: One option the incumbent coalition has considered is including both the **[+ ddp_name +]** and the **NSDAP**, but for obvious reasons, both parties have vetoed this proposal. ?]?][? if toleration_possible: By refusing to enter any toleration agreement, and with the bourgeois parties unwilling to let us lead the government, no majority can be found. As a result, we have shouldered much of the blame for the deadlock and are likely to suffer in the next elections. ?] With no viable alternatives, the Landtag faces dissolution, triggering new elections—an opportunity the **NSDAP** hopes to exploit by capitalizing on political instability and the perceived failure of parliamentary democracy.

local_election_thuringia.spd_majority.titleHtml: The **SPD** forms a majority government.
local_election_thuringia.spd_majority.bodyHtml: To the sheer horror of the right-wing parties in Thuringia, an unforeseen occurrence has swept over the state: a complete SPD majority. Members of the far-right cry foul; voter fraud, other forms of subterfuge, and attacks ranging to outright conspiracy is hurled at the results. Nonetheless, Red Thuringia is restored, without the revolutionary concerns of the **USPD**/**KPD**’s presence in the landtag. We have undertaken the purging of reactionary sentiments within the police, and revamped the state’s school curriculum to move away from the nationalistic values that remain prevalent. More work is set to be done, but at least Hindenburg’s gaze has been turned away… for now.

params.source: thuringia_coalition_menu

local_election_thuringia.thuringia_coali.bodyHtml: The bourgeois parties have historically been hostile to us in state politics, especially after the notorious **SPD**-**USPD**-**KPD** United Left government faced a Reichsexekution six years ago. They still haven't forgiven the **SPD** for this. Meanwhile, the surging **NSDAP**, now controlling [+ nsdap_r_thuringia +]% of the Landtag, is no longer content with mere toleration and demands a role in government. With the bourgeois parties determined to exclude us from power, Thuringia may well become the first state to appoint a Nazi minister.

local_election_thuringia.toleration_thur.titleHtml: The incumbent bourgeois-right government has fallen short of a majority.
local_election_thuringia.toleration_thur.subtitleHtml: We will offer our toleration to them, to prevent their dependence on the **NSDAP**.
local_election_thuringia.toleration_thur.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, through our reconciliation with the bourgeois parties, they have accepted our toleration to prevent the **NSDAP** from entering government. However, this provides valuable propaganda for the Nazis, who gain support at the expense of the **DNVP** and **CNBLP**, who are now tainted by their association with us.

local_election_thuringia.united_left_thu.titleHtml: The **SPD** will form a coalition government with the **KPD**.
local_election_thuringia.united_left_thu.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, despite reluctance on both sides due to fears that the reactionary Hindenburg will order a Reichsexekution if a coalition were to form. Red Thuringia is restored! Hindenburg’s patience is especially thin. Tread carefully.

london_economic_conference.subtitleHtml: The League of Nations unites to tackle the Great Depression...
london_economic_conference.bodyHtml: = London Economic Conference # TODO: if you've recovered, you get economic recovery # if you haven't recovered, you can either support Roosevelt or support the UK/France The League of Nations is hosting a conference to discuss the state of the global economy and potential solutions to the ongoing depression. All parties want to reduce tariffs to encourage trade. However, the Western powers are at an impasse; France and to a lesser extent Britain are calling for fixed currency exchange rates, while President Roosevelt of the United States wants to print new money to stimulate demand, calling for "controlled inflation". The Europeans want to reduce their debts to the US, while America favors continued full payments.

params.source: economic_recovery if unemployed < 15; no_recovery if unemployed >= 15

london_economic_conference.economic_reco.bodyHtml:
[? if wtb_adopted or budget <= 0: Germany has largely recovered from the crisis, owing in large part to the same sorts of economic policies that Roosevelt is pursuing. ?]
[? if not wtb_adopted and budget > 0: Germany has largely recovered from the crisis, without having to resort to budget deficits or devaluing the currency. ?]

london_economic_conference.no_business.titleHtml: This conference is none of our concern.
london_economic_conference.no_business.bodyHtml: The conference collapses, as expected. In response to the continued support for fixed currency exchange rates and the impasse on debts, the Americans pull out of the conference, leaving it with no agreements whatsoever. [? if unemployed >= 15 : Nevertheless, the world economy is slowly improving due in part to the economic stimulus and more liberal trade policies of the Roosevelt administration. ?] [? if unemployed < 15 : Nevertheless, the world economy is slowly improving due in part to the economic stimulus and more liberal trade policies of the Roosevelt administration as well as our own economic plan. ?]

london_economic_conference.no_recovery.bodyHtml: Germany, like the rest of the world, is still deep in the economic crisis, even if it has appeared to bottom out.

london_economic_conference.salvage.titleHtml: Can we try to salvage the negotiations?
london_economic_conference.salvage.bodyHtml: How should we try to salvage the negotiations?

choices.labelHtml: Try to convince France and Britain that slowly controlled inflation is possible and desirable.
Try to convince the US to reduce war debts for the sake of peace.

london_economic_conference.salvage_curre.bodyHtml: Wladimir Woytinsky, now part of our delegation to the conference, uses our successful implementation of the WTB-plan in order to argue for loosening currency valuation. The argument is at least somewhat convincing, and an agreement is reached, leading to increased inflation and demand stimulus throughout the world.

london_economic_conference.salvage_debts.bodyHtml: We try to argue that reducing war debts will reduce the risk of a future European war, using our successful disarmament and the reduction in Versailles reparation payments as an argument. The argument is at least somewhat convincing to the Americans, leading to an agreement to reduce debts from the Great War. This indirectly also improves our economy.

london_economic_conference.stable_curren.titleHtml: German representatives call for stable currency, along with Britain and France.
london_economic_conference.stable_curren.bodyHtml: As expected, the conservative German bankers support Britain and France's plan to stabilize currency exchange rates. In response to the continued support for fixed currency exchange rates and the impasse on debts, the Americans pull out of the conference, leaving it with no agreements whatsoever. [? if unemployed >= 15 : Nevertheless, the world economy is slowly improving due in part to the economic stimulus and more liberal trade policies of the Roosevelt administration. ?] [? if unemployed < 15 : Nevertheless, the world economy is slowly improving due in part to the economic stimulus and more liberal trade policies of the Roosevelt administration as well as our own economic plan. ?]

london_economic_conference.support_franc.titleHtml: Support France and Britain - we must have stable currency.
london_economic_conference.support_franc.bodyHtml: Our position brings us closer to other European powers. In response to the continued support for fixed currency exchange rates and the impasse on debts, the Americans pull out of the conference, leaving it with no agreements whatsoever.

london_economic_conference.support_roose.titleHtml: Support Roosevelt's ideas - we must devalue currency.
london_economic_conference.support_roose.bodyHtml: We support Roosevelt's plan for controlled inflation, leaving us at odds with the European powers. In response to the continued support for fixed currency exchange rates by France and Britain and the impasse on debts, the Americans pull out of the conference, leaving it with no agreements whatsoever.

long_war.titleHtml: Germany is gripped by civil war.
long_war.bodyHtml: Germany is currently in the grip of a civil war, a brutal affair that has no obvious end. Thousands of lives have already been extinguished, and it is likely that the war will not stop until Germany's cities are reduced to ruins. [? if is_favorable == 0 : The current conditions are not favorable for us. ?][? if west_relation >= 2: Our cause is popular in the West, but their sclerotic governments are reluctant to send us aid. ?][? if soviet_aid >= 1 : The Soviet Union has aided the Communists, but not the socialists and democrats, in an attempt to shape Germany's future government. ?][? if east_aid >= 1 : Poland and Czechoslovakia have sent some assistance against the fascists. ?]

params.source: eg_menu

long_war_2.titleHtml: There is nothing we can do.
long_war_2.bodyHtml: No matter our efforts, the war continues. Too many lives are extinguished. Refugees begin to flow into Germany, and trade suffers. Many are calling our Austrian interference a mistake.

choices.labelHtml: Perhaps we can receive aid from the Western powers, France and Britain.
Perhaps we can receive aid from the Soviet Union.
Perhaps our eastern neighbors, Poland and Czechoslovakia, can help us. If they know anything, they do not want fascists coming to power in Germany.

lower_militancy.bodyHtml: Bowing to the other parties' demands, we reduce the Reichsbanner's military training, thus inducing them to stay.

params.code: state.flags['rb_militancy'] *= 0.5;
params.source: rb_militancy *= 0.5

lower_tariffs.subtitleHtml: -2 budget. [? if tariffs <= -5 : There are no tariffs left to cut. ?]
lower_tariffs.bodyHtml: Lowering tariffs helps workers and the urban poor by reducing prices for basic necessities. In addition, other countries are pleased by lower tariffs, and are more willing to negotiate on many issues. Farmers are hurt by this policy, as cheap imported grain leads to ruin for some small producers. In general, cheap imports are detrimental for small-scale industries aimed at the domestic market. Those negatively affected have rallied behind the [? if not kvp_formed: **DNVP**?][? if kvp_formed: **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical":, stoking their urgency to reenter government to act upon this?].

Our efforts in cultivating republican loyalties in the police have proven their worth. ?]

params.source: war_menu

loyalty.bodyHtml: As with the Prussian state police, there are measures we can take to root out reactionary and anti-democratic sentiment in the police. We can improve training and recruiting procedures, and identify and remove known fascists and the like. Current interior police loyalty: [+ interior_police_loyalty : loyalty +]

luders.subtitleHtml: The most active woman within the **[+ ddp_name +]**, and strongly internationalist. Associated with the party's left wing.
luders.bodyHtml: Marie-Elisabeth Lüders, the second most important woman in the **[+ ddp_name +]**, and easily the most active advocate for the rights and wellbeing of women, children, and the workers of Germany, is elected to the leadership of the **[+ ddp_name +]**. This victory comes with the backing of Ernst Lemmer and his liberal trade unions, who have gained significant influence in recent months. Our relationship with the **[+ ddp_name +]** has greatly improved compared to how it was under Dietrich. Lüders is a strong internationalist and has previously advocated for Pan-European cooperation, which will benefit us in future negotiations. She was also one of the strongest opponents of the merger with the Young German Order, arguing against their antisemitism. However, it remains to be seen whether she will gain more votes than she loses due to her feminism, as many refuse to support her purely out of misogyny.

luther.titleHtml: Hans Luther, [? if luther_reichsbank: president of the Reichsbank?][? if not luther_reichsbank: leader of the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]?] and former chancellor.
luther.bodyHtml: Hans Luther, former Chancellor of the first federal right-wing coalition and key figure in addressing the hyperinflationary crisis, is certainly not lacking in the experience required to assume the presidency of the Reich. Among his peers, he stands out as relatively open to constructive cooperation with the **SPD**, though it is clear that he favors a presidential bourgeois government over continued socialist participation in power. Despite his party affiliation, he is widely viewed as a non-partisan candidate. His candidacy is supported by the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]. [? if not lvp_formed: He is also nominally supported by the **[+ ddp_name +]**. ?]

params.source: reactionary_candidates if reactionary_candidate_1932_count_2 > 0

choices.labelHtml: We await the decision of the Harzburg Front.

luther_fail.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, Luther has failed to command the majority of the **LVP** behind his candidacy. Following this result, Luther has resigned from his chairmanship and now endorses [+ luther_endorsed_candidate +] for the leadership race, however his endorsement fails to sway much delegates into his favor. Luther has now taken up a position as the President of the Reichsbank, still holding some sway over party affairs.

luther_win.bodyHtml: From former Chancellor to President, Hans Luther has secured the presidency. Known for his technocratic beliefs, he's unlikely to rock the boat in either political direction. Let’s hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

params.source: lvp_party_congress_1930_0

lvp_formed.bodyHtml: The momentum towards liberal unity has proven too great for the few holdouts within the **DVP**'s right wing to stand against. The party has officially voted to approve the merger with the **[+ ddp_name +]**, who have also done the same. Both parties will now work together to establish the framework of the new Liberal People's Party.

lvp_groko.bodyHtml: As a result of the left-liberal **[+ ddp_name +]** and conservative-liberal **DVP** having merged, we could go ahead with kicking the small **BVP** out of government. This will leave us with a majority Weimar Coalition.

choices.labelHtml: Form a Weimar Coalition.

lvp_loss.bodyHtml: With the death of Gustav Stresemann, the right wing of the **LVP** is much less likely to be accommodating of us. In addition, the liberals are electorally in decline, so perhaps our efforts are best spent elsewhere. However, given the influence of the **LVP** among the other right-leaning parties [? if president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate": and with President [+ president +] ?], it can still be helpful to influence them.

lvp_merger_1928.subtitleHtml: The future of the liberal movement will be decided here.
lvp_merger_1928.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Congress Stresemann has called an emergency party congress within the **DVP** over the contentious issue of a merger with **[+ ddp_name +]**. The Liberal Association has already made significant strides in laying the groundwork for a united liberal party, including the creation of a national framework and the drafting of a middle-class-oriented policy platform broadly supported by both parties. However, the right wing of the **DVP**, led by Ernst Scholz, remains the final stumbling block towards a united liberal party. They are determined to oppose the merger, wielding their substantial influence over the party and industrialists to rally against it.

lvp_merger_1928.lvp_formed.bodyHtml: The momentum towards liberal unity has proven too great for the few holdouts within the **DVP**'s right wing to stand against. The party has officially voted to approve the merger with the **[+ ddp_name +]**, who have also done the same. Both parties will now work together to establish the framework of the new Liberal People's Party.

lvp_merger_1929.subtitleHtml: The future of the liberal movement will be decided here.
lvp_merger_1929.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Congress The **DVP**, now under the interim leadership of Julius Curtius, is locked in open conflict with the party’s right wing and industrial backers over the proposed merger with the **[+ ddp_name +]**. With no other choice, the left wing of the **DVP** has called for an emergency party congress to formally vote on the merger. Meanwhile, the Liberal Association has made significant progress in preparing for a unified liberal party, establishing a national framework and drafting a middle-class-oriented policy platform that enjoys broad support from both sides. However, a defeat at this congress would spell the end of liberal cooperation for the foreseeable future, and will greatly demoralize the German middle.

lvp_merger_1929_2.subtitleHtml: The future of the liberal movement will be decided here.
lvp_merger_1929_2.bodyHtml: = **[+ ddp_name +]** Congress The **DVP** has made its decision in favor of merging the two parties; now, the fate of the unification rests with the [+ ddp_name +]. The most prominent proponents within the **[+ ddp_name +]** in favor of the merger are those in the business wing, who have pursued this goal for years. On the other hand, leftists within the **[+ ddp_name +]** strongly oppose the merger citing obvious concerns, as well as those who favor a potential merger with the **VNR** instead. A defeat in this decision would spell the end of liberal cooperation for the foreseeable future, severely demoralizing the German middle class, with the blame falling on the **[+ ddp_name +]**.

lvp_merger_1929_2.ddp_fail.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the **[+ ddp_name +]** have rejected the plans to create a united Liberal People's Party. It seems that the infighting that plagues the **[+ ddp_name +]** remains alive and well. This outcome has greatly demoralized the German middle and has forced the disbandment of the Liberal Association.

lvp_merger_1929_2.ddp_success.bodyHtml: As expected, the **[+ ddp_name +]** has followed the **DVP**'s decision and affirmed their support for a united Liberal People's Party. However, the leftists within the **[+ ddp_name +]** will wield little influence in the wider party, which will consist of twice as many **DVP** members as **[+ ddp_name +]** members.

lvp_merger_1929.dvp_fail.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, the efforts to unify the liberal parties have ended in failure. The right wing and industrial backers of the **DVP** successfully swayed a narrow majority to reject the merger proposal. This outcome has greatly demoralized the German middle and has forced the disbandment of the Liberal Association.

lvp_merger_1929.dvp_success.bodyHtml: The momentum towards liberal unity has proven too great for the holdouts within the **DVP**'s right wing to stand against. The party has officially voted to approve the merger with the **[+ ddp_name +]**, although the latter has yet to reach a final decision. The aftermath of the congress has significantly diminished the influence of the **DVP**'s right wing, and will shape the ideology of the Liberal People's Party if it is to form.

lvp_merger_1930.subtitleHtml: The future of the liberal movement will be decided here.
lvp_merger_1930.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Congress The **DVP**, under the leadership of [+ dvp_leader +], is locked in conflict with the party’s right wing and industrial backers over the proposed merger with the **[+ ddp_name +]**. With no other choice, [+ dvp_leader +] has called for an emergency party congress to formally vote on the merger. [? if dvp_leader == "Scholz" or dvp_leader == "Dingeldey": Since the leader of the **DVP** is a rightist himself, he will help convince reluctant party members that it is an alliance of necessity. ?][? if dvp_leader == "Luther": Hans Luther has been a long-time supporter for liberal unity, and will essentially use his sizable influence among the German bourgeoisie to almost guarantee the passage of the vote. ?] Meanwhile, the Liberal Association has made significant progress in preparing for a unified liberal party, establishing a national framework and drafting a middle-class-oriented policy platform that enjoys broad support from both sides. However, a defeat at this congress would spell the end of liberal cooperation for the foreseeable future, and will greatly demoralize the German middle.

lvp_merger_1930_2.subtitleHtml: The future of the liberal movement will be decided here.
lvp_merger_1930_2.bodyHtml: = **[+ ddp_name +]** Congress The **DVP** has made its decision in favor of merging the two parties; now, the fate of the unification rests with the [+ ddp_name +]. The most prominent proponents within the **[+ ddp_name +]** in favor of the merger are those in the business wing, who have pursued this goal for years. On the other hand, leftists within the **[+ ddp_name +]** strongly oppose the merger citing obvious concerns, but the flagging vote share of the German liberal parties has convinced the majority of the party to 'do something'. A defeat in this decision would spell the end of liberal cooperation for the foreseeable future, severely demoralizing the German middle class, with the blame falling on the **[+ ddp_name +]**.

lvp_merger_1930_2.ddp_fail.bodyHtml: As always, the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s left wing have rejected the plans to create a united Liberal People's Party. It seems that the infighting that plagues the **[+ ddp_name +]** remains alive and well. This outcome has greatly demoralized the German middle and has forced the disbandment of the Liberal Association.

lvp_merger_1930_2.ddp_success.bodyHtml: Perhaps surprisingly, the **[+ ddp_name +]** has followed the **DVP**'s decision and affirmed their support for a united Liberal People's Party. It seems that the leftists within the **[+ ddp_name +]** have finally lost their battle to maintain the position of a 'Social and Republican party in the Weimar party system. However, the leftists within the **[+ ddp_name +]** will wield little influence in the wider party, which will consist of twice as many **DVP** members as **[+ ddp_name +]** members.

The right wing and industrial backers of the **DVP** successfully swayed a narrow majority to reject the merger proposal. This outcome has greatly demoralized the German middle and has forced the disbandment of the Liberal Association.

lvp_merger_1930.dvp_success.bodyHtml: The momentum towards liberal unity has proven too great for the holdouts within the **DVP**'s right wing to stand against. The party has officially voted to approve the merger with the **[+ ddp_name +]**, although the latter has yet to reach a final decision. Despite this victory, many are halfhearted in their support of liberal unity, only viewing it as an alliance of necessity, which could spark some problems in the proposed wider party.

lvp_merger_threshold.subtitleHtml: The electoral threshold threatens to push both parties out of parliament.
lvp_merger_threshold.bodyHtml: = **DVP** Congress With the passage of a 5% electoral threshold, the two liberal parties now face the real risk of being shut out of parliament entirely—even with the influx of defectors from various bourgeois factions boosting their numbers. While current polling may look favorable, a single poor electoral cycle could wipe out their representation altogether. As a result, the two parties are being forced into cooperation, whether they like it or not. A new "Liberal Association" has already made significant strides toward unification, establishing a national framework and drafting a middle-class-oriented policy platform that commands broad support across both parties. Industrial backers have also thrown their weight behind the project, reasoning that a party compromised by the [+ ddp_name +]'s leftists is still preferable to no representation at all.

lvp_merger_threshold.dvp_success.bodyHtml: The momentum towards liberal unity has proven too great for the holdouts within the **DVP**'s right wing to stand against. The party has officially voted to approve the merger with the **[+ ddp_name +]**, although the latter has yet to reach a final decision. The aftermath of the congress has significantly diminished the influence of the **DVP**'s right wing, and will shape the ideology of the Liberal People's Party if it is to form.

params.source: lvp_party_congress_1930_0

lvp_party_congress_1928_0.subtitleHtml: The future of this new party will be decided here.
lvp_party_congress_1928_0.bodyHtml: = First **LVP** Party Congress The Liberal People's Party (**LVP**) has officially been founded! Hans Luther, former chancellor and **DVP** member, has been chosen as the interim leader of the new party. The **LVP**'s inaugural congress will play a major role in shaping the direction of the newly founded party, and most importantly, decide who will lead the liberal movement forward.

lvp_party_congress_1928_0.groko.bodyHtml: The bourgeois parties are pleased and somewhat surprised by this move.

params.source: cabinet_reformation

lvp_party_congress_1928_0.luther.bodyHtml: Hans Luther is once again chosen to lead the **LVP**, a long-time advocate for liberal and bourgeois unity, and a figure acceptable to both wings of the newly unified party. Meanwhile, the right wing of the **DVP**, despite their initial resistance to the merger, is now focusing on shifting the **LVP** further right, leveraging the support of the party's industrial backers.

lvp_party_congress_1928_0.lvp_groko.bodyHtml: As a result of the left-liberal **[+ ddp_name +]** and conservative-liberal **DVP** having merged, we could go ahead with kicking the small **BVP** out of government. This will leave us with a majority Weimar Coalition.

choices.labelHtml: Form a Weimar Coalition.

lvp_party_congress_1928_0.lvp_weimar.bodyHtml: As a result of the left-liberal **[+ ddp_name +]** and conservative-liberal **DVP** having merged, they demand that their members that were formerly apart of the **DVP** to be included in the government. We will have to reshuffle the cabinet.

lvp_party_congress_1928_0.weimar.bodyHtml: Expected, but the bourgeois parties are displeased by the exclusion of the **BVP** from the ruling coalition.

params.source: cabinet_reformation

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.bodyHtml: = Second **LVP** Party Congress The merger of two notoriously factionalized parties has unsurprisingly introduced great dysfunction into the internal politics of the **LVP**. Not even a unifying figure like Hans Luther has been able to quell the endless bickering among the party's factions. The economic depression has only deepened these divisions, with disagreements arising even on broadly supported issues like parliamentary government, making unified action nearly impossible. While Hans Luther is expected to secure re-election, scattered candidates across the party could emerge if the majority of the party loses confidence in Luther's leadership.

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.curtius.subtitleHtml: Curtius was a member of the former **DVP**, and is a committed Stresemannite and member of their left wing. He has since succeeded Stresemann on foreign policy matters.
lvp_party_congress_1928_1.curtius.bodyHtml: Julius Curtius, Stresemann's successor in foreign affairs and a former member of the **DVP**, has won the vote to succeed Luther for the chairmanship. Curtius is supported by the 'Pragmatic Center', and was put forth as a compromise candidate. As a former member of the **DVP**'s left wing, he is in favor of closer cooperation with us. However, his leadership has been quite uninspiring, to say the least. [? if foreign_minister_party == "LVP": The responsibilities of the foreign ministry prevent him from being involved in the day-to-day running of his party, which is now delegated to a group of his associates in the 'Pragmatic Center'. ?]

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.deadlock.bodyHtml: The vote has been deadlocked, with no candidate ahead by enough to constitute a majority. You, the player, now has free will to choose a compromise candidate. Spend it wisely.

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.dietrich.subtitleHtml: Dietrich was the former leader of the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s business wing, and is somewhat skeptical of cooperation with us.
lvp_party_congress_1928_1.dietrich.bodyHtml: Hermann Dietrich, formerly affiliated with the business wing of the **[+ ddp_name +]**, has been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Dietrich is mainly supported by smaller businesses and ruralites, and [? if chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government: is known for formulating Brüning's emergency decrees during his tenure as Finance Minister.?][? if not (chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government): is known for his fiscal conservatism.?] Despite this, Dietrich is not as extreme as the industrialists on the right of the party and remains open to cooperation with us if there is no other majority. However, his leadership has been quite uninspiring, to say the least. [? if agriculture_minister_party == "LVP" or economic_minister_party == "LVP": The responsibilities of his ministry prevent him from being involved in the day-to-day running of his party, which is now delegated to a group of his associates in the business wing. ?]

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.dingeldey.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey was a member of the former **DVP**, and commonly associated with the industrial-right of the party.
lvp_party_congress_1928_1.dingeldey.bodyHtml: Eduard Dingeldey, previously part of the movement for bourgeois unity, has now been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Dingeldey is backed by the industrial forces on the right of the party, alongside former **DVP** members. He appears to be focused on fostering closer cooperation with the array of parties between the **LVP** and the **DNVP**. However, Dingeldey has thus far proven to be an ineffectual leader, often capitulating to the right wing of the **LVP**. Recently, we’ve observed a deterioration in relations with his party, alongside a noticeable rightward shift in the **LVP**'s internal politics.

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.heuss.subtitleHtml: Heuss is a Social Republican, and a member of the former **[+ ddp_name +]**.
lvp_party_congress_1928_1.heuss.bodyHtml: Theodor Heuss, a rising star and former member of the **[+ ddp_name +]**, has been elected chairman of the Liberal People's Party. Backed primarily by the 'Social Republican Circle,' composed of former **[+ ddp_name +]** members and liberal intellectuals and newspapers, Heuss has also garnered support from the broader party due to his decently conservative stances on economic and national issues. Heuss's victory empowers the 'Social Republican' wing, strengthening our cooperation. Despite his personal leanings toward the right, Heuss remains one of the most committed and genuine supporters for liberal democracy within the **LVP**.

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.luther.bodyHtml: Hans Luther is expectedly re-elected as the leader of the **LVP**. He will navigate the party through the economic depression and will hopefully try to maintain bourgeois backing for the Weimar system.

lvp_party_congress_1928_1.luther_fail.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, Luther has failed to command the majority of the **LVP** behind his candidacy. Following this result, Luther has resigned from his chairmanship and now endorses [+ luther_endorsed_candidate +] for the leadership race. Luther has now taken up a position as the President of the Reichsbank, still holding significant sway over party affairs.

lvp_party_congress_1928_2_luther.subtitleHtml: Luther resigns from his party positions to accept the presidency.
lvp_party_congress_1928_2_luther.bodyHtml: = **LVP** Party Congress With Luther elected president, he naturally cannot continue serving as the **LVP**'s chairman. A party congress is convened to select his successor. This marks the first time Germany has elected a president from the political middle, and optimism within the party is running high. The candidates in the running belong to the younger generation, as the party looks to carry forward the momentum gained from Luther’s presidential victory.

lvp_party_congress_1928_2_luther.deadloc.bodyHtml: The vote has been deadlocked, with no candidate ahead by enough to constitute a majority. You, the player, now has free will to choose a compromise candidate. Spend it wisely.

lvp_party_congress_1928_2_luther.dieckma.subtitleHtml: Dieckmann is a member of the Saxon Landtag and a former member of the **DVP**, being a committed follower of Stresemann.
lvp_party_congress_1928_2_luther.dieckma.bodyHtml: (If you can find an image of him taken around this period of time, please message the modman.) Johannes Dieckmann, a relatively minor figure who only recently became president of the **LVP**'s parliamentary group in the Saxon Landtag, has been elected party chairman. A longtime associate of Stresemann and a member of the **DVP**'s left wing, Dieckmann even chaired a revolutionary soldiers' council in 1918. His youth and low profile have left him with few enemies—unlike Curtius—making him a palatable compromise. While he represents an improvement over Luther’s policies, it is a slight one.

lvp_party_congress_1928_2_luther.maier.bodyHtml: Reinhold Maier, a major figure in Württemberg politics and a rising star in the struggling party, has been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Youthful and energetic, he is less bound by dogma than many veteran members, making him a strong choice for a party plagued by defeatism and internal strife. His association with the former **[+ ddp_name +]**'s business wing isn't the best news for future cooperation. While still an improvement over Luther’s policies, it is only a slight one.

lvp_party_congress_1929_1.dingeldey.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey was a member of the former **DVP**, and commonly associated with the industrial-right of the party.
lvp_party_congress_1929_1.dingeldey.bodyHtml: Eduard Dingeldey, previously part of the movement for bourgeois unity, has now been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Dingeldey is backed by the industrial forces on the right of the party, alongside former **DVP** members. He appears to be focused on fostering closer cooperation with the array of parties between the **LVP** and the **DNVP**. However, Dingeldey has thus far proven to be an ineffectual leader, often capitulating to the right wing of the **LVP**. Recently, we’ve observed a deterioration in relations with his party, alongside a noticeable rightward shift in the **LVP**'s internal politics.

lvp_party_congress_1929_1.heuss.bodyHtml: Theodor Heuss, a rising star and former member of the **[+ ddp_name +]**, has been elected chairman of the Liberal People's Party. Backed primarily by the 'Social Republican Circle,' composed of former **[+ ddp_name +]** members and liberal intellectuals and newspapers, Heuss has also garnered support from the broader party due to his decently conservative stances on economic and national issues. Heuss's victory empowers the 'Social Republican' wing, strengthening our cooperation. Despite his personal leanings toward the right, Heuss remains one of the most committed and genuine supporters for liberal democracy within the **LVP**.

lvp_party_congress_1930_0.subtitleHtml: The future of this new party will be decided here.
lvp_party_congress_1930_0.bodyHtml: = First **LVP** Party Congress The Liberal People's Party (**LVP**) has officially been founded! Hans Luther, former chancellor and **DVP** member, has been chosen as the interim leader of the new party. The **LVP**'s inaugural congress will play a major role in shaping the direction of the newly founded party, and most importantly, decide who will lead the liberal movement forward. [? if lvp_ideology == "Right": Disappointingly, the right-wing shift of the predecessor parties has impacted this party as well. ?]

lvp_party_congress_1930_0.groko.bodyHtml: The bourgeois parties are pleased and somewhat surprised by this move.

params.source: cabinet_reformation

lvp_party_congress_1930_0.luther.bodyHtml: Hans Luther is chosen to lead the **LVP**, a long-time advocate for liberal and bourgeois unity, and a figure acceptable to both wings of the newly unified party. His influence among the German business community undoubtedly is what secured him the selection, it's hard to imagine the mixture of the dissenting factions of both predecessor parties being able to choose a single candidate. Meanwhile, the skeptics on the extremes of the party, despite their initial resistance to the merger, is now focusing on shifting the **LVP** further towards one end of the political spectrum. The **DVP** right will leverage the highly influential support of the party's industrial backers, while the **[+ ddp_name +]** left will attempt to lobby for policy that benefits the working class with their supporters in the labor unions.

lvp_party_congress_1930_0.lvp_groko.bodyHtml: As a result of the left-liberal **[+ ddp_name +]** and conservative-liberal **DVP** having merged, we could go ahead with kicking the small **BVP** out of government. This will leave us with a majority Weimar Coalition.

choices.labelHtml: Form a Weimar Coalition.

lvp_party_congress_1930_0.lvp_weimar.bodyHtml: As a result of the nominally left-liberal **[+ ddp_name +]** and conservative-liberal **DVP** having merged, they demand that their members that were formerly apart of the **DVP** to be included in the government. We will have to reshuffle the cabinet.

lvp_party_congress_1930_0.weimar.bodyHtml: An expected move, but the bourgeois parties are displeased by the exclusion of the **BVP** from the ruling coalition.

params.source: cabinet_reformation

lvp_party_congress_1930_1.bodyHtml: = Second **LVP** Party Congress The merger of two notoriously factionalized parties has unsurprisingly introduced great dysfunction into the internal politics of the **LVP**. Not even a unifying figure like Hans Luther has been able to quell the endless bickering among the party's factions. The economic depression has only deepened these divisions, with disagreements arising even on broadly supported issues like parliamentary government, making unified action nearly impossible. [? if chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government: The **LVP** has shifted significantly to the right due to their participation in [? if in_right_coalition: Brüning's center-right coalition?][? if not in_right_coalition: Brüning's emergency government?]. This election will be pivotal in determining their policy of cooperation with us in the foreseeable future.?] While Hans Luther is expected to secure re-election, scattered candidates from across the party could emerge if the majority loses confidence in Luther's leadership.

lvp_party_congress_1930_1.curtius.subtitleHtml: Curtius was a member of the former **DVP**, and is a committed Stresemannite and member of their left wing. He has since succeeded Stresemann on foreign policy matters.
lvp_party_congress_1930_1.curtius.bodyHtml: Julius Curtius, Stresemann's successor in foreign affairs and a former member of the **DVP**, has won the vote to succeed Luther for the chairmanship. Curtius is supported by the 'Pragmatic Center', and was put forth as a compromise candidate. As a former member of the **DVP**'s left wing, he is in favor of closer cooperation with us. However, his leadership has been quite uninspiring, to say the least. [? if foreign_minister_party == "LVP": The responsibilities of the foreign ministry prevent him from being involved in the day-to-day running of his party, which is now delegated to a group of his associates in the 'Pragmatic Center'. ?]

lvp_party_congress_curtius.bodyHtml: = **LVP** Party Vote Following the disastrous Austrian customs union project, which he was the architect of, he has tendered his resignation from both the Foreign Ministry and the leadership of the **LVP**. This debacle has significantly discredited him and his allies, leading to a rightward shift within the **LVP**. An internal election must now be held to determine Curtius’s successor. Many candidates who have previously lost to him in the last party congress have once again stepped up to replace him, significantly crowding the field. Newer candidates have also thrown their hats in the ring. The right wing of the **LVP** will rally behind Dingeldey, the left Social Republicans will support Heuss, and the pragmatic center prefers Dietrich. While the new candidates have a low chance of winning, they may emerge as a compromise if no candidate secures a majority.

lvp_party_congress_curtius.baumer.subtitleHtml: Leader of the **LVP**'s women's wing, and a moderate feminist. Has questionable views on the "national questions".
lvp_party_congress_curtius.baumer.bodyHtml: Somehow, Gertrud Bäumer, long-time deputy leader of the **[+ ddp_name +]** and now the leader of the **LVP**'s women's wing, has been elected to the leadership of the **LVP**. This is quite a bizarre development, but her victory can be attributed to her passionate nationalism and romanticism, as well as her questionable views on Jews and race, which have garnered the support of nationalists within the party. Additionally, some within the party cynically believe that by electing a woman, they can appeal to a broader female electorate. For us, Bäumer's background as a former **[+ ddp_name +]** member may work in our favor, improving our relationship with the **LVP**. However, it remains to be seen whether she will gain more votes than she loses due to her moderate feminist stance, as many refuse to support her purely out of misogyny.

lvp_party_congress_curtius.glatzel.subtitleHtml: Glatzel, a former member of the **DNVP** and **DVP**, advocates the idea of broadening the party's appeal to workers.
lvp_party_congress_curtius.glatzel.bodyHtml: Frank Glatzel, a trade unionist affiliated with the conservative white-collar union, the DHV, has been elected the new leader of the **LVP**. He advocates for a "New Nationalism," emphasizing solidarity among all classes to defend the country's "living space" and to foster freedom for the people. In his push for *Volksgemeinschaft*, aimed at reducing class conflict, he has incorporated more nationalistic and corporatist elements into the party platform. This vision gained him the support of nationalists and Stresemannites within the **LVP**, with the paramilitary group "Young German Order" even backing his leadership bid. As expected, this shift has caused concern among the remaining industrialists in the **LVP**, as the party moves away from its traditional sole focus on middle-class interests. This has resulted in a significant change in the party’s financial backing, with funding from big business dwindling and being replaced by donations and newly established dues. His dynamic leadership should be closely watched.

lvp_party_congress_curtius.stolper.bodyHtml: Gustav Stolper, a German-Austrian economist and the son of Jewish immigrants from Poland, has been elected chairman of the **LVP**, reinforcing a stereotype the party has long struggled to dispel. Despite this, Stolper—renowned for the economic program bearing his name—could be exactly what the **LVP** needs to revitalize its middle-class support. Relations have improved compared to Curtius's tenure, as Stolper's strained ties with parties to the right of the **LVP**—due to anti-Semitism—have made cooperation with us easier.

lvp_party_congress_dietrich.bodyHtml: = **LVP** Party Vote Hermann Dietrich has failed to meet the expectations of many within the party, with the **LVP** experiencing a sharp decline in recent local elections. His focus on governance has left him unable to personally manage party affairs, prompting the need for a more active leader. Dietrich has endorsed Reinhold Maier, a former **[+ ddp_name +]** member and rising star. Like Dietrich, Maier was part of the **[+ ddp_name +]**'s business wing and now enjoys the support of the **LVP**'s Pragmatic Center. Meanwhile, Heuss and Dingeldey have once again entered the race, representing the party’s left and right factions, respectively. With all candidates relatively young, this leadership contest is expected to inject a sense of dynamism into the party.

lvp_party_congress_dietrich.baumer.subtitleHtml: Leader of the **LVP**'s women's wing, and a moderate feminist. Has questionable views on the "national questions".
lvp_party_congress_dietrich.baumer.bodyHtml: Somehow, Gertrud Bäumer, long-time deputy leader of the **[+ ddp_name +]** and now the leader of the **LVP**'s women's wing, has been elected to the leadership of the **LVP**. This is quite a bizarre development, but her victory can be attributed to her passionate nationalism and romanticism, as well as her questionable views on Jews and race, which have garnered the support of nationalists within the party. Additionally, some within the party cynically believe that by electing a woman, they can appeal to a broader female electorate. For us, Bäumer's background as a former **[+ ddp_name +]** member may work in our favor, improving our relationship with the **LVP**. However, it remains to be seen whether she will gain more votes than she loses due to her moderate feminist stance, as many refuse to support her purely out of misogyny.

lvp_party_congress_dietrich.dingeldey.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey was a member of the former **DVP**, and commonly associated with the industrial-right of the party.
lvp_party_congress_dietrich.dingeldey.bodyHtml: Eduard Dingeldey, previously part of the movement for bourgeois unity, has now been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Dingeldey is backed by the industrial forces on the right of the party, alongside former **DVP** members. He appears to be focused on fostering closer cooperation with the array of parties between the **LVP** and the **DNVP**. However, Dingeldey has thus far proven to be an ineffectual leader, often capitulating to the right wing of the **LVP**. Recently, we’ve observed a deterioration in relations with his party, alongside a noticeable rightward shift in the **LVP**'s internal politics.

lvp_party_congress_dietrich.maier.bodyHtml: Reinhold Maier, a major figure in Württemberg politics and a rising star in the struggling party, has been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Youthful and energetic, he is less bound by dogma than many veteran members, making him a strong choice for a party plagued by defeatism and internal strife. For us, however, his closeness to Dietrich means cooperation has yet to improve significantly compared to his predecessor’s tenure. Perhaps this is for the best, as the **LVP**'s decline was expected to push it further to the right.

lvp_party_congress_dingeldey.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey faces a vote of no confidence!
lvp_party_congress_dingeldey.bodyHtml: = **LVP** Party Vote Dingeldey's tenure as leader of the **LVP** has been marked by a sharp decline in the party’s vote share and a decline in organizational activity. His right-wing positions and close ties to industrialists have made him a divisive figure, with many blaming the party’s rightward shift and association with big business for its dwindling appeal. Despite his unpopularity, the industrial-right remains firmly behind him, giving him a chance to survive the recently introduced vote of no confidence by the left of the party.

lvp_party_congress_heuss.curtius.bodyHtml: Julius Curtius, Stresemann's successor in foreign affairs and a former member of the **DVP**, has won the vote to succeed Luther for the chairmanship. Curtius is supported by the 'Pragmatic Center', and was put forth as a compromise candidate. As a former member of the **DVP**'s left wing, he is in favor of closer cooperation with us. However, his leadership has been quite uninspiring, to say the least. Dietrich is mainly supported by smaller businesses and ruralites, and [? if chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government: is known for formulating Brüning's emergency decrees during his tenure as Finance Minister.?][? if not (chancellor == "Brüning" and not spd_in_government): is known for his fiscal conservatism.?] Despite this, Dietrich is a huge step up from Dingeldey's leadership, and is open to cooperation. lvp_party_congress_heuss.dingeldey.subtitleHtml: Dingeldey was a member of the former **DVP**, and commonly associated with the industrial-right of the party.
lvp_party_congress_heuss.dingeldey.bodyHtml: Eduard Dingeldey, previously part of the movement for bourgeois unity, has now been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Dingeldey is backed by the industrial forces on the right of the party, alongside former **DVP** members. He appears to be focused on fostering closer cooperation with the array of parties between the **LVP** and the **DNVP**. However, Dingeldey has thus far proven to be an ineffectual leader, often capitulating to the right wing of the **LVP**. Recently, we’ve observed a deterioration in relations with his party, alongside a noticeable rightward shift in the **LVP**'s internal politics.

lvp_party_congress_heuss.heuss.subtitleHtml: Despite the party's decline, Heuss's liberal democratic ideals continue to enjoy strong support.
lvp_party_congress_heuss.heuss.bodyHtml: Fortunately, Heuss has survived the vote of no confidence and will remain the leader of the **LVP**, securing support from Curtius and many Stresemannites. This victory will temporarily silence dissent from the right-industrial faction and strengthen our ties with the party.

lvp_party_congress_heuss.heuss_fail.subtitleHtml: Unfortunately, the decline of the **LVP** has pushed the party further to the right.
lvp_party_congress_heuss.heuss_fail.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, Heuss has lost the vote of no confidence and must step down as leader, paving the way for a right-wing successor. With strong backing from the industrial-right faction of the **LVP**, Dingeldey is now the frontrunner in the upcoming leadership election. [? if not curtius_resign_lvp and not (curtius_banking_crisis and banking_crisis_seen): The Pragmatic Center has put forward Curtius as their candidate, leading Dietrich to withdraw and endorse him. ?][? if curtius_resign_lvp or (curtius_banking_crisis and banking_crisis_seen): The Pragmatic Center has nominated Dietrich as their candidate, though there is hesitation about electing yet another former **[+ ddp_name +]** member. ?]

lvp_popfront.bodyHtml: = The **LVP** leaves the Popular Front government! With the **[+ ddp_name +]** dissolving itself and joining with the **DVP** in a significantly more right-wing party, they have expectedly withdrawn their support of our incumbent Popular Front[? if in_popular_front_prussia and not in_popular_front: in Prussia?][? if in_popular_front_prussia and in_popular_front: in Prussia, and nationally?]. [? if in_popular_front: [? if popular_front_coalition >= 50: Fortunately, we still possess a majority without their votes, and they are able to leave government without causing much of a ruckus. ?][? if popular_front_coalition < 50: Unfortunately, the former **[+ ddp_name +]**'s votes was key for the survival of the Popular Front, and now our government lacks a majority without them. maier.subtitleHtml: A major player in Württemberg politics, he is now due for a promotion.
maier.bodyHtml: Reinhold Maier, a major figure in Württemberg politics and a rising star in the struggling party, has been elected chairman of the **LVP**. Youthful and energetic, he is less bound by dogma than many veteran members, making him a strong choice for a party plagued by defeatism and internal strife. His association with the former **[+ ddp_name +]**'s business wing isn't the best news for future cooperation, but he remains a significant improvement over Dingeldey's leadership.

mann_r1.bodyHtml: Heinrich Mann is a world-renowned novelist and poet who is also known to be a left-wing activist. His political sympathy lies with the far left, and he supported the revolutions in 1918 and 1919. He has long lived in the shadow of his better-known brother, Thomas Mann. Mann is willing to accept the nomination for president.

march_on_berlin.bodyHtml: = March on Berlin The far right is mobilizing. Paramilitary forces of the **Stahlhelm** and **SA**, organized under the Harzburg Front, have marched on Berlin, threatening to violently overthrow the government. They demand either immediate elections under the "supervision" of the nationalist paramilitaries, or else the immediate resignation of the government and the appointment of Adolf Hitler as chancellor[? if hitler_deported : , and the revocation of his deportation ?]. It is obvious that they are threatening a civil war if their demands are not met.

march_on_berlin.fight_2_pre_civil_war.bodyHtml: Our forces confront the fascists on the streets of Berlin, and armed fighting erupts. Neither side is dislodged from their positions.

march_on_berlin.fight_2_win.bodyHtml: Our forces confront the fascists, and somehow, the fascists retreat! They were overwhelmed by our display of strength, and have chosen to slink away. The attempted coup is over, at least for now. The show of force has reinvigorated support for the republic and for the **SPD**, and has weakened the fascists.

march_on_berlin.fight_constitution.titleHtml: This is unconstitutional! We will keep our positions in government, and ask the courts to keep us in power.
march_on_berlin.fight_constitution.bodyHtml: The courts agree that President [+ president +] is wrong to dismiss us, and that we should remain in the government. The President might respect the court's decision for now, but the fascists in the streets do not. They are still demanding snap elections or the resignation of the government, and will remain in the streets until we either meet their demands, or they are forced out.

march_on_berlin.left_front.bodyHtml: The **KPD** has taken an abstentionist position with regards to ministries. They claim to be participating as the "loyal opposition" in the worker's government, supporting us from the outside while also running their own propaganda campaigns to turn workers to their side. They seem to expect that we would inevitably fail, and that our failure would benefit them. Whatever their reasoning is, the **SPD** has control over the ministries of government.

march_on_berlin.new_elections_braun_reje.bodyHtml: The fascists reject our offer of free and fair elections. They are demanding that President [+ president +] dismisses the current government and appoints Hitler chancellor. [? if far_right_coalition >= 50 : They claim that since the far-right coalition has the majority in the Reichstag, they are constitutionally justified in appointing the chancellor. Unfortunately, their argument is not exactly wrong. ?]

march_on_berlin.new_elections_hindenburg.bodyHtml: With the mediation of various establishment figures, new elections are called for next month, without the use of fascist "electoral monitors".

params.source: new_elections_2

march_on_berlin.new_elections_hindenburg.bodyHtml: [? if president == "Hindenburg": Influenced by his inner circle and by the fascists in the streets, President Hindenburg rejects our offer of new free and fair elections, and again demands that we resign. ?][? if president != "Hindenburg": Influenced by the fascists in the streets—and his own sympathies, as the **Stahlhelm** is also taking part—President [+ president +] rejects our proposal for new free and fair elections, and once again demands our resignation. ?] There is no arguing.

march_on_berlin.new_elections_moderate.bodyHtml: Despite President [+ president +] standing with us against the far-right marchers, he remains under pressure from the fascists in the streets and prioritizes a peaceful resolution above all else. Still, [+ president +] refuses to accept any new election that is not truly free and fair.

march_on_berlin.new_elections_moderate_2.titleHtml: Free and fair elections it is!
march_on_berlin.new_elections_moderate_2.bodyHtml: The fascists, confident in their chances, agree to [+ president +]’s proposal to hold elections next month.

params.source: new_elections_2

march_on_berlin.new_elections_moderate_2.titleHtml: Any chance of a peaceful resolution is thrown out.
march_on_berlin.new_elections_moderate_2.bodyHtml: [+ president +] cannot bring himself to violate German democracy—or appoint a Nazi as Chancellor. Our only option now is to confront the fascists head-on, with the support of loyal government forces.

march_on_berlin.non_govt_menu.bodyHtml: It appears that President [+ president +] is looking favorably upon the fascist proposals. Chancellor [+ chancellor +] has announced plans to resign.

They claim to be participating as the "loyal opposition" within the Popular Front government, supporting us from the outside while also running their own propaganda campaigns to turn workers to their side. They seem to expect that the Popular Front would inevitably fail, and that our failure would benefit them.

marx_iv_collapse.bodyHtml: = Right-wing Coalition Dissolved The right-wing coalition comprising the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], **BVP**, **DVP**, and **DNVP**, led by Chancellor Wilhelm Marx, has been declared dissolved by the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] due to conflicts over school law regulations. While most coalition members supported the law, the **DVP** expressed concerns, advocating for the primacy of interdenominational schools and seeking to limit the church's influence. With talks having collapsed, new elections are scheduled for May, and the government will continue in a caretaker capacity.

marx_iv_collapse.good.bodyHtml: Our task is to prepare for the next elections where we stand to gain.

military_angry.subtitleHtml: The reactionary nest begins to voice its discontent aloud.
military_angry.bodyHtml: = Discontent in the Reichswehr The Reichswehr, despite its evident bias toward right-wing reactionary politics, has long portrayed itself as a non-partisan, neutral force in German affairs. Throughout most of the Weimar Republic’s history, it has largely refrained from overt political interference. However, Defense Minister Groener—alongside his longtime ally Kurt von Schleicher and Chief of the Army Kurt von Hammerstein-Equord—has now made public the military’s growing disagreements and concerns with the **SPD**. The Reichswehr remains widely respected across the political spectrum—except among the left-wing parties. Schleicher, long known as a political schemer, may attempt to exploit this to undermine our standing among our allies. We can either offer concessions to placate the military, or hold firm and do nothing at all.

military_angry.concessions.titleHtml: Perhaps another battleship will keep them happy?
military_angry.concessions.subtitleHtml: Conceding to the Reichswehr is viewed as a betrayal of our core values.
military_angry.concessions.bodyHtml: We have accepted Schleicher’s demands for increased funding toward the army’s modernization program, securing the purchase of new equipment for the small force. This decision has drawn intense criticism from the **Communists** and many within our own party, who condemn the diversion of funds into the black hole of the defense budget instead of toward welfare for women and children.

military_angry.idc.titleHtml: What are they going to do? Coup us?
military_angry.idc.bodyHtml: The Reichswehr won’t go so far as to overthrow us, but Schleicher’s decade-long web of connections is proving effective. We are also the victim of a renewed propaganda campaign by the nationalist parties[? if pacifism >= 5:, which has fortunately failed to gain traction?]. [? if president == "Hindenburg": As a key figure in President Hindenburg’s camarilla, he has played a major role in stoking the old man’s growing hostility toward us. ?]

military_angry.reform.subtitleHtml: The bourgeois parties will not be pleased.
military_angry.reform.bodyHtml:
Our request to dismiss Wilhelm Groener has been approved by our coalition partners. He is replaced by Hans Oster, a relatively minor officer in the German Army. While Oster shares the nationalist leanings common within the military and is conservative enough to be accepted as Groener’s successor, our lack of control over the Reichswehr Ministry limits us—we can only remove a handful of officials involved in political interference.
Schleicher has been dismissed from the Office for Ministerial Affairs, and von Hammerstein, for now, has remained notably quiet.

military_parity.titleHtml: But of course, Schleicher stipulates that we demand military parity.
military_parity.subtitleHtml: This will be a severe betrayal of our values!
military_parity.bodyHtml: General Schleicher has demanded that we raise the issue of rearmament, which remains restricted under the Treaty of Versailles. However, French Premier Édouard Herriot seized on this as an admission that Germany is, in fact, capable of paying its reparations and would simply redirect freed-up funds toward rearmament. [? if military_parity:[? if eu: However, with the formation of the European Union and its defense agreements, preventing Germany’s rearmament has become increasingly irrelevant. As a result, military restrictions are lifted!?][? if not eu: However, our exceptionally friendly relations with the Western Allies have led them to begrudgingly grant us flexibility in rearmament, believing that we could serve as a bulwark against the Bolsheviks.?] As a result, the **NSDAP** has lost yet another propaganda tool. military_parity_bruning.bodyHtml: General Schleicher, [? if president == "Hindenburg": the [? if not cvp_formed: **DNVP**?][? if cvp_formed: nationalists?], and President Hindenburg?][? if president != "Hindenburg": and the [? if not cvp_formed: **DNVP**?][? if cvp_formed: nationalists?]?] have pressured Brüning to raise the issue of rearmament, which remains restricted under the Treaty of Versailles, and the hated "war guilt" clause. Already wary of the right-wing elements in Brüning’s cabinet, the French have good reason to reject these demands. The controversy has only increased tensions within Brüning’s government.

military_policy.bodyHtml: #subtitle: Dealing with the Reichswehr. = Military Policy The Reichswehr is a deeply reactionary institution that has been generally hostile to any notion of socialism or democracy. However, we now control the military as part of the government. What should we do to reform it?

choices.labelHtml: Increase funding for the military to purchase its loyalty.
Reduce funding for the military so we have more for social spending.
Conduct a thorough reform of the ranks, reducing the influence of reactionaries and making it more hospitable to us.

military_policy.decrease_funding.bodyHtml: The military has fewer guns and fewer soldiers. There is no hint of a coup yet, but we do not know where the line will be drawn. The center-right parties are committed to the military and deeply opposed to our budget cuts. Many demobilized soldiers have joined the right-wing paramilitaries such as the **Stahlhelm** and **SA**, and weapons are missing from our stockpiles.

modinfo.faq.bodyHtml: = FAQ **Hindenburg keeps sacking me! How do I prevent it?** It's hard to prevent him from sacking you if you plan to stay in office for the full four years, but pausing reparations (by not exposing rearmament), keeping the Reichswehr loyal, maintaining a budget surplus, keeping a high pro republic support, a low coalition dissent, avoiding land reform, and keeping unemployment and NSDAP poll numbers low, all help. Remember, him sacking you is not the end of the world, and being free from the burden of government could be a blessing in disguise. Sometimes you have to accept it. **How impactful is government burden?** A main problem with newer players is that, they overestimate the negative effects of not completing government burden. It is not the end of the world if you miss a goal or two or three, some sacrifices are needed if you need to garner the budget for an economic plan. That said, you also can't afford to completely ignore the Labor Ministry; repeated failures there will significantly increase internal dissent. **How do I impact a party's ideologies and get certain paths? Is it RNG?** Nothing in Dynamic relies on RNG, aside from card draws. The Support for the Republic value plays a crucial role in determining party congress outcomes, particularly within the **DNVP**. The liberal parties, on the other hand, are primarily influenced by governmental actions—moving toward economic democracy and left-wing policies will push them rightward, while maintaining good relations and avoiding major socialist policies will bring them closer. Relations also matter significantly, making the negotiation skills of Müller and Braun highly valuable. **What happened to the WTB Plan?** Woytinsky only came up with the plan in late 1931 after the Banking Crisis, so to represent this, you need to get the event where Woytinsky proposes the concept in order to support it. The event is dynamic, and can trigger depending on factors such as: the state of the economy, deflation, labor faction strength, and most importantly internal party dissent. Appointing Woytinsky as an advisor aids significantly, as his presence passively increases the rate. **What is Dynamic Mode?** Dynamic mode is the intended way to play the mod, combining elements of both easy and historical modes. It reduces RNG with the shuffle leadership and card dismissal features of easy mode while retaining the starting variables of historical mode, such as relations and Reichsbanner strength. **How do I elect Stegerwald?** You will have to get Stegerwald as the leader of Prussia, either through Braun resigning, or having a right-wing coalition form. **How do I cross the rubicon?** Hindenburg needs to dismiss Chancellor Brüning following the 1932 Presidential elections. This unlocks Rubicon Mode, which remains active for the rest of the game. Since this is the historical sequence of events, you'll need to follow a similar political path, such as securing a Hugenberg-led **DNVP**, to have a better chance of unlocking it. **Why is the left path so hard?** Unlike Redux, this mod does not include any post–civil war content or additional **KPD** or revolutionary paths. This is primarily due to time constraints—by the time of release, the mod had already been in development for over 9 months. As a result, the only truly "viable" path is the Reformist one, given the immense difficulty of building socialism within a bourgeois democracy—especially with figures like Hindenburg as president and the hostility of the bourgeois parties. # for the angry redditors.... **Why can't I form a coalition with a moderate Christian-Socialist DNVP or KVP?** The Christian Socials of the DNVP, and the party as a whole, remain a racist and antisemitic party, though they are more willing to operate within a democratic framework. The "Christian Socialism" of Weimar Germany is not the Christian Socialism of today; a better comparison would be Austria’s Christian Social Party. It is a nationalist, corporatist, and deeply religious right-wing ideology. The KVP is still a strongly anti-Marxist and nationalistic party at heart, and it would be against everything they stand for to coalition with the socialists.
