presidential_election_1932_candidate.ges.bodyHtml: Otto Gessler, who served as Defense Minister for eight years following Noske’s departure and preceding Groener, is a conservative and a republican by reason rather than conviction—often at odds with his colleagues in the **DDP** throughout his tenure. He made little effort to reform the Reichswehr and played an active role in the Reichsexekution against our United Left governments in Saxony and Thuringia during the German October. Now, after stepping away from politics in early 1928, he seeks a return to the national stage. His candidacy is supported by the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?]. [? if not lvp_formed: He is also nominally supported by the **[+ ddp_name +]**, which has grown more right-wing and more accepting over the years. ?]

presidential_election_1932_candidate.gor.bodyHtml: The **NSDAP** has nominated Hermann Göring, who is expected to receive support solely from his own party. Normally, Hitler would have been their candidate, but for one reason or another, he is disqualified from the race. With his reputation as a decorated fighter ace from the Great War and his strong ties to the conservative establishment and industrial elites, Göring will win over some nationalists who might have otherwise been wary of Hitler. Still, Göring is widely expected to act as little more than a proxy, taking direction from the Nazi leader operating behind the scenes.

presidential_election_1932_candidate.hin.bodyHtml: President Hindenburg is, of course, running for re-election, and many in our party are prepared to support him as the last bastion of democracy against Hitler and the Nazis. The Hindenburg Mythos serves as a powerful rallying point for all parties, as he maintains high personal popularity despite everything Germany has endured. However, the more support he receives from the German left and center, the more Hindenburg views it as a stain on his personal honor. The refusal of August von Mackensen and other high-ranking officers with whom he served during the war to embrace his candidacy proved particularly painful to the Reich president. In response, he may shift further to the right after the election in an effort to restore his sense of honor and to appease his former comrades and friends on the German Right. This urge has only been reinforced by the Harzburg Front’s refusal to support him without concessions, as they see Hindenburg as the greatest obstacle to their rise to power.

We suspect that the Nazis are putting on a show of indecisiveness, and always had Hitler as as candidate in mind. ?][? if not hindenburg_run: Hitler is somewhat reluctant to run in the election, believing he cannot win outright. presidential_election_1932_candidate.run.bodyHtml: It takes effort to run a somewhat unexpected campaign. First, Braun has to be convinced to run. [? if hindenburg_run: He himself had supported voting for Hindenburg, and it takes a good deal of prodding to convince him of his destiny. ?][? if not hindenburg_run: It takes a good deal of prodding to convince him of his destiny. ?] [? if not lvp_formed: The [? if ddp_votes < 2: miniscule remnants of the?] [? if ddp_name == "DDP": **Democratic Party**?][? if ddp_name == "DStP": **State Party**?] aren't guaranteed to support us, [? if ddp_relation < 40: with a deterioration in our relationship?][? if ddp_relation >= 40: but are open to it due to their reluctance in supporting Hindenburg?]?][? if lvp_formed: The **LVP** aren't exactly the biggest fans of socialism, [? if lvp_relation < 40: with the deterioration in relations making their support a near impossibility.?][? if lvp_relation >= 40: but are at least open to it due to their reluctance in supporting Hindenburg?]?]. Who else will? Can we convince the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] to support Braun? What about the **Communists**?

It takes effort to launch a somewhat unexpected campaign. First, Eckener must be convinced to run. He isn't particularly eager to be the candidate of the socialists, as it would invite slander from the German Right—whom he feels a greater affinity with. With his status as a non-socialist—and even conservative—unity candidate, and his non-partisanship, Eckener is positioned to attract endorsements from a wide range of parties. However, much of this depends on their relationship with us, as our backing alone is enough to disgust many otherwise eager supporters. The [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]** and **DVP** are likely to back Eckener, although the **DVP** requires convincing. ?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP** is likely to back Eckener, although their industrial-right elements object to the arrangement. ?] The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is nominally supportive, although the **BVP** remains another problem. Finally, the **Communists**[? if left_split: and **SAPD**?] are firmly opposed to supporting a bourgeois conservative—for obvious reasons.

It takes effort to run a somewhat unexpected campaign. First, Rosenfeld has to be convinced to run. He isn't particularly eager to be promoted to the presidency from his lowly position in the party. His candidacy has severely limited our options for endorsements, but we can likely count on the support of the **KPD**[? if left_split: and **SAPD**?]. But who else? The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is likely hostile, and the liberals are irreconcilably opposed. Furthermore, many of our voters outside the working class have voiced objections to his candidacy and will not support him with much enthusiasm. Perhaps this will become the ultimate battle between the Marxist and bourgeois halves of the country.

presidential_election_1932_candidate.vor.titleHtml: Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, war hero of the Great War and [? if not cvp_formed: [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?]?][? if cvp_formed: **CVP**?] member.
presidential_election_1932_candidate.vor.bodyHtml: By some miracle for the German Right, they have managed to persuade Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck—renowned for his successful guerrilla campaign in German East Africa during the Great War—to run for the presidency. However, the circumstances now are far more dire than they were in 1925. The German Right is significantly less unified behind Lettow-Vorbeck than it had been for President Hindenburg. How Lettow-Vorbeck would govern remains uncertain. It is highly likely that, much like Hindenburg, a camarilla of close advisors would shape his decisions from behind the scenes. His candidacy is backed by the [? if not vorbeck_fallback: [? if not cvp_formed: [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?]?][? if cvp_formed: **CVP**?], along with a disparate coalition of minor bourgeois parties. ?][? if vorbeck_fallback: entirety of the Bürgerblock parties, who view him as their collective last hope at retaining power. ?]

presidential_election_1932_candidate.wes.titleHtml: Kuno von Westarp, [? if dnvp_leader != "Westarp": former?] leader of the **DNVP**, and an old friend of Hindenburg.
presidential_election_1932_candidate.wes.bodyHtml: Kuno von Westarp, a familiar figure in German politics, has long been a stalwart of the **DNVP**, once serving as both party leader and head of its parliamentary group. While not entirely opposed to his party’s participation in a republican system, he has made no secret of his monarchist aspirations. His rigid partisanship and staunchly anti-socialist convictions are likely to define his rule—perhaps even making him a more hostile figure than Hindenburg. It is imperative that we prevail over these forces of reaction if we are to have any hope of returning to government. His candidacy is backed by the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?], along with a disparate coalition of minor bourgeois parties.

presidential_election_1932_hindenburg.subtitleHtml: The President is to announce whether or not he will run again.
presidential_election_1932_hindenburg.bodyHtml: = Hindenburg's Announcement President Hindenburg has expressed his reluctance to run for re-election. At 84 years old, he prefers to spend his remaining years in retirement free from the burdens of his high office. While he has been open to serving longer if his term were extended by the Reichstag, the failure of those efforts, combined with his unwillingness to endure a grueling presidential campaign, has caused concern, particularly for Kurt von Schleicher[? if bruning_toleration_time: and Chancellor [+ chancellor +], on whom he depends to enact his decrees?]. Heinrich Sahm, the Mayor of Berlin, has formed a re-election committee to persuade Hindenburg to run again. This effort has included the collection of over [+ hindenburg_signatures +] million signatures and appeals from a wide array of figures and political parties across German society, including Artur Mahraun of the Young German Order, and controversial former Defense Ministers Otto Gessler and Gustav Noske. Impressed by the public support, Hindenburg is reconsidering his decision but insists that his candidacy must be backed by the German Right and veteran organizations rather than the German Left and Center. [? if not hitler_deported: Hitler?][? if hitler_deported: Goebbels?], Hugenberg, their parties, and the **Stahlhelm**—aligned with the national opposition—have demanded concessions in exchange for their support, despite the **Stahlhelm**'s general friendliness toward Hindenburg and its belief that he is one of their own. However, Hindenburg sees these demands as an affront to his personal honor and refuses to tie his candidacy to the dismissal of the current government or the appointment of Hugenberg and Hitler.

presidential_election_1932_hindenburg.hi.bodyHtml: President Hindenburg has decided not to run for re-election, citing his health problems and old age as the primary reasons. He feels that the current national situation doesn't warrant a reelection campaign. This development could be either beneficial or detrimental to us. If we wanted to rally behind Hindenburg to oppose Hitler and the Nazis, the absence of a unifying, widely supported national figure—one capable of garnering support from both the moderate left and right—leaves us at a disadvantage. On the other hand, if we decide to run a candidate of our own, the lack of someone with Hindenburg's charisma could make it easier for us to secure a victory. The absence of a candidate for the German middle and moderate right to rally behind creates a vacuum, which will likely be filled as other parties announce their candidates in the near future.

choices.labelHtml: Who will the candidates be now that Hindenburg is retiring?

presidential_election_1932_hindenburg.hi.bodyHtml: [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": The break of the **Stahlhelm** from the national opposition to endorse Hindenburg's candidacy, combined with the unconditional support of the Kyffhäuser League, has given Hindenburg the motivation to run for re-election. He is now convinced that his primary source of support will come from the right.?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": Despite Hindenburg rejecting the demands of the national opposition, he still (incorrectly) believes that the friendly leadership of the **Stahlhelm**, despite his rejection of their demands, would unconditionally support him. Together with the unconditional backing of the Kyffhäuser League, this has given Hindenburg the motivation to run for re-election, convinced his primary support would come from the right.?] Of course, a multitude of other factors contributed, including the signature campaign and Schleicher's persistence. The Sahm committee for Hindenburg's re-election has been dissolved and replaced by a much larger, national "United Hindenburg Committees" organization, which will work in coordination with the various local Hindenburg committees across the country. With the appointment of Westarp and Gereke to top positions, and the exclusion of socialist and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] politicians, they are attempting to position Hindenburg as the candidate of the moderate right.

presidential_election_1932_round_1.gessl.bodyHtml: Otto Gessler has made a comeback and won the presidency. Despite his[? if lvp_formed:  former?] affiliation with the **DDP**, he isn’t as friendly as his colleagues. However, he is a significant step up from Hindenburg. Let’s hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_1.give_.bodyHtml: Ironic, considering that seven years ago, we brokered a deal for Wilhelm Marx to resign in favor of Braun in exchange for our support for him in the presidential elections. Anyhow, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is now convinced to support Braun over Hindenburg. The Minister-President position is transferred to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]'s [+ prussia_leader +]. Hopefully, their support will outweigh the loss of popularity and internal dissent caused by the resignation of our most well-known figure.

presidential_election_1932_round_1.hinde.bodyHtml: As expected, the incumbent Hindenburg wins the presidency. Let's hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_1.hitle.bodyHtml: [? if nsdap_candidate_1932 == "Hitler" : Adolf Hitler of the **NSDAP** has won the presidency. He wastes no time in consolidating power. ?] [? if nsdap_candidate_1932 != "Hitler" : The **NSDAP** candidate [+ president +] has won. The first action President [+ president +] takes is inviting Hitler back into Germany, and appointing him chancellor. The Nazis waste no time in consolidating power. ?]

presidential_election_1932_round_1.jarre.bodyHtml: Perhaps surprisingly, Karl Jarres has made an unforeseen comeback and won the presidency. We hope that his governance will be an improvement over that of Hindenburg, and that he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_1.luthe.bodyHtml: From former Chancellor to President, Hans Luther has secured the presidency. Known for his technocratic beliefs, he's unlikely to rock the boat in either political direction. Let’s hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_1.no_ma.bodyHtml: There is no majority in this round. In the second round, any candidate who wins a plurality will win overall. What should we do? [? if dnvp_candidate_1932 == "Duesterberg": Due to [+ dnvp_candidate_1932 +]'s poor performance, he has withdrawn from the race and personally endorsed [? if reactionary_candidate_1_votes >= reactionary_candidate_2_votes: [+ reactionary_candidate_1932 +]?][? if reactionary_candidate_2_votes > reactionary_candidate_1_votes: [+ secondary_reactionary_candidate_1932 +]?]—despite widespread dislike of him among his supporters. Meanwhile, Hugenberg has urged his followers to abstain from the second round, drawing intense criticism from within his own party. How this will impact the runoff remains uncertain, but [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] is likely to capture a sizable share of these voters. ?][? if dnvp_candidate_1932 == "Hugenberg": Due to [+ dnvp_candidate_1932 +]'s poor performance, he has withdrawn from the race and urged his followers to abstain from the second round, drawing intense criticism from within his own party. How this will impact the runoff remains uncertain, but [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] is likely to capture a sizable share of these voters. ?] [? if hindenburg_confidence: Hindenburg has narrowly missed securing the required majority for a first-round victory, making his success in the runoff highly probable. With state and local elections just a month away, the industrialists and parties backing him have redirected their remaining campaign funds to those contests, confident that his victory is all but assured. This, however, presents a valuable opportunity for [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] to gain support among [+ dnvp_candidate_1932 +] voters and leverage their dominance in the presidential campaign to coincide with their local efforts. ?] [? if thalmann_votes < 15 and thalmann_votes: The **Communists** have suffered a demoralizing defeat, leaving many of their supporters disillusioned about the prospects of revolution—a future they once saw as inevitable given Germany’s current state. In the second round, many will abstain from voting altogether, while a small minority may even cast their ballots for [? if not spd_campaign: [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] ?][? if spd_campaign: [+ spd_candidate_1932 +] ?]in an effort to make their vote count. ?] [? if dnvp_candidate_1932: There had been discussions of Crown Prince Wilhelm running as a Harzburg unity candidate, a prospect the **NSDAP** showed interest in supporting. However, the **DNVP** and the **Stahlhelm** rejected the idea due to their hostility toward an accommodation with the **NSDAP**. The nail in the coffin was that his own father threatened to disinherit him if he stood for the "red republican presidential seat of an Ebert". He has since endorsed [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +]. ?] [? if hitler_support_hindenburg : In order to consolidate the vote for the right, and to prevent a socialist from becoming president, [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] is no longer running in the second round, and has switched his endorsement to Hindenburg. ?] [? if lib_drop_out_bourgeois : In order to consolidate the bourgeois electorate around a single candidate, [+ liberal_reactionary_candidate_1932_name +] has withdrawn from the race and endorsed [+ center_reactionary_candidate_1932_name +]. ?][? if z_drop_out_bourgeois : In order to consolidate the bourgeois electorate around a single candidate, [+ center_reactionary_candidate_1932_name +] has withdrawn from the race and endorsed [+ liberal_reactionary_candidate_1932_name +]. ?]

The disappointing performance of [+ dnvp_candidate_1932 +] has led the **Stahlhelm** to abandon its alliance with the **DNVP** and return to a stance of non-partisanship, blaming the party's lackluster support for their candidate for the poor showing. The shift of many right-wing organizations toward [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +]’s candidacy will cripple the parties caught between the Center and the extremes, polarizing the electorate between the Nazis and the Marxists—a strategy once championed by Hugenberg, now turned against him by his former ally. [? if not rlb_hindenburg: The RLB’s decision to endorse **[+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +]** rather than abstain has triggered a sharp break with the organization’s moderate affiliates. Their Württemberg branch, the **WBWB**, has been especially vocal, campaigning hard against the endorsement and in favor of [+ reactionary_candidate_1932 +]. Neither this backlash nor Hugenberg’s push for abstention has convinced the RLB to reverse course, and millions of rural voters are now expected to turn out for [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] in the next election. ?]

He is expected to pursue friendlier policies toward the **SPD** than Hindenburg did, and to provide a voice for the laborers of Germany. Let's hope he remains firm in keeping the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_1.thalm.bodyHtml: Ernst Thälmann of the **KPD** has won the presidency. Immediately, the far-right launches a coup attempt against the government. We have no choice but to unite with the **KPD** against the fascists...

presidential_election_1932_round_2.gessl.bodyHtml: Otto Gessler has made a comeback and won the presidency. Despite his[? if lvp_formed:  former?] affiliation with the **DDP**, he isn’t as friendly as his colleagues. However, he is a significant step up from Hindenburg. Let’s hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_2.hinde.bodyHtml: As expected, the incumbent Hindenburg wins the presidency. Let's hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power. [? if spd_support_reactionary and not bruning_time: The fact that, even with the votes from the socialists and Catholics, Hindenburg has failed to secure a majority in the first round has been a great embarrassment to him. Realizing that many of his former supporters have turned to Hitler, he is now shifting further to the right. ?] [? if spd_support_reactionary and bruning_time: The fact that [+ reactionary_candidate_1932 +] owed his reelection to the parties who opposed him in 1925 rather than those with whom he felt the closest natural affinity with is a source of great personal anguish to the aging president and severely strained his relations with Brüning and the conservatives who had orchestrated his reelection campaign. ?]

presidential_election_1932_round_2.hitle.bodyHtml: [? if nsdap_candidate_1932 == "Hitler" : Adolf Hitler of the **NSDAP** has won the presidency. He wastes no time in consolidating power. ?] [? if nsdap_candidate_1932 != "Hitler" : The **NSDAP** candidate [+ president +] has won. The first action President [+ president +] takes is inviting Hitler back into Germany, and appointing him chancellor. The Nazis waste no time in consolidating power. ?]

presidential_election_1932_round_2.jarre.bodyHtml: Perhaps surprisingly, Karl Jarres has made an unforeseen comeback and won the presidency. We hope that his governance will be an improvement over that of Hindenburg, and that he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_2.luthe.bodyHtml: From former Chancellor to President, Hans Luther has secured the presidency. Known for his technocratic beliefs, he's unlikely to rock the boat in either political direction. Let’s hope he continues to keep the Nazis out of power.

[? if spd_support_thalmann == 0 and kpd_support_spd == 0: Thälmann has also remained in the running, refusing to back what they view as the lesser evil.?] Following last month’s events, [+ dnvp_candidate_1932 +] has withdrawn from the race. His votes are expected to be [? if not hitler_support_hindenburg: split between [+ reactionary_candidate_1932 +][? if secondary_reactionary_candidate_1932:, [+ secondary_reactionary_candidate_1932 +]?] and [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +]?][? if hitler_support_hindenburg: redistributed to Hindenburg?]. presidential_election_1932_round_2.rosen.bodyHtml: Kurt Rosenfeld of the [? if not left_split: **SPD**?][? if left_split: **SAPD**?] has won the presidency! This is a moment of celebration for our party, and his victory is able to bolster our support. However, his leftism has sparked rumors of a planned "March on Berlin" by the **SA** and **Stahlhelm**, who see his election as tantamount to electing a **Communist**. Industrialists, equally displeased, may resort to protest through their own means.

presidential_election_1932_round_2.stege.bodyHtml: Adam Stegerwald has risen from union president to President of Germany. He is expected to pursue friendlier policies toward the **SPD** than Hindenburg did, and to provide a voice for the laborers of Germany. Let's hope he remains firm in keeping the Nazis out of power.

presidential_election_1932_round_2.thalm.bodyHtml: Ernst Thälmann of the **KPD** has won the presidency. Immediately, the far-right launches a coup attempt against the government. We have no choice but to unite with the **KPD** against the fascists...

presidential_election_1932_round_2.vorbe.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, a nationalist not far different from Hindenburg, has been elected president. A return to government under his leadership—his Camarilla certainly won’t allow it. Let’s hope he holds the line against the Nazis and abandons the dangerous taming strategy.

presidential_powers.subtitleHtml: The president can no longer dissolve the Reichstag at will, or call a Reichsexekution on state governments.
presidential_powers.bodyHtml: The wide-ranging presidential powers promised by the constitution are a potential gateway to authoritarianism. Thus, we can support reforms that limit the powers of the president, ending his power to unilaterally terminate an elected government and to remove state governments. The **KPD** is in favor of this reform, having been victims of the Reichsexekution in the past (when **KPD**-supported state governments in Thuringia and Saxony were removed). The democrats of the [? if not lvp_formed:**[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed:**LVP**?] also support this. [? if president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate": However, the opposition from conservatives is vehement, as they see a reduction in presidential powers as disrespectful to [+ president +]. ?] [? if z_relation <= 65 and (president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate") : Thus, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has been influenced to oppose these reforms[? if lvp_relation < 49 and (president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate") and lvp_formed: along with the majority of the **LVP**?][? if lvp_relation >= 49 and (president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate") and lvp_formed: however, the majority of the **LVP** is convinced somehow?]. ?] [? if z_relation > 65 and (president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate") : Despite this, the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] supports the proposed reform[? if lvp_relation < 49 and (president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate") and lvp_formed: however, the rightists in the **LVP** are unable to be convinced?][? if lvp_relation >= 49 and (president == "Hindenburg" or president_ideology == "Moderate") and lvp_formed: along with the majority of the **LVP**?]. ?] [? if president_ideology == "Left" : The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] supports this reform. ?]

choices.labelHtml: Call a constitutional referendum to pass the reform!

presidential_powers_2.bodyHtml: We have successfully passed a constitutional amendment to limit presidential powers! Hopefully this results in a less authoritarian Germany.

press_censorship.bodyHtml: With the powers Schleicher has handed to the new Ministry of National Guidance, fresh directives are now issued to editors, dictating what to print and what to suppress. It is censorship in all but name. Non-compliance brings swift consequences. We have already seen this unfold. The **DNEF** has been "acquiring" private newspapers and filling their offices with government loyalists, turning them into little more than state mouthpieces. Many other editors have been forced out of their posts—some for no reason other than being Jewish. [? if schleicher_spd_r >= 5: Schleicher, however, has been notably lenient with Vorwärts. Perhaps he is grateful for our past support—or perhaps he is simply waiting until we are too weak to resist. Collaboration, it seems, pays off? ?][? if schleicher_spd_influence >= 6 and schleicher_spd_r < 5: Using his growing influence over the **SPD**, Schleicher has even managed to install some of his own supporters to quietly "edit" the paper. It's jarring to see our supposed "newfound support" for rearmament—framed as a noble way to provide jobs—splashed across the front page. ?][? if schleicher_spd_influence < 6 and schleicher_spd_r < 5: It seems even our newspaper, Vorwärts, hasn't been spared from the crackdown. The offices are raided, staff arrested on dubious charges, and we can't even broadcast the truth for the workers to hear. ?] Stampfer hasn't been seen at his desk for some time now. Must be a long vacation.

pressure_drop.bodyHtml:
We have pressured the Justice Ministry to drop the case against the Weltbühne, raising tensions with our coalition.
The Western powers and all countries that feel threatened by German militarism are pleased that we have turned a chapter in our history. On the other hand, the Reichswehr disapproves of dropping the case.

prussia.subtitleHtml: Regain control over the Prussian police and secure participation in state government.
prussia.bodyHtml: Despite rejecting Braun’s offer a few months ago, Schleicher has since reconsidered. With such a popular statesman on his side, his rule will gain legitimacy in the eyes of the republicans and the public. Braun, in turn, will tirelessly advocate for a pro-Schleicher policy within the party. Now, with control over the democratic bulwark once again, we can reassert democratic oversight over the bureaucracy and the Prussian police force, reversing the purges enacted under Papen and Schleicher.

prussia_election_1928.great_popular_fron.bodyHtml: Somehow, the coalition is successfully formed! The conciliatory leadership of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and **KPD** helped make the negotiations possible. We still need a Minister-President; the only acceptable choice among the parties was[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. He is accepted with great reluctance to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and welcomed by the **KPD**.

prussia_election_1928.kpd_goals_prussia.bodyHtml: The **KPD** presents us with a list of demands for the Prussian coalition: [? if interior_goal_prussia >= 1 : - Ban the **SA** and **Stahlhelm**. ?] [? if rfb_goal_prussia = 1 : - Unban the **RFB**. ?] [? if bureaucracy_goal_prussia = 1 : - Purge the bureaucracy. ?] [? if free_kpd_goal_prussia = 1 : - Protect communist demonstrations. ?] They say that they expect to see these goals fulfilled in [+ kpd_ultimatum_prussia_timer +] months. Otherwise, they will vote to dissolve the coalition.

prussia_election_1928.left_coalition_pru.titleHtml: Is a United Left coalition possible?
prussia_election_1928.left_coalition_pru.subtitleHtml: **SPD** + **KPD** [? if sapd_formed: + **SAPD** ?] ([+ left_coalition_prussia +]%)
prussia_election_1928.left_coalition_pru.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the left coalition is successfully formed, without appointing a communist as Minister-President. The consensus choice for Minister-President, accepted by the **SPD**, **KPD**, is[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

prussia_election_1928.minority_grand_coa.bodyHtml: We have formed a minority coalition with the **SPD**, [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], [? if ddp_name == "DDP" and not lvp_formed: **Democratic**?][? if ddp_name == "DStP" and not lvp_formed: **State**?][? if lvp_formed: **Liberal People's**?] [? if not lvp_formed: (**[+ ddp_name +]**)?][? if lvp_formed: (**LVP**)?][? if not lvp_formed: , and **People's** (**DVP**)?] parties. However, there is a risk that the conservative establishment may call for a Reichsexekution against our government. The Grand Coalition parties have amended Landtag rules to require an absolute majority to elect a new Minister-President, enabling [+ prussia_leader +] to continue ruling as a caretaker government indefinitely. An attempt to repeal the change is unexpectedly blocked by the **KPD**, effectively making them a de facto tolerator of [+ prussia_leader +]. [? if far_right_coalition_prussia + z_r_prussia >= 50: Furthermore, the Center Party has engaged in delicate negotiations with the **NSDAP** over their potential entry into state government. prussia_election_1928.popular_front_2.bodyHtml: Somehow, both the **Communists** and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] are at the very least willing to entertain negotiations. Of course, **KPD** radicals and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] conservatives derail the negotiations almost immediately. The **KPD** demands leadership of the coalition for themselves, [? if spd_r_prussia > kpd_r_prussia : despite our higher vote share, ?]while the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is offended by the prospect of helping **Bolsheviks** enter government. Memories of the Reichsexekution against similar governments in Thuringia and Saxony remain vivid, standing as a cautionary tale. *Something* must be done to restore balance.

It seems like an absurd concept, but given our good relationships with both sides, it is not an impossibility. [? if president == "Hindenburg": Hindenburg might object to this, and may perform a Reichsexekution on our government, if such a coalition is formed.?]

prussia_election_1928.popular_front_succ.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the coalition is successfully formed! We still need a Minister-President; the only acceptable choice among the parties was [? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. He is accepted with great reluctance to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and welcomed by the **KPD**. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that the Popular Front government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, discrediting the left and center and eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. Our task is to prove them wrong. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

prussia_election_1928.schleicher_majorit.titleHtml: Schleicher forms a majority government with only the **DNEF**.
prussia_election_1928.schleicher_majorit.bodyHtml: With a majority in Prussia as well, Schleicher tightens his grip behind a democratic façade. The Prussian police are reshaped further to serve his purposes, and the government now sets education policy. A new curriculum is imposed, centered on discipline, nationalism, and hostility to socialism.

prussia_election_1928.schleicher_right_c.bodyHtml: Schleicher's preferred coalition is one with the right, cooperating with the hard line **DSU** to enact sweeping reforms to the education and policing system reformed under our years of rule. [+ prussia_leader +] has been selected as Minister-President of Prussia.

prussia_election_1928.social_christian_c.titleHtml: Can we form a Social-Christian Coalition?
prussia_election_1928.social_christian_c.bodyHtml: We have secured enough votes to form a "Social-Christian Coalition" government, bringing together the **SPD** and the **CVP**. Unexpectedly, thanks to our good relations and the relatively favorable leadership of the **[+ z_party_name +]**, we have successfully convinced them to join the coalition in Prussia—a region where the left wing of the Center has historically held significant influence. [? if prussia_leader != "Braun": [+ prussia_leader +] has been selected as Minister-President of Prussia.?]

prussia_election_1928.spd_majority.bodyHtml: Finally, the **SPD** can govern alone! Our long campaign of electioneering has paid off. We do not need to worry about coalition government; anything is possible. However, our former coalition partners are going to start drifting to the right. Braun is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia.

prussia_election_1928.tolerate_bourgeois.titleHtml: We must tolerate a bourgeois coalition.
prussia_election_1928.tolerate_bourgeois.bodyHtml: We have decided to tolerate a broad bourgeois government. This means that we will vote against no-confidence votes to make sure they fail, but also that we will not be directly participating as ministers in the government. prussia_reichsexekution_popular.subtitleHtml: The President attempts to overthrow the Prussian government.
prussia_reichsexekution_popular.bodyHtml: = Coup in Prussia A crisis! President [+ president +] has invoked the Reichsexekution to dismiss the Prussian government, citing its "inability to maintain order" amidst escalating clashes between the **SA**, Reichsbanner, and the increasingly militant **RFB**. However, the true motivation is clear: the left-wing coalition governing Prussia poses a direct threat to the conservative and nationalist establishment in Germany. The legality of this action remains highly questionable. The left-wing coalition has vowed to resist, while the streets are descending into chaos with mass protests and rising political violence.

prussia_reichsexekution_popular.defend.subtitleHtml: Labor will call a general strike. The Reichsbanner and the loyal elements of the Prussian police will resist the coup. The **KPD** remains unwavering in its support.
prussia_reichsexekution_popular.defend.bodyHtml: The Reichswehr and **Stahlhelm** are already surrounding Berlin, and the **SA** is supporting them. This could be civil war. We do realize that, correct?

choices.labelHtml: We will fight, even if it leads to a civil war.

prussia_v_reich.subtitleHtml: Oral proceedings begin in the legal challenge against Papen’s Reichsexekution.
prussia_v_reich.bodyHtml: = Prussia v. Reich The time has finally come for us, along with the Center Party, and the state governments of Bavaria and Baden, to argue for the unconstitutionality of the Prussian Reichsexekution. However, the leader of the state court, and president of the supreme court, is Erwin Bumke, a known reactionary and former **DNVP** member before taking his job. The main conditions under examination are whether the Prussian government failed to fulfill its constitutional obligations in maintaining public order and security, and whether the federal government had the constitutional right to intervene and appoint a Reich Commissioner to take over governance in Prussia indefinitely.

prussia_v_reich.papen.bodyHtml: The State Court has ruled that the Prussian government did not fail in its duties, meaning the use of force against a state refusing to follow the constitution was unlawful and the application of the Reichsexekution was unjustified. However, the court did affirm that the government could still appoint a Reich Commissioner and temporarily assume control of Prussia due to a perceived threat to public safety and order. Additionally, the court declared that the dismissal of the Prussian government was illegal and that Prussia’s representation in the Reichsrat must be restored. While acknowledging that the Prussian government remains legally intact, the judicial system’s reactionary nature meant that no practical change was enforced. The court’s ruling did not explicitly demand the reinstatement of the Prussian government, and the [+ chancellor +] government has ignored the decision. Holding the government accountable for this violation would require accusing President Hindenburg of breaching the law by signing the decree—an action the conservative judges find politically unacceptable.

The court has ordered the federal government to relinquish control over Prussia's ministries and to restore its representation in the Reichsrat. Papen complies with the ruling and reinstates the Prussian government under [+ prussia_leader +]. Unfortunately, they remain powerless against Hindenburg and Papen, who signed the decree in the first place.

prussian_affairs_dvp.bureaucracy.bodyHtml: The bureaucracy is deeply reactionary, and many abuse their power to favor the political right. By removing the pro-monarchy and pro-dictatorship elements, we can democratize it. Some of our opponents claim that we are infringing on individual freedoms, but perhaps the security of the republic requires it. The **DVP** fills up the bureaucracy with their own monarchist and industrialist sympathizers.

prussian_affairs_dvp.police_loyalty.bodyHtml: The police have historically been overrun with reactionaries, and we are trying to change this, little by little. We have improved the training and recruitment process to select for a broader demographic than the traditional conservatives, and to put a tighter leash on their political activity. In addition, we set up committees to investigate the ranks of the police and remove those with far-right sympathies. It is a slow and arduous work. The **DVP** is sabotaging against our efforts in favor for the right. Current police loyalty: [+ prussian_police_loyalty : loyalty +].

prussian_affairs_dvp.police_strength.bodyHtml: We have increased the size of the Prussian police.

prussian_affairs_dvp.prosecute_sa.bodyHtml: While an outright ban on the **SA** may be out of reach, we can make life as difficult as possible for the Storm Troopers. The most reckless among them can be prosecuted on charges of murder and related crimes, and we can ensure legal public demonstrations and meetings are protected from their unlawful disruptions.

prussian_affairs_majority.bodyHtml:
#subtitle: The state government of Prussia is a bulwark of democracy...
= Prussian Affairs
Prussia, by far the largest and most important state in Germany, is governed solely by our party, free from the compromises demanded by the bourgeois parties. This grants us the opportunity to pursue meaningful reforms. Under the capable leadership of Otto Braun, Prussia stands as the most stable and democratic government in the Republic.
All our actions have increased effectiveness. 
We can enact policies in Prussia.

In addition, we set up committees to investigate the ranks of the police and remove those with far-right sympathies. It is a slow and arduous work. Current police loyalty: [+ prussian_police_loyalty : loyalty +].

prussian_affairs_majority.police_strengt.bodyHtml: We have increased the size of the Prussian police.

prussian_affairs_majority.prosecute_sa.bodyHtml: While an outright ban on the **SA** may be out of reach, we can make life as difficult as possible for the Storm Troopers. The most reckless among them can be prosecuted on charges of murder and related crimes, and we can ensure legal public demonstrations and meetings are protected from their unlawful disruptions.

prussian_affairs.ban_rfb.bodyHtml: The ban is enthusiastically carried out by the police, perhaps too enthusiastically. The Communists take this as one more reason why the Socialists are traitors to the left. However, the moderate and center-right parties approve, as do the police.

prussian_affairs.ban_sa.bodyHtml: As it turns out, the Nazi **SA** has many allies in the police and bureaucracy. Our relationship with the police weakens, and the **SA** can still organize illegally, right under the police's noses. [? if sa_banned_pro : Nevertheless, the **SA** is substantially weakened by our ban. ?] [? if coup_progress >= 6: There are reports of an imminent coup by the far-right. We have disrupted some of these plans, but the threat is still present. ?]

By removing the pro-monarchy and pro-dictatorship elements, we can democratize it. Some of our opponents claim that we are infringing on individual freedoms, but perhaps the security of the republic requires it.

Hermann Göring is elevated to the position of Minister-President and immediately starts dismantling its democratic institutions. A wave of terror and repression unfolds, targeting the socialists and communists. Violence erupts in the streets, with bullets flying and leftists being killed or imprisoned.

The Minister-President position is transferred to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]'s [+ prussia_leader +].

prussian_coalition_formation.left_coalit.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the left coalition is successfully formed, without appointing a communist as Minister-President. The consensus choice for Minister-President, accepted by the **SPD**, **KPD**, is[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

However, there is a risk that the conservative establishment may call for a Reichsexekution against our government. The Grand Coalition parties have amended Landtag rules to require an absolute majority to elect a new Minister-President, enabling [+ prussia_leader +] to continue ruling as a caretaker government indefinitely. An attempt to repeal the change is unexpectedly blocked by the **KPD**, effectively making them a de facto tolerator of [+ prussia_leader +]. [? if far_right_coalition_prussia + z_r_prussia >= 50: Furthermore, the Center Party has engaged in delicate negotiations with the **NSDAP** over their potential entry into state government. However, despite being an enticing offer, it remains unlikely they would enter without also securing federal participation, as well as control over the Minister-President’s office and the Prussian police—demands the Center will never accept. ?]?] [? if prussia_leader != "Braun": [+ prussia_leader +] is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia. ?]

Of course, **KPD** radicals and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] conservatives derail the negotiations almost immediately. The **KPD** demands leadership of the coalition for themselves, [? if spd_r_prussia > kpd_r_prussia : despite our higher vote share, ?]while the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is offended by the prospect of helping **Bolsheviks** enter government. Memories of the Reichsexekution against similar governments in Thuringia and Saxony remain vivid, standing as a cautionary tale. *Something* must be done to restore balance.

params.source: popular_front_success

prussian_coalition_formation.popular_fro.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the coalition is successfully formed! We still need a Minister-President; the only acceptable choice among the parties was [? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work. He is accepted with great reluctance to the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and welcomed by the **KPD**. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that the Popular Front government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, discrediting the left and center and eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. Our task is to prove them wrong. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

prussian_concordat.subtitleHtml: The Prussian government has reached an agreement with the Vatican.
prussian_concordat.bodyHtml: = Prussian Concordat Despite our Otto Braun losing his position as the Minister-President of Prussia, he still possesses great influence within state politics and together with Center Party members, have negotiated a concordat with the Vatican.

choices.labelHtml: The Prussian government shall sign the concordat.

prussian_concordat.sign_concordat.bodyHtml: We have signed a Concordat between the Free State of Prussia and the Roman Catholic Church, guaranteeing religious freedom for Catholics in Prussia. This sets the stage for the negotiation of a national Concordat covering all of Germany. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": The Catholic members of the **DNVP** in Prussia are in open conflict with their leadership over the vote, with many leaving the party. ?]

prussian_coup.subtitleHtml: The Chancellor attempts to overthrow the Prussian government.
prussian_coup.bodyHtml: = Coup in Prussia A crisis! Chancellor [+ chancellor +] has ordered the dismissal of the Prussian government through a procedure known as the Reichsexekution. He claims the state government can no longer maintain order amid escalating street battles between the **SA**, Reichsbanner, and other paramilitary groups—despite his own administration having legalized them. [? if not altona_good: The recent clashes in Altona have handed him the pretext to depose the Prussian government?][? if altona_good: The surge in politically motivated violence has given Papen the pretext to depose the Prussian government?]. [? if prussia_leader == "Braun": With Otto Braun still abroad on convalescent leave following the heartbreaking events of the past few months?][? if prussia_leader != "Braun": With Minister-President [+ prussia_leader +] unwilling to risk a civil war to defend his administration?], Papen is moving to seize control. If this coup is successful, Papen will transfer control of Prussia to a reactionary Reichskommissar, a calculated move to win over the **NSDAP** by granting the **SA** free rein in the state. We suspect Defense Minister Schleicher to be the mastermind behind this scheme—another step in advancing his taming strategy. The legality of this action is dubious. Severing has responded that he'll only yield to force. Many of our members are prepared to resist.

prussian_coup_goerdeler.subtitleHtml: Goerdeler resigns the position to Papen.
prussian_coup_goerdeler.bodyHtml: = New State Consolidation Goerdeler, the Reichskommissar of Prussia, has announced his resignation in favor of Chancellor Papen, likely under pressure from both the chancellor and Schleicher as they move to consolidate power into the chancellery. Goerdeler, ever the conservative, sympathizes with these goals and steps down before Hindenburg can force the issue. It is clear this is part of Papen’s wider plan for a "New State"—a centralized, anti-democratic regime ruled by aristocrats and the rich. The upcoming Prussian elections have now been postponed indefinitely.

prussian_coup_schleicher.bodyHtml: #tags: event = Coup in Prussia President Hindenburg and Chancellor Schleicher have grown fed up with the political deadlock in Prussia and move to dismiss its government, replacing it with a Reichskommissar—likely one of their allies or another reactionary figure. The move carries plausible justification, with Hindenburg citing Prussia's "ungovernable" state, brought on by repeated failures to form a stable government and escalating clashes between state forces and paramilitaries in these troubled times.

prussian_coup.defend_2_civil_war.bodyHtml: Our forces confront the government troops and their supporters on the streets of Berlin, and armed fighting erupts. The reactionaries do not budge from their positions. We are caught at a disadvantage.

prussian_coup.defend_2_victory.bodyHtml: Our forces confront the government troops and their reactionary auxiliaries on their way to seize government offices, and somehow, our enemies retreat without a fight! They were overwhelmed by our display of strength, and have chosen to slink away. Chancellor [+ chancellor +] withdraws the dismissal of the Prussian government, at least for now. The show of force has reinvigorated support for the republic and for the **SPD**, and has weakened the fascists. It’s anticipated that Chancellor Papen will either resign or be deposed by the Camarilla for his embarrassing failure, as Hindenburg’s confidence in him has been utterly shattered.

prussian_coup.surrender.titleHtml: Give up on the Prussian government.
prussian_coup.surrender.subtitleHtml: We will attempt to fight this out legally.
prussian_coup.surrender.bodyHtml: On the morning of the coup, the decree is presented to the Prussian government. Despite fierce objections to its constitutionality—and Severing’s vow to yield only to force—a hundred thousand Reichswehr troops occupy key government buildings in Berlin. One by one, Severing and the police chiefs allow themselves to be removed without resistance. A pall of hopelessness and despair descends over Social Democracy. We have failed. Many in the Reichsbanner simply quit, demoralized by their leaders' lack of a call to action. President Hindenburg appoints the reactionary Franz von Papen as Reichskommissar of Prussia, tasked with dismantling the democratic structures we fought to preserve. This furthers Papen’s ambition for a “New State”—one that unites the chancellorship and the Prussian premiership under a single authoritarian hand.

raise_tariffs.subtitleHtml: +2 budget. Other countries will retaliate by increasing tariffs of their own. [? if tariffs > 5 : Further increases in tariffs will not raise revenue, as we have already nearly reached economic autarky. ?]
raise_tariffs.bodyHtml:
Increasing tariffs leads to higher prices for basic goods, increasing inflation and hurting consumption among the working class. Retaliatory tariffs reduce the competitiveness of German exports, raising unemployment among workers. They also lead to an atmosphere of international suspicion, reducing our ability to negotiate with other countries.
On the other hand, agricultural producers and some small businesses benefit from higher tariffs, as farmers can now command higher prices for grain, and formerly uncompetitive businesses are now able to function.

raumer.subtitleHtml: Backed by manu prominent industrialists from the **DVP**, von Raumer aims to strengthen the bourgiois.
raumer.bodyHtml: After several rounds of elimination voting at the **FKP**’s inaugural congress, Hans von Raumer secured the chairmanship by consolidating the party’s pro‑business wing. The moderate Frank Glatzel was the first to fall in the competition. In the penultimate round, Gottfried Treviranus withdrew and threw his support behind von Raumer, rather than the hard‑line monarchists. Industrialists and big‑business delegates, long allied with von Raumer, rallied en masse, joined by former **DVP** deputies and even some trade unionists, giving him a decisive edge over Kuno von Westarp in the final ballot. This represents an interesting development for us. While von Raumer is firmly linked to the industrialist wing of **FKP**, he has demonstrated firm support for Grand Coalitions in previous governments. He even has a good working relationship with Rudolf Hilferding. However, he would still be active in trying to limit our policies in any future government. Additionally, many of his own supporters in the industrialist wing would seek to prevent any coalition with us, so cooperation will still be more difficult than it was with Stresemann's **DVP**.

rb.bodyHtml: We have increased recruiting to the Reichsbanner.

rb_explode.bodyHtml: We have decided to cooperate with the government by preemptively dissolving the organization and turning over weapons before the ban is to take place. A notable amount of socialists have decided to fight on however, but without numbers or weapons, this ad-hoc group is destined for failure. Schleicher hasn't expressed the gratitude for our cooperation like we hoped. Perhaps we outlived our usefulness to him.

red_general.cabinet_reshuffle.titleHtml: Demand a reshuffle of the cabinet.
red_general.cabinet_reshuffle.subtitleHtml: Schleicher’s cabinet remains dominated by deeply reactionary holdovers from the Papen cabinet of barons.
red_general.cabinet_reshuffle.bodyHtml: Although many reactionary figures in the cabinet have already been replaced by Center Party appointees, further reform is needed to nudge Schleicher’s government toward a more democratic appearance. The Finance Ministry, previously held by Schwerin von Krosigk, is handed over to a more neutral, non-partisan banker. The Interior Ministry and the Minister without Portfolio post are assigned to the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?] moderate, Gottfried Treviranus. The Agricultural Ministry is granted to Hans Schlange-Schöningen, a [? if not kvp_formed and dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **CNBLP**?][? if kvp_formed: **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?] agrarian in support of peasant homesteads. Though these shifts may seem minor on the surface, the entry of more democratic-leaning ministers into the cabinet makes our continued support more palatable to both the party and our electorate—and subtly shifts the balance in key cabinet votes.

red_general.concessions.subtitleHtml: There's a limit to what we can demand, but we can look at our options.
red_general.concessions.bodyHtml: [? if prussia_leader == "Schleicher": Braun demands the restoration of his government in Prussia. ?] Labor demands the restoration of their rights and welfare. The **SPD** a cabinet reshuffle. We may only demand one, as to not push our luck.

red_general.convince_spd_schleicher.subtitleHtml: [? if chancellor == "Papen": It's almost impossible to argue to the party to pursue this line, at least with Papen as chancellor. ?][? if chancellor == "Schleicher": Cooperation with the General himself is not unthinkable, with his concessions made toward the unions. ?]
red_general.convince_spd_schleicher.bodyHtml: Slowly but surely, the ADGB leadership is beginning to warm to the idea of constructive cooperation with the so-called "Red General." However, much work remains to be done—many within the union, and the overwhelming majority of the **SPD**, remain firmly opposed to cooperating with the man [? if chancellor == "Papen": propping up the widely despised Papen cabinet?][? if chancellor == "Schleicher": who now heads a widely unpopular government?]. [? if wtb_adopted: Our adoption of the WTB Plan—and Schleicher’s public support for similar public works initiatives—has modestly increased the party’s willingness to consider cooperation. ?] [? if otl_prussian_coup_seen: Furthermore, his role in the coup against our Prussian government has only deepened the animosity toward both him and the **SPD**. ?] Rumors about our cooperation has damaged our standing among the working class.

red_general.labor.titleHtml: Demand more concessions for the trade unions, and restoration of the German welfare system.
red_general.labor.subtitleHtml: Push for higher wages, the repeal of Papen’s decrees, and the restoration of the eight-hour workday.
red_general.labor.bodyHtml: The Social General has lived up to his nickname: the means test for unemployment insurance has been abolished, and an eight-hour workday has been reinstated in select industries to "spread out" the work among more people. Funding for the Labor Ministry, gutted under Papen, has been restored, and welfare levels are climbing back from their absolute lows. The downside is clear—Schleicher now holds significant leverage over the unions, and many workers are beginning to place their loyalty in the chancellor, rather than the party that fought to make this possible.

red_general.prussia.titleHtml: Demand the reinstatement of our government in Prussia.
red_general.prussia.subtitleHtml: Regain control over the Prussian police and secure participation in state government.
red_general.prussia.bodyHtml: Despite rejecting Braun’s offer a few months ago, Schleicher has since reconsidered. With such a popular statesman on his side, his rule will gain legitimacy in the eyes of the republicans and the public. Braun, in turn, will tirelessly advocate for a pro-Schleicher policy within the party. Now, with control over the democratic bulwark once again, we can reassert democratic oversight over the bureaucracy and the Prussian police force, reversing the purges enacted under Papen and Schleicher.

Push the party toward a more cooperative line with von Schleicher.
Reiterate our opposition against the reactionaries.
Reiterate our opposition against the reactionaries.

red_general.schleicher_ties.subtitleHtml: More regular meetings will be held between the two groups.
red_general.schleicher_ties.bodyHtml: Regular secret meetings between the ADGB, the **SPD**, and von Schleicher are being held. This will aid in reducing the mutual distrust between the party and the government.

red_general.spd_schleicher_adopted.subtitleHtml: The unions have firmly decided, but convincing the party is a whole another matter.
red_general.spd_schleicher_adopted.bodyHtml: The ADGB leadership has now officially—although only in private—taken a stance in favor of cooperating with the "Red General." The union will attempt to leverage its influence over the **SPD** to push our hesitant party leadership toward adopting the same position. Gradually, a shift in opinion is becoming visible within the party. Otto Braun has now come out in support of making deals with the General.

reduce.bodyHtml: We do not need the international contacts at the moment.

reduce_reparations.titleHtml: The Western Allies are finally willing to pause our reparations payments!
reduce_reparations.bodyHtml: Finally, given both the economic circumstances and our continued negotiations, the Western Allies are willing to pause our reparations payments! Much of the credit must go to Western president Hoover, who has been friendlier towards us than the Europeans. This has reduced tensions within our government, and our party has gotten credit for the achievement.

reformist_leaders_resign.subtitleHtml: Reformist disagreements with our policies have grown too severe.
reformist_leaders_resign.bodyHtml:
= Reformist leaders resign
Our policy choices have greatly offended the reformist faction. Many of our most experienced leaders have resigned.

reformist_plan.bodyHtml: Job creation and stimulus are necessary, but deficit spending, especially with hyperinflation still fresh in memory, is simply unrealistic and reckless. The reformists argue that this plan is most likely to receive support from the bourgeois parties and is the most practical in the immediate term. Opponents in the Left and Labor factions criticize the plan for being inadequate in its ambition.

regressive.titleHtml: Lower taxes on the rich, while increasing consumption taxes (which affect the working class more).
regressive.subtitleHtml: This does not change overall revenue. [? if upper_tax_rates < -5 : Rich tax rates are too low to cut anymore. ?] [? if lower_tax_rates > 5 : Lower-class tax rates are too high to increase. ?]

reichsbank_dreyse.bodyHtml:
The Reichsbank, long known for its strict fiscal conservatism and obsessive anti-inflation stance, had already slashed Schleicher's initial public works decree by 15%. So, it was no surprise when news of even greater government spending met with their disapproval.
However, the endorsement of the campaign by Hjalmar Schacht—a respected banker and recently retired Reichsbank President credited with ending hyperinflation—has done much to calm the business community. Under government pressure, the Reichsbank is ultimately coerced into backing the plan, though not without forcing another 20% cut in funding.

reichsbanner.bodyHtml: #subtitle: Paramilitary organizing in defense of the republic. = Reichsbanner The *Reichsbanner* Schwarz-Rot-Gold is a mass organization for the defense of the Republic against the extremists who threaten it. Some would call it a paramilitary, although currently it is hardly any sort of military. It is officially associated with the pro-democratic parties -the **SPD**, [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], and **[+ ddp_name +]**, but by far the largest component is with the **SPD**. [? if workers_spd < 46 or workers_spd < workers_nsdap or workers_spd < workers_kpd : The Reichsbanner is having a more difficult time recruiting, as the **SPD** is no longer the dominant party among the workers. Many of its members have left. ?] #- Orient reichsbanner towards anti-fascism (only available if we have prioritized anti fascism)

reichsbanner_cvp.titleHtml: The **[+ z_party_name +]** Disaffiliates with the Reichsbanner
reichsbanner_cvp.subtitleHtml: Expectedly, the Christians have left the republican organization.
reichsbanner_cvp.bodyHtml: = The **[+ z_party_name +]** disaffiliates with the Reichsbanner The merger between the Catholics and the nationalists has compelled them to disaffiliate from the Reichsbanner, for obvious reasons. A small group from the Christian Left has remained in the organization, including figures like former Chancellor Joseph Wirth, who has defied orders to resign from the party’s leadership. It is expected that he will leave the party in the near future. In the meantime, the party is debating its stance on ties with the **Stahlhelm**, who are now awkwardly sandwiched between Hugenberg’s **DNF** and the Christians.

reichsbanner_cvp.let_go.bodyHtml: Despite the vigorous protest from the Christian Left faction, and the refusal of ardent republicans like Wirth to leave, this has dealt a significant blow to the organization. With the Christians gone, the Reichsbanner, in the public's eye, is nothing more than a socialist militia. The **Stahlhelm** has reaffirmed political neutrality, but leans closer to the more politically successful **[+ z_party_name +]**.

reichsbanner_cvp.wirth_retire.bodyHtml: Wirth, long a thorn in the side of the former Center due to his leftist leanings, has now left its more right-wing successor. He had considered joining the **SPD**, but our Marxist course ultimately alienated him from that path. He has since retired from party politics and now focuses on chairing various republican and Catholic organizations. Unfortunately, this remains a lone defection. The Christian Left faction has largely stayed within the [+ z_party_name +], where they wield little actual power and function more as a pressure group than a meaningful political force.

reichsbanner_cvp.wirth_spd.bodyHtml: Wirth, who has always been a close friend of the **SPD**—and who likely would have joined us long ago were it not for our Marxist foundations—has officially defected to the **SPD**! He’s done this before as a temporary protest against his party’s right wing, but this time, it looks like he’s here to stay. Our reformist party platform played a major role in overcoming his earlier hesitation. Unfortunately, this seems to be a lone defection. The Christian Left faction has largely remained within the **[+ z_party_name +]**, where they hold little real power and operate more as a pressure group than an influential bloc. [? if neorevisionism: Joseph Wirth has joined the Neorevisionist faction, owing to his impassioned support of the Weimar Republic. ?]

reichsbanner_lvp.subtitleHtml: Due to its militarization, the liberals are leaving the Reichsbanner.
reichsbanner_lvp.bodyHtml: = The **LVP** and the Reichsbanner The Reichsbanner has increasingly militarized, acquiring arms, conducting paramilitary training, and attracting a stream of radicalized **SPD** members. The **LVP** in particular is offended by this, as many of its members originate from the semi-monarchist **DVP** and even have **Stahlhelm** memberships. The organization's militarization has provided them with a pretext to sever formal ties with this republican organization.

reichsbanner_lvp.keep_them.bodyHtml: Seeing the strife that has filled Germany's streets, the **LVP** seem to be convinced that it is necessary for the Reichsbanner to be militarized, and will not leave the organization. Unfortunately, many die-hard **Stahlhelm** members within the party are constantly pressing for a reversal of this policy.

reichsbanner_lvp.let_go.bodyHtml: We have judged that the Reichsbanner's militancy is more important than maintaining a coalition with the **LVP**. reichsbanner_massive.bodyHtml: = Excessive Militarization of the Reichsbanner The argument that the militarization of the Reichsbanner is necessary to defend against the far-right **SA** and **Stahlhelm** no longer holds, given our dominance of the streets. With the threat now eliminated, the bourgeois parties fear it may instead function as a socialist militia. [? if not rb_exit: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] [? if not lvp_formed:and **[+ ddp_name +]** ?][? if not lvp_leave_reichsbanner and lvp_formed:and **LVP** ?]have threatened drastic consequences if the Reichsbanner isn't disarmed.?] [? if rb_exit and not cvp_formed: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?][? if not lvp_formed: and **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if not lvp_leave_reichsbanner and lvp_formed: and **LVP**?] have condemned the organization as nothing more than a socialist militia and have abandoned their strong opposition to the **Stahlhelm**.?][? if (rb_exit or cvp_leave_reichsbanner) and cvp_formed: The **CVP** [? if not lvp_formed: and **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if not lvp_leave_reichsbanner and lvp_formed: and **LVP**?] have condemned the organization as nothing more than a socialist militia and are getting noticeably friendly with the **Stahlhelm**.?] If no action is taken, we risk permanently alienating the bourgeois parties.

choices.labelHtml: Refuse to take any action, keeping the Reichsbanner the way it is.
We must lower the Reichsbanner's militancy.

reichsbanner_massive.let_go.subtitleHtml: The Reichsbanner is still needed, as the police cannot be trusted to do their job. [? if president == "Hindenburg" and spd_in_government: Hindenburg has threatened to sack our government if no action is taken. ?][? if spd_in_government and not in_left_front and not in_spd_majority: Our coalition partners will call a vote of no confidence. ?] The bourgeois parties will be forever antagonistic.
reichsbanner_massive.let_go.bodyHtml: We must not let our guard down; the Reichsbanner must remain militarized. Whether they like it or not, paramilitaries are here to stay. Unfortunately, the bourgeois parties[? if president == "Hindenburg":, and especially President Hindenburg?] now plainly see the Reichsbanner for what it is: our socialist militia. Non-socialist members of the paramilitary leave en masse, and the political establishment will be forever antagonistic to us.

reichskonkordat.titleHtml: What will happen to the Center Party?
reichskonkordat.bodyHtml: = Center Party Conference Having achieved his lifelong goal, Kaas sees little reason to remain as leader of the Center Party—a position he had long described as a burden and expressed displeasure with. As a result, a new leadership race is set to take place within the party, with Schleicher able to influence the outcome through his connections with Kaas and the Christian Trade Unions. The candidate backed by the Christian unions and those advocating for a more interconfessional Center Party rallies around Stegerwald. Franz Bracht, Schleicher's [? if not dsu_in_gov: former ?]Interior Minister[? if prussia_coup_lose: of Prussia and the Reich?], has rejoined the party and is Schleicher’s preferred candidate. Bracht is a true believer in Schleicher's vision for a new Germany—one less entangled in parliamentarianism—and aligns with the Center's right wing, though not as far right as Papen. However, due to his lack of influence within the party and limited prior experience, having served only as Mayor of Essen for eight years, it is Schleicher's backing that remains the key to elevating him to leadership.

reichstag.titleHtml: A vote of no confidence is introduced against Schleicher.
reichstag.bodyHtml:
It succeeds.
New Reichstag elections are scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +], Week [+ next_election_week +].

reichstag_1.bodyHtml: As expected, the objections raised by Schleicher’s spokesman—acting on direct orders—have sunk the Nazi motion. In response, the Center Party has introduced a compromise: a one-week extension of the recess to allow for further negotiations. Papen’s scheme has become considerably easier, as Schleicher is now forced to test the President’s support by requesting a decree to dissolve the Reichstag and postpone elections. But if Hindenburg denies the request, the question becomes unavoidable: who would succeed him? Papen? Hitler? Schleicher has squandered a critical opportunity to salvage his cabinet—and perhaps Germany itself. Had the elections been postponed just a few months, his position would likely have improved significantly. He stood to gain from the launch of Gereke’s public works program and the natural recovery of the global economy. Meanwhile, the Nazis, with no upcoming state elections to boost morale, would have been increasingly vulnerable to internal collapse—driven by mounting dissatisfaction with [+ nsdap_leader +] and the disintegration of the **SA**. None of this is to be.

reichstag_1_alt.bodyHtml: As expected, the **Communists** have attempted to secure approval for a change in the order of business to allow an immediate vote on a motion of no confidence against Papen, but however, the [? if dnvp_papen: **DNVP**?][? if not dnvp_papen and dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF**?][? if not dnvp_papen and dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?] had objected to the motion, delaying it. Before the vote was to begin, Chancellor von Papen has arrived inside the Reichstag to present his emergency decree to the chamber, one to dissolve it and one to postpone future elections. He had placed the folder on Reichstag President [? if reichstag_president == "Göring": Hermann Göring?][? if reichstag_president == "Löbe": Paul Löbe?][? if reichstag_president == "Eßer": Thomas Eßer?]'s desk, who read it to the floor. The chamber erupted in uproar, prompting police on standby to detain numerous Reichstag members involved in the violence, primarily from the **Communists**. News has quickly spread, and Papen has only narrowly escaped from the area before violent mobs assembled all across Berlin were formed to protest the violation of the constitution. Brüning and the Center Party vow to impeach President Hindenburg, if the Reichstag ever convenes. Germany's in for a violent civil war, and Papen shows no sign of backing down.

reichstag_2.bodyHtml:
[? if not schleicher_economy_time: However, Schleicher, having learned about Frick's plans to delay the Reichstag's reconvocation, has had a sudden change of heart. A new round of war games—this time not rigged—has revealed that the Reichswehr cannot survive fighting against all paramilitaries[? if prussia_leader == "Schleicher":, even with the Prussian police?][? if prussia_leader != "Schleicher":, and the Prussian police force as well?]. Despite his efforts to strengthen the army with streetfighting equipment and training, the limited but well-trained force remains unable to withstand being heavily outnumbered. ?][? if schleicher_economy_time: Schleicher, seeking to benefit from his public works program before calling for confrontation in the Reichstag that'll likely lead to new elections, has decided that Frick's proposal is most prudent. ?]
[? if not schleicher_economy_time: The chancellor makes it clear that he still hopes [+ nsdap_leader +] might have a sudden change of heart, but with his backup plan no longer viable, he pushes for the adoption of Frick's proposal. ?] The Reichstag is now adjourned until [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], Week [+ next_reichstag_week +], and Schleicher is expected to unveil his public works program during this time.

reichstag_2_alt.titleHtml: The government cannot adequately suppress unrest, civil war is inevitable.
reichstag_2_alt.subtitleHtml: We will fight, whether we choose to or not.

params.source: papen_civil_war

reichstag_3.titleHtml: Push for a compromise proposal (reconvene in three weeks, subject to review).
reichstag_3.bodyHtml: Together with the Center Party, our compromise proposal is accepted by all parties. The Reichstag will reconvene early in Week [+ next_reichstag_week +], [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], on the condition that the committee revisits the matter one week beforehand.

reichstag_4.titleHtml: Martial law is declared. The Reichswehr quells pockets of unrest.
reichstag_4.bodyHtml: The disorganized **SA** and **RFB** have failed to spark a mass uprising, and a civil war is averted. A widespread crackdown on paramilitaries have begun, with the Reichsbanner not even being spared.
