reichstag_impeach.titleHtml: Put forth a motion to remove President Hindenburg from office.
reichstag_impeach.subtitleHtml: A two-thirds majority in the Reichstag is required to succeed.
reichstag_impeach.bodyHtml: We are able to gather the support of [+ spd_r + kpd_r + sapd_r +]% of the Reichstag, with all **SPD**, **KPD**[? if sapd_formed: and **SAPD**?] deputies expected to vote in favor. Our effort is also aided by the fact that Hindenburg only has a few months left to live. [? if impeachment_ddp: The **[+ ddp_name +]** has been one of the only bourgeois parties standing up for the Weimar Republic and the constitution the party's founders drafted. We are expected to see their deputies vote with us. ?][? if not impeachment_ddp and not lvp_formed: Unfortunately, the **[+ ddp_name +]** has strayed too far from its former republican ideals, and now sees support for Hindenburg as a hard but necessary choice in the national interest. ?] [? if impeachment_dvp: The **DVP** were once staunch supporters of Hindenburg, but even the industrialists have grown tired of his antics and have lobbied the party to vote against the president. ?][? if not impeachment_dvp and not lvp_formed and dvp_exist: The **DVP** remains trapped in its reactionary spiral and will not support our motion. ?] [? if impeachment_lvp: The **LVP**, nominally a republican party, has remained faithful to its democratic convictions and will vote against President Hindenburg. ?][? if not impeachment_lvp and lvp_formed: The **LVP** has drifted far from its professed republican and democratic principles. Swayed by its reactionary right wing, it will reluctantly remain aligned with Hindenburg. ?] [? if impeachment_z: The Center Party, our ally since the Republic’s founding, stands with us to defend it. ?][? if not impeachment_z: The Center Party, our ally since the Republic’s founding, has unexpectedly sided with Hindenburg. Strained relations are to blame, as they now prioritize the survival of Treviranus’s government over principle. ?] [? if impeachment_bvp: Even the **BVP**—once deeply loyal to Hindenburg—has grown disillusioned with his anti-constitutionalist and erratic behavior, and now supports our effort. ?][? if not impeachment_bvp: The **BVP** has, as expected, remained loyal to President Hindenburg, despite their reported discontent over his anti-constitutional conduct. ?] The right-wing parties and nationalists remain Hindenburg’s most loyal supporters. Even Hugenberg recognizes the danger of a potential socialist president should Hindenburg be removed from office. The **NSDAP**[? if nvf_exist: and **NVF**?] will break with the **DSU** on the vote, and vote to impeach the president that has impeded their progress over and over again.

reichstag_impeach_2.bodyHtml: With a simple majority, the Reichstag has chosen to set aside our motion and instead proceed with a vote of no confidence in Treviranus first. Should the motion pass—as is likely—his government will collapse, and the Reichstag will likely be either adjourned or dissolved in the aftermath.

params.source: reichstag_impeach_3 if impeachment_votes >= 66.7; reichstag_impeach_fail_2 if impeachment_votes < 66.7

reichstag_impeach_3.bodyHtml:
[+ impeachment_votes +]% of the Reichstag has voted to recall President Hindenburg! But our fight is not over yet. A popular referendum is scheduled exactly one month from now to confirm the Reichstag’s decision.
If the referendum succeeds, a new presidential election will be held to determine Hindenburg’s successor. But if it fails, the constitution mandates that the Reichstag be dissolved and fresh elections called once again.
The referendum is scheduled for [+ impeachment_ref_month : month +] [+ impeachment_ref_year +], Week [+ impeachment_ref_week +].

reichstag_impeach_fail.titleHtml: The Reichstag shoots down our motion.
reichstag_impeach_fail.bodyHtml: With a simple majority, the Reichstag has chosen to set aside our motion. We must decide on the deal next.

params.source: treviranus_menu

reichstag_impeach_fail_2.bodyHtml: Despite our best efforts, we manage to rally only [+ impeachment_votes +]% of the Reichstag to our cause. We must decide on the deal next.

params.source: treviranus_menu

reichstag_nay.titleHtml: Vote against the motion of no confidence, and tolerate the cabinet.
reichstag_nay.subtitleHtml: The German parliamentary system desperately needs legitimacy. Forcing new elections now risks driving voters further into the extremes.
reichstag_nay.bodyHtml: Hindenburg is furious at what he sees as Treviranus’s betrayal—that he would even consider working with the socialists. After much deliberation, the President moves decisively: Treviranus is sacked, and a new successor is chosen under Papen’s influence.

reichstag_reconvene.titleHtml: Demand a reconvening of the Reichstag, with no dirty tricks this time.
reichstag_reconvene.subtitleHtml: [? if reichstag_fire_decree_schleicher: Different building, of course.?]
reichstag_reconvene.bodyHtml:
With our limited leverage, we are only able to negotiate the reconvening of the Reichstag. Schleicher has promised not to impede the chamber's right to assemble when it sees fit. The emergency restrictions on the free press and some political meetings have been lifted.
This is a disappointing outcome, but perhaps a vote of no confidence and new elections could turn the tide. After all, we will be able to harness the significant enthusiasm shown by the people in defiance of dictatorship.
The Reichstag will convene on [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], Week [+ next_reichstag_week +].

reject.bodyHtml: In the end, there is no uptake for Schleicher's schemes by any political party.

religion.titleHtml: The Catholic Church and Lutheran Church have long held political neutrality, perhaps that will change?
religion.bodyHtml: Prominent leaders of the Lutheran Church have endorsed President Hindenburg, arguing that despite their historical political neutrality, his reelection is a pressing necessity. Meanwhile, the Catholic Church is even more united in support of Hindenburg than it was for Wilhelm Marx in 1925. Catholic leaders, historically skeptical of Nazism, have actively discouraged their members from joining Nazi paramilitary organizations. This, combined with the strong support of Catholic-affiliated trade unions, will prove enormously significant in rallying a skeptical Catholic population behind a candidate whom most instinctively associate with Lutheran orthodoxy and Prussian authoritarianism.

Catholic leaders, historically skeptical of Nazism, have actively discouraged their members from joining Nazi paramilitary organizations. reparations.subtitleHtml: The debate over Germany's lost lands, the fulfillment of reparations, rearmament, and more.
reparations.bodyHtml: The reparations issue remains the most contentious point of contention between the two parties, with starkly opposing views on how to handle Germany’s financial obligations. The **DNVP**, including Treviranus himself, staunchly opposed the Young Plan and has previously clashed with the Center over foreign policy achievements such as the Locarno Treaties in the past.

reparations_left.bodyHtml: The Christians have used their influence to push for a more restrained and diplomatic foreign policy, aligning with the legacy of Stresemann. Reparations - Germany should be develop closer ties with the West, hoping for a revision of the Versailles treaty The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to peacefully settle disputes in the East The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament, but scale it down

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

reparations_moderate.bodyHtml: The Christians and nationalists have begrudgingly come to an agreement, as pragmatism wins the day; Germany can't simply refuse to pay. Reparations - Germany should seek a policy of fulfillment, hoping for a revision of the Versailles treaty The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to pressure Poland for the return of our former lands, peacefully later down the line The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich, referendum for Eupen-Malmedy The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament and refitting of the army

params.source: cvp_dnvp_menu

reparations_right.bodyHtml: The nationalists and Christian Socials have used their leverage to edit in their most important goals to the party program. Reparations - Germany must push for the complete abolition of reparations and the revocation of the "war guilt" clause, but will continue payments in the meantime The Eastern Policy - Germany should seek to pressure Poland for the return of our former lands, force if necessary later down the line The Western Policy - Closer ties between Austria and the Reich, push for an *Anschluss*, referendum for Eupen-Malmedy The Reichswehr - Continue the secret rearmament and refitting of the army

republic.bodyHtml: The Nazi and Communist propaganda machines have poisoned the public’s view of the Republic. Our goal is to counter their narrative with propaganda of our own.

republic_victory.bodyHtml: = Victory for the Republic In a chaotic civil war between the Reichsbanner and republican parties, **Stahlhelm** and the Reichswehr, and the **SA**: the anti-democratic forces are defeated! The infighting between the extremists have largely benefitted us. The battle lines hold, and the **SA**, **Stahlhelm**, and Reichswehr forces are defeated. Today, the forces of the republic prevail over the fascists and the reactionaries. There is a new revolution in Germany. Let us hope it produces a longer-lasting peace than the previous one.

resign.titleHtml: Resign our positions in the government.
resign.bodyHtml: We have resigned our positions in the government. We are replaced by the reactionary Goerdeler, who aims to bring the national opposition into government.

resources.bodyHtml: By transferring campaign funds to our coalition partners, we can make our policies more acceptable to them. Some would call this corruption, but perhaps it is necessary to save democracy.

response_to_antisemitism.bodyHtml: = Confronting Antisemitism Antisemitism has long been a latent feature of German society, but since the beginning of the economic depression, it has grown to a horrifying extent. The Nazis are the worst of it, but all the right-wing parties are deeply antisemitic. Regarding the **SPD** specifically, our right-wing enemies love to deploy their racist rhetoric against our many Jewish comrades, magnifying criticism of any minor transgression, and they call the entire **SPD** a Jewish party. We are a favorite target of their invectives.

choices.labelHtml: Antisemitism is the "socialism of fools". We will defeat them with real socialism.
Antisemitism is a crisis. Direct the full force of the Iron Front against antisemitism.
All Germans will suffer from fascism, not just the Jews. We do not need a separate policy for them.

response_to_antisemitism.all.bodyHtml: We do not need any special treatment for minorities.

response_to_antisemitism.if.bodyHtml: We develop an entire campaign against antisemitism under the auspices of the **Iron** **Front**. Hopefully our campaign can sway the workers away from Nazism.

return_to_normalcy.bodyHtml: = Return to Normalcy Germany is finally recovering from the Great Depression. As the economy gradually improves, the political crisis begins to unravel as well. Finally, the internal contradictions of the **NSDAP** have caught up to it. With the improving economic conditions, many business leaders are less interested in supporting them. Tensions between their remaining big capitalist funders and their lower middle class frontliners have come to a head, leading to desertions and public spats. This all saps Hitler's aura of strength, weakening Nazi support across a variety of demographics.

rights.bodyHtml:
With our limited leverage, we have managed to negotiate the reconvening of the Reichstag, with Schleicher promising not to obstruct the chamber's right to assemble as it sees fit. Furthermore, we secured an agreement that his government will not infringe upon the people's right to organize peacefully or on the freedom of the press, with Schleicher lifting all emergency restrictions. [? if reichstag_fire_decree_schleicher: This includes the repeal of the Reichstag Fire Decree. ?]
This is a disappointing outcome for all our efforts, but perhaps a vote of no confidence and new elections could turn the tide. After all, we can harness the significant public enthusiasm shown in defiance of dictatorship, and we need not fear further democratic backsliding—so long as Schleicher keeps his word.
The Reichstag will convene on [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], Week [+ next_reichstag_week +].

rohm_gay.titleHtml: **SA** Leader Ernst Röhm's Homosexuality Exposed
rohm_gay.subtitleHtml: The Prussian Ministry of the Interior uncovers shocking revelations about the Nazi leader...
rohm_gay.bodyHtml: = **SA** Leader Ernst Röhm's Homosexuality Exposed Wilhelm Abegg from the Prussian Ministry of the Interior has approached the **SPD** and informed us about three letters written by **SA** leader Ernst Röhm to Berlin nerve specialist Karl-Günther Heimsoth during his self-imposed exile in Bolivia. These letters, confiscated by the Prussian state police, are notable not for their political content but for Röhm’s candid discussions about his homosexuality—potentially exposing him to legal action. Röhm has never concealed his homosexuality, and Hitler has never taken offense at it. Despite Röhm facing multiple prosecutions under Paragraph 175 in the past, none have been successful. However, this time we now have definitive proof. What shall be our next move regarding these letters? > *"We oppose the disgraceful Paragraph 175 wherever we can; therefore we must not join the choir of those among us who want to banish a man from society because he is homosexual".* - Die Weltbühne, German weekly magazine

choices.labelHtml: We will publish the letters, as the revelation of such a high-ranking Nazi official being homosexual will undoubtedly harm their appeal among core demographics.
The **SPD** is nominally in favor of homosexual rights, and it would be in poor taste to expose such a personal matter.

rohm_gay.expose_rohm.bodyHtml: We have published the Röhm letters under the title *Der Fall Röhm* (The Röhm Affair), distributing the pamphlet across all corners of Germany. This has damaged the Nazi Party’s appeal among its more socially reactionary supporters and has even sparked a plot among some Nazi members to murder Röhm. The pamphlet argues that a party tolerating homosexuality at its highest levels must seek to "poison the people and destroy its moral strength." It warns that this would lead to Germany’s decline, akin to the fall of ancient Rome, and claims that by keeping Röhm in power, the Nazis are complicit in "knowingly and intentionally furthering the seduction of German youths into becoming homosexual minions." Despite this, Hitler has swiftly come to Röhm’s defense, publicly reaffirming his position as leader of the **SA**. The electoral performance of the Nazis remains largely unaffected, but the impression this controversy leaves on President Hindenburg may yet prove significant. Meanwhile, the pamphlet’s publisher, Helmuth Klotz, has been brutally beaten by Nazi deputies inside the Reichstag building as an act of revenge—an event that has overshadowed the scandal itself.

choices.labelHtml: Attempt to persecute Röhm! homosexual acts are prohibited by Paragraph 175, allowing us to open up legal action against him.

rohm_gay.no_expose_rohm.bodyHtml: It would be in poor taste for a party advocating for homosexual rights to attack someone for being gay. We’ve taken the high road, but many within our party feel we’ve missed an opportunity.

rohm_gay.persecute_rohm.bodyHtml: With definitive proof of Röhm violating Paragraph 175, the law criminalizing homosexual acts, we have been able to initiate legal action against him once more. Röhm is unable to deny the authenticity of the letters, and many have taken that as confirmation of their legitimacy. In the end, Röhm has been convicted under Paragraph 175 and sentenced to one year in prison. This has brought the scandal back into the spotlight, severely damaging the public perception of the **NSDAP** and **SA**.

root.start.bodyHtml: > *"Such a general development cannot be attributed to the false tactics of any single party or to the mistakes of individual leaders. On the contrary, the conduct of individual leaders is determined largely by the sentiments of the people as a whole. It would be erroneous, however, to regard the sentiments of the moment as reflecting the natural make-up and character of the people. They are merely the consequence of the special circumstances which have brought about this profound degradation of the entire nation."* - Karl Kautsky, *Hitlerism and Social Democracy*, 1934 This is a game of alternate history. While historical accuracy is a major concern, keep in mind that this is a *game*, and that any divergence from actual events will necessarily have to involve some element of make-believe. Nevertheless, please let the author know if there are any glaring mistakes. For more information on the politics and government of the German Republic, see the "Library" page on the top left. If this is your first time playing the game, it is strongly recommended that you read at least some of this information. **If you are playing this mod via the Mod Loader in base game, there will be various items missing (parliament colours, images, arrows, etc.). For the intended experience, please play using this link.**

= The Rubicon is Crossed
With the dismissal of Brüning’s government—despite its parliamentary majority—the foundations of democracy are crumbling before our eyes.
Whatever path Hindenburg takes now will be chosen not by the people, but by those who whisper in his ear.
Time slows. We enter the week-by-week struggle.

run_braun.bodyHtml: It takes effort to run a somewhat unexpected campaign. First, Braun has to be convinced to run. [? if hindenburg_run: He himself had supported voting for Hindenburg, and it takes a good deal of prodding to convince him of his destiny. ?][? if not hindenburg_run: It takes a good deal of prodding to convince him of his destiny. ?] [? if not lvp_formed: The [? if ddp_votes < 2: miniscule remnants of the?] [? if ddp_name == "DDP": **Democratic Party**?][? if ddp_name == "DStP": **State Party**?] aren't guaranteed to support us, [? if ddp_relation < 40: with a deterioration in our relationship?][? if ddp_relation >= 40: but are open to it due to their reluctance in supporting Hindenburg?]?][? if lvp_formed: The **LVP** aren't exactly the biggest fans of socialism, [? if lvp_relation < 40: with the deterioration in relations making their support a near impossibility.?][? if lvp_relation >= 40: but are at least open to it due to their reluctance in supporting Hindenburg?]?]. Who else will? Can we convince the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] to support Braun? What about the **Communists**?

run_eckener.bodyHtml: It takes effort to launch a somewhat unexpected campaign. First, Eckener must be convinced to run. He isn't particularly eager to be the candidate of the socialists, as it would invite slander from the German Right—whom he feels a greater affinity with. With his status as a non-socialist—and even conservative—unity candidate, and his non-partisanship, Eckener is positioned to attract endorsements from a wide range of parties. However, much of this depends on their relationship with us, as our backing alone is enough to disgust many otherwise eager supporters. The [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]** and **DVP** are likely to back Eckener, although the **DVP** requires convincing. ?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP** is likely to back Eckener, although their industrial-right elements object to the arrangement. ?] The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is nominally supportive, although the **BVP** remains another problem. Finally, the **Communists**[? if left_split: and **SAPD**?] are firmly opposed to supporting a bourgeois conservative—for obvious reasons.

run_rosenfeld.bodyHtml: It takes effort to run a somewhat unexpected campaign. First, Rosenfeld has to be convinced to run. He isn't particularly eager to be promoted to the presidency from his lowly position in the party. His candidacy has severely limited our options for endorsements, but we can likely count on the support of the **KPD**[? if left_split: and **SAPD**?]. But who else? The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is likely hostile, and the liberals are irreconcilably opposed. Furthermore, many of our voters outside the working class have voiced objections to his candidacy and will not support him with much enthusiasm. Perhaps this will become the ultimate battle between the Marxist and bourgeois halves of the country.

sa_ban.bodyHtml: With control of the Interior Ministry, we have used these revelations as a pretext to ban the **SA** nationwide[? if sa_banned:, as they can still operate outside of Prussia?]. This has led to a noticeable drop in political violence, effectively dealing a blow to the Nazis, who had relied on intimidation tactics to gain votes. However, the ban has not been as effective as initially hoped. Few weapons have been seized, because the plans to ban the SA were leaked by none other than General Kurt von Schleicher, who believes this move interferes with his "taming strategy." [? if president == "Hindenburg": He and the Reichswehr have submitted complaints to President Hindenburg, arguing that the accusations used to justify the **SA** ban equally apply to the Reichsbanner. The file presented to Hindenburg consists mostly of clippings from right-wing newspapers and a Reichsbanner training manual. Even Groener finds these charges groundless, but Schleicher wields significant influence over the aging president, who now believes that the ban must be extended to the Reichsbanner. ?] [? if sa_banned_pro: Nevertheless, the **SA** has been significantly weakened by the ban. ?]

sa_ban_braun.bodyHtml: With the victory of Social Democrat [? if president == "Braun": Otto Braun?][? if president == "Rosenfeld": Kurt Rosenfeld?], an uptick in paramilitary violence has been seen, and even rumors of a far-right coup. Prussian Minister of the Interior Carl Severing has ordered an emergency search of all Nazi and **SA** offices throughout the state. During the raids, evidence was uncovered that the Nazi Party headquarters in Munich had ordered to place **SA** units on high alert after the election. In the event of a [+ spd_candidate_1932 +] victory, these units were to immediately launch a coup d’état, which included the planned seizure of military installations and weaponry. The threat of a coup has granted the newly elected President a pretext to issue a nationwide ban of the **SA**, an opinion shared by many non-Nazi state governments. However, the more conservative, non-Nazi elements of the German right, as well as the Reichswehr itself, do not share our sense of alarm over the **SA**’s supposed coup plans and see no need for immediate action.

choices.labelHtml: We will use this revelation to commence a nationwide ban on the **SA**!
We will leverage this revelation to pressure the Interior Ministry into banning the **SA** nationwide!

We will present this damning evidence to Interior Minister [? if second_bruning_cabinet_seen: Wilhelm Groener?][? if not second_bruning_cabinet_seen: Joseph Wirth?] and use [+ president +] to pressure him for a nationwide ban on the **SA**.

sa_ban_braun_2.bodyHtml: With control of the Interior Ministry, we have used these revelations as a pretext to ban the **SA** nationwide, for their anti-constitutional plot to overthrow the government. This move has led to a noticeable decline in political violence, delivering a significant blow to the Nazis, who had relied heavily on intimidation tactics to secure votes. However, a leak about the ban managed to get out, allowing the Nazis to hide many of their weapons from being seized. [? if sa_banned_pro: Nevertheless, the **SA** has been significantly weakened by the ban. ?]

sa_ban_normal.bodyHtml: With the presidential elections approaching[? if next_election_year_prussia == year: and the next Prussian elections as well?], Prussian Minister of the Interior Carl Severing has ordered an emergency search of all Nazi and **SA** offices throughout the state. During the raids, evidence was uncovered that the Nazi Party headquarters in Munich had ordered **SA** units to be placed on high alert on election day. In the event of an anticipated [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] victory, these units were to immediately launch a coup d’état, which included the planned seizure of military installations and weaponry. [? if president == "Hindenburg" and spd_support_reactionary and hindenburg_run: The mere threat of such a coup has provided the **SPD** with exactly what it needed to reenergize its reluctant membership in support of Hindenburg’s campaign against [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +]?][? if president != "Hindenburg" or not spd_support_reactionary or not hindenburg_run: The mere threat of such a coup has provided the **SPD** with exactly what it needed to reenergize the workers against the Nazis?]. Non-Nazi state governments broadly support banning the **SA**, having lobbied the federal government for months on the issue. However, the more conservative, non-Nazi elements of the German right, as well as the Reichswehr itself, do not share our sense of alarm over the **SA**’s supposed coup plans and see no need for immediate action.

choices.labelHtml: We will use this revelation to commence a nationwide ban on the **SA**!
We will leverage this revelation to pressure the Interior Ministry into banning the **SA** nationwide!

We will present this damning evidence to Interior Minister [? if second_bruning_cabinet_seen: Wilhelm Groener?][? if not second_bruning_cabinet_seen: Joseph Wirth?] and push for a nationwide ban on the **SA**!

sa_ban_post.subtitleHtml: Wilhelm Groener, long-time Defense Minister and Brüning's strongest ally, is forced to resign...
sa_ban_post.bodyHtml: = Schleicher's Betrayal Schleicher’s unwavering belief in his "taming strategy," which involves bringing the **NSDAP** into the government, led him to successfully orchestrate the removal of Wilhelm Groener as Minister of Defense for enforcing the ban on the **SA**. Groener, unable to believe that Schleicher—his friend, protégé, and "adoptive son"—would betray him, became increasingly uncertain in his role, particularly in his dealings with Hindenburg and the Reichswehr leadership. Once Hindenburg was convinced that the Reichsbanner posed a greater threat than the **SA**, Schleicher seized the opportunity to push for Groener’s removal. Already plagued by self-doubt, Groener delivered an embarrassingly poor speech in the Reichstag defending the ban, effectively sealing his fate. Schleicher then forced the issue by threatening to resign alongside Chief of the Army Kurt von Hammerstein if Groener remained in office. Under mounting pressure and faced with Hindenburg’s anger, Groener ultimately resigned. We strongly suspect that Schleicher is in contact with the **NSDAP** and that this maneuver is merely a precondition for securing their support for a new right-wing government.

choices.labelHtml: The Brüning government is critically weakened and is set to become the next victim of Schleicher's schemes.

sa_ban_post.bruning_explode.bodyHtml: Groener, one of Brüning’s longest-standing and most loyal allies, is now out of the equation. Brüning, deeply loyal to him, was fully prepared to resign the chancellorship if Groener was forced out of the cabinet. However, unwilling to let Brüning risk his own position on his behalf, Groener chose to step down. His resignation as Minister of Defense has dealt a severe blow to the Brüning cabinet, further diminishing its chances of surviving the deepening political crisis triggered by the fallout from the local elections. Among Hindenburg’s inner circle of advisors, no one had been more steadfast in supporting Brüning than Groener. His departure has severely weakened the chancellor’s standing with the Reich President, leaving him fully exposed to the machinations of Schleicher and his entourage. With Groener gone, Schleicher is now free from external restraints to pursue his strategy of taming the Nazis, answerable only to Hindenburg. Sensing that Brüning has been fatally weakened, the Nazis have intensified their attacks on his government, seeking to bring it down once and for all.

sa_ban_pre.sa_ban_bruning_wirth.bodyHtml: Interior Minister Joseph Wirth, a strong anti-Nazi member of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]'s left wing, has found a strong urgency in our collected evidence to justify the ban on the **SA**. We have already noticed a significant drop in political violence, and this decree has dealt a strong blow to the Nazis, who have relied on intimidation to gain votes. However, the ban has not been as effective as initially hoped. Few weapons have been seized, because the plans to ban the **SA** were leaked by none other than General Kurt von Schleicher, who believes this move interferes with his "taming strategy." [? if president == "Hindenburg": He and the Reichswehr have submitted complaints to President Hindenburg, arguing that the accusations used to justify the **SA** ban equally apply to the Reichsbanner. The file presented to Hindenburg consists mostly of clippings from right-wing newspapers and a Reichsbanner training manual. Even Groener finds these charges groundless, but Schleicher wields significant influence over the aging president, who now believes that the ban must be extended to the Reichsbanner. ?] [? if sa_banned_pro: Nevertheless, the **SA** has been significantly weakened by the ban. ?]

sa_ban_pre.sa_ban_normal.bodyHtml: With the presidential elections approaching[? if next_election_year_prussia == year: and the next Prussian elections as well?], Prussian Minister of the Interior Carl Severing has ordered an emergency search of all Nazi and **SA** offices throughout the state. During the raids, evidence was uncovered that the Nazi Party headquarters in Munich had ordered **SA** units to be placed on high alert on election day. In the event of an anticipated [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +] victory, these units were to immediately launch a coup d’état, which included the planned seizure of military installations and weaponry. [? if president == "Hindenburg" and spd_support_reactionary and hindenburg_run: The mere threat of such a coup has provided the **SPD** with exactly what it needed to reenergize its reluctant membership in support of Hindenburg’s campaign against [+ nsdap_candidate_1932 +]?][? if president != "Hindenburg" or not spd_support_reactionary or not hindenburg_run: The mere threat of such a coup has provided the **SPD** with exactly what it needed to reenergize the workers against the Nazis?]. Non-Nazi state governments broadly support banning the **SA**, having lobbied the federal government for months on the issue. However, the more conservative, non-Nazi elements of the German right, as well as the Reichswehr itself, do not share our sense of alarm over the **SA**’s supposed coup plans and see no need for immediate action.

choices.labelHtml: We will use this revelation to commence a nationwide ban on the **SA**!
We will leverage this revelation to pressure the Interior Ministry into banning the **SA** nationwide!

We will present this damning evidence to Interior Minister [? if second_bruning_cabinet_seen: Wilhelm Groener?][? if not second_bruning_cabinet_seen: Joseph Wirth?] and push for a nationwide ban on the **SA**!

sa_ban_pre.sa_ban_pressure.bodyHtml: With our position in government, we pressure the Interior Ministry to ban the **SA** nationwide, for their anti-constitutional plot to overthrow the government. They quickly accede to these demands, banning the **SA** nationwide[? if sa_banned:, as they can still operate outside of Prussia?]. We have noticed a significant drop in political violence, and have dealt an effective blow to the Nazis, who have relied on their intimidation to gain votes. However, the ban has not been as effective as initially hoped. Few weapons have been seized, because the plans to ban the **SA** were leaked by none other than General Kurt von Schleicher, who believes this move interferes with his "taming strategy." [? if president == "Hindenburg": He and the Reichswehr have submitted complaints to President Hindenburg, arguing that the accusations used to justify the **SA** ban equally apply to the Reichsbanner. The file presented to Hindenburg consists mostly of clippings from right-wing newspapers and a Reichsbanner training manual. Even Groener finds these charges groundless, but Schleicher wields significant influence over the aging president, who now believes that the ban must be extended to the Reichsbanner. ?] [? if sa_banned_pro: Nevertheless, the **SA** has been significantly weakened by the ban. ?]

salvage.titleHtml: Can we try to salvage the negotiations?
salvage.bodyHtml: How should we try to salvage the negotiations?

choices.labelHtml: Try to convince France and Britain that slowly controlled inflation is possible and desirable.
Try to convince the US to reduce war debts for the sake of peace.

salvage_currency.bodyHtml: Wladimir Woytinsky, now part of our delegation to the conference, uses our successful implementation of the WTB-plan in order to argue for loosening currency valuation. The argument is at least somewhat convincing, and an agreement is reached, leading to increased inflation and demand stimulus throughout the world.

saxon_collapse.subtitleHtml: [? if saxony_leader == "Bünger": Wilhelm Bünger?][? if saxony_leader == "Heldt": Max Heldt?] faces a vote of no confidence.
saxon_collapse.bodyHtml: = Collapse of the Saxon Cabinet The [+ saxony_leader +] Cabinet's days are numbered following a dispute over the Saxon Reichsrat delegation's support for the Young Plan, which has led to a loss of confidence from the **DNVP**, **SLV**, and **NSDAP**. We can either exit the opposition and prop up the cabinet to avoid new elections, or maintain our role in opposition-supporting all votes of no confidences. [? if spd_coalition_possible_saxony >= 50: While a [? if lvp_formed and stegerwald_path: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed or not stegerwald_path: Grand?] Coalition with the liberals could be an option, the strong leftist leanings of the Saxon **SPD** make such an alliance unlikely. ?]

choices.labelHtml: We will form a [? if lvp_formed and stegerwald_path: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed or not stegerwald_path: Grand?] Coalition!

saxon_collapse.grand_coalition_saxony.subtitleHtml: We have somehow reconciled with the bourgeois parties, that they're willing to govern with us again.
saxon_collapse.grand_coalition_saxony.bodyHtml: Somehow, the bourgeois parties are willing to form a [? if lvp_formed and stegerwald_path: Weimar?][? if not lvp_formed or not stegerwald_path: Grand?] Coalition with us, replacing the [+ saxony_leader +] Cabinet and preventing the need for new elections. With the **ASPD** (whose Saxon chapter is notably more sane) now convinced of our reformist path, they have rejoined the Saxon **SPD**!

saxon_collapse.no_majority_saxony.bodyHtml: As expected, the bourgeois government in Saxony isn't able to survive the vote of no confidence. New elections are called for June, but the [+ saxony_leader +] Cabinet continues to operate as a caretaker government. This grants an opportunity for the **NSDAP** to exploit and capitalize on political instability and the perceived failure of parliamentary democracy.

saxon_collapse.united_left_saxony.titleHtml: We will form a United Left coalition with the **KPD**.
saxon_collapse.united_left_saxony.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, despite reluctance on both sides due to fears that the reactionary Hindenburg will order a Reichsexekution if a coalition were to form. Red Saxony is restored! As one of the most left-wing and industrial states in Germany, we will use our leverage to implement comprehensive reforms and transform Saxony into a stronghold of socialism. Hindenburg’s patience is especially thin. Tread carefully.

# Reminder of possible coalition outcomes from 1929/1930 Saxon elections:
# Heldt toleration, Schieck toleration, Heldt groko, 1930 Groko, Successful United Left, United Left Reichsexekution, SPD majority, Schieck majority, Nazis enter

saxony_reichsexekution_popular.bodyHtml: = Reichsexekution of Saxony President [+ president +] has invoked the Reichsexekution to dismiss the Saxon government, citing its "inability to maintain order" amidst escalating clashes between the **SA**, Reichsbanner, and the increasingly militant **RFB**. The militarization of the **RFB** has invoked memories of what transpired years prior. However, the true motivation is clear: the left-wing coalition governing Saxony poses a direct threat to the conservative and nationalist establishment in Germany.

saxony_reichsexekution_popular.defend_2_.bodyHtml: As the Reichswehr and their reactionary auxiliaries march into Saxony, armed fighting erupts between them and the leftist forces of the Saxon government. [+ president +] refuses to withdraw the Reichsexekution and orders more Reichswehr troops into Saxony.

The Reichsbanner and RFB confront the reactionaries on the road to Saxony and somehow, the enemy has retreated without a fight! scandi.bodyHtml: The programs of the Nordic socialists involve active government intervention in the economy. We can learn from their economic strategies, and how they moved beyond their working-class base to attract a broader set of constituents.

schacht_vs_hilferding.bodyHtml: = Schacht against Hilferding Reichsbank president Hjalmar Schacht has criticized Finance Minister Hilferding of the **SPD** for his budget, which he claims is unbalanced and contains too much social welfare and not enough tax cuts for top earners and businesses. More importantly, he is refusing to release loans necessary for the functioning of the government unless Hilferding either massively changes his budget or resigns. Of course, this criticism is unfounded, but the bourgeois establishment does not care.

choices.labelHtml: Work with him to shape the budget.

schacht_vs_hilferding.expose_him.bodyHtml: We expose to the public Schacht's dealings with the Nazis. For better or worse, he is cowed, and refrains from taking further actions against us.

schacht_vs_hilferding.hilferding_resign.bodyHtml:
With no other choice, Hilferding has resigned as Finance Minister, to be replaced by a [? if (in_grand_coalition or (in_weimar_coalition and lvp_formed)): center-right ?][? if not in_grand_coalition: technocratic ?] candidate.
[? if economic_minister_granted = 1: Our coalition partners have granted us the Economic Ministry to compensate. ?]

schemes.titleHtml: Demand the above, and also guarantees for the continued independence of political organizations.
schemes.bodyHtml: With our leverage, we have negotiated the reconvening of the Reichstag, with Schleicher promising not to obstruct the chamber's right to assemble as it sees fit. Furthermore, we secured an agreement that his government will not infringe upon the people's right to organize peacefully or on the freedom of the press, with all emergency restrictions lifted. The most controversial concession was the lifting of the ban on the **KPD**[? if sapd_formed: and **SAPD**?], a major retreat and an open sign of Schleicher's defeat. Although expectedly, the **RFB** remains banned. President Hindenburg, along with the industrialists and nationalists, have now completely lost confidence in the chancellor. A vote of no confidence and new elections are expected. We can harness the significant public enthusiasm shown in defiance of dictatorship and need not fear further democratic backsliding—so long as Schleicher keeps his word. The Reichstag will convene on [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], Week [+ next_reichstag_week +].

schiele.bodyHtml: [? if land_reform >= 1 : Due to the land reform policies enacted by our[? if not spd_in_government: previous?] government, the agrarian conservative elites have made it their strongest effort to rally the German right against them. This involves orchestrating a leadership change within the **DNVP**, the primary political home of agrarian conservatism. Treviranus has been ousted in a vote of no confidence, in favor of the president of the National Rural League (RLB), Martin Schiele. By electing the most influential figure in the agricultural community, they aim to safeguard the role of organized agriculture in Germany, viewing Treviranus as too aligned with middle class interests. ?][? if rural_spd_normalized >= 30 and land_reform == 0 : With the **SPD** making significant inroads among rural voters, the **DNVP** and its agrarian elites have ousted Treviranus in a vote of no confidence, to elect Martin Schiele, the president of the National Rural League (RLB). They believe Schiele, the most influential figure in the agricultural community, can halt this shift and preserve the longstanding alliance between agriculture and German conservatism, seeing Treviranus as too aligned with middle-class interests. ?][? if rural_nsdap_normalized >= rural_dnvp_normalized and rural_spd_normalized < 30 and land_reform == 0 : Due to the significant inroads made by the insurgent **NSDAP** among their primary rural voter base, the **DNVP** and its agrarian elites have ousted Treviranus in a vote of no confidence, to elect Martin Schiele, president of the National Rural League (RLB). They believe Schiele, the most influential figure in the agricultural community, can halt this shift and preserve the longstanding alliance between agriculture and German conservatism, seeing Treviranus as too aligned with middle-class interests. ?] Schiele’s election has led to the merger of the **CNBLP** into the **DNVP**, strengthening its hold on the countryside and uniting the RLB in lobbying for agrarian interests. This consolidation has given rise to the renewal of the Green Front, an umbrella group of the RLB, peasant unions, and some Catholic and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]-affiliated agricultural organizations.

schizo.bodyHtml:
Under the influence of Franz von Papen—and apparently Schleicher as well—Hindenburg has appointed Wilhelm III, eldest son of the last German Emperor, as Chancellor, reportedly with his father’s blessing.
It is clear the chaos of the past year has taken its toll. In the end, Hindenburg now trusts no one but his dearest friend, Papen. It's unknown of the former chancellor's reasoning behind such a pick, but perhaps he would've hoped that reinstating a monarchy, the people can rally around him as they once rallied around Hindenburg. 
A bloody three-way civil war is inevitable.

schleicher.subtitleHtml: Accusations of *Junker* misuse of government aid funds.
schleicher.bodyHtml: Although not directly related to recent negotiations, a scandal was revealed during a session of the Reichstag’s budget committee: a Center Party member leveled sweeping accusations of fraud against beneficiaries of the Eastern Aid program. Meant to rescue bankrupt estates, the funds were allegedly used instead for racehorses, luxury cars, and lavish holidays—at a time when millions of Germans were living in poverty. President Hindenburg himself has been implicated. His *Neudeck* estate—a gift from right-wing industrialists and the RLB in 1927—was transferred into his son Oskar’s name to avoid taxes. Though not legally contestable, the revelation that many of Hindenburg’s close friends also benefited has deeply unsettled the President, who is now inundated with complaints from his old allies. Given Schleicher’s reputation for shadowy political maneuvering, and the fact that these revelations surfaced just a day after his break with the RLB, many suspect that he orchestrated the leak as an act of revenge.

schleicher_1.schleicher.bodyHtml: This all but confirms our suspicions that General Schleicher is conspiring with the Nazis against the republican forces. Our relations with the "Red General" has worsened.

schleicher_1.schleicher_2.titleHtml: Von Schleicher offers to meet with the unions, and to ease their fears.
schleicher_1.schleicher_2.subtitleHtml: The unions are independent of the party, and have agreed to participate.
schleicher_1.schleicher_2.bodyHtml: The invitation for a direct meeting between Theodor Leipart, leader of the ADGB, and von Schleicher is declined. Instead, a larger meeting is held, including Papen, his Interior Minister, and the ADGB’s co-chairs. At the meeting, the union leaders confront Schleicher over alleged secret agreements with the **SA**, prompting both Schleicher and Papen to strike a more conciliatory tone in response to union complaints about unfair government treatment. Schleicher denies any such deals with the **SA**, insisting that the government's highest priority is reducing unemployment. Papen also requests the unions to use their influence to persuade the **SPD** to give the government time to deliver results. By the end of the meeting, the three unionists are left impressed by Schleicher, who hints at possible concessions to a “patriotic labor movement.” A line of communication between the ADGB and the government remains open—much to Wels’s frustration, as he aims to maintain a united front against the regime. (Leipart is granted an ability)

schleicher_10.subtitleHtml: [? if dvp_votes < 4 and dvp_leader != "Glatzel": Struggling at the polls, the party tries to stay relevant by merging into a larger bloc?][? if dvp_leader == "Glatzel": Glatzel's views align closely with the chancellor's?].
schleicher_10.bodyHtml: = **DVP** joins the **DNEF** [? if dvp_votes < 4 and dvp_leader != "Glatzel": The electoral decline of the **DVP** and the threat of being wiped out of parliament due to Germany's imperfect proportional system have forced the party to abandon its political independence and join Schleicher's **DNEF**. This decision has faced significant internal objections, as many still hope for an understanding with the bourgeois and right-wing parties to secure a place on their electoral list. ?] [? if dvp_leader == "Glatzel": Frank Glatzel, leader of the **DVP**, shares much ideological ground with Schleicher's new party—nationalism, corporatism, and the goal of a Volksgemeinschaft. A merger with the German National Unity Front has thus become inevitable. ?] [? if dvp_votes < 4 and dvp_leader != "Glatzel": Nonetheless, the **DVP** and its industrial backers will bolster the **DNEF** and legitimize it among the middle class, eliminating yet another option for non-Nazi bourgeois voters. ?] [? if dvp_leader == "Glatzel": Glatzel's vision of a "new nationalism" will carry a sizable following into his new political home, along with his affiliated white-collar union, the DHV, which he is bringing into the **DNEF** as well. ?]

schleicher_13.subtitleHtml: The miniscule party can no longer survive on its own.
schleicher_13.bodyHtml: = **[+ ddp_name +]** joins the **DNEF** With the **[+ ddp_name +]** effectively dead as a political force, many former politicians—especially on its right wing—have long advocated for its self-dissolution, believing only then could a new, unified force rise from its ashes. That belief has only strengthened with the rise of the **DNEF**. Now, more party members are calling for a formal merger into Schleicher's organization. His appeals to national unity have struck a psychological blow to the rank and file of a party that always championed the welfare and unity of the nation as a whole above all. Old-line democrats like Dietrich and Heuss remain the most resistant, committed republicans to the core. But figures like Lemmer and the party’s left wing are proving more susceptible to Schleicher’s calls for national unity. Nonetheless, a vote is conducted, and the opposition wins.

choices.labelHtml: The German National Unity Front welcomes its new member.

schleicher_13_alt.bodyHtml: = **LVP** joins the **DNEF** German liberalism has long been intertwined with nationalism, dating back to the revolutions of 1848. The image of left-liberals as pacifists is mostly a stereotype, with only a fringe minority truly committed to pacifism. This makes the **LVP** a natural candidate for incorporation into the **DNEF**, as it has long championed a Volksgemeinschaft—a national community to reconcile the classes in service of the nation—offered as an alternative to Marxist class struggle. [? if industrialists_dnef: The **LVP**, however, is drawn more by Schleicher’s promises to the industrialists, who dominate the party’s leadership. ?][? if not industrialists_dnef: Disillusionment with parliamentarianism and democracy has driven much of the party to back a strongman who can restore stability and tear up the disgraceful terms of Versailles. The committed democrats, mostly on the party’s left wing—figures like Heuss and Dietrich—are powerless to stop this. ?]

schleicher_14.subtitleHtml: Lambach forces the party into the front.
schleicher_14.bodyHtml: = **DNVP** joins the **DNEF** Walther Lambach and the Christian Socials have long championed a presidential government and the vision of a non-partisan strongman ruling above political factions. That strongman is Schleicher. With the formation of the **DNEF**, he sees little remaining reason to maintain the **DNVP** as a political force. He has urged his movement to merge into the German National Unity Front, pointing to their shared goal of a Volksgemeinschaft that includes the workers and their common desire to cast off the chains of Versailles. Lambach and Treviranus, over the objections of old guard figures like Westarp and Hergt, have pushed the party at an emergency congress to vote for immediate dissolution—a vote that passes once a "monetary incentive" is offered to on the fence lower-level members by Schleicher himself.

schleicher_15.bodyHtml: = Schleicher and Röhm Ernst Röhm has found little success in his efforts to rebuild the **SA**, and in maintaining its new political organization, the **NVF**. There are simply not enough funds to go around, as demoralized Nazis stopped contributing a while ago. Röhm's plan to wait for an opportune moment for his "national revolution" is no longer tenable, and a new approach has to be taken. Schleicher and Röhm goes years back, with the two becoming best friends near the turn of the decade, to the paranoia of Hitler. The two have very distinct political views however, and their cooperation only goes as far as a secret agreement promising that the **SA** would mobilize and fight along with the Reichswehr if Germany was attacked by a foreign invader. Now, the two aim to rekindle this bond, and Röhm has officially attached the **SA** to be subordinate to the Reichswehr, in exchange for more authority over its operations. The **NVF** has since been attached to the **DNEF** as well.

choices.labelHtml: The German National Unity Front welcomes its new member.

schleicher_15.schleicher_2.bodyHtml: God knows what Röhm might do with an official government position. Fortunately, everyone, including President Hindenburg, are intensely distrustful of Röhm's revolutionary views. schleicher_16.subtitleHtml: The most powerful men in Germany are brought into the fold.
schleicher_16.bodyHtml: = Schleicher and the Industrialists The German industrialists and big business leaders have maintained a friendly stance toward Schleicher, appreciating his prioritization of their interests over those of the agrarians and his efforts to stabilize the economy. However, concerns linger over his growing state intervention and the risk that his public works campaign could trigger runaway inflation. To address this, Schleicher has summoned a secret meeting with his allies and Germany’s leading industrialists. He will offer sweeping concessions: a guarantee of capitalism’s preservation and their continued dominance over labor within a corporatist framework. In return, they are expected to pool their resources for unrestricted use by the **DNEF**.

choices.labelHtml: The industrialists are granted their place in the new order.

schleicher_16.schleicher_2.bodyHtml: Schleicher continues to walk a tightrope between appeasing organized labor and retaining the favor of Germany’s industrial elite. Nonetheless, the **DNEF** secures over five million marks in funding from a consortium of German businesses—chiefly those tied to rearmament, who see Schleicher’s survival as essential to their own profits.

schleicher_17.subtitleHtml: Not even his blindly loyal party stands by him now.

schleicher_17.hugenberg_dnf.bodyHtml: Hugenberg and the **DNF**, once buoyed by their early popularity as one of the few parties to unconditionally back Papen, have since soured their relations with the chancellery. Hugenberg's demand for full control over the agricultural and economic ministries has strained ties, and his uncompromising opposition to Schleicher has sparked discontent within the **DNF**—a party once built entirely from his loyalists. Many of his former allies are now bewildered that Hugenberg would turn against a fellow reactionary, especially one who ostensibly shares his vision of steering Germany toward authoritarian rule. With Hugenberg’s personal fortune—once sustained by his media empire—running dry, and industrial backers remaining firmly opposed to his leadership, frustrated members and former confidants are abandoning ship. They now flock to the German National Unity Front, preferring to back Schleicher directly without Hugenberg standing in their way.

choices.labelHtml: The German National Unity Front welcomes its new members.

schleicher_17.hugenberg_dnvp.bodyHtml: Initially, Hugenberg and his **DNVP** initially stood to gain the most by backing the reactionary Papen cabinet. However, relations soured with the chancellery after Schleicher refused to grant him full control over the agricultural and economic ministries. His uncompromising opposition to Schleicher has sparked widespread discontent within the **DNVP**, eroding Hugenberg’s once unchallenged authority among both party leaders and the rank-and-file. Many find it bewildering that Hugenberg would oppose a fellow reactionary, especially one presumably sharing his goal of steering Germany toward authoritarian rule. With internal party democracy long dead—party congresses stacked with loyalists serving as mere rubber stamps—dissenters have little choice. Now, the majority within the party are seizing Schleicher’s lifeline: the absorption of friendly nationalists into the German National Unity Front, where they hope to finally gain a hand in shaping the chancellor's future policies.

choices.labelHtml: The German National Unity Front welcomes its new members.

Hugenberg is now left with his tiny **DNF**—no friends, no funds, and no influence on the national stage. There’s a strong chance he’ll give up entirely. But for now, he stubbornly clings on onto whatever influence he has left in his media empire. schleicher_18.subtitleHtml: Proposal for a united labor front between the republican unions.
schleicher_18.bodyHtml: = Organized Labor Under Threat We have observed extensive infiltration of Schleicher's supporters into the leadership of the ADGB, the Christian, and liberal trade unions—with the rank-and-file of all three even more inclined to back him. In response, a proposal for a united labor front—bringing together our ADGB, the Christian GcG formerly led by Stegerwald, and the Hirsch-Duncker liberal unions under Ernst Lemmer—has been floated by figures like our Wilhelm Leuschner and the Center's Jakob Kaiser. The hope is that such unity will allow organized labor to resist coercion from Schleicher’s government and secure a stronger position within the corporatist order he has been promoting, should it come to that.

choices.labelHtml: A united labor front is formed!

schleicher_18.schleicher_2.bodyHtml: Negotiations have progressed, but one major obstacle remains: the ADGB’s continued commitment to Marxism, setting it apart from the other unions that now advocate for class collaboration. The question stands—do we stay silent on this point, for the sake of unity?

schleicher_18.schleicher_2_pro.titleHtml: Go along with the Center's proposal.
schleicher_18.schleicher_2_pro.bodyHtml: The unification of the labor unions has complicated Schleicher's efforts to divide and conquer, depriving him of the option to play the more moderate unions against the ADGB. We have also agreed to coordinate unified action in response to any offensive measures his government may attempt in the coming months.

schleicher_18.schleicher_3.bodyHtml: Without coordination among the republican unions, Schleicher has moved quickly to strike separate deals with the more right-leaning organizations. The DHV, the conservative white-collar union, has been the first to pledge loyalty to the "new state," joined by the Hirsch-Duncker unions—too marginal to wield real leverage anyway. The Christian unions have been cozying up to Schleicher for months[? if z_in_gov:, and Stegerwald's entry into government has only accelerated these talks of cooperation between his cabinet and the unionists.?][? if not z_in_gov:, though they remain broadly wary of Schleicher and his true intentions.?] Their advocacy for a "pluralistic" model, where unions retain formal autonomy within a corporatist Germany, has only made Schleicher’s task easier. [? if schleicher_spd_influence >= 6: Schleicher has also been quietly cultivating allies within the ADGB itself. Voices calling for the rejection of Marxism and a break with the **SPD** are growing louder by the day. Damn it. ?]

schleicher_19.subtitleHtml: A state-controlled labor organization is established.
schleicher_19.bodyHtml: = German Labor Front Schleicher has been working intensively over the past weeks to forge a formal alliance between the trade unions and the state, focusing his efforts on the Christian associations. Their negotiations have now "succeeded"—with heavy doses of state intimidation and interference ensuring they accepted an offer that would have been unthinkable under normal circumstances. Under this agreement, the blue-collar Hirsch-Duncker, Christian, and the Strasserist **NSBO** unions are merged into the new German Labor Front (DAF). White-collar and civil servant unions, including the DHV, are folded into their own section within the Front. The right to strike is curtailed, and all members are made to pledge full loyalty to the so-called "national interest"—however the state chooses to define it. Local union leaders who refuse to join are having their offices raided, their funds confiscated, and themselves imprisoned. While membership in the German Labor Front is technically voluntary, access to benefits—and even basic protections—is now locked behind it, making participation all but mandatory. Furthermore, a new department is established in the DAF, tasked solely with spreading state propaganda and binding the workers more tightly into the Volksgemeinschaft. The chancellor is also able to palate the industrialists, by placing their power significantly above that of labor in the newly established corporatist framework.

schleicher_19.schleicher_adgb_choice.bodyHtml: Schleicher lacks the full leverage to force a fait accompli over the ADGB—at least for now. But we remain cornered, with few good options left. A sizable minority, perhaps even a plurality, of unionists have already fallen under his sway. And his threat is clear: the Reichswehr’s militia stands ready to act if no decision is reached before the deadline. Our good relations have kept him from forcing the issue—so far—but his patience is running out. What shall we do?

schleicher_19.schleicher_adgb_choice_1.titleHtml: Approve the ADGB's entry into the DAF.
schleicher_19.schleicher_adgb_choice_1.bodyHtml: The ADGB is now being absorbed into the DAF, with its new chairmen wasting no time denouncing all ties to political parties and pledging loyalty solely to the nation. Marxist doctrine is stamped out, and the radical **SPD** elements are purged without ceremony. The fall of the ADGB marks the beginning of the end. If even the workers have abandoned us—what power do we have left?

schleicher_19.schleicher_adgb_choice_2.bodyHtml: Are you sure? We have lost our opportunity a long time ago, resistance at this point will be frivolous.

schleicher_19.schleicher_adgb_choice_2_p.bodyHtml: We are alone. Nonetheless, we will do everything in our power to launch a general strike and fill the street with protesters.

schleicher_19.schleicher_adgb_influence.bodyHtml: Schleicher now wields extensive influence over the **SPD**, and even greater sway within our affiliated trade union, the ADGB. Exploiting this grip—alongside a relentless psychological campaign among the rank-and-file and open intimidation by the Reichswehr militia, which threatens action if no decision is made before the deadline—Schleicher forces their submission to the German Labor Front—soon to be integrated. The new ADGB chairmen waste no time: they denounce all ties to political parties and pledge loyalty to nothing but the nation. Marxist doctrine is stamped out, and the radical **SPD** members are purged without ceremony. The fall of the ADGB marks the beginning of the end. If even the workers no longer stand with us—what power do we really have left?

schleicher_19.schleicher_adgb_joever.bodyHtml: With Schleicher lacking the influence to influence the ADGB chairmen personally, or having the adequate relations with us to negotiate a more peaceful solution, violence is the only option. Across the country, ADGB offices are ransacked by the far-right paramilitaries and the Reichswehr, arresting leaders, confiscating funds, and repurposing offices to be used for the DAF. The fall of the ADGB marks the beginning of the end. If even the workers have abandoned us—what power do we have left?

schleicher_19.spd_lose.bodyHtml: The general strike proves short-lived. An endless supply of unemployed strikebreakers and Schleicher's own sympathizers within the unions render it largely ineffective. Protesters are shot, civilians killed. The Reichsbanner is no match for the Reichswehr. Seizing the moment, Schleicher expands his crackdown, accusing the **SPD** of conspiring with the **Communists** to incite revolution. Germany is lost.

schleicher_19.spd_med.titleHtml: Schleicher attempts to negotiate with us.
schleicher_19.spd_med.bodyHtml: The nationwide general strike against Schleicher's authoritarian regime has brought the country to a standstill. The chancellor could unleash the Reichswehr and far-right paramilitaries to brutally crush the protests—but for now, that remains a last resort. Instead, Schleicher has chosen to open negotiations with the opposition. Meanwhile, in defiance of the indefinite adjournment of the Reichstag, the republican parties have banded together to unofficially reconvene the chamber at a separate location, openly challenging federal authority. However, perhaps we have overestimated our strength—strikes rarely last with unemployment so high, especially with Schleicher’s sympathizers embedded within the unions themselves.

schleicher_2.titleHtml: Maintain the funding of the Reichsbanner.
schleicher_2.bodyHtml: It's good to maintain our own self-defense organization, just in case.

schleicher_2_dnf.bodyHtml: With Schleicher’s backing, the dissident factions have been absorbed into the **DNVP**, which has been "encouraged" to reform itself into a Rechtsblock[? if not dnvp_dnef:, and strong-armed into joining the German National Unity Front as well?], firmly aligned with the Schleicher government. Hugenberg is now left with his tiny **DNF**—no friends, no funds, and no influence on the national stage. There’s a strong chance he’ll give up entirely. But for now, he stubbornly clings on onto whatever influence he has left in his media empire. schleicher_2_pro.titleHtml: Go along with the Center's proposal.
schleicher_2_pro.bodyHtml: The unification of the labor unions has complicated Schleicher's efforts to divide and conquer, depriving him of the option to play the more moderate unions against the ADGB. We have also agreed to coordinate unified action in response to any offensive measures his government may attempt in the coming months.

schleicher_2.nay.titleHtml: Force the Reichsbanner to reject this offer, and persuade them to cut off communications with the general.
schleicher_2.nay.bodyHtml: Our explicit rejection of Reichsbanner participation in the program has caused discontent within both the ADGB and the Reichsbanner, who have nonetheless reluctantly yielded to the party leadership’s decision. As a socialist party, we cannot lend our support to what is, in essence, a thinly veiled rearmament scheme.

schleicher_2.wait.titleHtml: Persuade the Reichsbanner to remain non-committal for now, at before until the next election.
schleicher_2.wait.bodyHtml: We have secured a commitment from the Reichsbanner leadership not to make any official decision regarding participation in the *Reichskuratorium* before the upcoming elections—a compromise between the party factions. However, some local members may still choose to enroll in the training programs on their own initiative.

schleicher_2.yay.titleHtml: Approve the participation of the Reichsbanner and our youth organizations in the *Reichskuratorium*.
schleicher_2.yay.bodyHtml: The Reichsbanner is now officially participating in the Reich Institute to Promote Youth Fitness. Their board of trustees, with our input, has swiftly established infantry and naval training schools across the country. Reichsbanner youth are the primary recipients of specialized instruction from former and decommissioned Reichswehr officers, and we have secured considerable influence within the institute’s leadership. This program has strengthened the Reichsbanner and improved our relations with von Schleicher. However, our collaboration with an initiative authorized by the deeply unpopular [+ chancellor +] government has cost us support—many have defected to the **Communists**.

schleicher_20.subtitleHtml: The veterans organization is integrated into the state.
schleicher_20.bodyHtml: = Schleicher and the **Stahlhelm** The **Stahlhelm**, a veterans' and paramilitary organization that shares much of Schleicher's worldview and commands his respect, has long been courted by the chancellor for cooperation with the Reichswehr. To this end, Schleicher plans to subsidize the organization with state funds, gradually making it dependent on the state and available for use. Still, the general is irritated that its military exercises often overshadow the numerically inferior Reichswehr. Despite their shared views, **Stahlhelm** leaders Franz Seldte and Theodor Duesterberg remain wary of Schleicher’s encroachments on their independence. But with the **DNVP** now folded into the **DNEF**, the organization finds itself politically isolated, as even its rank-and-file begin to drift into subordination.

schleicher_20.schleicher_2.bodyHtml: Subordination is the last thing a self-proud veterans' organization like the **Stahlhelm** would accept—but attempts by its leaders to resist have only backfired. At a leadership conference between national and local chapters, they conceded that the era of paramilitaries and political maneuvering is over, and agreed to align the organization with the state in service of the national interest. In return, the **Stahlhelm** is granted official status as a veterans' association, while sympathetic leaders are rewarded with government posts. Many of its seasoned fighters and officers are absorbed into the Reichswehr, where they will be tasked with training the next generation of recruits.

schleicher_21.subtitleHtml: We handed Schleicher too much influence over us.
schleicher_21.bodyHtml: = The **SPD** Slips Away Low-ranking party members loyal to Schleicher have steadily climbed the ranks, until a new executive committee finally replaces the old guard that had served the party since the founding of the republic. At its head now stand Schleicher’s yes-men—figures like the notorious former Defense Minister Gustav Noske and Lothar Erdmann, a nationalist voice within the ADGB, fiercely hostile to the Treaty of Versailles and far closer to Schleicher’s ideology than the mere pragmatism of Braun or Leipart. The German National Unity Front welcomes its new member.

schleicher_22.subtitleHtml: Strasser realizes he has fallen into Schleicher’s trap.
schleicher_22.bodyHtml: = **DSU** Breaks with Schleicher Despite their pragmatism, the **DSU** are still Nazis at heart, clinging fully to their wicked ideology. Fortunately, despite entering government, they’ve found no path to revive their own party, nor a chance to strike at the Jews they claim hoard the nation’s wealth, or the capitalist system they rail against. Now, a bitter realization dawns on Strasser and his top Nazi lieutenants: they’ve been used. Schleicher has no intention of letting them control anything beyond the Interior Ministry. Worse, their party has been bleeding support in local elections, punished for failing to deliver on its grand promises. After all, it’s Schleicher the people thank for their jobs—not the **DSU**, whose fights with the Bolsheviks do little to put food on the table for their electoral base. The formation of the **DNEF** has only deepened the wound, as many of their former voters flock to this new pole of order and stability.

choices.labelHtml: Out of funds, out of followers, out of luck.

schleicher_22.schleicher_2.bodyHtml: The various Nazi splinter parties that have emerged are now beginning to collapse entirely. Burdening such a dynamic, revolutionary movement with the compromises of government—and failing to deliver real solutions to their base’s hardships—has sapped their morale and dried up donations. Overcome with resignation, Strasser announces his withdrawal from political life, intending to return to his old profession as a local pharmacist. Many other top Nazi figures follow suit, as [+ nsdap_leader +] remains too paranoid and vengeful to allow any splitters back into the **NSDAP**. The **DSU** has since fallen under the control of a radical clique of self-styled "national bolsheviks" surrounding Gregor Strasser’s more extreme brother, Otto Strasser. Yet only a handful of fanatics remain in this rump organization, while the "tamed" Nazis drift into the ranks of the **DNEF**, including most of its parliamentary delegation.

schleicher_23.subtitleHtml: A new faction takes shape within the **SPD**...
schleicher_23.bodyHtml: = Social Patriotism Emerges A newer faction of young and old socialists, led by ADGB unionist Lothar Erdmann, is rallying under the banner of "Social Patriotism." This group calls for a renewed bond between the workers, socialism, and the nation. Erdmann is the architect of the ADGB's nationalist shift in recent years, including its sharpened rhetoric against the Treaty of Versailles. This is plainly Schleicher’s handiwork—yet this emerging faction now holds real sway within our party, given the Chancellor’s grip on our more "patriotic" and loosely Marxist trade unions.

choices.labelHtml: Who said patriotism and socialism aren't compatible?
There's no war but the class war.

schleicher_23.socpat_against.bodyHtml: The Social Patriots advocate full support for Schleicher’s chancellorship and his rearmament program, believing that only through strength can Germany break free from the chains of Versailles and reclaim its rightful lands. Schleicher is displeased with our moves to curb the influence of his loyalists within the **SPD** — but for now, this ideology remains far from our party’s leadership. For now.

schleicher_23.socpat_pro.bodyHtml:
The Social Patriots advocate full support for Schleicher’s chancellorship and his rearmament program, believing that only through strength can Germany break free from the chains of Versailles and reclaim its rightful lands.
Schleicher, predictably, is pleased with our acceptance of this new political current—but his influence within our party is growing alarmingly fast. Perhaps too fast.

schleicher_3.titleHtml: Defund the Reichsbanner; the threat is no longer present.
schleicher_3.bodyHtml: With the Reichswehr keeping order in the streets, we have no further need for the Reichsbanner's self-defense role. Better to spend our scarce funds on electoral propaganda rather than weapons.

schleicher_3.schleicher.titleHtml: Hear what the general has to say.
schleicher_3.schleicher.bodyHtml:
ADGB leaders Theodor Leipart and Wilhelm Eggert have met with Chancellor-designate Schleicher, who promised to rescind Papen’s most offensive emergency wage decrees, launch a public works program, and abandon the former chancellor’s plans to impose his “New State” via presidential decree.
We are pleasantly surprised by these concessions, and Schleicher has earned some goodwill among the union leadership. Still, deep distrust remains—after all, he was the one controlling Papen when those very decrees and the unconstitutional postponement of elections were proposed.
> *"Republic or monarchy is not the question now, but rather what should this republic look like."*
 - Kurt von Schleicher

schleicher_4.nay.bodyHtml: Our explicit rejection of Reichsbanner participation in the program has caused discontent within both the ADGB and the Reichsbanner, who have nonetheless reluctantly yielded to the party leadership’s decision. As a socialist party, we cannot lend our support to what is, in essence, a thinly veiled rearmament scheme.

Their board of trustees, with our input, has swiftly established infantry and naval training schools across the country. Reichsbanner youth are the primary recipients of specialized instruction from former and decommissioned Reichswehr officers, and we have secured considerable influence within the institute’s leadership. This program has strengthened the Reichsbanner and improved our relations with von Schleicher. However, our collaboration with an initiative authorized by the deeply unpopular [+ chancellor +] government has cost us support—many have defected to the **Communists**.

schleicher_5.subtitleHtml: We must either confirm or deny a supposed deal between the ADGB and the chancellor.
schleicher_5.bodyHtml: = Political Truce with Schleicher With Theodor Leipart’s announcement that he would support a Schleicher cabinet if Papen were the only alternative, numerous leaks have surfaced to the public—much to the annoyance of those in the **SPD**. Many workers still view Schleicher as merely a continuation of the despised Papen cabinet, and it remains in our electoral interest to uphold total opposition to him. Meanwhile, the ADGB has sought to shape Schleicher’s proposed public works program and fears that a parliamentary ousting would pave the way for Papen’s return. The specifics of our negotiations have been exaggerated—and in many cases, outright misreported—creating a serious public relations crisis among the **SPD**’s working-class base. What should our stance be moving forward?

schleicher_5.nay.titleHtml: Pure disinformation, we never discussed a 'political truce'.
schleicher_5.nay.bodyHtml: Such nonsense, we will deny the fake news and distance ourself from the chancellor to prevent more incidents.

schleicher_5.yay.bodyHtml: In a public statement, the ADGB stops short of denying rumors of a political truce, instead arguing that the chancellor should be given a few months free from parliamentary interference to implement his public works program. The move has been justified to the **SPD** leadership by claiming it would peel voters away from both the **Communists** and the Nazis, while benefiting the workers we represent. Needless to say, the union representing the very workers who suffered under his predecessor has lost credibility in their eyes.

schleicher_6.subtitleHtml: An unauthorized meeting, but perhaps a welcome one?
schleicher_6.bodyHtml: = Braun Meets With Schleicher Otto Braun, former Minister-President of Prussia and leader of our reformist wing, has—without informing the **SPD** leadership—met privately with Chancellor von Schleicher. Braun proposed cooperation, on the condition that Schleicher relinquish federal control over Prussia and restore him to office with full authority, including the power to dissolve the Landtag. Braun suggested that, together, they could rule by decree and wage a determined campaign against the Nazis. Schleicher, however, was unenthusiastic. Having led the Prussian coup himself, he is reluctant to undo the federal consolidation of power. More importantly, unlike Braun, he is not committed to weakening the **NSDAP**; he still views them as a potential source of support for his cabinet—admiring the **SA**’s militarism and the **NSDAP**’s fanatical discipline as traits to be co-opted into the state.

schleicher_6.nay.bodyHtml: Nothing ultimately comes of the meeting. However, Braun becomes the first major political figure outside the unions to openly signal willingness to strike a deal with the chancellor.
