schleicher_cabinet_8_alt.bodyHtml:
= Expansion of Public Works
Adam Stegerwald at the Labor Ministry, working closely with Günther Gereke, has been formulating a massive billion-mark public works program to expand on Schleicher’s previously modest efforts. They recognize that large-scale public projects and state spending are Germany’s path out of the slump—and Schleicher is eager to approve more to propel the nation back to great power status.
However, the chancellor has been persistently pressing his ministers to focus on rearmament and infrastructure that would support it—such as the construction of the Autobahn, a new nationwide highway system, and state funding for armament companies. To Schleicher’s frustration, however, most of the funds will still be directed toward civilian development.
Nonetheless, the economic recovery continues.

schleicher_cabinet_8_alt.reichsbank.titleHtml: The cabinet still requires the Reichsbank’s approval, however.
schleicher_cabinet_8_alt.reichsbank.subtitleHtml: Reichsbank President - [? if luther_reichsbank: Hans Luther?][? if not luther_reichsbank: Friedrich Dreyse?]

params.source: reichsbank_luther if luther_reichsbank; reichsbank_dreyse if not luther_reichsbank

schleicher_cabinet_8_alt.reichsbank_drey.bodyHtml:
The Reichsbank, long known for its strict fiscal conservatism and obsessive anti-inflation stance, had already slashed Schleicher's initial public works decree by 15%. So, it was no surprise when news of even greater government spending met with their disapproval.
However, the endorsement of the campaign by Hjalmar Schacht—a respected banker and recently retired Reichsbank President credited with ending hyperinflation—has done much to calm the business community. Under government pressure, the Reichsbank is ultimately coerced into backing the plan, though not without forcing another 20% cut in funding.

schleicher_cabinet_8.interior.titleHtml: The Nazis crack down on the Reichsbanner and **RFB**!
schleicher_cabinet_8.interior.subtitleHtml: Ordered by Wilhelm Frick of the Interior Ministry.

schleicher_cabinet_8.interior_1.bodyHtml: With the Nazis now controlling the Interior Ministry, they hold jurisdiction over the federal police. [? if prussia_leader != "Strasser": Without control of the Prussian Interior Ministry, their reach is limited—though they have already begun turning the federal police into a force loyal to the Nazis. ?][? if prussia_leader == "Strasser": The Prussian Interior Ministry, however, is the real prize—its police force now answers entirely to them, with widespread purges of republican officials taking place. ?]Fortunately, Schleicher has barred Nazi Party members from joining the police, maintaining the same restriction already enforced in the Reichswehr. Lately, we have observed the police exclusively targeting Reichsbanner and **RFB** fighters, while openly shielding far-right demonstrations from our protests. They have even persuaded Schleicher to transfer command of the Reichswehr's militia to the Interior Ministry, citing the need for centralized control.

schleicher_cabinet_8.interior_2.bodyHtml: The Nazis have continued cracking down on even lawful leftist activity, on bogus claims of "inciting violence." It seems Frick is doing Schleicher's dirty work for him—cracking down on democrats and all, while Schleicher is still viewed highly in the eyes of many workers.

schleicher_cabinet_8.works.subtitleHtml: Ordered by Hjalmar Schacht of the Economic Ministry.
schleicher_cabinet_8.works.bodyHtml: Despite Hjalmar Schacht not being a Keynesian, he understands that large scale public works and state funded projected are the way out of Germany's slump, and for Germany to retake its great power status on the international stage. He believes that, since France and Britain are preoccupied with their own economic woes, the time is right for a mass industrialization and rearmament program. The construction of the "Autobahn", a new nationwide highway system, by poorly paid workers has begun, as an expansion of Schleicher's public works plans. A new innovative method for disguising rearmament has also been devised, a "MEFO bill", a system of promissory notes issued through a dummy company to secretly fund arms production while keeping the spending off the official government budget. However, he insists that a revival of Germany's economy should take precedent over rearmament.

schleicher_cabinet_8.works_alt.subtitleHtml: Ordered by Hjalmar Schacht of the Economic Ministry.
schleicher_cabinet_8.works_alt.bodyHtml:
Despite the public works campaign being expanded before Hjalmar Schacht took office as Economic Minister, he now seeks to build upon it—transforming it into a mass industrialization and rearmament program, more closely aligned with Schleicher's ambitions. Only then, he argues, can Germany hope to rival the major powers.
An innovative new method for disguising rearmament has also been devised: the "MEFO bill," a system of promissory notes issued through a dummy company to secretly finance arms production while keeping the spending off the official government books. Nevertheless, Schacht insists that reviving Germany's economy must take precedence over rearmament—for now.

schleicher_cabinet_9.subtitleHtml: The Christian and Free Unions are ecstatic!
schleicher_cabinet_9.bodyHtml: = Schleicher Enacts Concessions to Labor! Presumably aiming to win over the unions' affiliated parties—the Center Party and the SPD—and to bolster public confidence in his leadership at the grassroots level, Schleicher has enacted a new decree. An eight-hour workday is now mandated across most industries, intended to "spread out" employment among more workers. The means test for unemployment insurance has been abolished, and welfare funding has been increased to offset years of austerity. The Social General has lived up to his nickname. Yet, cynically, the cost is clear—Schleicher now wields significant leverage over the unions, and many workers are beginning to shift their loyalty toward the chancellor, who delivers results, rather than the opposition parties. His image as a strongman, standing above the old parties, is slowly conditioning the workers to accept a more authoritarian system.

schleicher_cabinet_9.labor.titleHtml: The decree is signed into law.
schleicher_cabinet_9.labor.bodyHtml: With Schleicher granting concessions to the workers on his own initiative—rather than under pressure from the SPD—he alone reaps the political rewards. Even some radicalized Communist workers begin to drift away, as the less ideological and politically disengaged prioritize their livelihoods over loyalty to their traditional parties. But hey, at least the workers aren’t suffering as much anymore. This alone has led the ADGB to adopt a friendlier stance toward the chancellor, giving Schleicher growing influence within our party, using the unions as his middleman.

schleicher_dead.titleHtml: Schleicher isn't the only one in bad health.
schleicher_dead.subtitleHtml: President Hindenburg will not survive the year as well.
schleicher_dead.bodyHtml:
President Hindenburg, now 86, is reportedly stricken with numerous ailments—bladder cancer, heart disease, and other suspected conditions kept from the public eye. Bedridden at his Neudeck estate, he requires constant care.
Two men of a fading generation are nearing their end.

schleicher_distance.bodyHtml: In recent months, Schleicher has gained significant sympathizers within the Reformist and Labor factions of the **SPD**. Sidelining them would provoke Schleicher’s distrust and stir dissent within their factions affected.

schleicher_dsu.titleHtml: Schleicher invites the **DSU** into cabinet?
schleicher_dsu.bodyHtml: Despite their addition barely doing much to grant Schleicher a majority, it signals a major step toward Schleicher's goal of integrating "favorable" Nazis into the state—as he acknowledges that this is how much he's going to get. Their poor electoral performance will grant them few cabinet posts, but there remains substantial risks in letting the Nazis govern. We could attempt to use our relations with the chancellor to prevent this, but he'll demand much concessions in return.

schleicher_dsu_nay.subtitleHtml: This is a point of no return.
schleicher_dsu_nay.bodyHtml: Exploiting our unusually good relations with the chancellor, we have moved to strike a deal with him to block Nazi entry into the cabinet. We have threatened mass action by organized labor and the withdrawal of the Reichsbanner from his plans. Yet Schleicher sees greater advantage in aligning with the Nazis regardless, and we are negotiating from a position of weakness. What shall we give up?

schleicher_dsu_nay_2.titleHtml: The **DSU** is kept away from government!
schleicher_dsu_nay_2.subtitleHtml: The Center Party has been flirting with a return to governance.
schleicher_dsu_nay_2.bodyHtml: Schleicher has suspended talks with the **DSU** by deliberately creating an impasse over control of the Interior Ministry. In the meantime, the absence of Nazis in the cabinet has made it tolerable for the Center Party to return to government, with Adam Stegerwald securing the Labor Ministry and the nominal Vice Chancellorship, alongside other members claiming the Transport and Justice portfolios. The **BVP** is also granted the Postal Ministry. [? if z_leader == "Kaas": Schleicher has also secured Ludwig Kaas's backing by promising the immediate negotiation of a Reichskonkordat with the Vatican. ?] [? if old_prussia_leader == "Schleicher": The Prussian Reichskommissar post is also handed from Schleicher to Goerdeler—a signal that Schleicher has genuinely abandoned Papen's scheme for state centralization, and gestures toward an eventual return to democratic governance once stability is restored. Braun is overjoyed at this, and argues that only a break with Schleicher would change his mind. ?] The liberals and minor bourgeois parties have also rallied behind Schleicher once again. As part of our arrangement, he acknowledges the **SPD**'s need to remain in opposition—a necessary measure, as a **Communist** surge is an outcome neither of us desires.

schleicher_dsu_yay.subtitleHtml: Schleicher will moderate their excesses, it's still a presidential government after all.
schleicher_dsu_yay.bodyHtml: Wilhelm Frick is nominated to the Interior Ministry[? if old_prussia_leader == "Schleicher": in both the Reich and Prussia, with the latter now under the control of [+ prussia_leader +], appointed as commissioner?]. Gregor Strasser takes the vice-chancellorship—a title without power. At the Nazis’ insistence, Hjalmar Schacht is named to the Economic Ministry as an independent. Hans Kerrl, a Nazi parliamentarian, receives the post of Minister without Portfolio. Schleicher blocks Nazi claims to the Labor Ministry, unwilling to provoke organized labor and still hoping to bring Adam Stegerwald—and the Center Party—into his coalition.

schleicher_failed.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, the coalition supporting the dissolution of the Reichstag does not constitute a majority. There will be elections as scheduled.

schleicher_influence_unlock.bodyHtml: = Schleicher's Influence Although Schleicher insists he has no intention of establishing a military dictatorship and claims the Reichswehr is merely stabilizing the nation in its time of need, we suspect he is maneuvering to consolidate power. This, of course, involves the infiltration of his supporters into the ADGB and the quiet persuasion of **SPD** leaders through shady deals and under-the-table arrangements. It is already evident that our decision-making is being compromised.

schleicher_labor.titleHtml: The ADGB falls under state influence.
schleicher_labor.subtitleHtml: Class collaborationism will undermine the workers' power.
schleicher_labor.bodyHtml: We have convinced the ADGB to appoint some sketchy pro-Schleicher unionists to many top positions in the organization. Only time will tell what Schleicher will instruct his followers to do, but we can guess it has something to do with class solidarity for the goal of Germany's rearmament. The working class is not entirely won over to the chancellor yet, and we stand to lose significant numbers of them to the **KPD**.

schleicher_majority_coalition.titleHtml: Schleicher forms a majority government with only the **DNEF**.
schleicher_majority_coalition.bodyHtml: Immediately after the election, the chancellor abandoned both dialogue and the appearance of cordiality with the other political parties. Power is his, and he intends to keep it. Without the constraints of the parliamentary system, he can do whatever he pleases. Only the collapse of his delicately built house of cards could topple a **DNEF** majority government.

schleicher_majority_coalition_prussia.titleHtml: Schleicher forms a majority government with only the **DNEF**.
schleicher_majority_coalition_prussia.bodyHtml: With a majority in Prussia as well, Schleicher tightens his grip behind a democratic façade. The Prussian police are reshaped further to serve his purposes, and the government now sets education policy. A new curriculum is imposed, centered on discipline, nationalism, and hostility to socialism.

choices.labelHtml: Adopt a policy of cooperation with the Red General!
Push the party toward a more cooperative line with von Schleicher.
Reiterate our opposition against the reactionaries.
Reiterate our opposition against the reactionaries.

schleicher_nay.titleHtml: Schleicher's words cannot be trusted, he'll backstab us at any moment.
schleicher_nay.bodyHtml: We have rejected Schleicher’s request for a meeting. His offer is simply too good to be true, and aligning ourselves with a militarist and reactionary like him would betray everything we stand for.

schleicher_reichsbanner.titleHtml: The Reichsbanner is integrated into the state.
schleicher_reichsbanner.bodyHtml: The Reichsbanner has been largely disarmed, with Schleicher promising increased funding for the police to maintain order in the streets. The **SPD** is demoralized, as many Reichsbanner members defect to the **KPD** and their **RFB**. We are now compelled to back the Reichswehr's auxiliaries in their campaigns against the **Communists**.

schleicher_reichstag_1.bodyHtml: = Reichstag Reconvenes Schleicher’s first test with the Reichstag comes immediately after his appointment, and he's expected to lose by a wide margin. To head off defeat, he offered Gregor Strasser of the **NSDAP** the vice chancellorship and control of Prussia, hoping Strasser could persuade the party to tolerate his government. However, [+ nsdap_leader +] would only accept the obedient Göring as leader. Nonetheless, despite the **NSDAP**’s uncompromising stance, they are seeking a respite—pushing for an early holiday recess and delaying any immediate showdown with the newly appointed cabinet.

schleicher_reichstag_1.reichstag.titleHtml: The **Communists** put forth a motion of no confidence.
schleicher_reichstag_1.reichstag.bodyHtml: The motion is defeated! In a surprise to the public, the **Communist** proposal to prioritize a no-confidence vote is voted down—thanks to support from the Nazis. But this is no act of reconciliation; it’s certainly not the toleration Schleicher deludes himself into believing stems from his connections with Strasser. In any case, after clearing a few remaining bills, the chamber agrees to a holiday recess of indefinite duration.

schleicher_reichstag_1.reichstag_2.titleHtml: Papen's decree on wages is repealed!
schleicher_reichstag_1.reichstag_2.bodyHtml: Schleicher has given his consent for the Reichstag to repeal one of Papen's more egregious decrees that had particulary offended the labor unions, as part of his prior promise and to calm their fury against the government.

schleicher_reichstag_2.titleHtml: The Reichstag Agenda Committee Discusses a Reconvocation
schleicher_reichstag_2.subtitleHtml: The chancellor is surprisingly eager to reopen the chamber.
schleicher_reichstag_2.bodyHtml: = Reichstag Reconvocation Decision Behind closed doors, the Reichstag’s agenda committee convenes to decide when to reconvene the chamber after the holiday break—and with our position on it, our spokesmen have a say. Representing the cabinet, Schleicher’s aide strikes a confident tone, declaring the government ready to face the chamber at any time—and even opposing any adjournment until no-confidence motions are dealt with. In response, the **Communists** table a motion to resume sessions early next week. [? if reichstag_president == "Göring": But the Nazi spokesmen show no interest, suggesting the decision be left to the Reichstag’s president, Göring—who, in the end, fails to gain backing from any other party. ?][? if reichstag_president != "Göring": But the Nazi spokesmen show no interest, and would rather back the Center Party's compromise motion. ?] The question is, how should our representatives vote?

schleicher_reichstag_2.reichstag_1.titleHtml: Vote for the **Communist** motion to reconvene the chamber.
schleicher_reichstag_2.reichstag_1.bodyHtml: We must bring down the Schleicher cabinet as soon as possible. But the **SPD** and the **Communists** lack the votes on the committee to push the proposal through, as the Nazis vote it down. Instead, the Center Party offers a compromise: the Reichstag will reconvene early in Week [+ next_reichstag_week +], [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], with the condition that the committee will reexamine the matter one week prior. This is accepted by all parties.

schleicher_reichstag_2.reichstag_2.titleHtml: Vote for the Nazi motion to grant responsibility to Göring.
schleicher_reichstag_2.reichstag_2.bodyHtml: For some reason, we have pushed for the Nazi proposal of letting Göring be in charge. However, our spokesmen simply laughed in our face at our "joke", and voted for the **Communist** motion. Eventually, the Center Party steps in with a compromise: the Reichstag will reconvene early in Week [+ next_reichstag_week +], [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], on the condition that the committee revisits the matter one week beforehand. All parties accept this arrangement.

schleicher_reichstag_2.reichstag_3.titleHtml: Push for a compromise proposal (reconvene in three weeks, subject to review).
schleicher_reichstag_2.reichstag_3.bodyHtml: Together with the Center Party, our compromise proposal is accepted by all parties. The Reichstag will reconvene early in Week [+ next_reichstag_week +], [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], on the condition that the committee revisits the matter one week beforehand.

schleicher_reichstag_3.titleHtml: The Reichstag Agenda Committee Discusses Reconvocation
schleicher_reichstag_3.bodyHtml: = Reichstag Reconvocation Decision The Reichstag, which Schleicher had urged to reconvene as soon as possible, is set to revisit its earlier decision to reconvene next week. The outcome will determine when the inevitable confrontation between the Schleicher cabinet and a hostile parliament will occur. The **KPD** and **SPD** spokesmen support reconvening the chamber as planned, while the **NSDAP**'s spokesman, Wilhelm Frick, has adopted a noticeably less confrontational tone. Frick shares many of Strasser’s concerns about [+ nsdap_leader +]’s all-or-nothing stance and fears that a new election would bring disastrous Nazi losses. Yet even figures like Goebbels believe they need more time, and the top Nazi leaders have pushed Frick to propose delaying the reconvening until the cabinet can present its budget in a few months. [? if not schleicher_economy_time: Nevertheless, Schleicher appears determined to continue his unwise strategy of offense—pushing for an immediate showdown with the Reichstag in hopes that [+ nsdap_leader +] will shift position to avoid new elections or, failing that, that Hindenburg will grant him an emergency decree. ?][? if schleicher_economy_time: It is expected that Schleicher will reverse his earlier, unwise strategy of confrontation and instead lend his support to Frick's proposal. ?] In any case, there’s enough support among the other parties to pass Frick’s motion to extend the recess, rendering our vote irrelevant.

schleicher_reichstag_3.reichstag_1.bodyHtml: As expected, the objections raised by Schleicher’s spokesman—acting on direct orders—have sunk the Nazi motion. In response, the Center Party has introduced a compromise: a one-week extension of the recess to allow for further negotiations. Papen’s scheme has become considerably easier, as Schleicher is now forced to test the President’s support by requesting a decree to dissolve the Reichstag and postpone elections. But if Hindenburg denies the request, the question becomes unavoidable: who would succeed him? Papen? Hitler? Schleicher has squandered a critical opportunity to salvage his cabinet—and perhaps Germany itself. Had the elections been postponed just a few months, his position would likely have improved significantly. He stood to gain from the launch of Gereke’s public works program and the natural recovery of the global economy. Meanwhile, the Nazis, with no upcoming state elections to boost morale, would have been increasingly vulnerable to internal collapse—driven by mounting dissatisfaction with [+ nsdap_leader +] and the disintegration of the **SA**. None of this is to be.

schleicher_reichstag_3.reichstag_2.bodyHtml:
[? if not schleicher_economy_time: However, Schleicher, having learned about Frick's plans to delay the Reichstag's reconvocation, has had a sudden change of heart. A new round of war games—this time not rigged—has revealed that the Reichswehr cannot survive fighting against all paramilitaries[? if prussia_leader == "Schleicher":, even with the Prussian police?][? if prussia_leader != "Schleicher":, and the Prussian police force as well?]. Despite his efforts to strengthen the army with streetfighting equipment and training, the limited but well-trained force remains unable to withstand being heavily outnumbered. ?][? if schleicher_economy_time: Schleicher, seeking to benefit from his public works program before calling for confrontation in the Reichstag that'll likely lead to new elections, has decided that Frick's proposal is most prudent. ?]
[? if not schleicher_economy_time: The chancellor makes it clear that he still hopes [+ nsdap_leader +] might have a sudden change of heart, but with his backup plan no longer viable, he pushes for the adoption of Frick's proposal. ?] The Reichstag is now adjourned until [+ next_reichstag_month : month +] [+ next_reichstag_year +], Week [+ next_reichstag_week +], and Schleicher is expected to unveil his public works program during this time.

schleicher_reichstag_4.titleHtml: Schleicher Faces a Vote of No Confidence!
schleicher_reichstag_4.subtitleHtml: Without a decree at the ready, the chancellor is doomed.
schleicher_reichstag_4.bodyHtml: = Vote of No Confidence [? if schleicher_time == 7: Following a shortened holiday adjournment—cut short by Schleicher's own suicidal insistence—the Reichstag is finally reconvening to decide the fate of his government. With Hindenburg refusing to grant him the emergency decree that had previously allowed Papen to dissolve the chamber and delay elections, Schleicher's narrow base of support—comprising parties to the left of Hugenberg but to the right of the Center Party, along with the liberals—is nowhere near enough to salvage his cabinet. ?][? if schleicher_time > 7: Following the extended holiday adjournment—the Reichstag is finally reconvening to decide the fate of his government. With Hindenburg refusing to grant him the emergency decree that had previously allowed Papen to dissolve the chamber and delay elections, Schleicher's narrow base of support—comprising parties to the left of Hugenberg but to the right of the Center Party, along with the liberals—is nowhere near enough to salvage his cabinet. ?] [? if schleicher_time == 7: Since Schleicher has already resigned, the vote will have little practical effect, serving only to underscore how deeply unpopular he has become. New elections must now be held, with the **NSDAP** particularly vulnerable to losses due to their internal divisions and the recent rollout of public works programs. Still, they cannot oppose the vote for obvious reasons, even as they desperately seek to avoid facing the electorate again. ?][? if schleicher_time > 7: This vote will only underscore his deep unpopularity and cripple his chances of pursuing meaningful policy during his remaining time as caretaker. New elections must now be held, with the **NSDAP** particularly vulnerable to losses due to their internal divisions and the recent success of public works programs. Still, they cannot oppose the vote for obvious reasons, even as they desperately seek to avoid facing the electorate again. ?]

schleicher_reichstag_4.reichstag.bodyHtml: Once again, the **Communists** push forward a vote of no confidence against Schleicher—and it passes, with [+ anti_schleicher_votes +]% of the Reichstag voting in favor. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": He is backed only by the various bourgeois parties positioned between the **DNVP** and the liberals[? if dvp_exist and not lvp_formed:, along with the **DVP**, which seeks to gain by standing as the only "[? if not kvp_formed: relevant?][? if kvp_formed: middle?]" pro-government party?]. ?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": He is backed only by the **DNVP**, along with the various right-wing parties situated between it and the liberals[? if dvp_exist and not lvp_formed:, and the **DVP**?]. ?][? if dstp_maintained: The **[+ ddp_name +]** has also backed the chancellor, with significant overlap in their respective views potentially paving way for the integration of the Young German Order into the state. ?][? if dsu_exist and dsu_r: The **DSU**, casting their first vote in parliament, has also backed the chancellor—signaling their goodwill and potential future support. ?] [? if not constructive_schleicher: Hindenburg will likely refuse to grant Schleicher additional emergency decrees, effectively reducing the chancellor to a lame duck. The President views Schleicher as a simple caretaker until negotiations between [+ nsdap_chancellor +] and the Camarilla concludes. ?][? if constructive_schleicher: Schleicher chooses to disregard the no-confidence vote, insisting he will only resign if a constructive majority unites behind an alternative candidate—something that has yet to occur. Fierce criticism follows from the **NSDAP** and **KPD**, while the republican parties express cautious approval. Still, his survival hinges on the tolerance of an increasingly impatient Hindenburg, who remains susceptible to Papen's maneuvering. ?] New Reichstag elections are scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +], Week [+ next_election_week +].

schleicher_reichstag_5.subtitleHtml: The Reichstag hesitates to confront Schleicher and trigger yet another round of elections.
schleicher_reichstag_5.bodyHtml:
= Reichstag Reconvenes
The Reichstag reconvenes under Schleicher, and nearly all parties present are unwilling to move against the popular chancellor on the chamber’s first day back. The opposition chooses to wait, looking for the inevitable misstep—a constitutional violation or a divisive policy—to use as a pretext and rallying point against him.
Meanwhile, Schleicher shows little concern over the threat of a no-confidence vote. He makes his position clear: unless a united bloc emerges with a viable successor, he will continue governing as usual, backed by Hindenburg.

schleicher_reichstag_5.reichstag.titleHtml: The **Communists** put forth a motion of no confidence.
schleicher_reichstag_5.reichstag.bodyHtml: As before, the motion to place a vote of no confidence on the agenda is defeated—thanks to support from elements of the Nazis, the Center Party, and various right-wing and bourgeois factions. With only a handful of bills scheduled, the agenda committee successfully pushes through a thirty-day adjournment, with the option for extension.

schleicher_reichstag_6.subtitleHtml: Schleicher has a decree to present.
schleicher_reichstag_6.bodyHtml:
= Reichstag Reconvenes
After the break cut short by Schleicher's insistence, the Reichstag is back in session. Reportedly, Schleicher has obtained Hindenburg's authorization for an unconstitutional decree, presumably in the vein of forcing the Reichstag's adjournment or cancelling new elections.
However, the situation has changed, Schleicher is much more popular and its expected that the backlash to an unconstitutional act will be more limited, and not be to the degree that it would provoke a civil war.

schleicher_reichstag_6.reichstag.bodyHtml: Schleicher immediately issues his decree to unconstitutionally adjourn the Reichstag indefinitely, declaring that the chamber will remain closed until the parties prove they can govern constructively again. Reactions inside the chamber are mixed: Schleicher's supporters applaud the chancellor’s show of strong leadership, while the **Communists** ignite brawls that police are forced to break up. In the following days, civil demonstrations are violently suppressed. Police disperse crowds with tear gas, street clashes erupt, and several civilians are killed. The strengthened Reichswehr and the divided stance of republicans make any serious rebellion futile. At least half of the **Communist** deputies in the Reichstag are arrested and sent to special courts for inciting violence. The **SPD** remains largely untouched[? if rb_militancy > 0.1:, though suspicious activity has been reported to be planned against the Reichsbanner?].

schleicher_reichstag_7.subtitleHtml: Schleicher faces a vote of no confidence!
schleicher_reichstag_7.bodyHtml:
= Reichstag Reconvenes
Let's cut to the chase.

schleicher_reichstag_7.reichstag.titleHtml: A vote of no confidence is introduced against Schleicher.
schleicher_reichstag_7.reichstag.bodyHtml:
It succeeds.
New Reichstag elections are scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +], Week [+ next_election_week +].

schleicher_reichstag_8.bodyHtml: = Snap Elections Called Chancellor Schleicher and the **DNEF** now see an opportunity to dramatically boost their seat share in fresh elections—paving the way to consolidate power and govern outright with only the loyal **DSU**, free from parliamentarianism. New Reichstag elections are scheduled for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +], Week [+ next_election_week +].

schleicher_reichstag_8.prussia_election.titleHtml: Schleicher pressures [+ prussia_leader +] for a double dissolution.
schleicher_reichstag_8.prussia_election.bodyHtml: Schleicher communicates to [+ prussia_leader +] that a double dissolution of the chambers of the Reich and Prussia is necessary for the legislature of the former to be accurate to the updated opinions of the people. The threat of federal action is also present.

schleicher_success.bodyHtml:
# hack to set next election time
The scheme has succeeded - there is a majority in the Reichstag backing Schleicher. New elections have been tentatively set for [+ next_election_month : month +] [+ next_election_year +].

schleicher_ties.subtitleHtml: More regular meetings will be held between the two groups.
schleicher_ties.bodyHtml: Regular secret meetings between the ADGB, the **SPD**, and von Schleicher are being held. This will aid in reducing the mutual distrust between the party and the government.

schleicher_time.bodyHtml: Former Chancellor Brüning has been dismissed—despite commanding a parliamentary majority. It appears Schleicher has struck an unwritten deal with the **NSDAP**, promising “fruitful cooperation” with a new right-wing cabinet that[? if sa_nationwide_ban: lifted the ban on the **SA** and?] called for new Reichstag elections. It’s a shame that Schleicher would fall for [+ nsdap_leader +]’s lies. But the real question now is: who will succeed Brüning?

params.source: successor_menu

schleicher_yay.titleHtml: Desperate times calls for desperate measures.
schleicher_yay.subtitleHtml: We'll hear him out and see what he has to offer.
schleicher_yay.bodyHtml: We have agreed to meet with Schleicher, who, alongside our affiliated trade unions, supports the WTB Plan. However, he has one key demand: a revitalization of the military industry and an increase in army funding. This would require shifting public work funds away from infrastructure and civic development toward military production and Germany’s rearmament. He also stipulates that the **SPD** must support Hindenburg's reelection campaign. In his view, revitalizing both the economy and the Reichswehr is essential for Germany’s return to great power status. Schleicher claims that our progress in negotiating a pause in reparations—along with our willingness to turn a blind eye to militarism—has earned his trust. Now, the decision is ours. Do we accept his offer?

schleicher_yay_2.titleHtml: We are defenseless—defenseless and without honor.
schleicher_yay_2.subtitleHtml: This is the point of no return.
schleicher_yay_2.bodyHtml:
We have been given one year to implement the WTB Plan, and Schleicher—once an active schemer calling for Hindenburg to dismiss the [+ chancellor +] government—is now working to prevent Hindenburg from dismissing us. Unfortunately, Schleicher has failed to convince Hindenburg to grant us emergency powers.
The public hasn’t noticed—at least, not yet. We must immediately begin implementing the WTB Plan.

schleichers_schemes.subtitleHtml: Chancellor Schleicher claims to have a plan to save Germany...
schleichers_schemes.bodyHtml:
#tags: event
= Schleicher's Schemes
Chancellor Kurt von Schleicher claims to have a plan to save Germany, and he has reached out to the Social Democrats with vague promises. He claims that in order to govern, the Reichstag must be temporarily suspended to prevent the Nazis and Communists from disrupting government, in effect giving him and Hindenburg dictatorial powers. In the meantime, he is enacting a public works program and job creation plan, which he claims will stabilize the economy, 
[? if works_program <= 0: The trade unions are somewhat favorable to Schleicher's plan, as they see a commonality between Schleicher's economic plan and the ADGB's WTB-plan for debt-funded job creation. However, the rest of our party is vehemently against Schleicher. ?]
Rumors are that Schleicher is also reaching out to the Nazis with similar promises of cooperation; he seems to believe that he can "tame" the Nazis. Most in our party do not trust him to not bring the Nazis to power. In addition, working with him would essentially mean the end of our claim to be a "democratic" party.
# if this works: delay elections by 1 year (requires over 50% support - need Z and DVP and others to join as well based on relations; DNVP might support? Also should depend on Hindenburg relations).

schleichers_wtb.subtitleHtml: General Kurt von Schleicher contacts our party...
schleichers_wtb.bodyHtml: #tags: event = Schleicher's Proposal General Kurt von Schleicher, head of the Reichswehr's Office of Ministerial Affairs and a major member of President Hindenburg's inner circle, has requested a meeting with the **SPD**'s leadership. The Red General, as he is called, has established contact with our trade unions, supporting our public works projects over austerity and deflationary policies. He claims that he can put in a good word for us and our WTB Plan to President Hindenburg—perhaps even securing its passage through emergency powers. However, Schleicher is a known schemer and a staunch anti-leftist. Should we trust what he has to say?

schleichers_wtb.schleicher_nay.titleHtml: Schleicher's words cannot be trusted, he'll backstab us at any moment.
schleichers_wtb.schleicher_nay.bodyHtml: We have rejected Schleicher’s request for a meeting. His offer is simply too good to be true, and aligning ourselves with a militarist and reactionary like him would betray everything we stand for.

schleichers_wtb.schleicher_yay.titleHtml: Desperate times calls for desperate measures.
schleichers_wtb.schleicher_yay.subtitleHtml: We'll hear him out and see what he has to offer.
schleichers_wtb.schleicher_yay.bodyHtml: We have agreed to meet with Schleicher, who, alongside our affiliated trade unions, supports the WTB Plan. However, he has one key demand: a revitalization of the military industry and an increase in army funding. This would require shifting public work funds away from infrastructure and civic development toward military production and Germany’s rearmament. He also stipulates that the **SPD** must support Hindenburg's reelection campaign. In his view, revitalizing both the economy and the Reichswehr is essential for Germany’s return to great power status. Schleicher claims that our progress in negotiating a pause in reparations—along with our willingness to turn a blind eye to militarism—has earned his trust. Now, the decision is ours. Do we accept his offer?

schleichers_wtb.schleicher_yay_2.titleHtml: We are defenseless—defenseless and without honor.
schleichers_wtb.schleicher_yay_2.subtitleHtml: This is the point of no return.
schleichers_wtb.schleicher_yay_2.bodyHtml:
We have been given one year to implement the WTB Plan, and Schleicher—once an active schemer calling for Hindenburg to dismiss the [+ chancellor +] government—is now working to prevent Hindenburg from dismissing us. Unfortunately, Schleicher has failed to convince Hindenburg to grant us emergency powers.
The public hasn’t noticed—at least, not yet. We must immediately begin implementing the WTB Plan.

The right wing of the **DVP** was crippled in the events of their last congress, but managed to claw back into power. The left of the party still have some control over internal affairs and can dissuade them from their worse excesses. Needless to say, this is bad news for our relationship with the **DVP**, and makes the formation of future governments involving us more difficult[? if in_grand_coalition:, and the current government untenable?].

To undo this, the far right has called a plebiscite on a new constitutional amendment. Stormtroopers are in the streets, "convincing" voters to support their proposal. Germany is nearing civil war.

choices.labelHtml: We will fight the fascists in the streets!
We can only defeat the fascists through democratic means!

seldte_takes_power.bodyHtml: With Seldte and Hergt in charge of Germany, presiding over a far-right "New Harzburg" Coalition ruling by presidential decree, the beginning of the end is near. However, the two coalition parties have irreparable differences over the German monarchy and next steps, and with the nationalists having an edge over their dynamic peers, it seems that this arrangement won't last. Furthermore, it is anticipated that the current government will avoid any moves to restore the monarchy until after the 1935 referendum, and the cabinet must survive until then. What are we to do now?

choices.labelHtml: We will fight on the streets to prevent Seldte from consolidating power.
We will vote against the government in the Reichstag.

seldte_takes_power.fight.bodyHtml: Do we realize that this means civil war, against the full force of the state?

choices.labelHtml: We are not ready for war. Instead, we will vote against the government in the Reichstag.

settle_reparations.titleHtml: We will finally settle the reparations issues with the Western Allies!
settle_reparations.subtitleHtml: The issue of reparations and future payments will finally be resolved.
settle_reparations.bodyHtml: With our success in negotiating a pause in reparation payments, the Western Allies have been convinced of our sincere commitment to pacifism and distancing from militarism. Additionally, France's new left-wing Prime Minister has been considerably more amicable than their predecessor. As a result, we have secured their agreement to a conference aimed at finally settling the reparations issue. In the end, Germany is required to make only a final payment of three billion marks, effectively ending future reparation obligations. This has greatly boosted investor confidence and sparked a new wave of capital inflows to Germany. This has greatly eased tensions within our government, with our party receiving credit for the achievement—much to the detriment of the **NSDAP**, which had built much of its appeal on the narrative of Germany’s "national slavery."

shorten_hours.subtitleHtml: Could we induce more hiring and reduce unemployment by reducing work hours?
shorten_hours.bodyHtml: Some in the labor movement argue that by reducing the maximum number of hours worked, employers would be induced to hire more workers, reducing unemployment. The argument also goes that this would be complementary to deflation, maintaining the same purchasing power for workers by cutting hours without cutting wages. Employers, however, resist this policy, arguing for more flexibility in hiring and firing.

sign_concordat.bodyHtml: We have signed a Concordat between the Free State of Prussia and the Roman Catholic Church, guaranteeing religious freedom for Catholics in Prussia. Additionally, during [+ foreign_minister +]'s trip to Paris, there has been success in bringing the French to consider withdrawing from the Rhineland early and to agree to another review of our reparations by foreign experts.

situation.titleHtml: Point out the gains of the **NSDAP**, who have capitalized on our lack of a program.
situation.bodyHtml: The collapse in our electoral performance and loss of voters to the **KPD** and **NSDAP** have opened the party's eyes, and they are now ready to support our plan as a means to present a solution for the workers. With our hard work, we have finally convinced the majority of the party to adopt the WTB plan! [? if spd_in_government == 1 : We can begin implementing the plan as soon as possible, as long as we have the Economic and Finance ministries. ?][? if spd_in_government = 0 : We should emphasize the plan in our electoral propaganda. ?]

socchrist_prussia_collapse.bodyHtml: = Democratic Bulwark Dismantled We have somehow antagonized the Christians involved in the Social-Christian Coalition ruling over Prussia, and they have called a vote of no confidence against us. [? if spd_r_prussia + kpd_r_prussia + sapd_r_prussia < 50: The only alternative coalition that can be formed with the current composition of the state parliament is a broad right-wing coalition, ranging from the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] to the [? if center_right_coalition_prussia >= 50: **DNVP**?][? if center_right_coalition_prussia < 50: **NSDAP**?]. socchrist_prussia_collapse.center_right_.bodyHtml: A center-right coalition is formed featuring an broad array of parties to the right of us. They will begin undoing years of reform and democratization that we fought hard to achieve and will let right-wing paramilitaries like the Stahlhelm and the Nazi **SA** run free. It won't take long for the government to collapse and for us to take power through new elections. But when it eventually does, we won't have much allies as our former coalition partners are beginning to shift to the right. When the time comes, who will stand with us? [? if z_leader != "Stegerwald": Adam Stegerwald?][? if z_leader == "Stegerwald": Heinrich Brüning?] of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia.

socchrist_prussia_collapse.far_right_coa.bodyHtml: There are enough votes for the Nazis and the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP** ?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF** ?] to form a coalition. Hermann Göring is elevated to the position of Minister-President and immediately starts dismantling its democratic institutions. A wave of terror and repression unfolds, targeting the socialists and communists. Violence erupts in the streets, with bullets flying and leftists being killed or imprisoned.

socchrist_prussia_collapse.left_coalitio.titleHtml: Is a United Left coalition possible?
socchrist_prussia_collapse.left_coalitio.subtitleHtml: **SPD** + **KPD** [? if sapd_formed: + **SAPD** ?] ([+ left_coalition_prussia +]%)
socchrist_prussia_collapse.left_coalitio.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the left coalition is successfully formed, without appointing a communist as Minister-President. The consensus choice for Minister-President, accepted by the **SPD**, **KPD**, is[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work.. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

social_catholic_coalition_cvp.bodyHtml: We have enough votes to form a "Social-Christian Coalition" government consisting of the **SPD** and the **CVP**. However, whether the **[+ z_party_name +]**—filled with nationalist and staunchly anti-Marxist elements—would ever truly accept such a coalition is another matter entirely. Still, the mere fact that they are even willing to engage in talks is an encouraging early sign.

social_liberal_coalition_wurttemberg.bodyHtml: With the formation of the **[+ z_party_name +]**, combined with the state Center Party's longstanding hostility toward our participation in government, a coalition with them is entirely out of the question. social_welfare.bodyHtml: = Social Welfare Policy The social welfare program, including unemployment insurance, healthcare, and old-age care, is the proudest achievement of the **SPD** in our time in government. There is continuous pressure to dismantle the welfare system[? if black_thursday_seen = 1 :, especially given the economic crisis ?]. #- @cancel_advisor_action

soclib_prussia_collapse.far_right_coalit.bodyHtml: There are enough votes for the Nazis and the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP** ?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNF** ?] to form a coalition. Hermann Göring is elevated to the position of Minister-President and immediately starts dismantling its democratic institutions. A wave of terror and repression unfolds, targeting the socialists and communists. Violence erupts in the streets, with bullets flying and leftists being killed or imprisoned.

soclib_prussia_collapse.left_coalition.titleHtml: Is a United Left coalition possible?
soclib_prussia_collapse.left_coalition.subtitleHtml: **SPD** + **KPD** [? if sapd_formed: + **SAPD** ?] ([+ left_coalition_prussia +]%)
soclib_prussia_collapse.left_coalition.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the left coalition is successfully formed, without appointing a communist as Minister-President. The consensus choice for Minister-President, accepted by the **SPD**, **KPD**, is[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work.. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

socpat.bodyHtml: The social patriot wing of the party, widely regarded as Schleicher's puppets, is the most supportive of the **SPD** and ADGB adopting a more nationalist stance.

params.source: changed if changed = 1

socpat_against.bodyHtml: The Social Patriots advocate full support for Schleicher’s chancellorship and his rearmament program, believing that only through strength can Germany break free from the chains of Versailles and reclaim its rightful lands. Schleicher is displeased with our moves to curb the influence of his loyalists within the **SPD** — but for now, this ideology remains far from our party’s leadership. For now.

socpat_pro.bodyHtml:
The Social Patriots advocate full support for Schleicher’s chancellorship and his rearmament program, believing that only through strength can Germany break free from the chains of Versailles and reclaim its rightful lands.
Schleicher, predictably, is pleased with our acceptance of this new political current—but his influence within our party is growing alarmingly fast. Perhaps too fast.

something_1.bodyHtml: Speeches are made. Votes are held. Bullets fly in the streets. Some socialists are killed or jailed. Others flee the country. What can votes even do at this juncture? The Reichstag is burned, ostensibly by a foreign communist. In the wake, the Nazis pass decrees giving them unlimited power. They, combined with the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **DNVP**?][? if dnf_formed: **DNF**?], will win a majority at the next elections. [? if nsdap_chancellor != "Hitler": Hitler is bought back from Austria and appointed chancellor. ?]

soviet_aid.bodyHtml: We send a call for help to the Soviet Union. The **KPD** receives the bulk of the aid, while the Reichsbanner and our loyal military units are left floundering. If we win, this does not bode well for our future.

params.source: long_war_intervention

soviet_economic_aid_no.bodyHtml: The Soviets are slightly upset, but they seemed to expect this answer.

soviet_economic_aid_yes.bodyHtml: The Soviets are pleased that we have sent them aid, and have not asked for anything specific in exchange. Our coalition partners are less pleased.

choices.labelHtml: Ask if Moscow could help repair our relations with the **KPD**.
Do the Soviets know about the Wittorf Affair? Do they know that we know?

soviet_economic_aid_yes_mil.bodyHtml: The Soviets are pleased that we have sent them aid, and have agreed to help train our military. The Reichswehr appreciates our support.

soviet_union_aid.titleHtml: How will the Soviet Union respond?
soviet_union_aid.subtitleHtml: The country ironically funding the Reichswehr's secret rearmament.
soviet_union_aid.bodyHtml: Despite the Soviet Union perhaps being indirectly responsible by training the officers battling their **Communist** brethren on the streets, many Soviet politicians are privately outraged as fleeing **KPD** politicians spread the news of their party's dissolution. However, despite this, Stalin has adhered to his policy of secretly aiding Germany in its rearmament through officer training and supplying armament technology. Schleicher's fears have thus subsided for now, with Stalin having near complete control over his party.

params.source: game_over

spd.bodyHtml: [? if largest_party != "NSDAP": In Reichstag tradition, as the **SPD** is the largest party, the Center Party feels bound to support us, regardless of our relations. ?][? if (z_relation >= 55 or hitler_right_coalition < 50) and largest_party == "NSDAP": However, the Center Party simply cannot bring itself to support elevating a Nazi to the Reichstag presidency, breaking with tradition to elect our candidate. ?] [? if largest_party != "NSDAP" and ((weimar_coalition >= 40) or (popular_front_coalition >= 50 and kpd_relation >= 50)): Paul Löbe is elected President of the Reichstag once more, a position he held for the majority of the republic. ?][? if not (largest_party != "NSDAP" and ((weimar_coalition >= 40) or (popular_front_coalition >= 50 and kpd_relation >= 50))): Unfortunately, very few other parties are willing—or have the votes—to back our candidate, Paul Löbe, and the chamber instead settles on the Center's Thomas Eßer. ?] However, the Reichstag agenda committee, over our objections, has voted for a two-week adjournment with the support of the parties to our right.

spd_alone.bodyHtml: Whether it is because we *cannot* or *will not*, we do not make ties with other parties at this moment.

spd_boycott.subtitleHtml: The workers may have a different mindset.
spd_boycott.bodyHtml: The efficacy of our boycott depends on two key factors: party dissent and our control over labor. If the Schleicher-sympathetic factions within the unions and the party choose to vote for the **DNEF** regardless, our boycott will be in vain. spd_coalition.titleHtml: The **SPD** will form a coalition government with the bourgeois parties.
spd_coalition.subtitleHtml: The Bavarian Peasants’ League had a falling out right? Let's utilize our contacts with their left wing. -1 resource
spd_coalition.bodyHtml: Somehow, we have brought the [? if not lvp_formed and ddp_r_bavaria: **[+ ddp_name +]** and?][? if lvp_formed and lvp_r_bavaria: **LVP** and?] Bavarian Peasants’ League to the negotiating table, despite their preference for working with the **BVP**. Through connections with the left-wing and liberal factions within the Bavarian Peasants’ League, we have overcome their reluctance—and now, we are in government! Bavaria has been governed by the political right ever since 1921, and the **BVP** has often covered for reactionary political activity. Now, we are able to change that and counter the **SA** thugs roaming the streets [? if sa_nationwide_ban: and more aggressively enforce the national ban of the organization that the conservative Held government had mostly ignored ?].

spd_governmental_burden.bodyHtml:
= Burden of Government
The weight of governance now falls upon our shoulders. It is our responsibility to maintain the delicate balance of appeasing our coalition partners while advancing our party's agenda. Our voter base mainly consists of the working-class and the unemployed, they expect us to enact the following policies during our tenure, or we will suffer consequences. [? if labor_minister_party != "SPD": So far, ceding control of the Labor Ministry to the bourgeois parties has left a poor impression with the workers. ?]
[? if spd_in_government : - Expand social welfare programs. ?]
[? if spd_in_government : - Promote worker ownership of industries. ?]
[? if spd_in_government : - Lower taxes or shift the tax burden to the wealthy. ?]
[? if spd_in_government : - Support workers in labor disputes. ?]
[? if spd_in_government : - Fund unemployment insurance through employers. ?]
[? if spd_in_government: - Advance women's rights. ?]
[? if spd_in_government: - Reform or expand education for workers. ?]
[? if spd_in_government and black_thursday_seen : - Institute an economic plan. ?]
[? if spd_in_government : - Secure low food prices for workers. ?]
[? if spd_in_government : - Reduce funding for the Reichswehr. ?]
They will expect to see at least two goals fulfilled every six months, or we will lose some of their support. Committing to austerity or conservative policies will automatically fail the goals.

spd_governmental_burden_peoples.bodyHtml: = Burden of Government The weight of governance now falls upon our shoulders. It is our responsibility to maintain the delicate balance of appeasing our coalition partners while advancing our party's agenda. Our voter base consists of a broad array of different classes, but mainly consists of the working-class and the unemployed. They expect us to enact the following policies during our tenure, or we will suffer consequences. [? if labor_minister_party != "SPD": So far, ceding control of the Labor Ministry to the bourgeois parties has left a poor impression with the workers. ?] **Primary Goals** [? if spd_in_government : - Expand social welfare programs. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Promote worker ownership of industries. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Lower taxes or shift the tax burden to the wealthy. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Support workers in labor disputes. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Fund unemployment insurance through employers. ?] [? if spd_in_government: - Advance women's rights. ?] [? if spd_in_government: - Reform or expand education for workers. ?] [? if spd_in_government and black_thursday_seen : - Institute an economic plan. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Secure low food prices for workers. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Reduce funding for the Reichswehr. ?] **Secondary Goals** [? if spd_in_government and black_thursday_seen : - Promote the moderate reformist plan. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Cut taxes. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Be neutral in labor affairs. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Raise tariffs. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Increase science funding. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Take steps towards the European Union or national concordat. ?] [? if spd_in_government : - Assist the rural working class. ?] They will expect to see at least two primary and one secondary goal fulfilled every six months, or we will lose some of their support. Committing to austerity or conservative policies will automatically fail the primary goal. Committing to radical left-wing policies will automatically fail the secondary goal.

spd_lead.bodyHtml: The Reichstag has reconvened for the first time since the election, with a significantly larger contingent of **NSDAP** members now present. The immediate issue at hand is the election of the President of the Reichstag. While the position has traditionally been a procedural one, it has taken on heightened importance under Papen's presidential government, given the President's authority to influence the agenda and adjourn sessions. By long-standing custom, the role is granted to the largest parliamentary delegation. That delegation isn't the **NSDAP**, but the Center Party backing them nonetheless is a key part of negotiations between the two parties. Without such backing, it is likely that our candidate, Paul Löbe, would be elected once again.

spd_lose.bodyHtml: The general strike proves short-lived. An endless supply of unemployed strikebreakers and Schleicher's own sympathizers within the unions render it largely ineffective. Protesters are shot, civilians killed. The Reichsbanner is no match for the Reichswehr. Seizing the moment, Schleicher expands his crackdown, accusing the **SPD** of conspiring with the **Communists** to incite revolution. Germany is lost.

spd_majority.bodyHtml: Finally, the **SPD** can govern alone! Our long campaign of electioneering has paid off. We do not need to worry about coalition government; anything is possible. However, our former coalition partners are going to start drifting to the right. Braun is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia.

spd_majority_2.bodyHtml: Finally, the **SPD** can govern alone! Our long campaign of electioneering has paid off. We do not need to worry about coalition government; anything is possible. However, our former coalition partners are going to start drifting to the right. Who should be chancellor?

spd_majority_wurttemberg.titleHtml: The **SPD** forms a majority government.
spd_majority_wurttemberg.bodyHtml: Somehow, we have captured the majority of seats, bypassing the coalition negotiation process and appointing an **SPD** Minister-President for the first time in a decade. Kurt Schumacher is elected as Minister-President.

params.source: election_menu

spd_med.titleHtml: Schleicher attempts to negotiate with us.
spd_med.bodyHtml: The nationwide general strike against Schleicher's authoritarian regime has brought the country to a standstill. The chancellor could unleash the Reichswehr and far-right paramilitaries to brutally crush the protests—but for now, that remains a last resort. Instead, Schleicher has chosen to open negotiations with the opposition. Meanwhile, in defiance of the indefinite adjournment of the Reichstag, the republican parties have banded together to unofficially reconvene the chamber at a separate location, openly challenging federal authority. However, perhaps we have overestimated our strength—strikes rarely last with unemployment so high, especially with Schleicher’s sympathizers embedded within the unions themselves.

spd_schleicher_adopted.subtitleHtml: The unions have firmly decided, but convincing the party is a whole another matter.
spd_schleicher_adopted.bodyHtml: The ADGB leadership has now officially—although only in private—taken a stance in favor of cooperating with the "Red General." The union will attempt to leverage its influence over the **SPD** to push our hesitant party leadership toward adopting the same position. Gradually, a shift in opinion is becoming visible within the party. Otto Braun has now come out in support of making deals with the General.

params.source: eg_menu

spd_victorious_2.bodyHtml:
We were forced to strike a deal with Kurt von Schleicher, abandoning our pacifist and anti-militarist roots. With his reputation as a schemer, he could betray us at any moment.
Was it really worth it?

params.source: eg_menu

spd_win.bodyHtml: The mass general strike has crippled the German economy, bringing the country to a complete standstill. With the Reichsbanner strong and organized, the government cannot simply crush the hundreds of thousands of socialist protesters flooding the streets. Meanwhile, in defiance of the indefinite adjournment of the Reichstag, the republican parties have banded together to unofficially reconvene the chamber at a separate location, openly challenging federal authority. The next few days will be chaotic—and decisive for Germany as a whole.

spending_same_post_depression.subtitleHtml: The increased levels of unemployment necessitate more spending on aid.
spending_same_post_depression.bodyHtml: Increasing welfare spending is necessary in light of the rise in unemployment, so we have essentially cut welfare. The workers are justifiably displeased - we are sacrificing their livelihoods to appease bourgeois demands for austerity. [? if in_popular_front or in_left_front: The **KPD** is turning against us for our welfare policy. ?]

stable_currency_out_of_gov.titleHtml: German representatives call for stable currency, along with Britain and France.
stable_currency_out_of_gov.bodyHtml: As expected, the conservative German bankers support Britain and France's plan to stabilize currency exchange rates. In response to the continued support for fixed currency exchange rates and the impasse on debts, the Americans pull out of the conference, leaving it with no agreements whatsoever. [? if unemployed >= 15 : Nevertheless, the world economy is slowly improving due in part to the economic stimulus and more liberal trade policies of the Roosevelt administration. ?] [? if unemployed < 15 : Nevertheless, the world economy is slowly improving due in part to the economic stimulus and more liberal trade policies of the Roosevelt administration as well as our own economic plan. ?]

stampfer.bodyHtml: = Friedrich Stampfer Friedrich Stampfer is the long-time editor-in-chief of Vorwärts, our party newspaper, and also a Reichstag member. He was historically part of the Majority **SPD** that supported our participation in the Great War, but also supports cooperation with the **KPD** to save the Republic. [? if kpd_truce: Since such a SPD-KPD cooperation can be considered achieved through a truce with the RFB, Stampfer is emboldened to direct Vorwärts fully towards placating internal dissent by supporting a Center position. ?]

start.bodyHtml: > *"Such a general development cannot be attributed to the false tactics of any single party or to the mistakes of individual leaders. On the contrary, the conduct of individual leaders is determined largely by the sentiments of the people as a whole. It would be erroneous, however, to regard the sentiments of the moment as reflecting the natural make-up and character of the people. They are merely the consequence of the special circumstances which have brought about this profound degradation of the entire nation."* - Karl Kautsky, *Hitlerism and Social Democracy*, 1934 This is a game of alternate history. While historical accuracy is a major concern, keep in mind that this is a *game*, and that any divergence from actual events will necessarily have to involve some element of make-believe. Nevertheless, please let the author know if there are any glaring mistakes. For more information on the politics and government of the German Republic, see the "Library" page on the top left. If this is your first time playing the game, it is strongly recommended that you read at least some of this information. **If you are playing this mod via the Mod Loader in base game, there will be various items missing (parliament colours, images, arrows, etc.). For the intended experience, please play using this link.**

statusquo.bodyHtml: Oskar Hergt has been re-elected once again. However, he and the national conservatives within the party are increasingly looking toward alliances with forces to their right, as their previous hostility toward the **DNF** continues to fade. Furthermore, the bourgeois elites influencing the party have pushed its leadership to reconsider some form of cooperation with the **NSDAP**, aiming to integrate them as a "constructive component of the state" through a so-called 'taming strategy'. Recently, discussions have emerged about a new referendum—one designed to unite the German right, much like the Young Plan referendum attempted, but this time focused on prematurely dissolving the Prussian Landtag. Given the radicalized political climate, such a move would allow the **NSDAP**, which currently holds a meager [+ nsdap_r_prussia +]% of seats, to make significant gains.

stay_course.bodyHtml: We will stay the course of toleration, for the sake of stability.

stegerwald.bodyHtml: Stegerwald will continue to evolve the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] into a Christian, democratic, German, and social party. Hopefully, Joseph Wirth and the left wing of the party will be able to keep him in check. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": However, the party will continue shifting to the right as it takes the **DNVP**'s place on the German right. ?] [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": Talks of a merger with the **DNVP** are becoming increasingly common—though support is limited to their People's Conservatives and Christian Socials. A merger remains impossible without one of those factions having strong, centralized leadership within their party. At the same time, we must prevent any government cooperation between them and the Center—lest we allow conditions for such a union to emerge. ?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": A merger with the **DNVP** is out of the question—at least with Hugenberg commanding the party. Still, there remains fertile ground on the anti-Hugenberg right. ?]

stegerwald_formation_1.bodyHtml: = [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] Reformation As the newly elected chairman of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?], Adam Stegerwald has been working to expand the party's reach in Protestant areas and quell opposition against his agenda. As a trade union leader himself, he has sizable influence over the Christian labor movement, which is already well-connected through entrenched network of alliances with various right-wing organizations. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": Cooperation between the various Christian labor unions have been heightened, and together, they are taking down our long-held dominance over the interests of the working-class. ?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": However, Hugenberg of the **DNVP** maintains strict oversight of its Christian Social wing, and will not tolerate any cooperation, making the process considerably more challenging without support of the **DNVP** affiliated unions. Furthermore, Hugenberg's inaction as the **DNVP** loses its main voter base is fueling significant internal turmoil over the party's future direction. ?] This has led to concerns from the labor wing of our party, as we can't afford to lose support of the largest demographic to the bourgeois.

stegerwald_formation_1.fightback_other.bodyHtml: If the bourgeois wants to appeal to the workers, then we will simply find support elsewhere. The **KPD** makes inroads on our inaction. The left of the **SPD** is opposed to this path, seeing it as diluting the class character of the party. On the other hand, reformists support branching out to different classes.

stegerwald_formation_1.fightback_working.bodyHtml: We increase our messaging among the workers, fighting back against the shift to the right. It isn't enough, but it is something.

stegerwald_formation_1.nothing.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] continues to eat into our party's primary voter base.

The reformation of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] away from its confessional roots has injected a dose of dynamism into the party, making it more willing to change and evolve with current conditions. Jakob Kaiser is a rising star on the left, Christian Left wing of the party, supporting Stegerwald's vision for a united Christian union but disagreeing with his right-wing policies.

stegerwald_formation_2.kaiser.bodyHtml: With our grassroots connections, we are able to secure the election of Jakob Kaiser to the chairmanship of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]. This has come as a complete shock to the political landscape, which has been shifting to the right recently. His progressive, left-wing views on contentious subjects like nationalizations and his vehement anti-Nazism are ahead of his time. Despite this victory, he finds himself at odds with the rest of his party, as his views are out of place. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": Furthermore, this has stopped the flow of **DNVP** moderates to the party, whose voters will head back to the [? if not kvp_formed: various smaller parties between the two parties?][? if kvp_formed: the **KVP**?]. ?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": Furthermore, this has stopped the process of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] taking over the **DNVP** of being the party of the right. ?] Due to the party's dynamism, he may be deposed if he proves to be too divisive.

stegerwald_win.bodyHtml: Adam Stegerwald has risen from union president to President of Germany. He is expected to pursue friendlier policies toward the **SPD** than Hindenburg did, and to provide a voice for the laborers of Germany. Let's hope he remains firm in keeping the Nazis out of power.

step_forward.titleHtml: The treaty is a step forward for peace.
step_forward.bodyHtml: Despite our misgivings about the treaty, it still represents a step forward for the cause of international peace.

stolper.subtitleHtml: Creator of the famed Stolper Program, and a Jew.
stolper.bodyHtml: Gustav Stolper, a German-Austrian economist and the son of Jewish immigrants from Poland, has been elected chairman of the **LVP**, reinforcing a stereotype the party has long struggled to dispel. Despite this, Stolper—renowned for the economic program bearing his name—could be exactly what the **LVP** needs to revitalize its middle-class support. Relations have improved compared to Curtius's tenure, as Stolper's strained ties with parties to the right of the **LVP**—due to anti-Semitism—have made cooperation with us easier.

streetfighting.truce_rfb.bodyHtml: We have made at least a temporary truce with the **KPD**, so that our respective paramilitaries will stop fighting.

strike_yeah.bodyHtml: Three days before the election, the strike brings all public transport in Berlin to a halt, garnering significant sympathy among the city's working class. The **KPD** and **NSDAP** are quick to throw their propaganda weight behind the strikers, each hoping for a breakthrough among working-class voters. We have urged workers to abstain from participating in the illegal strike—pointing out that it never actually met the required three-fourths quorum, and that BVG workers remain better off than most in Germany. Chancellor [+ chancellor +] has condemned the Nazi-Communist cooperation as a betrayal of the nation. While both the **RGO** and **NSBO** are involved in the same strike, there is little coordination beyond that. The **KPD**, however, stands to gain the most politically. Ultimately, the strike fizzles out after just a few days—unsustainable in a time of mass unemployment.

structure.titleHtml: Change the structure and funding of education.
structure.bodyHtml: Education in Germany has traditionally been organized on religious and class lines. Schools are often either Protestant or Catholic (or rarely Jewish), and religious classes are required in most mixed-denomination schools. In addition, the working class has at most eight years of public education in primary and middle schools, while the middle and upper classes have access to private schools and Gymnasiums that prepare students for universities. Thus, the universities tend to be dominated by conservatives and reactionaries, which has negative consequences for bureaucratic recruitment.

support_austria.titleHtml: Diplomatically support Austrian democracy against the Dollfuß dictatorship.
support_austria.bodyHtml: We provide verbal backing to Austrian democracy, wage a war of words against Austrofascism, and promulgate additional trade sanctions. Time will tell if it will be enough.

support_austria_2.titleHtml: Provide material support to Austrian democracy against the Dollfuß dictatorship.
support_austria_2.bodyHtml: In public, we provide verbal backing to Austrian democracy, wage a war of words against Austrofascism, and promulgate additional trade sanctions. Privately, we provide financial and various forms of "support" to our comrades in Austria in their struggle against dictatorship.

support_center.bodyHtml: We could try to boot the **KPD** from our governing coalition, and form a new government with the bourgeois parties.

choices.labelHtml: Form a Weimar Coalition?
Form a Weimar Coalition?
There is nothing we can do.

support_centrist.subtitleHtml: Let the depression play itself out.
support_centrist.bodyHtml:
Woytinsky and the trade unions vehemently criticize the centrists for their policy. The workers are starving; are we going to callously abandon them and side with bourgeois austerity? On the other hand, the centrists criticize Woytinsky for promising the workers false hope; their position is that nothing can be done to alleviate the depression. They also speak of the fear of another round of hyperinflation that may result from deficit spending.
Our policy course is currently that nothing can be done to alleviate the depression.

support_employers.subtitleHtml: Popular among the bourgeoisie, much less so among the workers.
support_employers.bodyHtml: The more radical workers despise our suppression of their strikes, recalling the days of Friedrich Ebert.

support_labor.subtitleHtml: Call for increased public works and fiscal stimulus.
support_labor.bodyHtml:
Our support of the WTB plan alienates the orthodox Marxists of the Centrist faction, and faces both opposition and support from a variety of sources across the spectrum. Leftists argue that the plan is flawed because it leaves capitalism intact, while some reformists are cautiously optimistic.
We have not yet convinced the party to formally adopt the plan. More work needs to be done.

support_labor_pre.subtitleHtml: Call for welfare spending and emergency relief for the workers.
support_labor_pre.bodyHtml: The Labor faction hasn't come up with a concrete solution to our economic woes yet, but has called for increased welfare spending in light of the rise in unemployment. Perhaps supporting their efforts will encourage a real solution to the crisis to be introduced.

support_left.subtitleHtml: Call for mass nationalizations and the transformation of the economy.

support_left_progress.bodyHtml: We attempt to convince the party to support a program of mass nationalizations in response to the economic crisis. Leftists argue that this policy is in accordance with our long-standing socialist platform, while reformists and some trade unionists argue that the plan is unrealistic, and that we need to focus on more immediate improvements to workers' lives. We have not yet formally adopted the plan. More work needs to be done.

support_moderate.subtitleHtml: Call for a limited program of job creation without deficit spending.

support_moderate_progress.bodyHtml:
We attempt to convince the party to support a moderate program of job creation without deficit spending. Advocates of the moderate plan argue that this plan is most likely to receive support from the bourgeois parties, and most practical in the immediate term. Opponents in the left and labor factions criticize the plan for being inadequate in its ambition.
We have not yet adopted the plan. More work needs to be done.

support_neo.bodyHtml: We support the new leaders, and start using new-style propaganda techniques in our campaigns. The results are uncertain so far...

choices.labelHtml: We should use this opportunity to change the party's leadership.

support_neorev.bodyHtml: Vorwärts prints editorials in support of neorevisionist ideas.

support_peoples_party.bodyHtml: In an emergency conference, we have decided to become a people's party that encompasses all of the regular people of Germany, not just the workers and urban poor. The Left and Center claim that our new party platform is a betrayal of our founding principles, a turn away from Marxism towards bourgeois opportunism. Whatever the case, we are now a party representing all of the people, not just the proletariat. Should we run a new campaign to publicize our new platform?

taming_lose.bodyHtml: With the appointment of [+ chancellor +] and the passage of the Enabling Act, Germany is lost. Schleicher, increasingly sidelined by health issues, fades into irrelevance. Following[? if president == "Hindenburg": President Hindenburg's and?] his[? if president == "Hindenburg": own?] death, General Werner von Blomberg assumes the presidency, marking the end of the failed taming experiment.
