thalmann.bodyHtml: The **Communists** will run Ernst Thälmann, their leader and candidate in 1925. If we were to not run a candidate, or to support a right-wing or bourgeois one, Thälmann and the **KPD** would greatly capitalize by painting themselves as the only left-wing option in the race. However, if our relations with the **KPD** are high enough, we may be able to convince him to drop out in favour of a unity candidate between our two parties.

choices.labelHtml: So, what is our decision? Should we run our own candidate?

thalmann_chancellor.bodyHtml: With great reluctance, President [+ president +] appoints [+ chancellor +] as chancellor. Immediately, [+ chancellor +] goes to work building a "Soviet Germany": consolidating as much power as possible in the **KPD**, purging state institutions of anti-communists, and sending street fighters against the "enemies of the people". In response to [+ chancellor +] being appointed Chancellor, the right-wing forces launches almost immediately launch an attempted coup. Troops of the **Stahlhelm** and Nazi **SA** enter Berlin and immediately begin clashing with our supporters! Reactionary officers within the Reichswehr have taken their troops out of the barracks and joined them with the **Stahlhelm** to stop the **KPD** from taking power. We are forced to be on the same side as the **KPD**, whether we want to or not.

thalmann_civil_war.bodyHtml: # TODO: depose the chancellor? Thälmann wastes no time in consolidating power, using all means available to reshape the government. In response, the far-right immediately launches a coup attempt. We have no choice but to unite with the **KPD** against the fascists...

thalmann_democrat.bodyHtml: Despite the victory of the anti-constitutionalist Thälmann, he appears to be respecting the constitutional constraints on presidential power, at least for now. There is no appetite on the right for a coup at this moment. The bourgeoisie have to live with a communist president, at least for now.

thiel.subtitleHtml: Thiel is a controversial unionist within the party, being more left wing than Glatzel.
thiel.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, Otto Thiel has been elected as the new leader of the **DVP**! Compared to his colleague Glatzel, Thiel leans further left within the party’s unionist faction. He has even voiced support for increased welfare spending, arguing that austerity measures would only deepen the hardships faced by the people. In his push for *Volksgemeinschaft*, he has begun introducing more labor-friendly policies into the party’s platform, backing collective bargaining rights and worker protections. As expected, the remaining industrialists within the **DVP** are outraged—even those with sympathies toward the late Stresemann. This has led to a dramatic shift in the party’s financial backing, as funding from big business dwindles and is replaced by donations and dues from the DHV and its affiliated members. [? if in_grand_coalition: We have noticed a significant decrease in coalition tensions. ?]

thuringia_coalition_menu.bodyHtml: The bourgeois parties have historically been hostile to us in state politics, especially after the notorious **SPD**-**USPD**-**KPD** United Left government faced a Reichsexekution six years ago. They still haven't forgiven the **SPD** for this. Meanwhile, the surging **NSDAP**, now controlling [+ nsdap_r_thuringia +]% of the Landtag, is no longer content with mere toleration and demands a role in government. With the bourgeois parties determined to exclude us from power, Thuringia may well become the first state to appoint a Nazi minister.

thuringia_reichsexekution_popular.bodyHtml: = Reichsexekution of Thuringia President [+ president +] has invoked the Reichsexekution to dismiss the Thuringian government, citing its "inability to maintain order" amidst escalating clashes between the **SA**, Reichsbanner, and the increasingly militant **RFB**. However, the true motivation is clear: the left-wing coalition governing Thuringia poses a direct threat to the conservative and nationalist establishment in Germany.

thuringia_reichsexekution_popular.defend.bodyHtml: As the Reichswehr and their reactionary auxiliaries march into Thuringia, armed fighting erupts between them and the leftist forces of the Thuringian government. Hindenburg refuses to withdraw the Reichsexekution and orders more Reichswehr troops into Thuringia.

The Reichsbanner and RFB confront the reactionaries on the road to Thuringia and somehow, the enemy has retreated without a fight! They were surprised by our resistance and Hindenburg has decided to not risk a civil war over Thuringia. This show of force has reinvigorated support for both the **SPD** and **KPD** and has weakened the fascists and reactionaries. Hindenburg's ire has also been turned away from us. For now.

toleration_dilemma.bodyHtml: There is no path to a majority government. One option would be to tolerate a broad bourgeois government, without cabinet participation from the **SPD** at all. This is the only viable option for a government, as the bourgeois parties refuse to cooperate with us in any other capacity. Otherwise, new elections have to be called, where the extremist parties stand to gain.

choices.labelHtml: Tolerate the bourgeois parties to prevent new elections.

toleration_saxony.titleHtml: We will enter a toleration agreement with the bourgeois parties.
toleration_saxony.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, we have been relegated to toleration of the bourgeois parties. The Schieck Cabinet is re-established, composed only of the [? if not lvp_formed: **DVP** and **[+ ddp_name +]**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?][? if stegerwald_path: and [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?]?].

toleration_thuringia.titleHtml: The incumbent bourgeois-right government has fallen short of a majority.
toleration_thuringia.subtitleHtml: We will offer our toleration to them, to prevent their dependence on the **NSDAP**.
toleration_thuringia.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, through our reconciliation with the bourgeois parties, they have accepted our toleration to prevent the **NSDAP** from entering government. However, this provides valuable propaganda for the Nazis, who gain support at the expense of the **DNVP** and **CNBLP**, who are now tainted by their association with us.

treviranus.titleHtml: Kuno von Westarp -[? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": Former?] **DNVP**
treviranus.subtitleHtml: Hindenburg's preferred choice once again, and [? if dnvp_leader != "Westarp":former?] **DNVP** party leader.
treviranus.bodyHtml: Westarp, despite being once again begged by an older and increasingly sick Hindenburg, has declined the offer. Instead, he recommends the appointment of rising star and Volkskonservativ leader Gottfried Treviranus. With deep ties to German industry, the Right, and a pseudo-republican veneer, Treviranus is a candidate aimed at stabilizing Germany’s worsening crisis. Much like Papen’s dismissal in favor of Schleicher, the political class breathes yet another sigh of relief. Even within the **SPD**, many find it easier to confront the devil they know rather than face Schleicher’s dynamic and unpredictable rule. Treviranus will seek to construct a working majority via parliament.

triumvirate.bodyHtml:
Both Hugenberg and Hergt lack the majority of votes needed within the party, and now are seeking a compromise solution between the two factions. A group of party members on the fence between the two, have suggested a triumvirate between Westarp, Hugenberg, and a representative from Prussia as a compromise, a proposal Hugenberg himself is supportive of, where he can control the party from the sidelines.
Westarp is not enthusiastic of such a proposal but agreed to take part in it for the sake of party unity. However, this arrangement is unstable and will not last long.

truce_rfb.subtitleHtml: The RFB will be added to the balance of power.
truce_rfb.bodyHtml: We have made at least a temporary truce with the **KPD**, so that our respective paramilitaries will stop fighting.

true_bourgeois_coalition_saxony.titleHtml: The bourgeois parties have garnered a majority to rule via parliament.
true_bourgeois_coalition_saxony.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, the bourgeois parties have secured a majority all on their own. The **NSDAP** is heavily demoralized by this defeat, as they are relegated to the powerless opposition role. They had expected the national political climate to benefit them, and to allow them to influence government.

understanding_enemy.subtitleHtml: Why did the Nazis gain so many votes?
understanding_enemy.bodyHtml: = Understanding the Enemy The Nazis' rise is unprecedented for a political party in modern Germany, and socialist intellectuals are doing their best to come to terms with the rapid rise of this dangerous party. # Harsch p. 106-109 The trade union researcher Theodor Geiger has written an article titled "Panik im Mittelstand", in which he describes the Nazis as being primarily a movement of the middle class, especially lower-middle civil servants and professionals who fear the proletarianizing effects of the Depression. Geiger argues that the middle class has been economically and politically unmoored, long split between many competing parties, squeezed between the big businesses and the proletariat. The mix of nationalist, anti-democratic, and loosely anti-capitalist rhetoric of the Nazis appeals to this group, perhaps only temporarily before the middle class discovers its true class interests. By contrast, the theoretician Alexander Schifrin understands the Nazis as a new, unprecedented type of political movement, a fascist party that has non-economic appeal across class lines. He calls to attention its use of violent propaganda and street demonstrations as central to their rise. # Harsch p. 77-78 Carlo Mierendorff, a leader of the "new revisionists", understands the Nazis as a politically incoherent but nevertheless powerful movement. They are kept together by the strength of their organizing machine and the emotional appeal of their nebulous ideology, which is able to attract less informed voters who voted based on feeling. Countering them would require a new style of campaigning, focused more on symbols and emotion rather than reason. It is possible that all or none of these hypotheses are correct. Whatever the case, there must be something we can do to stop their rise. # Georg Decker # Alexander Shifrin # Carlo Mierendorff

choices.labelHtml: The Nazis are the fault of the petit bourgeois. It is not our responsibility as a working-class party to stop them.
We can combat the Nazis by adopting a "People's Party" posture that might compete for support among the middle class.
We should use new Mierendorff's new propaganda methods to fight the the Nazis.
We must focus our work among the working class to prevent Nazi in-roads.

understanding_enemy.p1.bodyHtml: The Nazis are the fault of the petit bourgeoisie. It is not our responsibility as a working-class party to stop them.

understanding_enemy.p2.bodyHtml: We can combat the Nazis by adopting a "People's Party" posture that might compete for support among the middle class. In order to do this, we can create a new and inclusive vision of the party that encompasses all people who work for a living, which is almost everyone in the country save the aristocrats and top capitalists. [? if peoples_party = 0 : This effort faces great opposition from the left and center of our party, who would prefer a party focused on the working class. To fully adopt the vision of a people's party, we should increase our campaigning among other demographics. ?]

understanding_enemy.p3.bodyHtml: Working together with other "neorevisionists" such as Sergei Chakhotin, Mierendorff has developed new propaganda methods to fight the rise of the Nazis. They focus on visually striking symbols and repetitious slogans. Time will tell how effective they are.

understanding_enemy.p4.bodyHtml: The Nazis' appeals are making in-roads even among the working class, so we must redouble our propaganda campaigns among our base in order to prevent any Nazi attachment.

unemployment_insurance_1.bodyHtml: = Unemployment Insurance Crisis The economic crisis has caused mass layoffs all throughout Germany, affecting the industrial working class the hardest. Our welfare spending is increasing due to the greater need. In the midst of all this, our right-wing coalition partners in the **DVP**[? if ddp_ideology == "Right" and not dstp_formed:, **[+ ddp_name +]**?] [? if z_party_name != "CVP" and z_ideology != "Left": and Center?][? if (z_party_name == "CVP" and z_ideology != "Left") or (cvp_ideology == "Left" and cvp_formed): and **CVP**?] have a plan to cut benefits for the unemployed, lower taxes on the rich, and raise taxes on the working class, as part of a plan to balance the budget and discipline labor. They do not see a possibility for compromise. If we do not accept, they could blow up the coalition. [? if unemployment_insurance_crisis = 2 : This is the second such ultimatum thrown by the Right. Obviously, the bourgeoisie are trying to remove us from the government. ?]

unemployment_insurance_1_lvp.compromise.bodyHtml: The **LVP** ministers in the cabinet have offered a compromise that raises some taxes on the wealthy, along with lesser welfare cuts. Our members have mixed opinions on accepting this compromise. Reformists and Centrists support maintaining our government to keep the fascists and communists out, while Labor generally opposes any cuts, and the Left is opposed to compromises with the bourgeoisie. The **LVP** are themselves are split about this, the Reichstag delegation may go against the compromise fashioned by their own ministers. [? if lvp_ideology == "Left": However, the **LVP** has resisted the national shift towards the right for the most part. ?]If we do go ahead with this, the coalition hinges on the decision of the **LVP**.

choices.labelHtml: Reject the compromise and let this government fall.

unemployment_insurance_1.accept.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, we must accept this ultimatum if we are to maintain this coalition. The Nazis and **Communists** are waiting in the wings for us to fail, ready to pounce upon the instability that would result from a breakup of the governing coalition. The workers are furious at our betrayal, as are a good portion of our membership throughout the factions. Our loss is the **KPD**'s gain, and even the **NSDAP**, those lapdogs of the bourgeoisie, have joined in criticizing us for our austerity.

unemployment_insurance_1.compromise.bodyHtml: The **DVP** ministers in the cabinet have offered a compromise that raises some taxes on the wealthy, along with lesser welfare cuts. Our members have mixed opinions on accepting this compromise. Reformists and Centrists support maintaining our government to keep the fascists and communists out, while Labor generally opposes any cuts, and the Left is opposed to compromises with the bourgeoisie. The **DVP** themselves are split about this, the Reichstag delegation may go against the compromise fashioned by their own ministers. [? if dvp_ideology == "Left": However, the **DVP** has resisted the national shift towards the right for the most part. ?]If we do go ahead with this, the coalition hinges on the decision of the **DVP**.

choices.labelHtml: Reject the compromise and let this government fall.
Decide this at a later date.

unemployment_insurance_1.compromise_succ.bodyHtml: We have accepted the compromise offered by the bourgeoisie. Many of the workers and unemployed see this as a betrayal, although we present it as the successful aversion of a much worse alternative. Despite the intense lobbying by German industry, the **DVP** have voted for the compromise through the narrowest of votes.

unemployment_insurance_weimar.subtitleHtml: Our unemployment insurance programs need additional funding...
unemployment_insurance_weimar.bodyHtml:
= Unemployment Insurance Crisis
The economic crisis has caused mass layoffs all throughout Germany, affecting the industrial working class the hardest. Our welfare spending is increasing due to the greater need.
In the midst of all this, our unemployment insurance program is underfunded; the program was never budgeted for this much unemployment. We have to either increase funding or cut benefits.

unemployment_reduced.titleHtml: Unemployment has been reduced from its peak.
unemployment_reduced.bodyHtml: While still uncomfortably high, unemployment levels are nowhere near their peak. This is a success of our economic policy.

params.source: eg_menu

unemployment_reduced_2.bodyHtml: Unemployment levels have fallen substantially! This is a success of our economic policy.

params.source: eg_menu

union_unity.bodyHtml: We have reduced tensions with the Labor faction, and increased its strength in the party.

unions_declare_independence.subtitleHtml: Labor's disagreements with our policies have grown too severe.
unions_declare_independence.bodyHtml: = Unions Declare Independence Our policy choices have greatly offended the labor movement. Union leaders have declared that they are independent of any political party, and some have been seen seeking accommodation with the **KPD** and even the **NSDAP**. Most workers remain loyal to the **SPD**, although their affiliation is less solid. Many workers move left[? if sapd_formed:, to the **KPD** or the nascent **SAPD**?]. Others move in a more nationalist direction, as the ADGB signals its willingness to work with the right to solve the economic crisis. [? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": This also has the effect of strengthening the Christian Labor movement within the **DNVP**. ?] Much of our working-class base has defected, and labor's influence in our party has greatly diminished.

unions_declare_independence_lambach.subtitleHtml: Labor's disagreements with our policies have grown too severe.
unions_declare_independence_lambach.bodyHtml: = Unions Declare Independence Our policy choices have greatly offended the labor movement. Union leaders have declared that they are independent of any political party, and some have been seen seeking accommodation with the extremists on the far-left and far-right. However, a sizeable majority of unionists however are identifying with the Christian Socials of the **DNVP**, who now control their leadership. Most workers remain loyal to the **SPD**, although their affiliation is less solid. Many workers move left[? if sapd_formed:, to the **KPD** or the nascent **SAPD**?]. Others move in a more nationalist direction, towards the **DNVP** as the ADGB signals its willingness to work with the Christian Socials to solve the economic crisis. Much of our working-class base has defected, and labor's influence in our party has greatly diminished.

unions_declare_independence_schleicher.subtitleHtml: Labor's disagreements with our policies have grown too severe.
unions_declare_independence_schleicher.bodyHtml: = Unions Declare Independence Our policy choices have greatly offended the labor movement. Union leaders have declared that they are independent of any political party, and some have been seen seeking accommodation with the **KPD** and even the **NSDAP**. However, most unionists are now seeking an accommodation with Chancellor Schleicher[? if dnef_formed: and his **DNEF**?][? if not dnef_formed:, pressuring him to establish a political vehicle of his own?]. In doing so, they have stepped away from Marxist ideology and shifted toward a more pragmatic laborist stance. Nonetheless, most workers remain loyal to the **SPD**, although their affiliation is less solid. Many workers move left[? if sapd_formed:, to the **KPD** or the nascent **SAPD**?], while others are drawn in a nationalist direction, as the ADGB signals its readiness to cooperate with the Red General to tackle the crisis. Much of our working-class base has defected, and labor's influence in our party has greatly diminished.

united_front.subtitleHtml: The consensus view within the **SPD**: we are, afer all, a democratic party.
united_front.bodyHtml: We continue to argue for a united opposition of the democratic parties against the unpopular [+ chancellor +] government, and win support among the people for doing so.

united_front_majority.subtitleHtml: Given our absolute majority in the government, we have no need of cooperating with Schleicher — and can instead aim to widen the united front against those who would bring the Republic down.
united_front_majority.bodyHtml: We continue to decry the anti-democratic opposition as ruinous to the Republic, highlighting the role chancellor [+ chancellor +] plays in stabilizing the situation. This helps our support among the people.

united_left.titleHtml: We persuade the **Communists** to let us take a more active role in their campaign efforts.
united_left.subtitleHtml: They have been putting themselves at the forefront. -1 resources
united_left.bodyHtml: For some reason, the **Communists** aren't particularly grateful for our endorsement of [+ communist_candidate_1932 +]; perhaps it's due to orders from Moscow. Anyhow, we have managed to convince their leadership to allow us to participate together in joint rallies and other efforts.

params.source: campaigning_thalmann

united_left_saxony.titleHtml: We will form a United Left coalition with the **KPD**.
united_left_saxony.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, despite reluctance on both sides due to fears that the reactionary Hindenburg will order a Reichsexekution if a coalition were to form. Red Saxony is restored! As one of the most left-wing and industrial states in Germany, we will use our leverage to implement comprehensive reforms and transform Saxony into a stronghold of socialism. Hindenburg’s patience is especially thin. Tread carefully.

united_left_thuringia.titleHtml: The **SPD** will form a coalition government with the **KPD**.
united_left_thuringia.bodyHtml: Surprisingly, despite reluctance on both sides due to fears that the reactionary Hindenburg will order a Reichsexekution if a coalition were to form. Red Thuringia is restored! Hindenburg’s patience is especially thin. Tread carefully.

united_left_wurttemberg.titleHtml: The **SPD** will form a coalition government with the **KPD**?
united_left_wurttemberg.bodyHtml: Even as the forces of the bourgeoisie have remained numerous in the Landtag, the newly unified Left has triumphed over the reigning coalition and inserted ourselves into a new Red Württemburg. Of course, the rabidly anti-socialist nature of the previous government does not make this transition easy, with mass purges of the police force to ensure that we can retain our influence with communist assistance. We can expect that **Stahlhelm** units, met with such a loss in the elections, will soon bring their fury to the stairs of the Reichstag.

unity_government.subtitleHtml: **SPD** + **[+ z_party_name +]** + **BVP** + [? if not lvp_formed: **[+ ddp_name +]** + **DVP**?][? if lvp_formed: **LVP**?] + **Others** ([+ neo_weimar_coalition +]%)
unity_government.bodyHtml: The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] leader, [? if z_leader == "Joos": Joseph Joos?][? if z_leader == "Kaiser": Jakob Kaiser?], clearly sees the threat from the ascension of the anti-democratic extremist parties, and thus tries to negotiate a "Government of National Unity" to save the republic. This coalition would be led by Joseph Wirth, a left-leaning member of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] and former chancellor, and would encompass all of the constitutional parties. Our role in this government might be limited, however.

choices.labelHtml: No, we will not accept this offer.

unity_government_2.bodyHtml: We have formed a new unity government of all the constitutional parties! We have a limited choice in ministries for this government.

urge_against_austerity.subtitleHtml: This will be significantly more difficult with the DNVP in government.

urge_failure.bodyHtml: Unfortunately, our negotiations have met with failure. The center-right parties increasingly see us as a nuisance, and might not wish to continue these negotiations.

urge_paramilitary.titleHtml: Urge Brüning to grant us stronger actions against political extremists, and to restrict certain rights.
urge_paramilitary.bodyHtml: Carl Severing and other Prussian officials have successfully urged Brüning to issue an emergency decree expanding police authority to suppress political extremism. The decree imposes restrictions on political meetings, organizations, newspapers, and posters, all of which now require police approval beforehand. As a result, several Nazi and Communist newspapers have been banned, triggering violent clashes between their supporters and the police. [? if president == "Hindenburg": President Hindenburg has reluctantly signed the decree, but is losing patience with Brüning for yielding to our demands. ?]

vonc_hergt.bodyHtml: Oskar Hergt, who was once forced to resign nearly a decade ago over his decision to allow a free vote on the Dawes Plan—the very plan that rescued Germany from hyperinflation and ushered in the Golden Twenties—is now tendering his resignation once again after failing to impose party discipline. History seems to be repeating itself: the **DNVP** is once again deeply divided, with its pragmatic wing supporting Brüning while its emboldened right wing aligns with the national opposition. The party now faces a fateful decision—either accept the bitter pill of working within the system or risk catastrophic consequences, possibly even the destruction of the Weimar Republic itself.

vonc_lambach.bodyHtml: Walther Lambach, a strong supporter of Brüning and, to some extent, democracy, has enforced party discipline to ensure the Reichstag delegation votes in favor of Brüning. However, the anger many within his party has against him and his Christian Social ideals has split the party almost down the middle.

choices.labelHtml: Can we form a Social-[? if not lvp_formed: Liberal?][? if lvp_formed: Liberal?] Coalition?
Could we get the **KPD** to abstain?

vonc_moderate.bodyHtml: [? if dnvp_leader == "Schiele": Martin Schiele, a strong supporter of Brüning—and his Minister of Agriculture—has successfully persuaded the agrarian wing of the **DNVP** to oppose the vote of confidence. He also enlists the support of Westarp and incumbent cabinet members to lobby the rest of the party. However, some radical members, who remained in the party solely due to their shared hatred of Hugenberg, are expected to defy party discipline. ?][? if dnvp_leader == "Westarp": Kuno von Westarp, a longtime leader of the **DNVP** and one of Brüning's strongest supporters, has rallied members from all wings of the party to oppose the proposed vote of no confidence, warning of the political and economic instability that would follow if it passed. However, some radical members, who remained in the party solely due to their shared hatred of Hugenberg, are expected to defy party discipline. ?]

We do not have a voice in the government, but we are responsible for its continued stability. The left of our party opposes this plan, and would rather that we hold new elections.

vorbeck.titleHtml: Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, war hero of the Great War and [? if not cvp_formed: [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?]?][? if cvp_formed: **CVP**?] member.
vorbeck.bodyHtml: By some miracle for the German Right, they have managed to persuade Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck—renowned for his successful guerrilla campaign in German East Africa during the Great War—to run for the presidency. However, the circumstances now are far more dire than they were in 1925. The German Right is significantly less unified behind Lettow-Vorbeck than it had been for President Hindenburg. How Lettow-Vorbeck would govern remains uncertain. It is highly likely that, much like Hindenburg, a camarilla of close advisors would shape his decisions from behind the scenes. His candidacy is backed by the [? if not vorbeck_fallback: [? if not cvp_formed: [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?]?][? if cvp_formed: **CVP**?], along with a disparate coalition of minor bourgeois parties. ?][? if vorbeck_fallback: entirety of the Bürgerblock parties, who view him as their collective last hope at retaining power. ?]

vote_threshold.subtitleHtml: Change the vote threshold to 5% for parties to be represented in the Reichstag.
vote_threshold.bodyHtml: # The left is opposed to this. Some political thinkers believe that the proliferation of minor parties is responsible for the instability of the republic. They believe that a higher electoral threshold will reduce the influence of small radical parties. Parties that win a plurality in a constituency will maintain their representation, a gift to regional parties such as the **BVP**. The smaller parties will obviously oppose this reform. [? if z_relation > 30 : The [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] supports this reform, while their **BVP** partners oppose it. ?] [? if kpd_relation > 50 and kpd_normalized >= 0.1 : Perhaps surprisingly, the **KPD** supports this reform. ?] [? if nsdap_normalized >= 0.2 : The **NSDAP** supports this reform, as they believe they have something to gain. ?] The **SPD** Left opposes this change, as they believe it to be anti-democratic.

choices.labelHtml: Call a constitutional referendum to pass the reform!

# this should result in a redistribution of votes - other parties should not get so many votes anymore. maybe ddp and dvp get a recovery of middle-class votes? or maybe they flow to the others.

war_guilt.bodyHtml:
= Reichstag War Guilt Inquiry
The War Guilt Inquiry has been an intermittent Reichstag committee for investigating the causes of the Great War and the German defeat. So far, it has faced massive resistance from the military establishment[? if president == "Hindenburg": up to President Hindenburg?].

war_guilt.pure_history.bodyHtml: The history is being compiled, as it always has been.

war_guilt.restart.bodyHtml: What is the goal of this tribunal?

choices.labelHtml: To provide a historical record of the events of the war.
To revise the popular German histories and finally put to rest the "stabbed in the back" myth.

war_guilt.rewrite.bodyHtml: Destroying the "stabbed in the back" myth, in addition to finally correcting the historical record, would do a great deal to improve our party's reputation. This is why it would be resisted by the military establishment every step of the way.

weimar_mega_win.titleHtml: The Weimar Republic Marches On
weimar_mega_win.bodyHtml: At the turn of the decade, the Great Depression and widespread disillusionment with the Weimar system left few optimists in Germany. Yet, the Republic—forged by the will of the people all those years ago—has weathered a crisis of unprecedented proportions. Social Democracy endures, as do its detractors. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, choosing to forget and forgive. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own.

weimar_mega_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - One and a Half Party system The **SPD**'s rule over Germany has endured for decades, following its sublime management of the Great Depression and successful expansion of support beyond the urban working class. To this day, the **SPD** retains its status as the "natural governing party," having only been out of office during brief stints in times of crisis. Only a united coalition of all parties from the **SRPD** to the **DNVP** has ever managed to take power—only to quickly collapse, paving the way for yet more years of **SPD** rule.

weimar_mega_win_b.bodyHtml: Title: Subending B - Bloc Politics The Weimar Coalition has begun to fracture, as the Center Party exits the alliance and repositions itself as a center-right force. However, lingering animosity toward the parties further to the right prevents any formal unification. Instead, the newly formed Christian People's Party has opted to form a new electoral alliance—the "People's Bloc"—alongside the **DNVP** and the newly established **NLP**—which is essentially a renamed continuation of its predecessor. We are only able to enter government as part of a "left bloc" with the **RDP**, **CSRP**, and **LSPD**. This has continued to this day, but the inclusion of the purportedly neo-Nazi **NDPD** into the People's Bloc—capitalizing on public discontent over a refugee crisis sparked by wars in an impoverished and unstable Africa—is deeply concerning.

weimar_prussia_collapse.left_coalition.bodyHtml: Somehow, surprisingly, the left coalition is successfully formed, without appointing a communist as Minister-President. The consensus choice for Minister-President, accepted by the **SPD**, **KPD**, is[? if left_split == 1: **SAPD** member?] Kurt Rosenfeld, who [? if left_split == 0: belongs?][? if left_split == 1: belonged?] to the left faction of the **SPD**, and had a history of defending **KPD** members through his work.. In response to the **KPD**'s entrance into the government, the right-wing takes a "wait-and-see" approach for now. They expect that our government will be unstable and incompetent, and will collapse of its own accord, eventually enabling the destruction of the Weimar Republic. [? if in_left_front: The right will be more active in resisting our rule considering we are also ruling with the **KPD** on the federal level too. ?]

weimar_prussia_collapse.right_coalition.bodyHtml: A right coalition is formed, albeit with an extremely narrow majority. They will begin undoing years of reform and democratization that we fought hard to achieve and will let right-wing paramilitaries like the Stahlhelm and the Nazi **SA** run free. It won't take long for the government to collapse and for us to take power through new elections. But when it eventually does, we won't have much allies as our former coalition partners are beginning to shift to the right. When the time comes, who will stand with us? [? if z_leader != "Stegerwald": Adam Stegerwald?][? if z_leader == "Stegerwald": Heinrich Brüning?] of the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] is selected to be the Minister-President of Prussia.

weimar_rally.bodyHtml: = Republican Coordination Thanks to our historically strong ties with the Weimar coalition parties, they have once again rallied to defend the republic we helped establish. The *Deutscher Republikanischer Reichsbund* (German Republican Reich League), once a non-partisan alliance of figures from all three parties, has now been restructured into an active political organization—intended to complement the efforts of the Reichsbanner. Membership has surged, and fresh funding has arrived from all three coalition parties. The question now is: what will we do with control of this new organization?

weimar_referendum.bodyHtml: = Weimar Constitution Referendum After months of campaigning and propaganda by both sides, the German people have come to vote on the referendum for the revision of the Weimar Constitution, which has taken the backseat in comparison to the devastating economic depression. The far-right parties are also abstaining from supporting this referendum.

weimar_timeline.bodyHtml: = Timeline of the SPD and the Republic (until 1928) **1875**: The SPD is formed as a merger of the General German Workers' Association, founded by Ferdinand Lassalle, and the Social Democratic Workers' Party of Germany, led by Wilhelm Liebknecht and August Bebel. Eventually, the SPD grows to become the largest party in the German Empire. **1914**: The Great War begins. The SPD votes in favor of war credits, with substantial internal dissent. This begins a policy of *Burgfriedenspolitik*, a general peace between all political parties and trade unions. **1917**: The USPD, a left-wing anti-war split from the SPD, is formed. **1918**: Following defeats in the war and uprisings by soldiers, sailors, and workers, SPD leader Philip Scheidemann proclaims the German Republic, and Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicates from his throne. An armistice is declared, ending the Great War. Conflict between center-left social democrats and far-left radicals erupts in the streets of Berlin and elsewhere. **1919**: The Spartacist Uprising, in which communist workers attempt to seize control of government, is launched. The uprising is defeated by the Social Democratic government, now led by President Friedrich Ebert and Chancellor Philipp Scheidemann, with the support of the far-right Freikorps militas. The two key leaders of the uprising, Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht, are murdered by the Freikorps. The Treaty of Versailles is signed under great protest from all political factions in Germany, officially ending the Great War. The Weimar Constitution is signed. The first "Weimar Coalition" government is formed, led by the SPD, DDP, and Center (Z) parties. **1920**: The Kapp Putsch, an attempt by reactionary actors within the military to take power, is launched, and is defeated by the workers with a general strike. This is followed by left-wing uprisings in the Ruhr, which are defeated by the Reichswehr and Freikorps. The Weimar Coalition is defeated in the elections, with the right and far left increasing in vote share. Elected governments in this period are very unstable, often only lasting a matter of months. There is a split in the USPD, with the majority faction joining with the KPD and the Soviet Union's Communist International (Comintern) alliance. **1921**: Communist uprisings in Saxony and Hamburg are defeated. Matthias Erzberger, the Center Party leader who signed the Versailles Treaty, is assassinated. **1922**: The Treaty of Rapallo is signed, which normalized relations with the Soviet Union. Walther Rathenau, the DDP Foreign Minister, is assassinated. The SPD reunites with most of the remaining USPD. **1923**: Hyperinflation begins, largely due to the economic policy of "passive resistance" against the French occupation of the Ruhr and the Versailles reparations. The currency is rapidly devalued as prices for necessities rise to billions of Reichsmarks. The government launches a Reichsexekution against Saxony, which was led by a joint SPD-KPD government. The Nazi "Beer Hall Putsch" is launched in Munich, and fails, with the arrest of Hitler. Eventually, new policies manage to stabilize the currency, and the French occupation ends. **1924**: Parliamentary elections are held in May and December, the latter leading to the bourgeois-right governments that last until 1928. Hitler is released from prison. The Dawes Plan for the repayment of the Versailles reparations is negotiated, which reduces payments and increases economic growth. Germany begins to enter a period of relative stability, with the end of the hyperinflation crisis. **1925**: President Friedrich Ebert dies, and new presidential elections are held, leading to the narrow election of Paul von Hindenburg in the second round. Hindenburg is a war hero and a right-wing reactionary. The SPD adopts the Heidelberg Program as its party platform. The Locarno Treaties are signed, which confirmed Germany's post-war western borders. **1926**: A referendum on the expropriation of the princes, supported by the SPD and KPD, fails.

weimar_win.titleHtml: The Weimar Republic Limps Forward
weimar_win.bodyHtml: Following the scarring experience of the Nazi movement’s rapid rise and implosion, the flaws of the Weimar system became impossible to ignore. But in the end, the fascists and communists who once battled in the streets now stand together in soup lines. Though a number of neo-Nazi movements would emerge after [+ nsdap_leader +]’s mask of sanity slipped, the ideology itself remains irrevocably discredited. No war as destructive as the Great War would come again. Slowly, Germany and the Western Allies began to rebuild relations, choosing to forget and forgive. Fascism never takes root as a dominant force, and the primary threat to European democracy becomes the resurgent Soviet Union. The Spanish Civil War ends in 1936 with a Republican victory. [? if austria_defeat: In 1939, Austria's Austrofascist regime collapses under popular revolt.?][? if sdapo_win or force_peace: In 1938, Austria's ruling **SDAPÖ** successfully holds a referendum confirming their Anschluss into Germany. ?][? if long_war_2: The war in Austria is eventually won by the Austrofascists, who receive generous aid from a fascist Italy.?] Isolated and denied any success in his expansionist aims in Yugoslavia and Greece, Mussolini is deposed in a royalist coup led by King Victor Emmanuel III, and Italy returns to democratic governance[? if long_war_2:, leading to Austria’s government democratizing as a consequence of losing its benefactor?]. Africa remains colonized until the 1970s and 80s. Independence, when it comes, is negotiated largely on the terms of the colonizers. Exploitation persists under a different guise. The Cold War unfolds along different lines, as a "state capitalist" Soviet Union remains intact, forming a bloc with the authoritarian Kuomintang-ruled Republic of China and post-independence India, which fought a bloody war to escape British rule in the 1950s. This tri-polar alliance has solidified into a global axis of its own. [? if not (pro_republic < 50 and spd_votes < 25 and z_ideology == "Right" and z_relation < 35 and dnvp_ideology == "Radical"): Today, Germany is governed by a stable two-and-a-half party system, rotating power between a non-Marxist **SPD**, the centrist **CVP**, and the liberal **LDPD**. However, a surging **NDPD** has emerged on the far right, capitalizing on public discontent over a refugee crisis driven by wars in an impoverished and unstable Africa. ?]

weimar_win_a.bodyHtml: Title: Subending A - The World's Most Unstable Republic The political deadlock that defined the gravest crisis of the Weimar Republic has persisted over the years. The **DNVP** has never been fully reconciled with a system it was fundamentally opposed to from the start. Meanwhile, the estrangement of the Center Party from the Weimar Coalition has only deepened right-wing hostility toward the **SPD**. The presidency has remained out of reach for the **SPD**, with successors to Hindenburg's worldview continuing to preside over Germany and obstruct our return to executive power. In 1939, a recession—sparked by European instability and rising tensions with the Soviet Union—triggered another wave of extremism. The Reichswehr was forced to step in to prevent a "March on Berlin" by both communists and fascism. Though real democracy was formally restored in the 1960s following massive public discontent, the **DSU** has remained a persistent force on the far-right. Recently rebranding itself as the **NDPD**, it has capitalized on growing public anger over a refugee crisis driven by continued war and instability across Africa.

weltbuhne.bodyHtml: # if the SPD controls the judiciary then they can just cancel the trial (at the expense of DVP relations). # If in a grand coalition then the SPD can pressure the coalition to cancel the trial at the expense of dissent. # If the trial goes ahead, then reparations negotiation process gets set back by a few steps and relations with the west suffers. = The Weltbühne Trial The left-wing news and literary magazine Weltbühne has been targeted by the national authorities for allegedly revealing state secrets. The magazine published articles alleging a secret rearmament program by the Reichswehr, in contravention of the Treaty of Versailles. The military authorities obviously do not want this information to be known. It does not help that the magazine's editor, Carl von Ossietzky, is a well-known pacifist. We can try to persuade our coalition partners to drop the case, but they will likely resist. ?]

westarp.bodyHtml: Kuno von Westarp, a familiar figure in German politics, has long been a stalwart of the **DNVP**, once serving as both party leader and head of its parliamentary group. While not entirely opposed to his party’s participation in a republican system, he has made no secret of his monarchist aspirations. His rigid partisanship and staunchly anti-socialist convictions are likely to define his rule—perhaps even making him a more hostile figure than Hindenburg. It is imperative that we prevail over these forces of reaction if we are to have any hope of returning to government. His candidacy is backed by the [? if dnvp_ideology == "Radical": **KVP**?][? if dnvp_ideology == "Moderate": **DNVP**?], along with a disparate coalition of minor bourgeois parties.

wirth_retire.bodyHtml: Wirth, long a thorn in the side of the former Center due to his leftist leanings, has now left its more right-wing successor. He had considered joining the **SPD**, but our Marxist course ultimately alienated him from that path. He has since retired from party politics and now focuses on chairing various republican and Catholic organizations. Unfortunately, this remains a lone defection. The Christian Left faction has largely stayed within the [+ z_party_name +], where they wield little actual power and function more as a pressure group than a meaningful political force.

wittorf_affair.bodyHtml: = Wittorf Affair Our spies and contacts amongst the communists have brought news of a scandal engulfing the **KPD** leadership. An associate of **KPD** chairman Ernst Thälmann, a **KPD** official named John Wittorf, is accused of embezzling campaign funds, diverting thousands of Reichsmarks for personal use, and Thälmann is accused of covering up the affair. The party's central committee considers this charge serious. The Conciliators in the **KPD**, a faction opposed to the party's present hard-line policy, are said to have leaked this information to aid them in the intra-party struggle. Dissident communists in the Leninbund also have information about this affair, and are planning to publish it. What should we do with this information?

wittorf_affair.nothing.bodyHtml: The information spreads without our help, leading to some loss of **KPD** support among the workers.

wittorf_affair.publicize.titleHtml: We will publicize the scandal to damage the **KPD** and Thälmann.
wittorf_affair.publicize.bodyHtml: Our newspapers are among the first to publicize the affair, bringing a torment of criticism to the hypocrisy of the communists. We have damaged the **KPD**'s standing among the workers, but also perhaps closed the door on further cooperation. In the end, Stalin's pressure helps to keep Thälmann from facing much in the way of consequences.

wittorf_affair.secret.titleHtml: It is best to keep this information secret. Prevent the Leninbund and dissident **KPD** members from spreading this.
wittorf_affair.secret.bodyHtml: Some among our leadership consider it unsavory to engage in cloak-and-dagger scheming. However, keeping this secret might be necessary to work with the **KPD**, and the information might become useful later.

women_rb.titleHtml: Allow women to join the Reichsbanner.
women_rb.subtitleHtml: -1 resources - This might cause a backlash from existing members.
women_rb.bodyHtml: The suggestion to allow women into the Reichsbanner is ridiculed by most, except for Toni Sender. But this is an exceptional time, and we need anyone who is willing to join. Thus, we organize specialized units for women, [? if homosexual_rights > 0: and even some covert units for transsexuals and homosexuals?]. After allowing women to join, the number of comrades who leave is more than balanced out by the number of radicalized women and others who join. However, many of our departed members were veterans, and many of the new members have no experience with military-style training.

womens_rights.bodyHtml: = Women's Rights According to the Constitution, women are equal to men, but this is not followed in practice. Women in the workforce are not paid equally for the same work, in addition to often being pushed out of employment after marriage. Men are still favored in marriage and family policy, and there are restrictions on women's rights in many other domains. And that is not to mention the overwhelming patriarchal culture present in Germany. For better or for worse, the Socialists stand virtually alone in supporting increased rights for women, and even within the party, the leadership does not consider it a priority. [? if spd_r < 50 : Unfortunately, women still disproportionately support the bourgeois parties. ?]

choices.labelHtml: Institute policies that help women in the workforce.
Reform marriage, divorce, and property law.
Improve welfare for single mothers and children.
Do not enact any policies for now.

working_hours.bodyHtml:
While a 40-hour work week was declared during the German Revolution in 1918, enforcement has become increasingly porous over the years. The capitalists have successfully added numerous exceptions and loopholes, returning to the old regime of forced overtime for workers.
Now, with the force of the Labor Ministry, we are finally enforcing the rights of workers to their own time. The bourgeoisie and their political representatives are displeased.

works.subtitleHtml: Ordered by Hjalmar Schacht of the Economic Ministry.
works.bodyHtml: Despite Hjalmar Schacht not being a Keynesian, he understands that large scale public works and state funded projected are the way out of Germany's slump, and for Germany to retake its great power status on the international stage. He believes that, since France and Britain are preoccupied with their own economic woes, the time is right for a mass industrialization and rearmament program. The construction of the "Autobahn", a new nationwide highway system, by poorly paid workers has begun, as an expansion of Schleicher's public works plans. A new innovative method for disguising rearmament has also been devised, a "MEFO bill", a system of promissory notes issued through a dummy company to secretly fund arms production while keeping the spending off the official government budget. However, he insists that a revival of Germany's economy should take precedent over rearmament.

works_alt.subtitleHtml: Ordered by Hjalmar Schacht of the Economic Ministry.
works_alt.bodyHtml:
Despite the public works campaign being expanded before Hjalmar Schacht took office as Economic Minister, he now seeks to build upon it—transforming it into a mass industrialization and rearmament program, more closely aligned with Schleicher's ambitions. Only then, he argues, can Germany hope to rival the major powers.
An innovative new method for disguising rearmament has also been devised: the "MEFO bill," a system of promissory notes issued through a dummy company to secretly finance arms production while keeping the spending off the official government books. Nevertheless, Schacht insists that reviving Germany's economy must take precedence over rearmament—for now.

wtb_conceptualized.bodyHtml: = Fiscal Stimulus The worsening economic situation[? if banking_crisis_seen:, made worse by the Banking Crisis?], the rising strength of the Nazis, and the declining strength of Social Democracy have pushed many in our Labor faction away from the policy stance that nothing can be done to alleviate the depression. Chief economist of the ADGB, Wladimir Woytinsky has outlined a national action plan to stimulate the economy through public works, with the backing of union chairman Fritz Tarnow and the **SPD**'s agricultural spokesman, Fritz Baade. We can either support their attempts to craft a formal plan, committing to an active economic policy, or retain our current course, which holds that nothing can be done to alleviate the depression.

choices.labelHtml: The economic crisis is simply the nature of capitalism; nothing can be done except wait it out.
Action is needed; we cannot stand idly by while the workers suffer.
We agree that an active economic policy is needed, but one without deficit spending.
The WTB plan is simply a bandage over capitalism; we should use this crisis as an opportunity to end it through mass nationalizations.

wtb_conceptualized.center_plan.bodyHtml: Woytinsky is promising the workers false hope; nothing can be done to alleviate the depression. We also express concern about the fear of another round of hyperinflation that may result from deficit spending.

wtb_conceptualized.left_plan.bodyHtml: We should use this economic crisis to transform Germany toward actual socialism, in accordance with our long-standing socialist platform. Reformists and the Woytinsky group argue that the plan is unrealistic and that we need to focus on more immediate improvements to workers' lives.

wtb_conceptualized.reformist_plan.bodyHtml: Job creation and stimulus are necessary, but deficit spending, especially with hyperinflation still fresh in memory, is simply unrealistic and reckless. The reformists argue that this plan is most likely to receive support from the bourgeois parties and is the most practical in the immediate term. Opponents in the Left and Labor factions criticize the plan for being inadequate in its ambition.

wtb_conceptualized.wtb_plan.bodyHtml:
We cannot, as the party for the workers, stand idly by as they suffer. *Something* must be done, and it must happen soon. With our encouragement, Woytinsky will present an official plan in the next few months.
> *"Now, however, we stand at the sickbed of capitalism not only as diagnosticians, but also—well, what can I say?—as doctors who want to heal? Or as happy heirs who can't wait for the end and would prefer to give it a helping hand with poison? This dual role, doctor and heir, is a damned difficult task."*
 - Fritz Tarnow, 1931.

wtb_continuation.titleHtml: Look back on our results, and continue our implementation...
wtb_continuation.bodyHtml: Our spending on public works has resulted in a lower need for unemployment insurance and welfare, and increased tax receipts through the multiplier effect as the new money courses through the economy, recuperating some of our spending. We continue to invest most of the new revenue into the program. The economy is doing better, finally. Even the bourgeois parties are beginning to see the light. [? if in_popular_front or in_left_front: The **KPD**, however, still opposes our policy of "rescuing" capitalism. ?]

wtb_plan.bodyHtml: Alright, but what can we do? Hilferding is stubborn in his belief that nothing can be done and will try his best to rally the party against the WTB plan.

wtb_proposed.subtitleHtml: Wladimir Woytinsky and the ADGB have presented a proposal.
wtb_proposed.bodyHtml: = The WTB Plan Following Woytinsky's announcement of intentions to draft a national action plan to stimulate the economy through extensive public works, he, Tarnow, and Baade have presented the WTB Plan, named after them, to the ADGB and **SPD** leadership. While the ADGB has shown enthusiasm and formally adopted the plan, the **SPD**'s economic expert, Rudolf Hilferding, along with Rudolf Breitscheid and party leader Otto Wels, are much more resistant, showing significant skepticism. The fear of inflation caused by funding the plan through public works, especially with hyperinflation still fresh in memory, and the unwillingness to "play doctor at the bedside of capitalism," are the main reasons for the Centrists' reluctance. Maybe they can be convinced?

choices.labelHtml: Woytinsky is promising the workers false hope, retain our current policy.
Action is needed, and is needed now. We will attempt to convince the **SPD** to formally adopt the plan.

wtb_proposed.center_plan.bodyHtml: Woytinsky has good intentions, but Hilferding knows best. Nothing can be done to alleviate the depression. However, we have been increasingly under fire from the ADGB for our opposition, as they formally adopted the plan themselves and consolidated their demands at their "Crisis Congress." The Centrists are slowly losing their grip on the party.

wtb_proposed.labor_influence.titleHtml: Use the ADGB and the Labor faction's influence to force the party to accept the plan.
wtb_proposed.labor_influence.bodyHtml: An internal vote within the **SPD**'s leadership is called to finally settle the matter. After a contentious debate, the majority of the party is convinced by Woytinsky's reasonings, and outnumbered, the Centrists under Hilferding are defeated. With our hard work, we have finally convinced the majority of the party to adopt the WTB plan! [? if spd_in_government == 1 : We can begin implementing the plan as soon as possible, as long as we have the Economic and Finance ministries. ?][? if spd_in_government = 0 : We should emphasize the plan in our electoral propaganda. ?]

wtb_proposed.situation.titleHtml: Point out the gains of the **NSDAP**, who have capitalized on our lack of a program.
wtb_proposed.situation.bodyHtml: The collapse in our electoral performance and loss of voters to the **KPD** and **NSDAP** have opened the party's eyes, and they are now ready to support our plan as a means to present a solution for the workers. With our hard work, we have finally convinced the majority of the party to adopt the WTB plan! [? if spd_in_government == 1 : We can begin implementing the plan as soon as possible, as long as we have the Economic and Finance ministries. ?][? if spd_in_government = 0 : We should emphasize the plan in our electoral propaganda. ?]

wurttemberg_coalition_menu.bodyHtml: The Center Party in Württemberg has historically been unfriendly toward us, opting to continue governing in a minority coalition with the **DNVP** as they view us as incapable of governing, even when a Weimar Coalition was possible in 1928. Under the stable leadership of Eugen Bolz and Wilhelm Bazille, Württemberg has surprisingly managed to mitigate the worst effects of the economic depression. However, its police force is notorious for its anti-socialist bias, targeting us more aggressively than the more violent Nazis.

yay.titleHtml: Perhaps he can still be convinced?

yay_strike.titleHtml: Campaign for the strike, and launch a propaganda campaign among the workers.
yay_strike.subtitleHtml: The strike enjoys great sympathy among Berlin's working class, despite its political motives.
yay_strike.bodyHtml: Through our active efforts to rally reluctant workers—despite the strike being largely unnecessary due to our own union’s negotiations—we have surpassed the required three-fourths majority of all employees in favor. We are now participating in a strike alongside elements of the **RGO** and **NSBO**, a fact the bourgeois parties are quick to attack us for.

yay_strike_2.bodyHtml: Three days before the election, the strike brings all public transport in Berlin to a halt, gaining significant sympathy among the city's working class. The **KPD** and **NSDAP** quickly back the strikers, each hoping to make a breakthrough among working-class voters. However, the **SPD** benefits the most, as most strikers are from the Gesamtverband, reigniting worker support for the party. Chancellor [+ chancellor +] condemns the Nazi-Communist-socialist alliance as a national betrayal. Arbitrary arrests are made, paramilitary violence erupts, and clashes with police lead to numerous casualties. Ultimately, the strike fizzles out after just a few days—unsustainable in a time of mass unemployment.

yes.titleHtml: The power of Reichsexekution exists for a reason, and times like this call for it.
yes.subtitleHtml: President [+ president +] will remove Strasser's cabinet, by force if necessary.
yes.bodyHtml: Expectedly, the Nazis refuse to stand down.

yes_history.bodyHtml: As part of normalizing relations with the **KPD**, we have to acknowledge the wrongdoings of our past. We have expelled Noske, and have held public commemorations for those killed by troops during the uprisings. This leads to tensions with the moderates and reformists within our party, and criticism from the conservative and liberal parties.

young_plan_campaign.bodyHtml:
= Young Plan Referendum
While the Young Plan seems to be a positive development for the country, the Right are gathering signatures to initiate a referendum this December. While the referendum itself is likely to fail, their propaganda is striking a chord with many, especially amid the ongoing depression. 
It comes down to us to campaign against the rhetoric of those that seek to destroy our republic. [? if spd_in_government: We are able to use government resources for this campaign, lowering the cost for our party. ?]

choices.labelHtml: Campaign in favor of the Young Plan and against the referendum.
Do not campaign on the Young Plan, one way or another.

[? if radio >= 2: Our radio network has helped us spread our message. ?][? if pacifism >= 3 and nationalism <= 50 : We have rallied the workers to the cause of internationalism. ?]Although the bourgeois are not too pleased for us having monopolized the campaign for the Young Plan.

young_plan_referendum.bodyHtml:
= Young Plan Referendum
After months of campaigning and propaganda by both sides, the German people have come to vote on the referendum against the Young Plan, which has taken the backseat in comparison to the devastating economic depression. 
Passing the referendum would need to require the approval of more than 50% of those eligible to vote, rather than a majority of those that do vote. This makes it impossible for the referendum to succeed, even with the recent economic depression.

young_plan_referendum.results.bodyHtml: The referendum easily fails, with only around [+ young_plan_votes +]% of voters participating in it. It seems that nationalism is not omnipotent in Germany, despite everything. [? if young_plan_votes >= 20: However, the support for the referendum is higher than expected. ?][? if young_plan_votes < 12: The support for the referendum was lower than expected, this should weaken the right-wing parties. ?] The **NSDAP** is the main beneficiary of this campaign to the detriment of the [? if not dnf_formed: **DNVP**?][? if dnf_formed: **DNF**?].

young_plan_right_coalition.bodyHtml: = The Young Plan and the fall of the coalition The Foreign Ministry under Gustav Stresemann has agreed to the Young Plan, an agreement with the Western powers to reduce Germany's reparation payments and give us more fiscal autonomy. Simultaneously, France will agree to withdraw its military occupation from the Rhineland. While this seems to be a positive development for the country, the **DNVP**, despite their moderation, opposes the plan, claiming that any reparations are a form of national slavery. They have called for a vote of no confidence against the government, supported by the **NSDAP**, **DNF** and the **KPD**, and for a referendum on the Young Plan. We can either vote to bring down the government and hold new elections, or "tolerate" a government led by the remaining bourgeois parties.

z_in_gov.bodyHtml: The Center Party claims its ministerial positions, with Adam Stegerwald securing the Labor Ministry, and other members taking the Transport and Justice portfolios. With Ludwig Kaas’s connections in Rome, the negotiation of a Reichskonkordat is fast-tracked and set to be ready for signing in a few weeks. However, their entry into government has strained our relations, as they had previously stood in united opposition with us.

z_right_party_congress.bodyHtml: = [+ year +] [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] Conference With Hugenberg’s hardliners tightening their grip over the **DNVP**, any prospect of a merger with the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] has evaporated. But a new path to expansion has emerged. The party leadership now turns its attention to the fragmented remains of the anti-Hugenberg right—figures like Westarp and his **KVP**—as potential candidates for absorption. The consequences are obvious. Bringing these elements into the fold would drag the [? if z_party_name != "CVP": Center Party?][? if z_party_name == "CVP": **CVP**?] further to the right—foreclosing any serious cooperation with the **SPD** and entrenching the party within the conservative camp. A vote is now before them: merge with the **KVP**—or continue the status quo.
